en: The northern part of Texel, originally a separate dune island, later joined to Texel by a sand dike, after which the Eierland polder was formed by enclosing the mudflats. Extensive nature reserves lie on both the sea side and the Wadden side. The Eierlandse Gat (between Texel and Vlieland) is a seal reserve.

name: Eiger
en: A mountain peak in Switzerland, 3970 metres high.

name: Eijkmanstraat
en: Christiaan Eijkman (1858-1930), physician and bacteriologist, professor at Utrecht University. He discovered the cause of beriberi and received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1929.

name: Eikenplein
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Eikenweg
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Eilandsgracht
en: This neighbourhood once had many tanneries, where the hides of elk (elanden), deer, bears and so on were worked.

name: Einthovenstraat
en: Willem Einthoven (1860-1927), Leiden professor of physiology and heart specialist, inventor of the string galvanometer. He received the Nobel Prize in 1924.

name: Eisdenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Eisingastraat
en: Eise Eisinga (1744-1828), Frisian amateur astronomer. He built a planetarium that still exists in Franeker.

name: Ekangala
en: A village in South Africa, in the KwaNdebele area (formerly Transvaal) in the province of Mpumalanga.

name: EKapa
en: A South African name for Cape Town (colloquial).

name: Ekingenstraat
en: A church village on Noord-Beveland (Zeeland) drowned in 1532.

name: Eksteenfontein
en: A South African place name.

name: Eksterstraat
en: The bird (the magpie).

name: Elandsgracht
en: This neighbourhood once had many tanneries, where the hides of elk (elanden), deer, bears and so on were worked.

name: Elandsstraat
en: This neighbourhood once had many tanneries, where the hides of elk (elanden), deer, bears and so on were worked.

name: Elbaweg
en: An Italian island in the Mediterranean. Napoleon was exiled to Elba in 1814.

name: Elberveld
en: A South African place name.

name: Elckerlijcstraat
en: A fifteenth-century morality play (Everyman), attributed to Petrus van Diest. Its full title is 'Den spieghel der Salicheyt van Elckerlijc'.

name: Eldorado
en: Spanish for 'the gilded one', after a myth about an initiation ritual of the Muisca people of Colombia, in which a new chief had himself covered entirely in gold dust and swam in a mythical lake. The legend slowly changed from a person into a land of gold, sought for centuries by conquistadors, the French, the English and the Dutch.

name: Elegaststraat
en: A character from the Middle Dutch chivalric romance 'Karel ende Elegast'.

name: Elektronstraat
en: The smallest quantity of negative electricity, one of the building blocks of the atom.

name: Elementenstraat
en: The unit (cell) in a galvanic battery.

name: Elfendansstraat
en: The name refers to the poem 'Elvendans' (elves' dance) by Jacqueline E. van der Waals (1868-1922), included in the collection 'Nieuwe Verzen' (1909).

name: Elim
en: (Fragment) to Park Frankendael.

name: Elisabeth Adriaansestraat
en: Elisabeth (Betsy) Adriaanse (Roermond, 1906 - Chur, 1939) was a pioneer as a lawyer and a campaigner for women's suffrage.

name: Elisabeth Boddaertstraat
en: Jonkvrouw Elisabeth Boddaert (1867-1948) founded homes for neglected children in the Netherlands.

name: Elisabeth Samsonstraat
en: Surinamese businesswoman (1715-1771) who belonged to the class of fairly well-off free mulattoes (people of mixed descent). Unlike many whites in the colony, she could read and write. She lived as an equal with the white Carl Otto Creutz. In the slave society, despite racist opposition, she won herself an important position.

name: Elisabeth van Dorpstraat
en: Elisabeth (Lizzy) van Dorp (Arnhem, 5 September 1872 - Banyubiru, 6 September 1945) was a pioneer as a lawyer, economist and politician, and a campaigner for women's suffrage.

name: Elisabeth Wolffstraat
en: Elisabeth Wolff, née Bekker (Betje Wolff) (1738-1804), writer. With Aagje Deken she wrote, among others, 'Sara Burgerhart' and 'Willem Leevend'.

name: Eliza van Calcarstraat
en: Eliza Carolina Ferdinanda van Calcar-Schiotling (1822-1904), educator and writer. In 'De dubbele roeping der vrouw' (the double calling of woman) she argued for education for women.

name: Elizabeth Anscombestraat
en: Elizabeth Anscombe (1919-2001) was a British analytic philosopher.

name: Elizabeth Cady Stantonplein
en: American activist (1815-1902) who campaigned for women's suffrage in the United States. She extended her activism to Europe too, and in 1888 helped found the International Council of Women.

name: Ella Fitzgeraldstraat
en: Ella Jane Fitzgerald (1917-1996), regarded as one of the most important American jazz singers in history. Her hallmarks included a range of four octaves, clear diction and a gift for scat singing.

name: Ellert Vlieropstraat
en: A captain of the Beggars' fleet who fought at the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

name: Elpermeer
en: A nature reserve in the Grollo forestry (Drenthe).

name: Elpermeerpad
en: A nature reserve in the Grollo forestry (Drenthe).

name: Elsje Christiaensbrug
en: Elsje Christiaens was an 18-year-old Danish girl who was strangled on the Dam in 1664 because she had killed her landlady with an axe. She was hanged on the gallows field.

name: Elsrijkdreef
en: A former farm in Amstelveen.

name: Elstarstraat
en: A Dutch apple variety, yellow-green with a red blush, bred from a cross of Golden Delicious and Ingrid Marie.

name: Elzenhagensingel
en: The name of a farm on the Buikslotermeerdijk, demolished in 1964.

name: Elzenstraat
en: The tree (the alder).

name: Emanuel van Meterenstraat
en: Southern Netherlandish merchant and historian (1535-1612), whose works include 'Historie der Nederlandscher oorlogen' (history of the Netherlands wars).

name: Emanzana
en: A nature reserve in South Africa, east of Johannesburg, known for its sulphur spring, which the area's first inhabitants called Emanzana. The Zulu name Emanzana means 'healing water'.

name: Emfuleni
en: A municipality in South Africa, in the province of Gauteng. The Zulu name means 'place where there are many rivers'. The municipality got the name because it lies beside the Vaal river.

name: Emilie Knappertstraat
en: The founder of social work in the Netherlands (1860-1952).

name: Emmalaan
en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934), second wife of King Willem III, Queen Regent from 1890 to 1898, and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

name: Emmaplein
en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934), second wife of King Willem III, Queen Regent from 1890 to 1898, and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

name: Emmastraat
en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934), second wife of King Willem III, Queen Regent from 1890 to 1898, and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

name: Emmeline Pankhurststraat
en: English campaigner for women's suffrage (1858-1928), among other things head of the English society for women's suffrage. In London she gave public lectures and organised protest marches. She was arrested several times for her militancy. Pankhurst died in 1928, the year the women of Great Britain got the vote.

name: Emmikhovenstraat
en: An area in the Land van Altena (Noord-Brabant) drowned in the St Elizabeth's flood.

name: Emmy Andriessestraat
en: Photographer (1914-1953). During the Second World War she joined a group of photographers later known as 'De Ondergedoken Camera' (the hidden camera) and made a photo report of the Hunger Winter in Amsterdam. After the war she concentrated mainly on portrait photography.

name: Empangeni
en: A town in South Africa, in the province of KwaZulu-Natal.

name: Endumeni
en: A town in South Africa, formerly Dundee, in the province of KwaZulu-Natal. The Zulu name means 'place of the thunderstorm'; lightning often strikes the Endumeni hill.

name: Engcobo
en: A town in South Africa, in the Eastern Cape province.

name: Enge Kerksteeg
en: After the Oude Kerk, which the alleys lead to from the Warmoesstraat, part of which was originally called Kerkstraat.

name: Enge Lombardsteeg
en: After the nearby lommerd, or Bank van Lening (pawnshop), founded in 1614.

name: Engelsesteeg
en: The alley was already called this in the sixteenth century. There used to be many inns here, which shows it was a popular neighbourhood, perhaps particularly with English sailors.

name: Enkeldoorn
en: A South African place name.

name: Enkhuizerplein
en: The Noord-Holland town of Enkhuizen.

name: Enkhuizerstraat
en: The Noord-Holland town of Enkhuizen.

name: Ennemaborg
en: A late-medieval Groningen borg (fortified manor) near Midwolde (Groningen), restored around 1700. In its present form a stately country house.

name: Enneüs Heermabrug
en: This bridge is named after Enneüs Heerma (1944-1999). He was an alderman of Amsterdam for the CDA from 1978 to 1986. He then became state secretary, first for Foreign Trade and later for Housing. From 1994 to 1997 he led the CDA group in the House of Representatives.

name: Enny Vredestraat
en: (Belongs to Enneüs Heerma) He was an alderman of Amsterdam for the CDA from 1978 to 1986. He then became state secretary, first for Foreign Trade and later for Housing. From 1994 to 1997 he led the CDA group in the House of Representatives.

name: Entabeni
en: A game reserve in South Africa, in the province of Limpopo. The name means 'the place of the mountain', after its position in the mountainous Waterberg region. The area is part of a World Heritage site.

name: Entrepotdok
en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot, and in part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

name: Entrepotdoksluis
en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot, and in part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

name: Entrepothaven
en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot. In part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

name: Entrepothof
en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot, and in part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

name: Entrepotkade
en: Named after its function. The dock was built in 1827; imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid (a bonded warehouse, entrepot). The warehouses have lost their function as an entrepot, and in part of them the upper floors have now been converted into homes (Binnenkadijk).

name: Eosstraat
en: A figure from Greek mythology, also known as Aurore or Aurora: the goddess of sunrise and the dawn.

name: Epicurusstraat
en: Greek philosopher (341-270 BC). His philosophy held that only insight and a moral life lead to happiness.

name: Erasmusgracht
en: Desiderius Erasmus (1467-1536), humanist, who fiercely attacked the abuses in the Roman Catholic Church. His best-known work is 'In Praise of Folly'.

name: Ereprijsstraat
en: The plant.

name: Erich Salomonstraat
en: German-Jewish photojournalist (1886-1944), a pioneer of candid photography, in which people are photographed without their noticing. A grand master of political documentary and society photography.

name: Erik de Roodestraat
en: Also Eric the Red. A Norse navigator who settled in Iceland in 960 and from there discovered Greenland in 985.

name: Ernest Staesplein
en: The title of an 1874 prose collection by the Flemish writer Anton Bergmann (1835-1874).

name: Ernest Staesstraat
en: The title of an 1874 prose collection by the Flemish writer Anton Bergmann (1835-1874).

name: Ernst Cahn en Alfred Kohnbrug
en: Ernst Cahn, the man with whom Alfred Kohn (died 1941) ran the Koco ice-cream parlours, the home base of Jewish fighting squads in the Second World War.

name: Ernst Cahnsingel
en: Resistance fighter (1889-1941), owner of the ice-cream parlour 'Koco' on the Van Woustraat, from which resistance to anti-Jewish riots was organised in 1941.

name: Ertshaven
en: Ore boats used to be unloaded at this quay.

name: Ertskade
en: Ore boats used to be unloaded at this quay.

name: Escudolaan
en: The escudo is the currency of Portugal.

name: Eshowe
en: Eshowe is a town in South Africa whose name was inspired by the sound of the wind blowing through the native Dlinza forest.

name: Esmoreitstraat
en: A fourteenth-century Flemish abel spel (a serious secular play).

name: Esplanade de Meer
en: The former Ajax stadium De Meer.

name: Esther de Boer-van Rijkstraat
en: Actress (1854-1937). She played the part of Kniertje in Herman Heijermans's 'Op hoop van zegen' more than a thousand times.

name: Ethekwini
en: A port city in South Africa, formerly Durban, in the province of KwaZulu-Natal. The Zulu name means 'place where the ocean and the earth meet'.

name: Etnastraat
en: A volcano on the Italian island of Sicily, the highest and most active volcano in Europe.

name: Etty Hillesumbrug
en: Etty Hillesum (Middelburg, 15 January 1914 - Auschwitz, c. 30 November 1943) was a Jewish writer who wrote her diaries in the first years of the Second World War.

name: Eudorinastraat
en: A microscopic water creature, a flagellate alga. Because it contains chlorophyll it can assimilate carbon dioxide.

name: Eurokade
en: The name of the future European currency.

name: Europaboulevard
en: Named after the continent. The naming followed the resolution of the Consultative Assembly of the Council of Europe of 29 December 1957, which called on every municipality in Europe to give a square or street the name Europe, to help promote the idea of European unity. With this naming the name Westerscheldeplein (council decision of 30 January 1935) and the name Scheldestraat for part of that street (council decision of 16 February 1927) were abolished.

name: Europaplein
en: Named after the continent. The naming followed the resolution of the Consultative Assembly of the Council of Europe of 29 December 1957, which called on every municipality in Europe to give a square or street the name Europe, to help promote the idea of European unity. With this naming the name Westerscheldeplein (council decision of 30 January 1935) and the name Scheldestraat for part of that street (council decision of 16 February 1927) were abolished.

name: Eva Besnyöstraat
en: Hungarian-Dutch photographer (1910-2003), born in Budapest, who came to the Netherlands in the 1930s. Known for her socially engaged reportage, architectural photography and portraits.

name: Eva Schalkbrug
en: Eva Schalk (1890-1978) was the first woman on a water board. She was for 27 years a hoofdingeland (board member) of the Buikslotermeer polder and for 21 years a hoofdingeland of the Hoogheemraadschap (regional water board).

name: Everard van Reijdhof
en: Historian (1550-1602), councillor of the Frisian stadholder Willem Lodewijk. His works include 'Historie der Nederlandscher oorlogen' (history of the Netherlands wars), an important source for knowledge of the Dutch Revolt.

name: Eversdal
en: A South African place name.

name: Evert Cornelisstraat
en: Conductor and pianist (1884-1931). Second conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra from 1910 to 1919, then conductor of the Utrecht City Orchestra.

name: Evert van der Wallbrug
en: Evert van der Wall (1944-2003) was alderman for education and youth affairs in Amsterdam for the PvdA from 1979 to 1983. In 2002 he became chairman of the Oost-Watergraafsmeer district. He worked for the development of Oostpoort with a central district hall and a community school, and that is why this bridge is named after him.

name: Evertsweertplantsoen
en: A village near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland (Zeeland) drowned in 1530.

name: Evertsweertstraat
en: A village near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland (Zeeland) drowned in 1530.

name: Ewoud Worststraat
en: A Beggar admiral (died 1574) who took part in the uprising in Vlissingen in 1572 and the siege of Middelburg in 1573.

name: Ezelsbrug
en: The name of this bridge (donkey bridge) recalls the hard struggle the residents had to wage against the car lobby, which would rather have seen bridges for ordinary traffic here. They often felt like donkeys that kept stumbling over the same stone. The name also refers to the memory aid called an ezelsbruggetje (a mnemonic). The bridge was officially opened on 14 March 1987 by having a donkey walk across it.

name: F.C. Dondersstraat
en: Franciscus Cornelis Donders (1818-1889), world-famous ophthalmologist.

name: Faas Wilkesstraat
en: Servaas Wilkes (1923-2006), footballer. With his elegant play he was Johan Cruijff's great role model. He was the first Dutchman to play for a top foreign club. Until 1998 he held the Dutch national team record with 35 goals in 38 internationals.

name: Fagelstraat
en: Caspar Fagel (1629-1688), who in 1672 succeeded Johan de Witt as Grand Pensionary of Holland.

name: Fahrenheitsingel
en: Gabriel Daniel Fahrenheit (1686-1736), German by birth, who settled in the Netherlands as a physicist. In 1715 he set the freezing point of the thermometer at 32 degrees and the boiling point at 212 degrees. The Fahrenheitstraat was originally called De Wetstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 31 October 1901).

name: Fahrenheitstraat
en: Gabriel Daniel Fahrenheit (1686-1736), German by birth, who settled in the Netherlands as a physicist. In 1715 he set the freezing point of the thermometer at 32 degrees and the boiling point at 212 degrees. The Fahrenheitstraat was originally called De Wetstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 31 October 1901).

name: Falckstraat
en: Anton Reinhard Falck (1777-1843), statesman and lawyer, one of the leaders of the revolution of 1813. Under King Willem I he was Minister of Education, Industry and the Colonies. Founder of the Leesmuseum (reading society). The street was laid out on a filled-in part of the Achtergracht.

name: Fannius Scholtenstraat
en: Cornelis A. Fannius Scholten (1767-1832), lawyer in The Hague. During the revolution of 1813 he was, with Melchior Kemper, commissioner of the General Government in Amsterdam, and afterwards Councillor of State in extraordinary service.

name: Fanny Blankers-Koenlaan
en: Francina Elsje Blankers-Koen (1918-2004), athlete. She won four gold medals at the 1948 Olympic Games in London. In 1999 the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) named her 'Female Athlete of the Century'.

name: Fanny Durackstraat
en: Australian swimmer who won gold in the 100 metres freestyle at the 1912 Olympic Games in Stockholm, the first woman to win Olympic swimming gold.

name: Fanny Mendelssohnstraat
en: Fanny Mendelssohn was a German composer and pianist.

name: Faradaystraat
en: Michael Faraday (1791-1867), English physicist and chemist, founder of the electromagnetic theory of light.

name: Fazantenweg
en: The game bird (the pheasant).

name: Februariplein
en: After the February Strike of 25 and 26 February 1941, a protest strike against the first raids in the Jewish quarter.

name: Feike de Boerlaan
en: Feike de Boer (1892-1976), director of the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland' (Netherlands Steamship Company) from 1934 to 1946. He held countless other posts, among them board member of the N.V. Nederlandsch-Indische Steenkolen Handel Maatschappij and of the N.V. Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij. From 1945 to 1946, exactly three hundred days, he was burgomaster of Amsterdam.

name: Ferdinand Bolstraat
en: Painter (1616-1680), a pupil of Rembrandt, who painted portraits and regents' group portraits, among other things. (The boundary with the Gerard Doustraat was set more precisely by council decision of 9 June 1921.)

name: Ferdinand Huyckstraat
en: A historical novel by Jacob van Lennep about life in Amsterdam in the eighteenth century.

name: Ferguutstraat
en: A thirteenth-century Celtic (Arthurian) chivalric romance.

name: Ferrarisstraat
en: Galileo Ferraris (1847-1897), Italian mathematician and physicist, discoverer of the principle of rotating (three-phase) current.

name: Ferry Ploegerstraat
en: Ferdinand Ploeger (1915-1944), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Bloemendaal.

name: Fibigerstraat
en: Johannes Andreas Grib Fibiger (1867-1928), Danish physician, a well-known scientist in cancer research. He received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1926.

name: Fijnje van Salverdastraat
en: Johannes Gerardus Wijbo Fijnje van Salverda (1796-1889), water management and railway engineer and inventor. As chief engineer of Rijkswaterstaat he was put in charge of the improvement of the Nieuwe Waterweg.

name: Filips van Almondestraat
en: Naval hero (1646-1711), admiral in the Nine Years' War against France of 1688 to 1697.

name: Finsenstraat
en: Niels Finsen (1860-1904), Danish physician, inventor of the Finsen lamp named after him, for light therapy. He received the Nobel Prize in 1903. From 26 July 1939 until it was given this name, the street was part of the Bunsenstraat.

name: Firststraat
en: Ruth First (1925-1982), journalist, daughter of Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe who came to South Africa. She wrote about the evil consequences of apartheid. After several arrests she fled to England, where she kept working for the anti-apartheid movement. In 1982 she was murdered by the South African secret service.

name: Fizeaustraat
en: Armand Hippolyte Fizeau (1819-1896), French physicist, inventor of a method for measuring the speed of light.

name: Flamingostraat
en: A bird that lives in subtropical regions and occasionally appears in temperate zones too.

name: Flammarionstraat
en: Camille Flammarion (1842-1925), French astronomer and author of many popular works on astronomy and geology.

name: Fleerde
en: The name of a patrician house in Bergharen (Gelderland).

name: Flevopark
en: Named after Lake Flevo, from which the Zuiderzee formed.

name: Flevoparkweg
en: Named after Lake Flevo, from which the Zuiderzee (now the IJsselmeer) formed.

name: Flierbosdreef
en: The name of several farms, among them in Wouw (Noord-Brabant) and Stedum (Groningen).

name: Florapad
en: The collective name for the plant world. Originally the Roman goddess of spring and flowers.

name: Floraparkweg
en: The collective name for the plant world. Originally the Roman goddess of spring and flowers.

name: Floraweg
en: The collective name for the plant world. Originally the Roman goddess of spring and flowers.

name: Florence Nightingalestraat
en: British nurse (1820-1910), nicknamed the lady with the lamp, known from the Crimean War of 1854. She became the pioneer of modern nursing and was a forerunner of the Red Cross.

name: Florijn
en: The name of farms in Groenlo (Gelderland) and Wassenaar (Zuid-Holland). In Eibergen (Gelderland) it is the name of a hamlet.

name: Floris van der Laakenstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1919-1945), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad at Hattem. He was commander of the radio service of the Raad van Verzet (Resistance Council).

name: Floris Versterstraat
en: Painter (1861-1927), a pupil of Breitner and at first an impressionist. He painted still lifes, portraits and landscapes.

name: Fluessenlaan
en: A lake in southern Friesland.

name: Fluitschipstraat
en: A seventeenth-century cargo ship (the fluyt), a three-master with a rounded hull.

name: Foekje Dillemastraat
en: Athlete (1926-2007), rival of Fanny Blankers-Koen over 200 metres. After a compulsory sex test in 1950 she was banned for life, on the grounds that she was not fully a woman. The criteria were later changed, and after her death she was rehabilitated.

name: Foeliedwarsstraat
en: One of the products, important at the time, brought from the East Indies and stored here in the East India Company's warehouses (foelie is mace).

name: Foeliestraat
en: One of the products, important at the time, brought from the East Indies and stored here in the East India Company's warehouses (foelie is mace).

name: Foersterhof
en: Friedrich Wilhelm Foerster (1869-1959), founder of the modern work school (arbeidsschool).

name: Fogostraat
en: A volcano in Cape Verde that is still active.

name: Fokke Simonszstraat
en: Arend Fokke Simonsz (1755-1812), Amsterdam bookseller, poet and prose writer, who lived on the Looierssloot. Fokke was for a time in charge of the archives and antiquities, of which he left descriptions. The street was laid out on the Nieuwe Looierssloot, filled in in 1873.

name: Fokkemast
en: One of the masts (the foremost) of a ship: the foremast.

name: Fokkezeil
en: One of the sails of a ship (the foresail).

name: Fonteinkruidstraat
en: The name comes from the pondweed genus, of the family of the same name. Its leaves lie on the water surface or float under water, and its flowers are in green spikes.

name: Foppingadreef
en: A state, or farmstead, near Dronrijp (Friesland).

name: Forintplantsoen
en: The currency of Hungary (the forint).

name: Formosastraat
en: The island of Formosa, or Taiwan, off the coast of China, occupied by Japan until 1945 and Chinese after that. Taiwan is now in effect an independent state, although China regards the island as a Chinese province. The name, incidentally, is Portuguese: 'ilha formosa' means 'the beautiful island'.

name: Fortuinstraat
en: Named after the shipyard Het Fortuin (fortune), which was on the island of Wittenburg in the second half of the seventeenth century.

name: Fosfaatweg
en: Named after the phosphate factory to which this road and quay lead. Before 1949 the road was part of the Ringweg in the Amsterdammer Polder.

name: Foucaultstraat
en: Jean B.L. Foucault (1819-1868), French physicist. He demonstrated the rotation of the earth with a pendulum hung in the Panthéon in Paris, and discovered the induction (eddy) currents named after him.

name: Fraijlemaborg
en: The name of an estate in Slochteren. A borg was originally a stone fortification; the province of Groningen once had many borgen. The Fraeylemaborg is now a museum with period rooms.

name: Frambozenstraat
en: The fruit of the raspberry bush.

name: Frances Harperstraat
en: Frances Ellen Watkins Harper (1825-1911) was an African-American poet and writer.

name: Francisco Faleirostraat
en: An exiled Portuguese scholar who entered Spanish government service. His scientific work dealt with navigation and its problems. He supported Ferdinand Magellan in finding the route around South America.

name: Franciscus Claessenstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1894-1945), born in Helden, died in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp.

name: Frank Martinus Arionstraat
en: Frank Martinus Arion, pen name of Frank Efraim Martinus (Curaçao, 1936 - Curaçao, 2015), was a writer, poet and linguist. He worked in the Netherlands, Suriname and the Netherlands Antilles, and wrote in Dutch and Papiamentu. In 1955 Martinus Arion left for the Netherlands to study Dutch language and literature at Leiden University. There he came into contact with Cola Debrot, with whom he published his first collection of poems in 1957. He then founded an Antillean magazine, Encuentro Antilliano, with others. His debut novel Dubbelspel (double play, 1973) was his greatest success. In 1975 he taught at the teacher-training institute in Paramaribo. After Bouterse's coup the family left for Curaçao, where Martinus Arion concentrated on standardising and promoting Papiamentu. In 1996 his doctoral thesis on the origins of Papiamentu appeared: The Kiss of a Slave. Papiamentu's West-African Connections. In 2001 he was awarded the Cola Debrot Prize. In 1992 Arion was made a Knight of the Order of Orange-Nassau, but in 2008 he announced that he wanted to give the decoration back to the Dutch state. He believed that the Netherlands was recolonising the Antilles.

name: Frank van der Goesstraat
en: Journalist and writer (1859-1939), a well-known socialist theorist. Co-founder of 'De Nieuwe Gids', founder of the SDAP in 1894, and foreign editor of 'Het Volk'.

name: Frankemaheerdpad
en: Named after a farm in Warffum (Groningen).

name: Frankenstraat
en: The franc is the currency of France, Belgium, Luxembourg and Switzerland.

name: Frans Bastiaansestraat
en: W.A.F. Bastiaanse (1868-1947), poet and writer. He wrote the Geschiedenis der Nederlandsche Letterkunde (history of Dutch literature, 1927).

name: Frans de Wollantstraat
en: An eighteenth-century Dutch military engineer who made his name in Russia under Catherine the Great as a designer of hydraulic works and builder of the city of Odessa.

name: Frans Duwaerstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1911-1944), born in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad there too.

name: Frans Halsstraat
en: Painter (1580-1666) of portraits and militia group portraits.

name: Frans Naerebouthof
en: A Vlissingen pilot, known as a rescuer at sea (1748-1818). He became famous above all at the wreck of the Woestduin in 1779.

name: Frans van Mierisstraat
en: Frans van Mieris the Elder (1635-1681), painter of genre and history pieces. His father and his son were also well-known painters.

name: Franz Kafkastraat
en: Franz Kafka (1883-1924) was a German-language writer regarded as one of the most important authors of the twentieth century.

name: Franz Zieglerstraat
en: Photographer (1893-1939) who photographed members of the royal house and Hague society. Official court photographer from 1929.

name: Fraunhoferstraat
en: Joseph Fraunhofer (1787-1826), German physicist. He improved many optical instruments and discovered the lines in the solar spectrum (the Fraunhofer lines).

name: Fré Cohenbrug
en: Frederika Sophia Cohen (1903-1943), graphic artist, whose brochures, covers, bindings and other work gave 1930s design its face. She worked for the Amsterdam city printing office from 1929 to 1941, giving her own twist to influences from Jugendstil, the Amsterdam School and De Stijl. She went on working while in hiding until she was betrayed.

name: Fred Petterbaan
en: Frederik Hermanus Petter was a trade unionist and one of the leaders of the railway strike of 1903.

name: Fred. Roeskestraat
en: Frederik J. Roeske (1868-1961), conductor of the Royal Male Choir Apollo from 1891 to 1953, and also composer of music for a great many songs. Before it got this name, the street was part of the Prinses Irenestraat.

name: Fred. Thomasstraat
en: Fredericus F.X.M.D. Thomas (1906-1959), journalist, editor of the daily 'De Tijd' and author of 'Amsterdam, stad van mijn hart' (Amsterdam, city of my heart).

name: Frederik Hendrikplantsoen
en: Prince Frederik Hendrik (1584-1647), son of Prince William of Orange's fourth marriage, half-brother of Prince Maurice, and stadholder from 1625. His success as a military commander earned him the name 'stedendwinger' (tamer of cities). For some years the Frederik Hendrikplantsoen was first called Frederik Hendrikplein (council decision of 20 January 1886).

name: Frederik Hendrikstraat
en: Prince Frederik Hendrik (1584-1647), son of Prince William of Orange's fourth marriage, half-brother of Prince Maurice, and stadholder from 1625. His success as a military commander earned him the name 'stedendwinger' (tamer of cities). For some years the Frederik Hendrikplantsoen was first called Frederik Hendrikplein (council decision of 20 January 1886).

name: Frederik van Dorpstraat
en: A member of the Compromise of Nobles, of East Frisian descent (1547-1612). He fought at Heiligerlee and took part in the capture of Den Briel and the relief of Leiden.

name: Frederik van Eedenstraat
en: Writer and psychiatrist (1860-1932), co-founder of the literary magazine 'De Nieuwe Gids'. From 1894 he went his own way and founded a cooperative commune in Bussum. His works include 'Van de koele meren des doods' (the deeps of deliverance).

name: Frederiksplein
en: Prince Frederik Willem Karel (1798-1881), second son of King Willem I. Partly through his support the building of the Paleis voor Volksvlijt was promoted (opened 1864, burnt down 1929).

name: Frederiksstraat
en: Around 1880 Frederik Schröder provided a building loan for the houses along this street, which was then to be laid out, and so the street was named after him. The street was taken over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under this name.

name: Freek Oxstraat
en: Frederik Johannes Marius Ox (1920-1944), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, killed on 15 June 1944 in a gunfight with Germans in the Euterpestraat (now the Gerrit van der Veenstraat).

name: Fregatstraat
en: A fast-sailing three-masted ship (a frigate).

name: Fregelaan
en: Gottlob Frege (1848-1925), German mathematician and philosopher, professor in Jena. He was the first to give a consistently worked-out reduction of mathematics to logic, and designed the Begriffsschrift, a symbolic notation for logic.

name: Fresiastraat
en: The plant.

name: Freule Wttewaalpad
en: Freule Christine Wilhelmine Isabelle Wttewaal van Stoetwegen (1901-1986), politician, member of the House of Representatives for the Christian Historical Union from 1945 to 1971. She sat on the parliamentary inquiry committee (1949-1956) that investigated the policy of the Dutch government in London during the Second World War.

name: Frida Katzstraat
en: Frida Mackay-Katz (Amsterdam, 29 July 1885 - Aerdenhout, 30 March 1963) was a pioneer as a lawyer and as a municipal, national and local politician, and a campaigner for women's suffrage.

name: Frieslandstraat
en: The province. Several nearby streets are named after Frisian castles.

name: Frissenstein
en: The name of a manor house in Deil (Gelderland).

name: Frissensteinpad
en: The name of a manor house in Deil (Gelderland).

name: Frits Rotganshof
en: Photographer (1912-1978), a master of the panoramic photograph. During the Second World War he secretly photographed the German occupation. After the war he photographed the activity in the ports of Rotterdam and Amsterdam. In the 1960s Rotgans worked on aviation photography and photomontages.

name: Fritz Conijnstraat
en: Fritz Gerhard Marie Conijn (1923-1944), resistance fighter and student, born in Alkmaar, executed by firing squad in Vught.

name: Fritz Dietrich Kahlenbergstraat
en: Filmmaker (1916-1995), who also took many photographs during the Second World War. In 1944 he brought the Amsterdam group of photographers together to record the last year of the occupation. The group later became known as 'De Ondergedoken Camera' (the hidden camera).

name: Fröbelstraat
en: Friedrich Wilhelm August Fröbel (1782-1852), German educator, who founded the first kindergarten in 1827.

name: Funenkade
en: The strip of land on which the Czaar Peterstraat, among others, was laid out came inside the city with the expansion of 1658 and was afterwards called the Funen. The name recalled the Danish island of Funen, where Admiral De Ruyter won a naval battle against the Swedes in 1659.

name: Funenpark
en: The strip of land on which the Czaar Peterstraat, among others, was laid out came inside the city with the expansion of 1658 and was afterwards called the Funen. The name recalled the Danish island of Funen, where Admiral De Ruyter won a naval battle against the Swedes in 1659.

name: Funke Küpperstraat
en: Albert Funke Küpper (1894-1934), illustrator and caricaturist, who worked for the political-satirical weekly 'De Notenkraker'.

name: G.J. Scheurleerpad
en: Gerardus Jacobus Scheurleer (1886-1948), tennis player, many times Dutch doubles champion with, among others, Diemer Kool.

name: G.J. Scheurleerweg
en: Gerardus Jacobus Scheurleer (1886-1948), tennis player, many times Dutch doubles champion with, among others, Diemer Kool.

name: G.J.M. Sarlemijnstraat
en: Gerardus Josephus Maria Sarlemijn (1909-1993), Amsterdam architect. With Adriaan Evers he designed in the conservative Bossche School style. He received the city of Amsterdam's Golden Pin for listing the city's monuments.

name: G.T. Ketjenweg
en: Gerard Tileman Ketjen, dealer in drugs and paints and the original founder of AKZO Nobel. In 1835 he founded the Ketjen sulphuric acid works on what is now the Marnixstraat. From 1916 production was concentrated in Amsterdam-Noord. In 1969 the Ketjen works merged with the company AKU to form AKZO.

name: Gaandeweg
en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

name: Gaasp
en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp.

name: Gaasperdammerpad
en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp.

name: Gaasperdammerweg
en: After the hamlet of the same name on the small river Gaasp.

name: Gaasperparkpad
en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp.

name: Gaasperplas
en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp. The Gaasperplas itself is an artificial lake up to 35 metres deep, created by digging sand for building the Bijlmermeer.

name: Gaasperplaspad
en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp. The Gaasperplas itself is an artificial lake up to 35 metres deep, created by digging sand for building the Bijlmermeer.

name: Gaasperzoompad
en: The name comes from the small river Gaasp.

name: Gaaspstraat
en: The small river Gaasp, the part of the Weespertrekvaart that was not dug.

name: Gaasterlandpad
en: The southern part of Friesland, between Stavoren and Lemmer. Here are the only places where the Frisian coast does not need dikes to protect it.

name: Gaasterlandstraat
en: The southern part of Friesland, between Stavoren and Lemmer. Here are the only places where the Frisian coast does not need dikes to protect it.

name: Gabriël Metsustraat
en: Painter (1629-1667), mainly of genre pieces, and a pupil of Gerard Dou. A street had already been named after Metsu on 10 June 1880, but that name was changed to Paulus Potterstraat in 1893.

name: Gabriela Mistralstraat
en: Gabriela Mistral (1889-1957) was a Chilean poet, the first Latin American to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Gaffelaarspad
en: A ship with a flat bottom and a round stem, used mainly on inland waterways.

name: Gaffelstraat
en: A farm implement (a pitchfork) for pitching hay.

name: Galantstraat
en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

name: Galastraat
en: A sweet, juicy apple from New Zealand, a variety that arose in the first half of the twentieth century.

name: Galgenbrug
en: The name (gallows bridge) refers to the view from this bridge of the gallows of the Volewijk, which stood there until 1795.

name: Galgenstraat
en: The view from this street of the gallows of the Volewijk is the origin of this name. In 1662 the city council decided to change the name to Prinsendwarsstraat, but that name never caught on.

name: Galggouw
en: This gouw (village road), in the municipality of Broek in Waterland, owes its name to an old gallows field.

name: Galileïplantsoen
en: Galileo Galilei (1564-1642), Italian mathematician, professor at Pisa and Padua. He discovered the laws of falling bodies and of the pendulum, built the first telescope and discovered many celestial bodies.

name: Galjoenstraat
en: A heavy, cumbersome sailing ship of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries (a galleon), with three or four masts and a high forecastle and sterncastle.

name: Galjootstraat
en: A ship: a flat-bottomed merchant ship with leeboards for coastal trade (a galliot).

name: Galvanistraat
en: Luigi Galvani (1737-1798), Italian physicist, who discovered electricity generated by chemical action.

name: Galwin
en: A corrupted spelling of the Irish port of Galway, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Gamerenstraat
en: The Gamerenstraat (formerly Van Gamerenstraat) is named after Virginie Gameren (Curaçao, 19 March 1833 - date and place of death unknown). Virginie was an enslaved woman who fought for her freedom by starting legal proceedings against her owner. She won, and so forced the Ministry of the Colonies to grant her freedom. She took the surname Gameren, which gave her and her children autonomy.

name: Ganzebloemstraat
en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

name: Ganzenhoefpad
en: The name of a farm on the Vecht near Maarsseveen (Utrecht).

name: Ganzenveldstraat
en: The Ganzenveld is part of the Schoorl dunes (Noord-Holland).

name: Ganzenweg
en: The water bird (the duck).

name: Garcia Lorcastraat
en: Federico García Lorca (1898-1936) was a progressive Spanish poet and playwright.

name: Gare du Nord
en: A major railway station in the north of Paris, opened in 1864.

name: Garstkamp
en: The name of a farm near Beesd (Gelderland).

name: Gasthuismolensteeg
en: On the city rampart (the Singel), where the alley is now, stood the mill of the Sint Elisabethsgasthuis (fifteenth and sixteenth centuries). The Sint Elisabethsgasthuis was the city's oldest hospital, founded in the fourteenth century. In 1492 its building was added to the city hall. Both buildings were later demolished to build the new city hall (now the palace). Before 1913 this was the Wijde Gasthuismolensteeg; earlier still the names Molensteeg and Benninghstraat occur.

name: Gatwickstraat
en: The name of one of London's airports.

name: Gebroeders A. en B. Wolfswinkelweg
en: The brothers Antoon (1919-1942) and Bertus (1921-1942) Wolfswinkel, resistance fighters. They distributed clandestine material, collected money for the resistance and belonged to a sabotage group at the Fokker factory in Amsterdam-Noord, where they worked. They took an active part in the February Strike of 1941. On 19 November 1942 both were executed by firing squad at Soesterberg.

name: Gedempt Hamerkanaal
en: Refers to the former Hamerkanaal (gedempt: filled in).

name: Gedempte Begijnensloot
en: The hof (courtyard), founded in the fourteenth century, was built to house beguines (lay sisters). The Begijnhof, together with the Sint Luciënklooster, was originally surrounded entirely by water. Behind the houses of the Kalverstraat ran a ditch, the Begijnensloot, which led from the Spui, not yet filled in at the time, to the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. This ditch was neglected, and so what remained of it was filled in in 1865. It was given the name Gedempte Begijnensloot, a name made official by a council decision in 1914.

name: Gedempte Insteekhaven
en: This side basin (insteekhaven) was part of the shipyard of the Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM). Several floating dry docks lay in it. It was filled in to build housing on the site.

name: Geduld
en: The ability to wait a long time to reach a goal (patience).

name: Geelbekstraat
en: The songbird (the yellowhammer), of the finch family.

name: Geelvinckssteeg
en: On the corner of this alley there once stood two warehouses called De Geelvinck. The name first appears in the last years of the sixteenth century.

name: Geer Ban
en: The Geer Ban, or Vrije Geer, was one of the four parts that made up the municipality of Sloten in earlier centuries. A ban was in the old days an administrative district; a number of bannen together formed a bailiwick.

name: Geerdinkhof
en: A very old name of a plot of land at Vasse near Tubbergen (Overijssel).

name: Geerdinkhofpad
en: A very old name of a plot of land at Vasse near Tubbergen (Gelderland).

name: Geerdinkhofweg
en: A very old name of a plot of land at Vasse near Tubbergen (Gelderland).

name: Geert Geertsenbrug
en: Geert Geertsen was the birth name of Desiderius Erasmus (1467-1536). Because his Dutch name is linked to the word begeerte (desire), he took the Latin word for desire as his first name and the Greek word as his surname.

name: Geert Grootestraat
en: Philosopher (1340-1384), founder of the Brethren of the Common Life. He railed against the abuses in the church, but also against heretics. He founded the religious renewal known as the Modern Devotion.

name: Geertje Wielemaplein
en: Swimmer (1934-2009), who won a silver medal in the 100 metres backstroke at the 1952 Olympic Games in Helsinki. In 1954 she became the Netherlands' first Sportswoman of the Year.

name: Geertruida van Lierstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1915-1969), involved in many clandestine activities and a member of the Amsterdam resistance group CS-6.

name: Geervliet
en: An old little town (town rights 1381) on the Brielse Maas and the now silted-up Bernisse (Zuid-Holland).

name: Geldersekade
en: At the city's second expansion on the east side, today's Geldersekade was the city moat. So the inner bank (on the Zeedijk side) is the oldest, built around 1500. The other side lay outside the city until 1585. In the seventeenth century the old side was called partly Keulse kaai (Cologne quay) and further on Gelderse kaai, and for a short time also Londense kaai or Engelse kaai. The names came from the landing stages here where ships moored that sailed to the towns of Gelderland, to Cologne, London and other English ports. Some remains of the city wall built here around 1500 between the Waag and the Schreierstoren can still be found in the quay wall and by the Bantammerbrug. To match the name of the quay, in 1911 the alley previously called Leliestraat was renamed Geldersesteeg.

name: Geldersekade
en: At the city's second expansion on the east side, today's Geldersekade was the city moat. So the inner bank (on the Zeedijk side) is the oldest, built around 1500. The other side lay outside the city until 1585. In the seventeenth century the old side was called partly Keulse kaai (Cologne quay) and further on Gelderse kaai, and for a short time also Londense kaai or Engelse kaai. The names came from the landing stages here where ships moored that sailed to the towns of Gelderland, to Cologne, London and other English ports. Some remains of the city wall built here around 1500 between the Waag and the Schreierstoren can still be found in the quay wall and by the Bantammerbrug. To match the name of the quay, in 1911 the alley previously called Leliestraat was renamed Geldersesteeg.

name: Geldershoofd
en: The name of a country estate near Brummen (Gelderland). Before their renovation in 1983, the buildings Geldershoofd and Gravestein together formed the Gliphoeve building.

name: Geleenstraat
en: A small river in South Limburg that flows into the Maas at Stevensweert.

name: Geleyn Bouwenszstraat
en: A captain of the Sea Beggars at the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

name: Gelrestraat
en: The old name of Gelderland. Also a county (1046-1339) and then, until 1795, a duchy, roughly matching today's Gelderland plus part of Limburg and Germany.

name: Generaal Vetterstraat
en: Jacobus Augustinus Vetter (1837-1907), military commander-in-chief of the expeditions to Lombok (1894) and Aceh (1896).

name: Generatorstraat
en: The machine for generating electric current.

name: Genhoes
en: Genhoes castle, or Oud-Valkenburg, near Valkenburg (Limburg), built around 1500: a late-Gothic main building of marlstone, altered and extended in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and restored from 1962.

name: Gentiaanplein
en: The plant family (gentians).

name: Gentiaanstraat
en: The plant family (gentians).

name: George Balanchinestraat
en: George Balanchine was an American choreographer of Georgian descent, regarded as one of the most important choreographers of twentieth-century classical ballet.

name: George Gershwinlaan
en: American composer and pianist (1898-1937) who worked jazz elements into classical music. He wrote the opera 'Porgy and Bess' and countless musicals, as well as piano works, orchestral works and concertos.

name: George Gershwinplein
en: American composer and pianist (1898-1990) who worked jazz elements into classical music. He wrote the opera 'Porgy and Bess' and countless musicals, as well as piano works, orchestral works and concertos.

name: George Madurobrug
en: George John Lionel Maduro (1916-1945) was a resistance man of Antillean descent who died in the Dachau concentration camp. The miniature city of Madurodam in The Hague is named after him.

name: George Sandstraat
en: Pseudonym of Aurore Dupin, Baroness Dudevant (1804-1876), French novelist. Through her free way of life and in her work she stood up for the unrestrained development of women. She counts as the first truly emancipated woman of the modern era.

name: George Sliekerkade
en: George Christiaan Slieker (1861-1945), the first Dutch film exhibitor, who toured fairs and markets with his travelling cinema.

name: George Westinghousestraat
en: American engineer (1846-1914) who invented the Westinghouse brake named after him: an air brake, used especially on the railways.

name: Ger van Zanenbrug
en: Ger van Zanen (1929-2015) was a passionate nature lover and from 1960 until his death a member of the Royal Dutch Natural History Society, Amsterdam (KNNV). Under his leadership a great deal of field-biology research and surveying was done in Amsterdam. Ger van Zanen was always ready to show anyone interested the way in nature. The bridge leads from the housing area to the Ruige Riet, a valuable, still untouched nature area that is part of the Sloterpark. The area is rich in mushrooms, among other things, and people on mushroom walks mostly cross the bridge and will all remember Ger van Zanen. On 14 February 2004 Ger van Zanen received the Amsterdam Nature and Environment Prize on behalf of the KNNV Amsterdam branch from alderman Stadig.

name: Geraardsbergenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of East Flanders.

name: Geraniumweg
en: The garden and house plant.

name: Gerard Borstkade
en: Jacobus Gerardus Gerbrant Borst (1902-1975), internist, for 35 years professor at the University of Amsterdam and head of the internal medicine clinic at the Binnengasthuis. During the war years he was, among other things, one of the leaders of the doctors' resistance. Founder of modern blood transfusion therapy.

name: Gerard Brandtstraat
en: Remonstrant theologian (1626-1685) who wrote church history at first and poetry later. Until 1896 the street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel and was called H.G. Kosterstraat, after a building contractor (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 5 October 1880).

name: Gerard Callenburgstraat
en: Fleet commander (1642-1722). Captain of Admiral De Ruyter's flagship, he took part in the naval battles of Solebay (1672) and off Etna (1676) and in the capture of Gibraltar (1704).

name: Gerard Douplein
en: Painter (1613-1675), a representative of the Leiden school, a pupil of Rembrandt and teacher of, among others, Metsu and Van Mieris.

name: Gerard Doustraat
en: Painter (1613-1675), a representative of the Leiden school, a pupil of Rembrandt and teacher of, among others, Metsu and Van Mieris.

name: Gerard Hulst van Keulenstraat
en: From 1756 Gerard Hulst van Keulen (1733-1801) ran the well-known firm of Van Keulen, which for two centuries (c. 1680-1885) was based in Amsterdam on the corner of the Nieuwebrugsteeg and the Prins Hendrikkade. The firm specialised in making and selling sea charts and nautical instruments, and published and sold books, mainly on nautical subjects.

name: Gerard Revebrug
en: Gerard Kornelis van het Reve (1923-2006), writer and poet. With Harry Mulisch (1927-2010) and Willem Frederik Hermans (1921-1995) he formed the Big Three of post-war literature. His works include 'De avonden' (the evenings, 1947), 'Werther Nieland' (1949) and 'Nader tot U' (nearer to thee, 1966). He received the P.C. Hooft Prize (1968) and the Prize for Dutch Literature (2001).

name: Gerard Ruttenhof
en: Film director (1902-1982). With 'Dood water' (dead water, 1934), about the building of the Afsluitdijk, and 'Rubber' (1935), about a planter's wife in Suriname, he made two important Dutch feature films of the 1930s.

name: Gerard Schaepstraat
en: Councillor and schepen (alderman) of Amsterdam (1594-1666), ambassador to the English and Danish courts.

name: Gerard Terborgstraat
en: Painter (1617-1681) of portraits and genre pieces.

name: Gerardus van der Groeplaan
en: Resistance fighter (1922-1945) who worked at the Fokker factory in Amsterdam-Noord and belonged to a sabotage group there. He distributed 'De Waarheid' and raised money for the resistance. Sentenced to death in 1942, a sentence commuted to life imprisonment with penal servitude. Freed by the French, he died on 16 July 1945.

name: Gerda Brautigamstraat
en: Gerarda Brautigam (1913-1982), politician and journalist. Editor at Het Vrije Volk from 1945 to 1967 and member of the House of Representatives for the Labour Party (PvdA) from 1963 to 1972. She worked above all for consumer affairs, which made her very well known.

name: Gerda Tarobrug
en: Gerda Taro (1910-1937) was the first woman photographer at the front. She fought against Nazism, and her passion has made her a symbol of anti-fascism.

name: Gerrie Knetemannlaan
en: Racing cyclist (1951-2004), nicknamed 'de Kneet'. His greatest success was the world road championship in 1978.

name: Gerrie Mührenbrug
en: Gerrie (Gerrit) Mühren.

name: Gerrit Bronkepad
en: Gerrit Bronke (nineteenth century) designed the church in Holysloot (a national monument) in 1846. For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Gerrit Mannourystraat
en: Mathematician and philosopher (1867-1956), professor at the University of Amsterdam and one of the most important Dutch mathematicians of this century.

name: Gerrit Stuyverstraat
en: A Sea Beggar who fought at the relief of Haarlem in 1572.

name: Gerrit van den Boschpad
en: Resistance fighter (1911-1944) who played an important part in distributing the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid'. He died in the Dachau concentration camp.

name: Gerrit van der Puijstraat
en: A resident of Sloten (1915-1988) who worked for the Sloten community for many years.

name: Gerrit van der Veenstraat
en: Gerrit Jan van der Veen (1902-1944), resistance fighter and sculptor by profession, who won the Prix de Rome for his sculpture. He took an active part in the resistance. Van der Veen was one of the instigators of the attack on the population register (27 March 1943) and was executed by firing squad in the dunes near Overveen. The street was previously called Euterpestraat, after the muse of music and poetry, and during the occupation of 1940-1945 was notorious because the German Sicherheitsdienst (SD) was based in the girls' secondary school (Meisjes-HBS).

name: Gerrit van Erkelstraat
en: Gerrit van Erkel (1860-1937), leader of the radical-socialist trade union movement.

name: Gerrit Versteegstraat
en: Architect (1873-1938) who built part of Tuindorp Watergraafsmeer, worked with Hendrik Berlage on the western part of the Transvaalbuurt, and designed the housing blocks on the Koekoekstraat in Noord.

name: Gerritsloot
en: The origin of the name is unclear.

name: Geschutswerf
en: Geschut (ordnance) is the collective name for cannon and heavy machine guns. The street lies where the Ordnance Yard of the Admiralty of Amsterdam was; guns were made here in the eighteenth century.

name: Geulstraat
en: A small river in South Limburg, a tributary of the Maas. The Geul valley forms part of the border with Belgium.

name: Geurt Brinkgrevebrug
en: Monument conservationist, sculptor and writer (1917-2005). An advocate for preserving the historic city centre, he eventually brought about a turning point in thinking about the old cultural heritage. He also played a major part in keeping the old street pattern of the Nieuwmarkt neighbourhood. He received the Silver Medal (Zilveren Penning) in 1982.

name: Geuzenkade
en: At first meant as a term of abuse (geuzen: beggars), but taken as a title of honour by the allied nobles in the fight against Spain. Later the fighting name of all opponents of Spain in the Eighty Years' War. The Korte Geuzenstraat was earlier part of the Geuzenstraat.

name: Geuzenstraat
en: At first meant as a term of abuse (geuzen: beggars), but taken as a title of honour by the allied nobles in the fight against Spain. Later the fighting name of all opponents of Spain in the Eighty Years' War. The Korte Geuzenstraat was earlier part of the Geuzenstraat.

name: Gevlebrug
en: The Swedish port of Gävle on the Gulf of Bothnia, an important timber export port and now one of Sweden's largest oil ports.

name: Gevlewater
en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

name: Gibraltarstraat
en: The southern tip of Spain, named here for the naval battle against the Spanish in 1607 in which Jacob van Heemskerck was killed.

name: Gierzwaluwbrug
en: The common swift (Apus apus) is a very special bird. Swifts spend almost their whole lives in the air: they eat, drink, mate and even sleep on the wing! They land only in spring at a fixed nest site, usually under roof tiles. They breed in almost every city in Europe, including the centre of Amsterdam, and catch mainly midges in flight. They are enormously fast and agile in the air, but once landed on the nest they can only shuffle on their short legs. In the Bijlmerweide by the G-buurt, seven bridges have been given bird names beginning with G. City ecologists gave a workshop about birds to children from the local Kidsclub, who then chose their favourite species. So each bridge got a unique name that suits the nature around it. These names are part of a naming project carried out in 2024.

name: Giessenburg
en: A lost castle at Giessen-Oudekerk, of which some remains survive.

name: Gieterij
en: This and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM). To recall that former use, the names of the various workshops were used for the streets, in this case the shipyard's foundry (gieterij).

name: Gietersstraat
en: Named after 't Giethuis, the city's gun and bell foundry, which stood here from 1614 to 1821. The street name first came into use in the eighteenth century.

name: Gijsbrecht van Aemstelstraat
en: After Gijsbrecht IV (c. 1235-1303), the last lord of Aemstel to be Lord of Amsterdam, and bailiff of Amstelland. Made famous by Vondel's tragedy.

name: Gijsbrecht van IJselsteinstraat
en: Bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland from 1358 to 1361.

name: Gillis Steltmanstraat
en: A Sea Beggar who became known at the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

name: Gillis van Ledenberchstraat
en: Clerk of the States of Utrecht (1550-1618), a supporter of Van Oldenbarnevelt, imprisoned by Prince Maurice. The street was earlier called Tweede Hugo de Grootdwarsstraat (council decisions of 13 October 1897 and 1 September 1908).

name: Glauberweg
en: Johann Rudolf Glauber (1604-1670), German chemist and physician. He discovered the laxative effect of the Glauber's salt named after him, used against bile complaints.

name: Glitterstraat
en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

name: Gloriantstraat
en: A fourteenth-century abel spel (a serious secular play).

name: Goed Geluimd hof
en: The name belongs to the theme 'Sociaal en tevreden wonen' (Social and contented living) for the G-buurt Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

name: Goeman Borgesiusstraat
en: Hendrik Goeman Borgesius (1847-1917), liberal statesman, Minister of the Interior from 1897 to 1901 (Compulsory Education Act, Housing Act, Accidents Act).

name: Goereestraat
en: Part of the Zuid-Holland island of Goeree-Overflakkee.

name: Golfbaanpad
en: A path by the De Hoge Dijk golf course.

name: Gooiluststraat
en: An estate in 's-Graveland, of which the Corversbos was originally also part. 's-Graveland is a stretch of Gooi heath from which the sand was dug away (afzanding). Once the sand was removed, Amsterdam regents laid out country estates and nurseries here in the seventeenth century.

name: Gooioord
en: The name of a manor house in Bussum (Noord-Holland).

name: Gooise Kant
en: A neighbourhood access road that comes out on and connects to the K-buurt and the Gooiseweg.

name: Gooiseweg
en: The road leads towards Het Gooi.

name: Gordijnensteeg
en: Named after the sixteenth- and seventeenth-century residents Willem and Samuel du Gardijn. At that time the alley was also known as Bloeddwarsstraat.

name: Gorontalostraat
en: A town on the island of Sulawesi (Celebes) in Indonesia.

name: Gorsstraat
en: A name used in Zuid-Holland for vegetated land outside the dikes that floods only at high water (elsewhere called schor or kwelder: salt marsh).

name: Gosschalklaan
en: Isaac Gosschalk (1838-1907), one of the most important Dutch architects of the nineteenth century. In 1885 Gosschalk was commissioned by the Imperial Continental Gas Association to design the buildings of the Westergasfabriek.

name: Goudbalpad
en: An old Dutch pear variety. The street lies on the former De Bongerd allotment complex.

name: Gouden Leeuw
en: The name of a farm in the Haarlemmermeer (the golden lion). (The name also occurs in Hummelo and Leiden.)

name: Goudestein
en: A castle near Maarssen on the Vecht, dating from 1754, built for the Amsterdam burgomaster Huydecoper.

name: Goudreinetstraat
en: The fruit, a variety of apple (golden reinette).

name: Goudriaanstraat
en: Bernardus Hermanus Goudriaan (1796-1842), chief engineer of Rijkswaterstaat, appointed by the government to assess the first railway plans.

name: Goudsbloemstraat
en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

name: Goudvinkbrug
en: The bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is perhaps the most beautiful bird in the country. Males and females both have a black head. The male can be recognised by his bright rose-red belly and cheeks. Bullfinches are in this park all year round, but despite their bright colours they are hard to see. Many inconspicuous little brown birds sing beautifully, but this handsome bird can only make squeaking sounds. You can't have everything. In the Bijlmerweide by the G-buurt, seven bridges have been given bird names beginning with G. City ecologists gave a workshop about birds to children from the local Kidsclub, who then chose their favourite species. So each bridge got a unique name that suits the nature around it. These names are part of a naming project carried out in 2024.

name: Gouwenaarssteeg
en: Named after the broker Willem Jac. Gouwenaar, who lived on the corner of the Stromarkt around 1600.

name: Govert Flinckstraat
en: Painter (1615-1660), a pupil of Rembrandt, known above all for his militia group portraits and portraits.

name: Gowin Knightstraat
en: English physician (1713-1772) who in the eighteenth century published on magnetic experiments relating to the compass used by sailors.

name: Graaf Florisstraat
en: Floris V (1254-1296), Count of Holland, murdered by the nobles. Count Floris granted Amsterdam its oldest known privilege, which in 1275 gave 'den luden bij Amstelredam' (the people near Amstelredam) exemption from tolls. It is also the oldest dated document in which the name Amsterdam appears.

name: Graafschapstraat
en: A much-used name for part of the Achterhoek in Gelderland, originally the old county (graafschap) of Zutphen. Part of the street was renamed Jacob Soetendorpstraat in 1978.

name: Graanstraat
en: The collective name for the farm crops that belong to the grass family (grain).

name: Graftdijkerstraat
en: A village in Noord-Holland between the Beemster and the Schermer.

name: Graham Bellstraat
en: Alexander Graham Bell (1847-1922), Scottish physicist, who built the first practical telephone.

name: Gran Paradiso
en: The highest mountain entirely within Italy, 4061 metres.

name: Granaatstraat
en: A semi-precious stone (garnet).

name: Granidastraat
en: A tragedy by P.C. Hooft (1602-1605).

name: Grasrijk
en: A former farm on the Uitweg, demolished to build the garden city of Osdorp.

name: Grasweg
en: The commonest and largest plant family (grasses).

name: Gravenstraat
en: The counts of the House of Hainaut (1299-1345). When they were in Amsterdam, they stayed at an inn that stood here at the time. The little street appears as early as the beginning of the fifteenth century as 's-Gravenstraat (the count's street).

name: Gravestein
en: Named after a Surinamese plantation. Before their renovation in 1983, the buildings Gravestein and Geldershoofd together formed the building called Gliphoeve.

name: Grensstraat
en: Before 1896 the street formed the boundary (grens) between Amsterdam and Nieuwer-Amstel.

name: Grevelingenstraat
en: A sea channel between the islands of Goeree and Schouwen, now closed off from the open sea by the Grevelingendam.

name: Grianestraat
en: A tragicomedy by Bredero from 1612.

name: Griendstraat
en: The collective name for a growth of woody plants (mostly willows) that are cut regularly (osier beds). Griend or grint land lies in or along water.

name: Griftstraat
en: A dug channel on the Veluwe that flows into the IJssel at Hattem.

name: Grimbergenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Grimburgwal
en: After the water called the Grim, which formed the city's southern boundary from 1342 to about 1400 (grim = muddy ditch).

name: Grimnessesluis
en: This fixed bridge is named after the water called the Grim (muddy ditch), which formed the city's southern boundary from 1342 to about 1400.

name: Griseldestraat
en: A sproke from 1393. A sproke is a medieval rhymed tale, comparable to a boert or farce.

name: Groen van Prinstererstraat
en: Guillaume Groen van Prinsterer (1801-1876), statesman and historian, leader of the Anti-Revolutionaries from 1849 to 1866, and a fierce opponent of liberals and Roman Catholics.

name: Groenburgwal
en: The land between the Kloveniersburgwal and the Zwanenburgwal, where the cloth-drying frames stood and which was added to the city in 1593, was then the site of the dye works. This canal was therefore originally called Verwersgracht (dyers' canal). Early in the seventeenth century the name Groenburgwal arose, because there were green dye works here in particular.

name: Groene Ridderhof
en: After Jan Claesz. Groene Ridder, properly Backer (1588-?). He owned the ship De Groene Ridder (the green knight), but around 1631 decided to run a skippers' inn by the Kadoelenbreek. Around 1538 he sold it again. On this spot, level with Landsmeerderdijk 195, there has been an inn or café ever since.

name: Groene Ridderpad
en: After Jan Claesz. Groene Ridder, properly Backer (1588-?). He owned the ship De Groene Ridder (the green knight), but around 1631 decided to run a skippers' inn by the Kadoelenbreek. Around 1538 he sold it again. On this spot, level with Landsmeerderdijk 195, there has been an inn or café ever since.

name: Groene Spechtbrug
en: The green woodpecker (Picus viridis) hacks a hole in a tree to make its nest. Hacking it out takes more than two weeks, so they often use an existing hole. Green woodpeckers have a very long, sticky tongue with which they can lick insects out from behind the bark. But they mainly eat ants, on the ground. You can recognise them easily by their moss-green back and the red cap on their head. A funny fact: they can also laugh very loudly! In the Bijlmerweide by the G-buurt, seven bridges have been given bird names beginning with G. City ecologists gave a workshop about birds to children from the local Kidsclub, who then chose their favourite species. So each bridge got a unique name that suits the nature around it. These names are part of a naming project carried out in 2024.

name: Groenehuyzen
en: A former farm in the old municipality of Sloten.

name: Groenendaalstraat
en: An estate near Heemstede (Noord-Holland).

name: Groeneveen
en: An old sixteenth-century patrician house in Velsen (also called Papenburg).

name: Groenhoedenveem
en: A veem is a company that stores goods in its warehouses and delivers them from there. Each veem had its own emblem, after which it was named. These could be hats of different colours and shapes (among them Groenhoeden, green hats, and Klapmutsen). They also took their names from where their workmen came from (among them the Vriesseveem and the Zeeuwse Veem).

name: Groenhoven
en: The name of several farms (Leiden, Loosduinen, Wassenaar and Kerkwijk).

name: Groenlandia
en: A whaler that sailed from Oostzanerwerf around 1759, owned by the shipowner Aard Speciaal (1717-1760).

name: Groenlandstraat
en: An island in the Atlantic Ocean, north-east of Canada. Greenland is part of the Kingdom of Denmark and is the largest island in the world.

name: Groenlust
en: A farm on the Noorderweg, against the Enge Wormer, in the Wijde Wormer.

name: Groenmarktkade
en: Groenmarkt is short for Groentemarkt (vegetable market), held here from 1896 to 1934. In 1934 the Centrale Markthallen opened on the Jan van Galenstraat, after which this vegetable market was closed.

name: Groenpad
en: A former lane in the old municipality of Sloten.

name: Groentemarktbrug
en: Named after the vegetable market held near here until 1934. In that year the trade moved to the Centrale Markthallen.

name: Groentepraambrug
en: The name of this bridge recalls the time when many vegetable barges sailed from the west via the Admiralengrachten and the Kostverlorenkade to the Marnixstraat, where the vegetables were traded. Pramen are low little boats that can easily pass through polder ditches and under footbridges.

name: Groesbeekdreef
en: The name of the dreef (avenue) above it.

name: Groetstraat
en: The Noord-Holland village on the edge of the dunes.

name: Groezestraat
en: Silted-up land outside the dikes with light vegetation, also known as kwelder, gors, schor or schol (salt marsh).

name: Groningenstraat
en: The province. The adjoining streets are named after Groningen castles (borgen).

name: Groot Blankenberg
en: A former castle, destroyed in 1381. On its site now stands the house Blankenberg, built as a convent in 1825, near Cadier en Keer (Limburg).

name: Groot-Essenburg
en: A building from 1652 near Hierden on the Veluwe, built on the foundations of a thirteenth-century castle and restored in 1929.

name: Groote Braak
en: The name refers to the breach of the Spaarndammerdijk in a north-westerly storm in 1675. The water of the IJ then tore a gap 140 metres wide and almost 10 metres deep in the defences.

name: Grootslagstraat
en: A large polder west of Enkhuizen.

name: Grootzeil
en: One of the sails of a ship (the foresail).

name: Grootzeilhof
en: One of the sails of a ship (the foresail).

name: Grossglockner
en: The highest mountain in Austria, 3787 metres.

name: Grote Beerstraat
en: The constellation (the Great Bear).

name: Grote Bickersstraat
en: These streets are on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr Johan Bicker (1591-1653), a shipbuilder and merchant, and a schepen (magistrate) and burgomaster of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets later laid out on the island automatically took the name of its founder.

name: Grote Die
en: Literally 'great water', to distinguish it from the Kleine Die further on. The overtoom (a place where boats were hauled over a dam) was level with the Nieuwendijk.

name: Grote Diestraat
en: Literally 'great water', to distinguish it from the Kleine Die further on. The overtoom (a place where boats were hauled over a dam) was level with the Nieuwendijk.

name: Grote Haven
en: A harbour on the side canal to Nieuwendam.

name: Grote Ruwenberg
en: Of this castle near Sint-Michielsgestel (Noord-Brabant) only a small tower with loopholes remains. The rest was altered and extended into a reformatory.

name: Grote Wittenburgerstraat
en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

name: Grubbehoeve
en: A farm near Albergen, in Tubbergen (Overijssel). It is named after the Grubbe family, mentioned as early as 1394.

name: Guggenheimlaan
en: The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright and built in 1956, known for the gallery that spirals around the central hall. The core of its modern art collection was assembled by the multimillionaire Solomon Guggenheim.

name: Guido Gezellestraat
en: Flemish priest and poet (1830-1899) with a very large body of work, above all a nature poet.

name: Guldehandsteeg
en: The sign of the inn 'In de gulde Hant' (in the golden hand) gave the name here. The inn stood on the corner with the Warmoesstraat in the sixteenth century. The alley ends in water steps down to the Damrak, which is why the name Watersteeg also occurs in the Middle Ages. The present name was put back in the street register around 1980, after being left out for about a hundred years.

name: Gulden Kruis
en: The name of a patrician house in Beverwijk (Noord-Holland).

name: Gulden Kruispad
en: The name of a patrician house in Beverwijk (Noord-Holland).

name: Gulden Winckelplantsoen
en: After a poem by Vondel from 1613.

name: Gulden Winckelstraat
en: After a poem by Vondel from 1613.

name: Guldenpromenade
en: Until the euro was introduced on 1 January 2002, the guilder was the Dutch currency.

name: Gunterstein
en: A castle on the right bank of the Vecht near Breukelen, built in the thirteenth century and lived in by Johan van Oldenbarnevelt from 1611 to 1619. The present building was put up after the French destroyed it in 1672.

name: Gustav Mahlerlaan
en: Austrian composer and conductor (1860-1911), one of the most important conductors of his time. His compositions linked late Romanticism with the modern period of classical music. Mahler had a special bond with Amsterdam, which he first visited in 1903 at the invitation of Willem Mengelberg, conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra. That visit began a close relationship between the orchestra and the composer.

name: Gustav Mahlerplein
en: Austrian composer and conductor (1860-1911), one of the most important conductors of his time. His compositions linked late Romanticism with the modern period of classical music. Mahler had a special bond with Amsterdam, which he first visited in 1903 at the invitation of Willem Mengelberg, conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra. That visit began a close relationship between the orchestra and the composer.

name: Gutserstraat
en: Someone who cuts out wood, for example, with a gouge (guts: a chisel with a hollow blade). The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Guus Trestorffstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1905-1944), born in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad there.

name: Gwijde van Henegouwenbrug
en: Also Guy of Avesnes, or Gui d'Avesnes (1253-1317), Bishop of Utrecht. He personally administered the possessions of the Lords of Amstel. Just before his consecration in Utrecht, in 1300 or 1301, he granted Amsterdam its town rights.

name: Gyroscoopweg
en: A fast-spinning body built symmetrically around an axis of rotation, used for ship's compasses. The instrument was invented by Foucault.

name: H. Cleyndertweg
en: Hendrik Cleyndert A.zn (1881-1958), originally a grain merchant in Nieuwendam by trade. He founded government care for landscape and recreation, and was a board member of the Society for the Preservation of Nature Monuments in the Netherlands (Natuurmonumenten), Bond Heemschut and the Hendrick de Keyser Society.

name: H. Diesveldsingel
en: The name is misspelt. Johannes Henricus (Harry) Diesveldt (1918-1944), resistance fighter and Engelandvaarder (one who escaped to England). He returned from England as a secret agent and wireless operator, was arrested in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad in Vught.

name: H. Gerhardstraat
en: Hendrik Gerhard (1829-1886), Amsterdam tailor and one of the socialist pioneers, co-founder of De Dageraad in 1856. He represented the 'First Socialist International', founded in 1864, in the Netherlands.

name: H. Stolleplantsoen
en: Heinrich Wilhelm Christian Stolle (1924-2006), architect and furniture designer. He was in a partnership with Frans van Gool and Arnold Oyevaar that designed 1100 homes in the Buikslotermeer.

name: H.A.J. Baanderskade
en: Herman Ambrosius Jan Baanders (1876-1953), architect of the Amsterdam School. His designs include the Amsterdams Lyceum on the Valeriusplein and housing on the Rooseveltlaan and the Uiterwaardenstraat.

name: H.J. Algrastraat
en: Hendrik Algra (1896-1982), journalist and Anti-Revolutionary politician, editor-in-chief of the 'Friesch Dagblad'. From 1946 to 1969 he sat in the Senate (Eerste Kamer) for the Anti-Revolutionary Party, concentrating on defence, foreign affairs and education.

name: H.J.E. Wenckebachweg
en: Henri Johan Eduard Wenckebach (1861-1924), founder and director of the Koninklijke Nederlandsche Hoogovens en Staalfabrieken (Royal Dutch Blast Furnaces and Steelworks). The street's first name (Industrieweg, council decision of 2 October 1963) was withdrawn at the request of the municipality of Ouder-Amstel, because Duivendrecht already had an Industrieweg.

name: H.J.M. Walenkampstraat
en: Hermanus Johannes Maria Walenkamp (1871-1933), architect and graphic designer, who trained with P.J.H. Cuypers. His work includes the Zaanhof housing in the Spaarndammerbuurt.

name: H.M. Kraaijvangerstraat
en: Herman Kraaijvanger (1903-1981), architect, who set up an architectural practice with his brother. The firm's pre-war work belongs to the tradition of Dutch brick architecture and was built almost entirely for Catholic clients.

name: H.T. Zwiersplantsoen
en: Henri Tino Zwiers (1900-1992), architect, born in Amsterdam, a Dutch pioneer of building with prefabricated elements, as in Terrasdorp. From 1938 he was a professor in Delft.

name: Haag en Veld
en: A patrician house in Velsen (Noord-Holland), first mentioned in 1671.

name: Haaksbergweg
en: The name of a hill near Haaksbergen.

name: Haardstee
en: The name of a farm near Steenderen (Gelderland).

name: Haardsteebrug
en: The name of a farm near Steenderen (Gelderland).

name: Haarlemmer Houttuinen
en: To extend the existing timber stores, some plots were set aside after 1612 for stacking timber (houttuinen: timber yards). They got this name from their position parallel to the Haarlemmerstraat and Haarlemmerdijk. It took on the character of a street when the quay was widened and built up with houses in the nineteenth century and the railway embankment was laid. Around 1970 that character changed again when most of the buildings were demolished and a wide road was built to take traffic off the Haarlemmerdijk and Haarlemmerstraat. The widening also removed the Westerdokstraat, the Korte Westerdokstraat and the Teerplein.

name: Haarlemmerdijk
en: The city of Haarlem. Before the city's expansion of 1593 the Haarlemmerpoort (Haarlem gate) stood at the end of the Nieuwendijk, so the Haarlemmerdijk lay outside the city. In 1593 the stretch as far as the Korte Prinsengracht was brought inside the city and named Haarlemmerstraat. Some years later (1612) the next stretch became city territory but kept the name Haarlemmerdijk. From about 1615 the Haarlemmerpoort (by Hendrick de Keyser) stood on the Haarlemmerplein. In 1837 that gate was pulled down and rebuilt, and at King Willem II's entry into the city in 1840 it was renamed Willemspoort.

name: Haarlemmermeerstraat
