en: The municipality of that name, formed after the lake was drained in 1852.

name: Haarlemmerplein
en: The city of Haarlem. Before the city's expansion of 1593 the Haarlemmerpoort (Haarlem gate) stood at the end of the Nieuwendijk, so the Haarlemmerdijk lay outside the city. In 1593 the stretch as far as the Korte Prinsengracht was brought inside the city and named Haarlemmerstraat. Some years later (1612) the next stretch became city territory but kept the name Haarlemmerdijk. From about 1615 the Haarlemmerpoort (by Hendrick de Keyser) stood on the Haarlemmerplein. In 1837 that gate was pulled down and rebuilt, and at King Willem II's entry into the city in 1840 it was renamed Willemspoort.

name: Haarlemmersluis
en: This bridge is named after the Haarlemmerstraat, the road out of Amsterdam to Haarlem.

name: Haarlemmerstraat
en: The city of Haarlem. Before the city's expansion of 1593 the Haarlemmerpoort (Haarlem gate) stood at the end of the Nieuwendijk, so the Haarlemmerdijk lay outside the city. In 1593 the stretch as far as the Korte Prinsengracht was brought inside the city and named Haarlemmerstraat. Some years later (1612) the next stretch became city territory but kept the name Haarlemmerdijk. From about 1615 the Haarlemmerpoort (by Hendrick de Keyser) stood on the Haarlemmerplein. In 1837 that gate was pulled down and rebuilt, and at King Willem II's entry into the city in 1840 it was renamed Willemspoort.

name: Haarlemmervaart
en: The canal to Haarlem.

name: Haarlemmerweg
en: The main road to Haarlem.

name: Haarlerbergpad
en: The name of a hill near Haarle (Overijssel), a rise in the push moraine from the penultimate ice age (200,000-130,000 years ago).

name: Haarlerbergweg
en: The name of a hill near Haarle (Overijssel), a rise in the push moraine from the penultimate ice age (200,000-130,000 years ago).

name: Hacquartstraat
en: Carolus Hacquart (1640-1730), musician, who wrote pieces for the viola da gamba and was a gamba player at the court of the Oranges.

name: Hagedoornplein
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Hagedoornweg
en: The shrub (hawthorn). Part of the square was renamed Plein Spanje '36-'39 in 1986.

name: Hageland
en: A region in Belgium, in the province of Brabant.

name: Hagenau
en: The Hagenau estate on the Veluwe, originally owned by the stadholder Willem II.

name: Hajo Brugmanshof
en: Historian (1868-1939). His works include a history of Amsterdam in eight volumes (1933).

name: Hakfort
en: A sixteenth- and seventeenth-century castle, altered in 1788, near Vorden (Gelderland). It is named after the knight Bernt van Hackfort (died 1559).

name: Halmaheirastraat
en: One of the islands of the Moluccas (Indonesia).

name: Halteriastraat
en: A microscopic water creature, a ciliate. Large stiff hairs make it move in jumps; smaller hairs create a current in the water that wafts food inside.

name: Halvemaansbrug
en: This fixed bridge takes its name from the Halvemaansteeg. The origin of that name may lie in the façade of Halvemaansteeg no. 18, marked 'Van Ouds de Halve Maan' (of old the Half Moon).

name: Halvemaansteeg
en: The origin of this name may lie in the façade of no. 18, marked 'van ouds de Halve Maan' (of old the Half Moon). It is also possible that the bridge gave the name: in 1626 the Halvemaansbrug was given a half-curved shape (now straight). But the alley's name is already mentioned at the beginning of the seventeenth century, so it would be older than the bridge.

name: Hamerstraat
en: (Belongs to Piet Meerburg) During the German occupation he rescued many adults and children from the Hollandsche Schouwburg and the crèche opposite it, together with Lau Mazirel and Walter Süskind, among others. He was also one of the founders of the nearby Kriterion cinema, run by students of the University of Amsterdam.

name: Hammarbystraat
en: A waterside district in south Stockholm that has been renovated and redeveloped since the 1990s.

name: Hamontstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Han Hollanderlaan
en: Hartog Hollander (1886-1943), legendary radio reporter, whose reports did much to popularise sport in the Netherlands. He died in the Sobibor extermination camp.

name: Han Lammersbrug
en: Han Lammers (1931-2000) worked as a journalist for the ANP, the Algemeen Dagblad and De Groene Amsterdammer before becoming a city councillor and alderman in Amsterdam for the PvdA in 1970. In 1965, with Jan Nagel among others, he was involved in founding the renewal movement Nieuw Links (New Left). As alderman for urban development, Lammers set urban renewal in motion. He had plans drawn up to demolish whole neighbourhoods: from the Jordaan to the Dapperbuurt, completely new districts were to be built from scratch, with a quite different street plan. Residents formed action groups, which in the end successfully fought this model of urban renewal. Lammers was also closely involved in building the east line of the Amsterdam metro. He bore the activists' anger during the clearance and demolition of homes in the Nieuwmarkt neighbourhood in 1975. Lammers had no doubts about building and later extending the metro: 'Necessary things always happen,' he said. From 1976 to 1984 Lammers was landdrost (governor) of the public body of the Southern IJsselmeer Polders, part of what later became the province of Flevoland. From 1984 to 1986 he was burgomaster of Almere, and from 1986 to 1996 Queen's Commissioner of the province of Flevoland.

name: Han van Zomerenbrug
en: Han van Zomeren (1920-1941) was a graphic artist active in the resistance during the German occupation. He printed pamphlets calling for resistance. He was executed by firing squad on the Laren heath in 1941 and reburied in the Field of Honour in Overveen in 1952.

name: Handbalstraat
en: Refers to a handball club that was here.

name: Handboogstraat
en: In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries the Crossbow (Voetboog) and Longbow (Handboog) Doelen, militia halls, were built on the Singel. Both had a shooting orchard that stretched to behind the houses on the Kalverstraat. In 1649 two streets were laid out on the grounds of these orchards and named Handboogstraat and Voetboogstraat.

name: Händelstraat
en: George Frideric Handel (1685-1759), German-English composer. Besides operas he composed 32 oratorios, six concerti grossi, twenty organ concertos, chamber music, songs and festive music.

name: Hanedastraat
en: The name of one of Tokyo's airports.

name: Hannie Dankbaarpassage
en: Henriëtte Christine Jaqueline Dankbaar (1952-2007), politician, the first GroenLinks district chair in Amsterdam (Oud-West, 1990-2002). She came from the PSP and was loved for her great social commitment.

name: Hannie Schaftbrug
en: Hannie Schaft (1920-1945) was a Haarlem communist and resistance fighter, known as the Girl with the Red Hair. She carried out several attacks on Germans and collaborators, and for that she was shot dead by the Germans in the dunes near Bloemendaal on 17 April 1945. On 27 November 1945 her body was reburied in the Field of Honour at Bloemendaal in Overveen.

name: Hanny Michaelisbrug
en: Hanny Michaelis (Amsterdam, 19 December 1922 - Amsterdam, 11 June 2007) was a poet, writer and translator. She made her debut in 1949 with Klein voorspel (little prelude). Up to 1971 five more collections of new poems appeared. She also wrote (autobiographical) prose and made a number of translations.

name: Hans Katanhof
en: Resistance fighter (1919-1943), a student, born in Hilversum, executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

name: Hans Kressebrug
en: Hans Kresse was an important comic artist and a born Amsterdammer, who became known for his comic strips of Eric de Noorman (Eric the Norseman). Kresse made many comics and stories based on history that became world-famous.

name: Hans Meerum Terwogtweg
en: Albert Hendrik Magdalus Meerum Terwogt (1883-1960), the doyen of sports journalists. For forty years he was sports editor of the 'Nieuwe Rotterdamsche Courant'.

name: Hans Onversaagdstraat
en: A Beggar captain at the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

name: Haparandadam
en: A Swedish port on the Gulf of Bothnia, a timber port.

name: Haparandaweg
en: A Swedish port on the Gulf of Bothnia, a timber port.

name: Hardwareweg
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Haringbuisdijk
en: A ship used for herring fishing (a herring buss).

name: Haringpakkersbrug
en: While in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the herring sellers mostly lived on the Nieuwendijk, this and other alleys along that dike were home to the herring packers. Until 1913 the alley was called Kapelsteeg, but it was then renamed Haringpakkerssteeg because of confusion with the other Kapelstegen.

name: Haringvlietstraat
en: A sea channel from the Hellegatsplein to the North Sea (between Voorne and Zuid-Beveland), now closed off from the open sea by a dam.

name: Harkstraat
en: The gardening tool (the rake).

name: Harmoniehof
en: A basic concept of music theory (harmony).

name: Haroekoestraat
en: An island of the Moluccas (Indonesia).

name: Harriet Freezerstraat
en: Pseudonym of Harriët Wilhelmina Vriesendorp-Eybergen (1911-1971), writer and journalist. She wrote for 'De Groene Amsterdammer' and 'Het Parool', was an editor of the monthly 'Opzij', and was involved in founding Man Vrouw Maatschappij. Her well-attended lectures made an important contribution to improving the position of women.

name: Harry Banninkstraat
en: Composer (1929-1999), arranger and pianist. His work includes the music for Annie M.G. Schmidt's musicals, among them 'Heerlijk duurt het langst' and 'Ja zuster, Nee zuster'.

name: Harry Koningsbergerstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1924-1945), born in Blokzijl, executed by firing squad in Zeist.

name: Hart Nibbrigstraat
en: Ferdinand Hart Nibbrig (1866-1915), painter and lithographer of portraits and landscapes, a representative of neo-impressionism.

name: Hartelstein
en: A former castle near Itteren (South Limburg), of which a fortified farmstead with seventeenth-century remains survives.

name: Hartenstraat
en: Recalls the tanners and the hide trade once based in this neighbourhood. Hart is an old form of hert (deer).

name: Hartmanbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after the tobacconist André Hartman, who was killed in a robbery at his shop on 6 November 1993. The bridge is also a tribute to his wife An Hartman and to all shopkeepers who do their work in dangerous circumstances.

name: Hasebroekstraat
en: Johannes Petrus Hasebroek (1812-1896), minister and writer. Under the pseudonym Jonathan he wrote, among other things, 'Waarheid en droomen' (truth and dreams).

name: Haspelsstraat
en: Abraham Haspels (1893-1942), resistance fighter, born in the municipality of Haarlemmermeer and executed by firing squad in Amersfoort. He was involved in, among other things, the February Strike of 1941.

name: Hasselaerssteeg
en: Pieter Dircks Hasselaer (1554-1616), merchant and regent. In 1587 he bought the brewery 'De Witte Arent' on the corner of the alley and the Prins Hendrikkade. Before he settled in Amsterdam he had won great fame as a militia ensign during the siege of Haarlem. The alley was earlier called the Trouweloossteegje (faithless alley), recalling the former St Jacob's chapel, where divorces were proclaimed.

name: Hatostraat
en: The name of the airport of Willemstad, Curaçao.

name: Havankbrug
en: Havank, pseudonym of Hendrikus Frederikus (Hans) van der Kallen (Leeuwarden, 19 February 1904 - Leeuwarden, 22 June 1964), was a Dutch writer. Havank began his career as a writer of detective novels in Amsterdam, where he wrote his first two novels. He is best known for his 'Schaduw' (Shadow) series.

name: Haveneilandschutsluis
en: Named after the adjoining inner harbour, which is connected to the IJmeer by a lock.

name: Havenkom A
en: The name speaks for itself (harbour basin A). Basins B and D have been filled in.

name: Havenkom C
en: The name speaks for itself (harbour basin A). Basins B and D have been filled in.

name: Havenstraat
en: A mooring place for ships (harbour).

name: Havikshorst
en: An old havezate (now a country house) from 1753, surrounded by a wide moat, near De Wijk (Drenthe).

name: Havikslaan
en: The bird of prey (the goshawk).

name: Haya van Someren-Downerstraat
en: Haya Victoria van Someren-Downer (1926-1980), politician, a member of the VVD. From 1959 to 1968 she sat in the House of Representatives, where she dealt mainly with education, media, and transport and water management. From 1974 to 1980 she was a member of the Senate (Eerste Kamer), where she worked on education and Kingdom affairs.

name: Hazelaarstraat
en: The broadleaf tree that bears hazelnuts.

name: Hazenstraat
en: The hare, a rodent. The name was given because of this animal's skin. The street lies near the old tanners and the hide trade.

name: Heathrowstraat
en: The name of one of London's airports.

name: Hebridenlaan
en: A Scottish island group of about five hundred islands, of which about a hundred are inhabited. The main islands are Lewis and Skye.

name: Hecht en Sterkhof
en: Hecht en Sterk, also known as Storkoe, was a coffee plantation on the Commewijne river in the district of Commewijne in Suriname. At its height in 1819 it covered more than 1000 akkers (fields). After emancipation in 1863 the plantation recruited no contract labourers and probably went out of production soon after. In 1910 the government bought it to make it, together with Frederiksburg, a government plantation, set up to grant land to contract workers.

name: Hechtelstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Hectorstraat
en: A figure from Greek mythology: army commander, son of the king of Troy.

name: Hederabrug
en: Hedera is the scientific name for ivy.

name: Heemstedestraat
en: A town in Noord-Holland that has grown together with Haarlem.

name: Heer Halewijnstraat
en: A medieval song about a murderer of women who is himself killed by a princess.

name: Heermoesstraat
en: A plant of the horsetail family (field horsetail) that can store substances such as heavy metals from its surroundings in its own cells. Horsetail has long been used for many ailments, among them as a diuretic, for joint pain and to strengthen the skeleton and connective tissue.

name: Heesterveld
en: The name of a farm near Nuland (Noord-Brabant).

name: Hegelhof
en: Georg W.F. Hegel (1770-1831), German philosopher, who had a great influence on the development of philosophy. He was a professor in Berlin. One of his followers in the Netherlands was Bolland.

name: Hegeraatstraat
en: H.J. Hegeraat (1874-1919), schoolteacher and later a journalist on the daily 'Het Volk'. Author of several socialist battle songs.

name: Heggerankweg
en: The climbing plant (bryony) that grows in hedges and scrub.

name: Heibrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after the Heisteeg, on which it lies. The Heisteeg takes its name from a corner house called 't Hayblok, already mentioned at the beginning of the sixteenth century. Until 1606 an unofficial name for this bridge was Strontenburgerbrug (roughly, dung-town bridge), because of the nuisance caused by two nearby shipyards.

name: Heidotistraat
en: Heidoti is a village in the Boven-Saramacca resort in the northern part of Suriname, inhabited by Maroons of the Kwinti people.

name: Heiligeweg
en: After the Miracle of Amsterdam, the chapel 'Ter Heilige Stede' (later the Nieuwezijds Kapel) was founded between the Rokin and the Kalverstraat. For the pilgrims a road was then laid beside the Heiligewegsevaart (later the Overtoom) from Sloten to the Kalverstraat, called the Heiligeweg (holy way). Our street is what remains of that pilgrimage route. In old documents the Leidsestraat is also called Heiligeweg.

name: Heiligewegsluis
en: After the Miracle of Amsterdam, the chapel 'Ter Heilige Stede' (later the Nieuwezijds Kapel) was founded between the Rokin and the Kalverstraat. For the pilgrims a road was then laid beside the Heiligewegsevaart (later the Overtoom) from Sloten to the Kalverstraat, called the Heiligeweg (holy way). Our street is what remains of that pilgrimage route. In old documents the Leidsestraat is also called Heiligeweg.

name: Heimansweg
en: Eduard (Eli) Heimans (1861-1914), naturalist. An Amsterdam schoolteacher, he wrote a series of books on birds and flowers with J.P. Thijsse. Together they founded the Dutch Natural History Society and the magazine 'De Levende Natuur'. Heimans died on a geological excursion.

name: Hein Donnerbrug
en: Jan Hein Donner (1927-1988) was a chess grandmaster who was Dutch champion several times. He was also a polemicist and a columnist for NRC Handelsblad.

name: Heining
en: Named after a polder outside the dikes in the former IJ, which after the Grote IJ polders were made became a separately drained area within them. The name indicates land that yields little hay. It came to Amsterdam through the boundary settlement with Haarlemmerliede en Spaarnwoude in 1963.

name: Heinzestraat
en: Gustav Adolph Heinze (1820-1904), German by birth, conductor in Amsterdam of the German Opera, the Liedertafel Euterpe and the Vincentius concerts. From 1862 to 1885 director of the Toonkunst music school. He composed cantatas and oratorios.

name: Hekelveld
en: Probably, when this land still lay outside the walls, flax was hackled here (hekelen: combing flax), to be made into rope on the neighbouring ropewalks. In 1604 there were still two houses whose gable stones recalled this craft. The Hekelveld was originally a canal and was filled in around 1865.

name: Hekla
en: A volcano in Iceland, 1491 metres high.

name: Helena Kuipers-Rietberghof
en: Helena Theodora Kuipers-Rietberg (1893-1944), resistance fighter, born in Winterswijk, died in the Ravensbrück concentration camp. She was known as the mother of the 'Landelijke Organisatie voor hulp aan onderduikers' (the national organisation for help to people in hiding, the L.O.). She also had a part in distributing the clandestine paper 'Trouw'.

name: Helena Mercierstraat
en: A forerunner of the women's movement in Amsterdam (1839-1910), and a writer on social subjects.

name: Helene Madisonstraat
en: American swimmer who won gold in the 100 metres freestyle at the 1932 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

name: Hélène Swarthstraat
en: Hélène Lapidoth, née Swarth (1859-1941), poet of love poetry, for a time much admired by many and in later years a forgotten figure.

name: Helicopterstraat
en: A rotor aircraft that can rise and descend vertically, built in 1933 by the aircraft maker J. Sikorsky, an American born in Russia.

name: Heliotroopstraat
en: An ornamental shrub, originally from South America.

name: Hella Haasseplein
en: Hélène Serafia Haasse (1918-2011), writer of novels, essays, poetry and plays. She received the P.C. Hooft Prize in 1983 and the Prize for Dutch Literature in 2004. She wrote a record 3 Boekenweekgeschenken (Book Week gift books), among them 'Oeroeg' (1948), perhaps her best-known work. She is among the Dutch authors most read abroad.

name: Hellenburg
en: A lost castle in the area of Goes, whose foundations have now been uncovered.

name: Hellingstraat
en: The name refers to the two concrete slipways (hellingen) on the NDSM site, used to launch ships.

name: Helmgrasstraat
en: A native perennial pioneer plant of the grass family (marram grass), important in forming dunes.

name: Helmholtzstraat
en: Hermann von Helmholtz (1821-1894), German physician and physicist, inventor of the ophthalmoscope.

name: Helsingforsbrug
en: Helsingfors is the Swedish name for Helsinki, the capital of Finland. The names in the Houthavens are named after places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Hembrugstraat
en: After the former railway bridge over the Noordzeekanaal, which obstructed the port of Amsterdam. The bridge was demolished after the railway tunnel (the Hemtunnel) came into use.

name: Hemonylaan
en: The brothers Frans Hemony (1609-1667) and Pieter Hemony (1619-1680), bell founders of the carillons in the Oude Kerk, the Zuiderkerk, the Westerkerk and the Munttoren.

name: Hemonystraat
en: The brothers Frans Hemony (1609-1667) and Pieter Hemony (1619-1680), bell founders of the carillons in the Oude Kerk, the Zuiderkerk, the Westerkerk and the Munttoren.

name: Hemsterhuisstraat
en: Tiberius Hemsterhuis (1685-1766), classical philologist, professor in Amsterdam (philosophy) and later at Franeker and Leiden (Greek and national history).

name: Hemweg
en: After a former islet, the Hem, in the old IJ. The Hem was at first a spit of land that only later became an island through erosion of its banks. The word is the same as 'ham', now known only in 'inham' (inlet). A last stretch of the Hemweg still exists; originally the road began at the Spaarndammerbuurt.

name: Hendrik Bulthuisstraat
en: Barber (1892-1948) from the Frisian village of Bergum, designer of the B.M. sailing dinghy and a pioneer of sailing as a popular sport.

name: Hendrik de Bruynstraat
en: Hydraulic engineer (1815-1885), known for the water-management works he built in Surabaya (Dutch East Indies).

name: Hendrik Dienskestraat
en: Resistance hero and office clerk, born in Schiedam in 1907, died in 1945 in Helmstedt (Germany).

name: Hendrik Godfroidhof
en: Hendrikus Godfroid (1899-1943), resistance fighter, born in Arnhem, died in Scheveningen prison. He worked on the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid'.

name: Hendrik Hosstraat
en: Hendrik Pieter Hos (1906-1944), resistance fighter, born in Haarlem and executed by firing squad in Scheveningen. He was in the leadership of the national network of the clandestine paper 'Vrij Nederland'.

name: Hendrik Jacobszstraat
en: Violin maker who made violins between 1690 and 1740 on the model of the Italian Amati.

name: Hendrik Jonkerplein
en: Amsterdam industrialist (1778-1843) who in 1806 founded the factory for steam engines and other machinery that once stood here. Before 1956 this was the Bickersplein. The naming followed a request from N.V. Hk. Jonker en Zn, which turned 150 that year.

name: Hendrik Soeteboomstraat
en: Historian (1616-1678) who wrote several books about Waterland, among them 'De historie van Waterland' and 'De Waterlanders' (1660).

name: Hendrik van Wijnstraat
en: Historian (1740-1831), founder of the General State Archives (1802). He wrote supplements and notes to the 'Vaderlandsche Historie' of the historian Jan Wagenaar.

name: Hendrik Veldhuishof
en: Resistance fighter (1922-1944) who set up a printing works in Blaricum for the clandestine paper 'Trouw', where other clandestine printing was also done. He was arrested in June 1944 and executed by firing squad in Vught soon afterwards.

name: Hendrik Werkmanstraat
en: Hendrik Nicolaas Werkman (1882-1945), artist, printer and resistance fighter. Printer for the collective 'De Blauwe Schuit', which published critical pieces about the German occupation. Executed by firing squad in 1945.

name: Hendrikje Stoffelsstraat
en: Rembrandt van Rijn's life companion (1626-1663). Around 1647 she joined his household as a maidservant and soon lived with the painter. She probably modelled for several works. She was buried in the Westerkerk.

name: Hendrikus Rempestraat
en: Resistance fighter (1903-1944), born in Amsterdam, died in Bruttig (Germany).

name: Henegouwenstraat
en: A province in the south of Belgium (Hainaut).

name: Henk Curièrekade
en: Peter Heinrich Curière (1911-1981), a legendary figure in the Spaarndammerbuurt for his positive and active involvement in the neighbourhood's urban renewal and as chairman of the neighbourhood improvement committee.

name: Henk Gortzakstraat
en: Hendricus Gortzak (1909-1989), politician, member of the Communist Party Holland. During the occupation he was involved in the activities of the now illegal Communist Party of the Netherlands. In 1948 he entered the House of Representatives for the CPN, and from 1952 to 1958 he led its parliamentary group. In 1958 Gortzak was expelled after a conflict with the party leadership.

name: Henk Henriëtstraat
en: Painter and graphic artist (1903-1945).

name: Henk Hienschstraat
en: Hendrik Jan Hiensch (1912-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, died in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp.

name: Henk Sneevlietpad
en: Hendricus J.F.M. Sneevliet (1883-1942), politician and an active figure in the trade union movement in the Netherlands and the former Dutch East Indies. Internationally known as a communist for his contacts with China and Russia. As a resistance man he was executed by the Germans.

name: Henk Sneevlietweg
en: Hendricus J.F.M. Sneevliet (1883-1942), politician and an active figure in the trade union movement in the Netherlands and the former Dutch East Indies. Internationally known as a communist for his contacts with China and Russia. As a resistance man he was executed by the Germans.

name: Henkenshage
en: A castle in Sint-Oedenrode, founded in the fifteenth century and partly in the seventeenth, altered in the nineteenth century.

name: Hennetjesbrug
en: This fixed bridge was probably once a narrow wooden chicken bridge (hennetje: little hen).

name: Henri Bergsonstraat
en: French philosopher and physicist (1859-1941), author of 'Creative Evolution' (1907). He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1927.

name: Henri Berssenbruggehof
en: Photographer (1873-1959) who photographed street life and the ordinary (working) man and portrayed the cultural elite of the Netherlands. Known for his harmonious compositions, strong contrasts of light and dark, and perfected printing methods.

name: Henri Borelstraat
en: Prose writer and playwright (1869-1933), author of stories of the Indies and novels set in The Hague.

name: Henri Dunantstraat
en: Jean Henri Dunant (1828-1910), Swiss writer and philanthropist, who founded the International Red Cross in 1864. In 1901 he received the first Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Henri Polaklaan
en: Trade union leader and politician (1868-1943), co-founder of the SDAP in 1894 and Amsterdam's first social-democratic city councillor. In 1894 he founded the General Dutch Diamond Workers' Union, which later took the initiative in founding the NVV (trade union federation). With this naming in 1945 the name Plantage Franselaan was dropped. Early in the eighteenth century it was called the Achterlaan.

name: Henri Zagwijnstraat
en: Composer (1878-1954) of chamber music and choral works.

name: Henric van Veldekehof
en: Flemish poet (second half of the twelfth century), whose works include 'De Legende van Sint-Servaes' and a great many 'Minnesangen' (love songs).

name: Henrick de Keijserplein
en: City architect and sculptor (1565-1621). In Amsterdam he built the first Exchange, the Westerkerk, Zuiderkerk and Noorderkerk, and the Montelbaanstoren and Munttoren. In Delft his work includes the tomb of William of Orange.

name: Henrick de Keijserstraat
en: City architect and sculptor (1565-1621). In Amsterdam he built the first Exchange, the Westerkerk, Zuiderkerk and Noorderkerk, and the Montelbaanstoren and Munttoren. In Delft his work includes the tomb of William of Orange.

name: Henrietta Leavittbrug
en: Henrietta Swan Leavitt (1868-1921), American astronomer. She discovered a relationship between the brightness and the period of pulsation of certain stars. Her discovery let astronomers calculate for the first time the distance between distant galaxies and the earth. Her work also formed the basis for calculating the expanding universe.

name: Henriëtte Bosmansstraat
en: Pianist and composer (1895-1952), who composed songs, mostly to French texts, and performed as a pianist at home and abroad.

name: Henriëtte Roland Holststraat
en: Henriëtte Roland Holst, née Van der Schalk (1869-1952), poet. For many years a militant socialist, in her poems and verse dramas too.

name: Henriëtte Ronnerplein
en: Henriëtte Ronner, née Knip (1821-1909), painter, mainly of dogs and cats.

name: Henriëtte Ronnerstraat
en: Henriëtte Ronner, née Knip (1821-1909), painter, mainly of dogs and cats.

name: Henriëtte van Heukelom-van den Brandelerbrug
en: Hendrika Jacoba van den Brandeler-Heukelom (1884-1985), composer and pianist, a pupil of Dirk Schäfer (1873-1931) among others. Her works include songs, a requiem for her father, and a Stabat Mater performed by the Concertgebouw Orchestra in 1913.

name: Hensbroekerstraat
en: A village in Noord-Holland, between Alkmaar and Hoorn.

name: Herbert Spencerhof
en: English philosopher and sociologist (1820-1903), a follower of Rousseau.

name: Hercules Seghersstraat
en: Hercules Pieterszoon Seghers (1589-1638), etcher and landscape painter. Seghers's influence can be seen in the works of Rembrandt and Ruisdael. Only in the twentieth century did his manner of painting come to be highly valued.

name: Herculesstraat
en: In Greek mythology Hercules is the strong hero, the son of the supreme god Zeus.

name: Herderhof
en: Johann Gottfried Herder (1744-1803), German philosopher and writer, who had a great influence on Goethe.

name: Herengracht
en: After the Heren Regeerders (the lords who governed the city; in the old days the city was not administered but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch when in 1612 it was widened into today's canal, the first of the three main canals. The stretch beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658, as does the Nieuwe Herengracht.

name: Herenmarkt
en: After the Heren Regeerders (the lords who governed the city; in the old days the city was not administered but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch when in 1612 it was widened into today's canal, the first of the three main canals. The stretch beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658, as does the Nieuwe Herengracht.

name: Herenstraat
en: After the Heren Regeerders (the lords who governed the city; in the old days the city was not administered but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch when in 1612 it was widened into today's canal, the first of the three main canals. The stretch beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658, as does the Nieuwe Herengracht.

name: Herentalsstraat
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Herfststraat
en: The autumn season. The street came over in 1966 from the abolished municipality of Weesperkarspel under the name Vechtstraat (council decision of Weesperkarspel, 29 November 1957), but that name could not be kept because of confusion with the existing Vechtstraat.

name: Herikerbergweg
en: A hill near the hamlet of Herike, municipality of Markelo (Overijssel).

name: Heringa-State
en: A castle in Marssum near Leeuwarden, also called Poptaslot, built in the sixteenth century and restored in 1908.

name: Herinkhave
en: Originally a fourteenth-century house near Tubbergen (Overijssel), now a simple moated havezate from 1723.

name: Herman Bonpad
en: Hermanus J. Bon (1873-1945), known to all as Pa Bon. For many years a champion and leader of school football matches in Amsterdam.

name: Herman de Manstraat
en: Pseudonym of the Jewish novelist Salomon Hamburger (1898-1946), a convert to Roman Catholicism. His works include the novel 'Het wassende water' (the rising water).

name: Herman Gorterstraat
en: Poet (1864-1927) who made his name above all with his great nature poem 'Mei' (May, 1889). He wrote 'Kritiek op de Literaire beweging der Tachtigers' (a critique of the literary movement of the Eighties) and was for many years a militant Marxist socialist.

name: Herman Heijermansweg
en: Journalist, novelist and playwright (1864-1924). He wrote many novels set in Amsterdam, some under the pseudonym Samuel Falkland. His great success was the play 'Op hoop van zegen' (The Good Hope).

name: Herman Hellingplantsoen
en: A Beggar captain who served under Governor Diederik Sonoy during the siege of Amsterdam (1572-1578). Helling was killed in 1577, together with the captain Nicolaas Ruychaver, in a failed attempt to take the city hall on the Dam.

name: Herman Poortstraat
en: Poet and writer (1886-1933), known above all as a lecturer on literary subjects for the Volksuniversiteit (adult education) and as a theatre critic. His works include a study of Bredero.

name: Herman Robbersstraat
en: Man of letters (1868-1937), author of novellas and novels, and also editor-in-chief of Elsevier and a critic.

name: Hermanus Coenradistraat
en: Resistance fighter (1909-1941), an electrician, born in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad in The Hague.

name: Hermietenstraat
en: After a house that stood on the corner of the Rokin at the beginning of the seventeenth century, called 'De Heremyt'. Until 1912 this was the Hermietensteeg. That year the alley was widened to six metres and steeg (alley) was changed to straat (street). Hermiet comes from heremiet, meaning hermit.

name: Hermitagelaan
en: The Hermitage Museum in St Petersburg, one of the largest museum complexes in the world. Its collection began with the precious private imperial collection of paintings. It is famous for its works by Titian, Rubens and above all Rembrandt.

name: Herschelstraat
en: Friedrich W. Herschel (1738-1822), English astronomer. He made reflecting telescopes and discovered the planet Uranus.

name: Hertingenstraat
en: A church village in Zeeuws-Vlaanderen drowned around 1500.

name: Hertspieghelweg
en: A didactic poem by Spieghel (1549-1612), merchant and man of letters.

name: Hertzogstraat
en: James B.M. Hertzog (1866-1942), South African statesman and general in the Boer War of 1899 to 1902. Several times a minister, and in 1924 Prime Minister of the Republic of South Africa.

name: Hertzstraat
en: Heinrich Rudolf Hertz (1857-1894), German physicist, founder of radio telegraphy. The unit of frequency is named after him.

name: Herwijk
en: The English port of Harwich, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Hessenbergweg
en: The name of a hill east of Heerlerheide (Limburg).

name: Hestiastraat
en: A figure from Greek mythology: the eldest daughter of Chronos and Rhea and sister of Zeus, goddess of the hearth and of hospitality.

name: Het Breed
en: These names were given for the meaning of the word (broad field), as a counterpart to Het Hoogt and Het Laagt.

name: Het Dok
en: The street was laid out on the site of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij (Amsterdam Dry Dock Company), which staff in the neighbourhood simply called Het Dok (the dock).

name: Het Hoogt
en: Named after its position (the high one), as a counterpart to Het Laagt.

name: Het Laagt
en: The name (the low one) was given to the path laid out at street level, so it describes its position. The residential street above it, at the level of the third storey, was named Het Hoogt (the high one).

name: Het Nauw
en: The narrow passage (nauw: narrows) of water between the Ransdorper Die and the Holysloter Die.

name: Het Slochter
en: Slochter is another word for a navigation channel.

name: Hettenheuvelweg
en: A hill near Bergh in Montferland (Gelderland).

name: Heusdenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Heverleestraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Hexaanweg
en: A tropical product, a component of petrol (hexane), transhipped in the port of Amsterdam.

name: Hilbert van Dijkhof
en: Resistance fighter (1906-1944), a milk seller by trade, born in Kampen, executed by firing squad in Bloemendaal.

name: Hildebrandstraat
en: The pseudonym of Nicolaas Beets.

name: Hildegard von Bingenstraat
en: Hildegard von Bingen was a German composer, but also a scientist (cosmology, botany), abbess and philosopher.

name: Hildo Kropplein
en: Hildebrand Lucien Krop (1884-1970), city sculptor and painter. His works include the Berlage monument in Amsterdam. His decorations and sculptures on Amsterdam's bridges and buildings made him very important to the 'Amsterdam School'.

name: Hildsven
en: The fen (ven) on the west side of the municipality of Moergestel in the province of Noord-Brabant, a nature reserve.

name: Hillegomstraat
en: A town in Zuid-Holland, on the border with Noord-Holland.

name: Hillenraadt
en: A moated sixteenth-century nobleman's house in Swalmen (Limburg), altered and enlarged in later centuries.

name: Hilverbeekstraat
en: An estate near 's-Graveland, founded in the seventeenth century by Amsterdam patricians.

name: Hilversumstraat
en: A town in Het Gooi.

name: Hiridostraat
en: A mountain in Somalia.

name: Hirschpassage
en: Named after the former fashion house Hirsch en Cie, which opened in 1882 on the corner of the Leidseplein and the Weteringschans. Its management had trained at Hirsch in Brussels, itself a branch of the German Hirsch concern, which was entirely oriented to French fashion.

name: Hobaostraat
en: A peak on Bonaire.

name: Hobbemakade
en: Meindert Hobbema (1638-1709), landscape painter, a pupil of Ruisdael.

name: Hobbemastraat
en: Meindert Hobbema (1638-1709), landscape painter, a pupil of Ruisdael.

name: Hodenpijlkade
en: A small village near Schipluiden in the Westland.

name: Hoek van Hollandstraat
en: A village at the mouth of the Nieuwe Waterweg, part of the municipality of Rotterdam since 1914.

name: Hoekenes
en: A small island in the former IJ. The word nes means a spit of land.

name: Hoekenesgracht
en: A small island in the former IJ. The word nes means a spit of land.

name: Hoekenespad
en: A small island in the former IJ. The word nes means a spit of land.

name: Hoekenesplantsoen
en: A small island in the former IJ. The word nes means a spit of land.

name: Hoekenrode
en: The name of an old farm in De Bilt (Utrecht).

name: Hoekenrodepad
en: The name of an old farm in De Bilt (Utrecht).

name: Hoekschewaardplein
en: The Zuid-Holland island (the Hoeksche Waard).

name: Hoekschewaardweg
en: The Zuid-Holland island (the Hoeksche Waard).

name: Hoekslootstraat
en: The name Hoeksloot appears on eighteenth-century maps of Rijnland and its surroundings. After about 1800 the ditch is called Hoornsloot. It still runs along the Amstelveenseweg and, in Amstelveen, along the Emmakade.

name: Hoendiepstraat
en: A canal in the province of Groningen.

name: Hof van Eden
en: The Garden of Eden was, according to the Hebrew Bible, a garden in or equal to the perfect and beautiful Paradise where Adam and Eve lived.

name: Hof van Groenen
en: Probably an earlier name of the seventeenth-century ridderhofstad (knightly manor) and manorial estate in Delfland that appears in 1771 as Groeneveld.

name: Hof van Versailles
en: The Palace of Versailles, south-west of Paris, one of the most impressive Baroque buildings in Europe, built for Louis XIV and largely completed between 1661 and 1690.

name: Hofgeest
en: The name of a patrician house in Velsen (Noord-Holland).

name: Hofmeesterstraat
en: Someone on passenger boats who takes care of the meals and serves at the buffet (a steward).

name: Hofmeyrstraat
en: Jan Hendrik Hofmeyr (1845-1912), South African statesman, who campaigned to keep Dutch in use in South Africa.

name: Hofwijckstraat
en: An autobiographical work by Constantijn Huygens from 1651. It was also the name of his country house in Voorburg, which still exists.

name: Hogeboomspad
en: The name of a path that once lay north of Leimuiden and was swallowed by the Haarlemmermeer. A hogeboom is a high footbridge, in principle made of just one tree trunk or beam.

name: Hogehilweg
en: The Hoge Hil, a rise near Domburg (Zeeland).

name: Hogelandplein
en: The Hogeland (also written Hoogeland) is the region of the province of Groningen north of the Reitdiep and the Damsterdiep. The name refers to the relatively high ground, caused by silting from the sea; the soil is therefore sea clay.

name: Hogendijk
en: A region in Groningen north of the Reitdiep and the Damsterdiep. The name refers to the high position of its sea-clay soil compared with the peat areas to its south.

name: Hogevecht
en: A patrician house on the Vecht between Loenen and Breukelen.

name: Hogeweg
en: So named by the council of the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer because the road lies at the front of the polder.

name: Hogewerf
en: A former ridderhofstad (knightly manor), now a farm, near Oud-Beijerland, named after its former owner, Lord Hubrecht Hoogewerff.

name: Holbeinstraat
en: Hans Holbein the Younger (1497-1543), German painter and engraver.

name: Holendrechtdreef
en: A watercourse on the border of Noord-Holland and Utrecht.

name: Holendrechterweg
en: A watercourse on the border of Noord-Holland and Utrecht.

name: Holendrechtplein
en: A watercourse on the border of Noord-Holland and Utrecht.

name: Holendrechtstraat
en: A watercourse on the border of Noord-Holland and Utrecht. The Holendrechterweg runs along this water and used to lie entirely in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. With the annexation of 1966 part of the road came onto Amsterdam territory.

name: Hollandia Kattenburgpad
en: A raincoat factory that stood here until the end of the 1960s. A monument on this path commemorates the tragic events of 11 November 1942, when 367 Jewish employees of the Hollandia Kattenburg raincoat factory were arrested by the Germans and, with family members taken from their homes, deported to the concentration camps. Only eight of the employees survived the camps.

name: Hollandiagracht
en: The first Dutch film company to produce and distribute films and documentaries on a regular basis. The Hollandia film factory was founded in 1912 and expanded with a theatre company in 1913. It went bankrupt in 1922.

name: Hollandse Tuin
en: The name of one of the many shipyards along the Grote Bickersstraat in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Hollemanstraat
en: Arnold F. Holleman (1859-1953), chemist, professor in Amsterdam from 1905 to 1926. His chemistry textbooks have been translated into many languages.

name: Holterbergweg
en: The name of a hill near Holten (Overijssel).

name: Holtmeulen
en: A castle in Tegelen, Frederik Hendrik's headquarters at the siege of Venlo in 1646.

name: Holwerdahof
en: Jan Hendrik Holwerda (1873-1951), archaeologist and historian, director of the National Museum of Antiquities in Leiden. His works include 'Nederland's vroegste beschaving' (the Netherlands' earliest civilisation, 1925).

name: Holy
en: A former ridderhofstad (knightly manor) north of Vlaardingen (Zuid-Holland).

name: Holysloter Die
en: A creek south of Broek in Waterland.

name: Homme Hettingastraat
en: A Frisian grietman (district magistrate) and member of the Compromise of Nobles (1566), who joined the army of Louis of Nassau in 1568.

name: Hondecoeterstraat
en: Melchior d'Hondecoeter (1636-1695), painter of animals and still lifes.

name: Hondiusstraat
en: Jodocus de Hondt or Hondius (1563-1612), cartographer, engraver and publisher from Ghent working in Amsterdam, mainly of maps and atlases (including the Mercator atlas).

name: Hondsrugweg
en: A ridge of hills in Drenthe.

name: Honingen
en: Originally a thirteenth-century moated castle of the lords of Kralingen, east of Rotterdam. Lumey was imprisoned here in 1573.

name: Honselersdijkstraat
en: A village near Naaldwijk, in the Westland.

name: Honthorststraat
en: Gerard van Honthorst (1590-1656), painter of portraits and night scenes, court painter to Frederik Hendrik.

name: Hoofddorpplein
en: A village, the main town of the municipality of Haarlemmermeer.

name: Hoofddorpweg
en: A village, the main town of the municipality of Haarlemmermeer.

name: Hoofdweg
en: The former municipality of Sloten gave the name for its function: a wide central main road (hoofdweg). After the annexation of 1921 the road was extended north to the Bos en Lommerplein.

name: Hooge Venne
en: A former farm in the old municipality of Sloten.

name: Hoogheemraadweg
en: A hoogheemraad is a board member of a hoogheemraadschap, a regional water board that oversees several water boards and polders. Amsterdam includes parts of the Amstelland, Rijnland and Waterland water boards; Amstelland and Waterland have since merged into a larger whole.

name: Hoogoorddreef
en: A manor house near Hilversum, built around 1900 (Noord-Holland).

name: Hoogoordplein
en: A manor house near Hilversum, built around 1900 (Noord-Holland).

name: Hoogte Kadijk
en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

name: Hoogwoudstraat
en: A village in Noord-Holland.

name: Hooistraat
en: Mown and dried grass (and some other crops), used as fodder in livestock farming (hay).

name: Hooivletstraat
en: A flat-bottomed boat used to carry hay.

name: Hoopende Swaen
en: A whaler of the Oostzaan shipowner Pieter Swan, which sailed the seas east of Greenland between 1759 and 1775.

name: Hoorneboeg
en: An estate near Hilversum (Noord-Holland).

name: Hoornsestraat
en: After the Noord-Holland town of Hoorn, once an important Zuiderzee town, as its many monumental buildings still show.

name: Hoornsloot
en: Probably named after the town of Hoorn.

name: Hoptille
en: A hamlet with a bridge of the same name west of Hijlaard (Friesland).

name: Hoptillepad
en: A hamlet with a bridge of the same name west of Hijlaard (Friesland).

name: Hornhaven
en: The former island De Hoorn or Horn in the old IJ. After the Noordzeekanaal was built, the island could still be clearly made out in the landscape of the Grote IJpolder, but the extension of the Westhaven (around 1960) dug it away entirely. 'Horn' means corner and was given to coastal features similar to a 'nes' or 'ham'. This horn's full name was Zaanderhorn: a spit of land belonging to the western part of Zaanden, the forerunner of Zaandam.

name: Hornweg
en: The former island De Hoorn or Horn in the old IJ. After the Noordzeekanaal was built, the island could still be clearly made out in the landscape of the Grote IJpolder, but the extension of the Westhaven (around 1960) dug it away entirely. 'Horn' means corner and was given to coastal features similar to a 'nes' or 'ham'. This horn's full name was Zaanderhorn: a spit of land belonging to the western part of Zaanden, the forerunner of Zaandam.

name: Horst Blankenburgbrug
en: Horst Blankenburg, born 10 July 1947 in Heidenheim an der Brenz (Germany). Twice Dutch champion, twice KNVB Cup winner, three times winner of the European Cup, twice winner of the European Super Cup and once winner of the Intercontinental Cup, he played 188 league matches for Ajax. In 1969 Ajax became the first Dutch club to reach the final of the prestigious European Cup, today's Champions League. Ajax lost that final, but two years later, in 1971, won the most important prize in football after all. In the two following years Ajax retained the title, confirming itself as the standard-bearer of Dutch football. Not only the titles but the way they were won, with modern, attacking football, made Ajax an international sensation. Coach Rinus Michels moulded this rare concentration of talent into a legendary team that was both untouchable and trend-setting at home and abroad.

name: Hortensiastraat
en: An ornamental shrub (hydrangea).

name: Hortusbrug
en: After the Hortus Botanicus opposite.

name: Hortusplantsoen
en: After the Hortus Botanicus opposite. The quay used to be called Muidergracht, but because of confusion with the Plantage Muidergracht this name was set in 1911.

name: Houdringe
en: A nature reserve in De Bilt (Utrecht).

name: Houthalenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Houthaven
en: Built in 1873 and enlarged in 1878, for goods shipped through the port of Amsterdam (houthaven: timber harbour).

name: Houthavengracht
en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

name: Houthavenkade
en: Goods that were and are shipped through the port of Amsterdam.

name: Houthavenweg
en: Goods that were and are shipped through the port of Amsterdam.

name: Houtkopersburgwal
en: Named after the many timber merchants (houtkopers) and their yards that settled along this water in the seventeenth century. Until 1878 the cross street was called Vlooienburgsteeg.

name: Houtkopersdwarsstraat
en: Named after the many timber merchants (houtkopers) and their yards that settled along this water in the seventeenth century. Until 1878 the cross street was called Vlooienburgsteeg.

name: Houtmandwarsstraat
en: The brothers Cornelis (c. 1540-1599) and Frederik Houtman (died 1625), who in 1595/1597 made the first voyage under the Dutch flag to the East Indies for Amsterdam merchants. Cornelis made a second voyage; Frederik was governor on Ambon for six years and became governor of the Moluccas.

name: Houtmankade
en: The brothers Cornelis (c. 1540-1599) and Frederik Houtman (died 1625), who in 1595/1597 made the first voyage under the Dutch flag to the East Indies for Amsterdam merchants. Cornelis made a second voyage; Frederik was governor on Ambon for six years and became governor of the Moluccas.

name: Houtmanstraat
en: The brothers Cornelis (c. 1540-1599) and Frederik Houtman (died 1625), who in 1595/1597 made the first voyage under the Dutch flag to the East Indies for Amsterdam merchants. Cornelis made a second voyage; Frederik was governor on Ambon for six years and became governor of the Moluccas.

name: Houtrijkstraat
en: After the former village of Houtrijk en Polanen, now Halfweg. The street was earlier called Tweede Spaarndammerstraat (council decision of 30 March 1881). In 1978, because the street pattern changed, part of the street was renamed and added to the Assendelftstraat.

name: Houtveemkanaal
en: After the adjoining timber warehouses (houtvemen).

name: Hoyerpad
en: A character in the work of the writer Nescio. Nescio (Latin: 'I do not know') is the pseudonym of Jan Hendrik Frederik Grönloh (1882-1961), known above all for his stories 'De uitvreter' (the freeloader) and 'Titaantjes' (little titans).

name: Huddekade
en: Johannes Hudde (1628-1704), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1672 to 1704 and an expert in water management. The former Hogesluis (built 1662, demolished 1883) was built to his design.

name: Huddestraat
en: Johannes Hudde (1628-1704), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1672 to 1704 and an expert in water management. The former Hogesluis (built 1662, demolished 1883) was built to his design.

name: Hudsonhof
en: Henry Hudson (c. 1565-1611), English navigator, who sailed for the Dutch East India Company in 1609. On his last voyage, in 1610, he discovered the Hudson Bay, named after him, between Labrador and Canada.

name: Hudsonstraat
en: Henry Hudson (1550-1611), English navigator in the service of the Dutch East India Company. He discovered the Hudson Bay, named after him, between Labrador and Canada (1610).

name: Hugo de Grootgracht
en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

name: Hugo de Grootkade
en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

name: Hugo de Grootplein
en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

name: Hugo de Vriesbrug
en: Botanist (1848-1935), professor at the University of Amsterdam from 1880 to 1918. He developed mutation theory, which holds that characteristics change in jumps. The theory applies to all living organisms, not only plants.

name: Hugo de Vrieslaan
en: Botanist (1848-1935), professor at the University of Amsterdam from 1880 to 1918. He developed mutation theory, which holds that characteristics change in jumps. The theory applies to all living organisms, not only plants.

name: Hugo Floris Ruysstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1924-1943), born in Bussum, executed by firing squad in Haarlem.

name: Hugo Verriesthof
en: Flemish priest and man of letters (1840-1922), a contributor to the literary magazine 'Van nu en straks'. His works include 'Twintig Vlaamsche koppen' (twenty Flemish heads).

name: Huidekoperstraat
en: Pieter Huidekoper (1798-1852), burgomaster of Amsterdam from 1842 to 1849, who campaigned for better public housing. The text on a memorial plaque to him reads: 'Hij was der stede goed, hij deed den arme wel' (he was good to the city, he did well by the poor).

name: Huidenstraat
en: After the hide trade (huiden: hides) concentrated here in earlier centuries.

name: Huifkarpad
en: The type of caravan (a covered wagon, huifkar) in use around 1900. The street name refers to the caravan site here.

name: Huigenbos
en: The name of farms in Scherpenzeel (Gelderland) and Egmond-Binnen (Noord-Holland).

name: Huismanshof
en: A huisman is the head occupant of a house in the countryside.

name: Huiswoudhof
en: Otto Huiswoud (Paramaribo, 1893 - Amsterdam, 1961) and Hermina Huiswoud, née Dumont (British Guiana, 1905 - Amsterdam, 1998). In New York Otto Huiswoud became involved in social issues, and in 1914 he joined the Socialist Party. In 1919 he was a co-founder of the Communist Party of the United States. In 1926 he married Hermina, who was also involved in the international communist movement: she worked as a translator for the Communist International (Comintern) and wrote for the monthly The Negro Worker. After the Second World War the couple moved to Amsterdam, where Otto Huiswoud was chairman of the Vereniging Ons Suriname from 1954 to 1961. Together they organised anti-colonial, political and cultural activities.

name: Huiswoudstraat
en: Otto Huiswoud (Paramaribo, 1893 - Amsterdam, 1961) and Hermina Huiswoud, née Dumont (British Guiana, 1905 - Amsterdam, 1998). In New York Otto Huiswoud became involved in social issues, and in 1914 he joined the Socialist Party. In 1919 he was a co-founder of the Communist Party of the United States. In 1926 he married Hermina, who was also involved in the international communist movement: she worked as a translator for the Communist International (Comintern) and wrote for the monthly The Negro Worker. After the Second World War the couple moved to Amsterdam, where Otto Huiswoud was chairman of the Vereniging Ons Suriname from 1954 to 1961. Together they organised anti-colonial, political and cultural activities.

name: Hullenbergweg
en: The name of a hill near Bennekom (Gelderland).

name: Hulstweg
en: The shrub with hard, prickly leaves and red berries (holly).

name: Humberto Delgadoplein
en: Portuguese general (1906-1965). In the presidential election of 1958 he was the opposition candidate against the official candidate of the dictator Salazar. He lost through large-scale electoral fraud and terror by the secret police. In 1965 he was murdered by the secret services of Spain and Portugal.

name: Humberweg
en: The broad estuary of the English rivers Trent and Ouse. The name is known in the coal trade, because English coal is shipped from the surrounding areas.

name: Huntum
en: A patrician house on the Vecht, south of Vreeland.

name: Huntumbrug
en: A patrician house on the Vecht, south of Vreeland.

name: Huntumdreef
en: A patrician house on the Vecht, south of Vreeland.

name: Huntumpad
en: A patrician house on the Vecht, south of Vreeland.

name: Hunzestraat
en: A small river that rises in Drenthe and widens into the Zuidlaardermeer on the border of the province of Groningen.

name: Hygiëaplein
en: The goddess of health in Greek mythology.

name: Hygiëastraat
en: The goddess of health in Greek mythology.

name: Ibizastraat
en: A Spanish island in the Mediterranean, part of the Balearic Islands.

name: Iepenplein
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Iepenweg
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: IJ-tunnel
en: The road through the tunnel under the IJ, opened on 30 October 1968.

name: IJburglaan
en: The name fits the Amsterdam tradition in which artificial islands and peninsulas have names ending in -burg. The name IJburg makes clear that the place lies in the IJmeer.

name: IJdok
en: Part of the Westerdokseiland.

name: IJdoornlaan
en: The polder outside the dike just east of the village of Durgerdam, a nature reserve of hay meadows and reed beds.

name: IJhaven
en: The IJ was once an arm of the Zuiderzee. In 1865-1872 it was reclaimed when the Noordzeekanaal was built, and in 1872 it was closed off from the Zuiderzee by the IJdijk and the Oranjesluizen.

name: IJmeer
en: The IJmeer is a border lake in the Netherlands. It lies between the De Nes polder, Pampushaven, the Hollandse Brug and the mouth of the IJ at IJburg, divided between the provinces of Noord-Holland and Flevoland.

name: IJplein
en: After the buildings of the Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij were demolished, a square was planned at the start of the Meeuwenlaan, and the planners called it the IJplein in advance. The name IJplein stuck, but no square was made; instead there are three parallel streets that all bear the name: an example of an inaccurate name.

name: IJpromenade
en: The IJ was once an arm of the Zuiderzee. In 1865-1872 it was reclaimed when the Noordzeekanaal was built, and in 1872 it was closed off from the Zuiderzee by the IJdijk and the Oranjesluizen.

name: IJsbaanpad
en: Named after the ice rink on the IJsclub grounds, to which the road leads.

name: IJselmondestraat
en: One of the Zuid-Holland islands.

name: IJselstraat
en: The river IJssel, a branch of the Rhine, runs from Westervoort to the IJsselmeer.

name: IJslandtpad
en: The eighteenth-century farmstead on the Middenweg, later joined to the still existing Frankendael, and demolished early in the nineteenth century.

name: IJsselmeerstraat
en: Named after the IJsselmeer.

name: IJssloot
en: The origin of this name is unknown.

name: IJzerhof
en: A river in Belgium.

name: IJzerwerkerstraat
en: A craftsman who works iron and steel (ironworker). The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Ilpendammerstraat
en: A village in Waterland on the Noordhollandsch Kanaal.

name: Ilperveldstraat
en: A nature reserve in the municipalities of Landsmeer and Waterland, a brackish peat area.

name: Imbos
en: A hilltop between Arnhem and Laag-Soeren, a nature reserve since 1937 and part of the Veluwezoom National Park.

name: Immanuel Kanthof
en: German philosopher (1724-1804), professor at Königsberg (Germany) and one of the greatest thinkers of his time. His works include the 'Critique of Pure Reason'.

name: Imogirituin
en: The Indonesian town of Imogiri, on a hill seventeen kilometres south-east of Yogyakarta. The town is famous for its seventeenth-century royal cemetery. In 1646 Sultan Agung was the first to be buried there.

name: Imstenrade
en: An old country house near Heerlen (Limburg).

name: Ina Boekbinderbrug
en: Ina Boekbinder (Assen, 1915 - Hilversum, 1987) was a Jewish resistance fighter in the Second World War. She helped Jewish children go into hiding and delivered ration coupons to people in hiding. She also carried Sten guns in her bicycle bags and raided a bandage depot.

name: Inaristraat
en: Lake Inari, in northern Finland near the Russian border.

name: Ingelandenweg
en: The ingelanden are the landowners in a polder, who are assessed for the polder charges and elect the polder board.

name: Ingenhouszhof
en: Jan Ingenhousz (1730-1799), physicist, discoverer of the respiration of plants.

name: Ingogostraat
en: A place in Natal (South Africa) where the Boer general Joubert defeated the British in 1881 (First Boer War).

name: Inlaagstraat
en: An inlaagdijk is a dike built further back because the original dike threatens to be undermined by the waves and has to be given up as the main defence. Here it refers to a former strip of land north-west of Sloterdijk.

name: Insulindeweg
en: The name Multatuli gave to what was then the Dutch East Indies, from the Latin 'insula' = island.

name: Internetstraat
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Inzet
en: Inzet, in the sense of dedication.

name: Ir. B. Bijvoetbrug
en: This bridge is named after the architect Bernard Bijvoet (1889-1979), a representative of the 'Nieuwe Bouwen' (Dutch modernism). His designs include the Zonnestraal Sanatorium and the Hotel Gooiland in Hilversum. He was closely involved in building the nearby Muziektheater on the Waterlooplein.

name: Ir. Jakoba Mulderplein
en: Jakoba Mulder (1900-1988), chief architect of the urban expansion section and later head of the urban development department of Amsterdam's Public Works Department. Her most important work was the design of the Amsterdamse Bos.

name: Irawan Soejonostraat
en: Resistance fighter (1919-1945), a member of an Indonesian resistance group in Leiden later named after him.

name: Isa van Eeghenbrug
en: Isabelle Henriette van Eeghen (1913-1996), archivist and historian. Between 1944 and 1978, at the City Archives near this bridge, she produced many works, among them a substantial study of Amsterdam's booksellers. She arranged the purchase of Jacob Olie's (1834-1905) photograph collection. A board member of the Genootschap Amstelodamum, she received the Silver Medal (Zilveren Penning) in 1971.

name: Isaäc Asscherpad
en: Founder of the Asscher diamond-cutting works in the Tolstraat. He lived from 1843 to 1902.

name: Isaac Gogelweg
en: Isaac Jan Alexander Gogel (1765-1821), statesman and Patriot, founder of several kinds of taxes. In 1814 King Willem I consulted Gogel on his financial affairs.

name: Isaac Israëlsbrug
en: Isaac Israëls (1865-1934) was the son of Jozef Israëls (1824-1911) and also a painter. With George Breitner, Willem Witsen, Jac. van Looy and Jan Eduard Karsen he was a representative of the Amsterdam school of painting. He painted factory girls and impressions of the city, among other things. At the 1928 Olympic Games in Amsterdam he won a gold Olympic art medal in painting for his picture 'De Rode Ruiter' (the red rider). This bridge connects to the Breitnerstraat and lies near the Willem Witsenstraat.

name: Isaac Titsinghkade
en: Lawyer (1744-1812), envoy in China and Japan, and also a physician, merchant, diplomat, philosopher and collector of Japonica. He worked for the Dutch East India Company for 32 years.

name: Isaak Gosseshof
en: Historian (1873-1940), professor in Groningen, who with N. Japikse wrote the 'Handboek tot de staatkundige geschiedenis van Nederland' (handbook of the political history of the Netherlands).

name: Isabella Richaardsstraat
en: Isabella Johanna Alyda Richaards (1904-1985), the first woman member of parliament in Suriname (1963-1969) since universal suffrage was introduced there in 1948. Suriname's Women's Day falls on the date she took her seat in parliament: 14 May.

name: Isarweg
en: A tributary of the Danube that flows past the German city of Munich.

name: Iseoplantsoen
en: The lake Lago d'Iseo, in the province of Lombardy in northern Italy.

name: Isolatorweg
en: An insulating material or body on which electrical conductors rest (an insulator).

name: Israël Queridostraat
en: Writer (1872-1932), originally a diamond worker. For many years literary contributor to the 'Algemeen Handelsblad', he wrote several novels about the life of ordinary Amsterdammers.

name: Ite Boeremastraat
en: Ite Boerema (1902-1980), surgeon, professor of surgery at the University of Amsterdam from 1946 to 1973. He built the hyperbaric pressure chamber in the Wilhelmina Gasthuis.

name: Iwan Kantemanplein
en: Iwan Hugo Kanteman (1908-1945), resistance fighter, born in Suriname. From 1940 until his arrest in 1944 he worked for the air-raid protection service in Amsterdam. From 1943 he worked clandestinely for the CPN and distributed 'De Waarheid'. After his arrest he was taken to several concentration camps and died of illness and exhaustion in Buchenwald.

name: J. Calsstraat
en: Jozef Maria Laurens Theo Cals (1914-1971), politician, member of the KVP. Among other posts he was Minister of Education, Arts and Sciences from 1952 to 1963, above all the man behind the Mammoetwet (mammoth law), which regulated all of secondary education. In 1965 he became Prime Minister. His cabinet fell in the 'night of Schmelzer' (22 November 1966).

name: J. de Koostraat
en: Jan de Koo (1841-1909), at first a minister and later an influential journalist, founder of 'De Groene Amsterdammer'.

name: J. Drijverweg
en: Jan Drijver (1896-1963), director and secretary of the Society for the Preservation of Nature Monuments (Natuurmonumenten) and secretary of the Dutch Society for the Protection of Birds.

name: J. Dunnebierstraat
en: Jacob Dunnebier (1904-1988), architect. With the architect Cees Ronstadt he was responsible for renovating several buildings in the city centre.

name: J.A. dèr Mouwstraat
en: Johan Andreas dèr Mouw (1862-1919), man of letters and doctor of classics, who wrote under the pseudonym Adwaita. His poetry holds Eastern mysticism in Western forms.

name: J.C. Breenstraat
en: Johannes C. Breen (1865-1927), historian and city archivist of Amsterdam.

name: J.C. Schröderstraat
en: Jan Christiaan Schröder (1871-1938), journalist, for many years editor-in-chief of the daily 'De Telegraaf', where he wrote among other things the column 'Dagboek van een Amsterdammer' (diary of an Amsterdammer).

name: J.C. van Epenstraat
en: Johannes Christiaan van Epen (1880-1960), architect of the Amsterdam School, whose designs include housing on the Amsteldijk, the Saffierstraat and the Harmoniehof.

name: J.F. Ankersmitstraat
en: Johan Frederik Ankersmit (1871-1942), journalist. He began at 'De Telegraaf' and from its founding in 1900 until 1937 worked for the daily 'Het Volk'.

name: J.F. Berghoefplantsoen
en: Johannes Franciscus Berghoef (1903-1994), architect, professor at the Technische Hogeschool in Delft from 1947 to 1969, and one of the most important representatives of the Delft School. In 1939, with J.J.M. Vegter, he won the competition for Amsterdam's city hall.

name: J.F. van Hengelstraat
en: Johannes Frederik van Hengel (1887-1975), director of the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland' from 1919 to 1946. He held countless other posts, among them board member of the Amsterdam Port Authority and of the Maritime Museum in Amsterdam.

name: J.G. Suurhoffstraat
en: Jacobus Gerardus Suurhoff (1905-1967), politician. Except for the war years and a few months in 1946, he was a member of the House of Representatives for the SDAP and later the PvdA from 1939 to 1952 and from 1959 to 1961. From 1949 to 1952 he was second chairman of the Nederlands Verbond van Vakverenigingen (NVV, trade union federation). Minister of Social Affairs (1952-1958) and Minister of Transport and Water Management (1965-1966).

name: J.H. Hisgenpad
en: Julius Heinrich Hisgen (1875-1957), a well-known player in the Dutch national cricket team and one of the pioneers of Dutch cricket.

name: J.H. van Heekpad
en: Jan Herman van Heek (1873-1957), textile manufacturer from Twente, who did much for nature conservation and for the protection of medieval buildings, especially in Gelderland and Utrecht.

name: J.H. van Heekweg
en: Jan Herman van Heek (1873-1957), textile manufacturer from Twente, who did much for nature conservation and for the protection of medieval buildings, especially in Gelderland and Utrecht.

name: J.J. Cremerplein
en: Jacobus Johannes Cremer (1827-1880), man of letters, whose works include 'Fabriekskinderen' (factory children, a plea for child protection) and 'Overbetuwsche Novellen'.

name: J.J. Cremerstraat
en: Jacobus Johannes Cremer (1827-1880), man of letters, whose works include 'Fabriekskinderen' (factory children, a plea for child protection) and 'Overbetuwsche Novellen'.

name: J.J. Viottastraat
en: Joannes Josephus Viotta (1814-1859), physician in Amsterdam of Italian descent, and also a composer of church music and of popular songs to texts by J.P. Heije.

name: J.J.M. Vegterstraat
en: Architect (1906-1982), one of the most important representatives of the Delft School. In 1939, with J.F. Berghoef, he won the competition for Amsterdam's city hall.

name: J.M. den Uylstraat
en: Johannes Marten (Joop) den Uyl (1919-1987), social-democratic statesman. He was, among other things, alderman for economic affairs in Amsterdam, Minister of Economic Affairs in the Cals cabinet (1965-1966) and from 1967 leader of the Labour Party group in the House of Representatives, before he became Prime Minister in 1973. From 1977 to 1981 he led his party in opposition. In the second Van Agt cabinet (1981-1982) he was Minister of Social Affairs and Employment.

name: J.M. van der Meylaan
en: Johan Melchior van der Mey (1878-1949), architect of the Amsterdam School and one of the founders of expressionism in architecture. His designs include the Scheepvaarthuis.

name: J.P. Kloosstraat
en: Jan Piet Kloos (1905-2001), architect, who designed many schools, hospitals and centres for the elderly, such as the one on the Schoenerstraat in Noord. He worked uncompromisingly in the spirit of the Nieuwe Bouwen and functionalism.

name: J.S. Ruppertstraat
en: Johan Stephaan Ruppert (1877-1934), one of the leaders of the Amsterdam Christian federation of union executives and of the Christian trade union movement.

name: J.W. Siebbeleshof
en: He lived from 1904 to 1985 and for years worked for the interests of older residents of the Nieuwmarkt neighbourhood. The Centre for the Elderly for people from the neighbourhood is largely thanks to him.

name: Jaagpad
en: The name recalls the time of the trekschuit (towed passenger barge), when the barge driver used his horse to pull the boats along the canal. Many waterways (trekvaarten) had a towpath (jaagpad).

name: Jaap Edenstraat
en: Sportsman (1873-1925), the only person to have been world champion in both skating and cycling. He won his first world skating title in 1893, and was world cycling champion in 1894 and 1895. His world record over 5000 m skating, set in 1894, stood for seventeen years.

name: Jaap Kunstbrug
en: Jaap Kunst (Groningen, 12 August 1891 - Amsterdam, 7 December 1960), Dutch ethnomusicologist and one of the founders of the modern discipline. Kunst began studying the violin at an early age and became seriously interested in Dutch folk culture. After graduating from the University of Groningen in 1917, he joined a string trio that toured the Dutch East Indies. Kunst stayed on in Java (Indonesia) until the mid-1930s, working for the government, and collected and studied the indigenous music there, especially that of the Javanese gamelan. In 1930 his growing reputation as an authority on Indonesian music made him musicologist to the Dutch government. He began to make extensive expeditions, collecting many musical instruments, recordings, books and photographs. In 1934 Kunst returned to the Netherlands, and in 1936 he became curator at the Royal Tropical Institute in Amsterdam, where he began one of the largest musicological collections in Europe.

name: Jaap Nunes Vazstraat
en: (Belongs to Jaap Kunst) In 1930 his growing reputation as an authority on Indonesian music made him musicologist to the Dutch government. In 1934 Kunst returned to the Netherlands, and in 1936 he became curator of the Royal Tropical Institute in Amsterdam.

name: Jaap Speyerstraat
en: (Belongs to Jaap Kunst) And he began one of the largest musicological collections in Europe.

name: Jaargetijden
en: The seasons. Nearby lie the Winter-, Lente-, Zomer- and Herfststraat (winter, spring, summer and autumn streets). The municipality of Weesperkarspel had earlier called the street Schoolstraat. After that municipality was abolished the name had to be changed, because Amsterdam already had a Schoolstraat.

name: Jac. P. Thijsseplein
en: Jacobus P. Thijsse (1865-1945), primary and later secondary schoolteacher and a well-known botanist and zoologist. With Eli Heimans he founded the Dutch Natural History Society. He was co-founder and secretary of the Society for the Preservation of Nature Monuments in the Netherlands, and known as a writer for his 'Geïllustreerde Flora van Nederland' and the Verkade albums.

name: Jachthavenweg
en: The road runs past the marinas on the Nieuwe Meer.

name: Jacob Bontiusplaats
en: Physician in the service of the Dutch East India Company (1592-1631). He studied the flora and fauna around Batavia (now Jakarta), the administrative centre of the former colony of the Dutch East Indies.

name: Jacob Burggraafstraat
en: Partner of the shipbuilder Jan Witheyn, to whom in 1656 the first shipyard on the island of Wittenburg was leased.

name: Jacob Cabeliaustraat
en: A Sea Beggar of the Eighty Years' War, who fought at the capture of Den Briel (1572) and the defence of Alkmaar (1573).

name: Jacob Catskade
en: Jacob Cats (1577-1660), also known as Vadertje (Father) Cats, poet and statesman, among other things Grand Pensionary of Holland and West-Friesland under Frederik Hendrik. His didactic poetry made him hugely popular.

name: Jacob de Rijkhof
en: Amsterdam grain merchant (1541-1584) who joined the Sea Beggars and in 1572 took part in the capture of Den Briel. He then became commander of Veere.

name: Jacob Frankhof
en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), a travelling salesman, born in Amsterdam, died in Sobibor (Poland).

name: Jacob Geelstraat
en: Man of letters and philologist (1789-1862) who campaigned against outdated art forms.

name: Jacob Groenplantsoen
en: Jacob Andries Groen Jr (1925-1987), historian, who wrote a great deal about the history of Amsterdam, especially Amsterdam-Noord. He is known among other things for his book 'Rondom Volewijck en Tolhuis' and his journalism for the daily 'De Noord-Amsterdammer'.

name: Jacob Honigstraat
en: Burgomaster of Zaandijk and founder of the antiquarian society for the Zaan region. Before 1930 the street was called Meijerstraat. It has been part of Amsterdam since 1 August 1966.

name: Jacob Husleystraat
en: Jacob Otten Husly (1730-1795), member of an Amsterdam family of architects. His buildings include Felix Meritis.

name: Jacob Krausstraat
en: Hydraulic engineer (1861-1951), Minister of Water Management in 1905 and 1908, who directed the building of harbour works in Chile.

name: Jacob Krüsestraat
en: Resistance fighter (1905-1944), born in Amsterdam, died in the Oranienburg concentration camp. Krüse worked for the clandestine paper 'Trouw' and for the 'Landelijke Organisatie voor hulp aan onderduikers' (the national organisation for help to people in hiding, the L.O.).

name: Jacob Marisplein
en: Painter (1837-1899), mainly of landscapes and Amsterdam street scenes.

name: Jacob Marisstraat
en: Painter (1837-1899), mainly of landscapes and Amsterdam street scenes.

name: Jacob Melkmanstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1902-1943), a travelling salesman by trade, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

name: Jacob Obrechtplein
en: Composer (1430-1505), for many years active abroad, among other things as a choirmaster. He composed a great many masses and motets. The street was taken over in 1896 from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the name Paviljoenstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 7 February 1896).

name: Jacob Obrechtstraat
en: Composer (1430-1505), for many years active abroad, among other things as a choirmaster. He composed a great many masses and motets. The street was taken over in 1896 from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the name Paviljoenstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 7 February 1896).

name: Jacob Paffstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1915-1966) who on 30 April 1944 took part in the raid on the remand prison (Huis van Bewaring) on Amsterdam's Weteringschans.

name: Jacob Tilstraat
en: A Beggar captain (1544-1584) who distinguished himself above all in the battle on the Zuiderzee against Bossu in 1573.

name: Jacob van Arteveldestraat
en: A novel by the Flemish writer Hendrik Conscience (1812-1883). Jacob van Artevelde lived from about 1290 to 1345 and was a Flemish popular leader.

name: Jacob van Lennepkade
en: Prose writer (1802-1868), mainly of historical novels, among them 'De roos van Dekama' and 'Ferdinand Huyck'.

name: Jacob van Lennepkanaal
en: Prose writer (1802-1868), mainly of historical novels, among them 'De roos van Dekama' and 'Ferdinand Huyck'.

name: Jacob van Lennepstraat
en: Prose writer (1802-1868), mainly of historical novels, among them 'De roos van Dekama' and 'Ferdinand Huyck'.

name: Jacob van Maerlantstraat
en: Flemish sexton (c. 1235 - c. 1300) from the village of Maerlant near Den Briel, later town clerk of Damme. The leading figure among the thirteenth-century Dutch (Diets) poets, known above all for his didactic poems.

name: Jacob van Wassenaar Obdamstraat
en: Jacob Baron van Wassenaer, Lord of Obdam (1610-1665), Dutch lieutenant-admiral, who was blown up with his ship at the Battle of Lowestoft in the Second Anglo-Dutch War.

name: Jacob van Weesenbekestraat
en: Secretary to William of Orange (1524-1575).

name: Jacoba Mosselhof
en: In the Dutch Protestant League, Jacoba Mossel started the discussion on whether women could work as religious teachers and preachers. She asked the executive to admit women to the training for religious teachers, and it agreed.

name: Jacoba van Tongerenbrug
en: Resistance fighter (1903-1967). As a social worker she took part in clandestine activities such as courier work, and then founded Groep 2000, an organisation of 140 people that helped up to 4500 people in hiding. She was nicknamed 'De bonnenkoningin' (the coupon queen) for smuggling ration coupons in a special waistcoat. She received the Yad Vashem distinction in 1990.

name: Jacobus van Looystraat
en: Man of letters and painter (1855-1930), known for his autobiographical cycle of novels 'Jaapje-Jaap-Jacob'. For some years he was on the editorial board of 'De Nieuwe Gids'.

name: Jacques Oppenheimstraat
en: Legal scholar (1849-1924), professor of constitutional and administrative law in Groningen and Leiden, and later also of international law. In 1913 he chaired the State Commission on proportional representation.

name: Jacques Veltmanstraat
en: Louis Jacques Veltman (1817-1907), actor. Besides the popular 'marqué', the villain in the melodramas, he was also a talented actor in the classical genre.

name: Jaddanbaikade
en: Jaddanbai was an Indian classical composer who, besides composing, also had talents for singing, dancing, acting and film production.

name: James Bradleystraat
en: English astronomer (1693-1762), Fellow of the Royal Society, appointed Savilian Professor of Astronomy at Oxford in 1721 and later Astronomer Royal. In 1728 he put the speed of light at 301,000 km/s, which mattered for navigation.

name: James Cookstraat
en: English explorer (1728-1779) whose discoveries include the east coast of Australia.

name: James Rosskade
en: James Clark Ross (1800-1862), English polar explorer, who led the Antarctic expedition of 1839-1843.

name: James Wattstraat
en: Scottish engineer (1736-1819), whose improvements made the steam engine practical. The unit of power of electric current is named after him. The street was earlier called Hans Lipperheijstraat (council decision of 10 January 1923).

name: Jan Abelszstraat
