en: A Beggar captain of the Eighty Years' War, known from the battle on the Ems in 1568, who took part in the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

name: Jan Beijerpad
en: Jan (Johannes Hendrikus) Beijer (1944-1994), a birdwatcher who often visited the Diemerzeedijk.

name: Jan Bernardusstraat
en: Probably named after a resident or landowner of the time. Before the annexation of 1896 the street belonged, under the same name, to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

name: Jan Bongastraat
en: A Frisian grietman (district magistrate), member of the Compromise of Nobles in 1566 and a captain under Louis of Nassau. He was killed fighting Rennenberg in 1580.

name: Jan Boterenbroodstraat
en: Architect (1886-1936) of the Amsterdam School, whose designs include Huize Lydia on the Roelof Hartplein and housing in Tuindorp Nieuwendam.

name: Jan Bottemastraat
en: Resistance fighter (1908-1944) who played an important part in caring for people in hiding. He was commander of the Amsterdam-Noord knokploeg (K.P., armed resistance squad), and was executed by firing squad in Wormerveer.

name: Jan C. de Voshof
en: Jan Cornelis de Vos (1855-1931), actor and director, called Jan C. by his colleagues. For many years with the Vereeniging Het Nederlandsch Tooneel, he was a guide to many young actors and actresses.

name: Jan Celestraat
en: Johannes Cele (1347-1417), educator and school organiser, rector of the famous Zwolle town school, which with that of Deventer laid the foundation of early Dutch humanism.

name: Jan Cupidohof
en: The coxswain of the lifeboat Brandaris (1869-1938). Under his command 261 shipwrecked people were rescued.

name: Jan de Greefstraat
en: Architect (1784-1834), whose buildings include the warehouses on the Entrepotdok.

name: Jan de Jonghkade
en: Gerrit Jan de Jongh (1845-1917), director of Rotterdam's Public Works and one of the founders of modern Rotterdam. Under his leadership an electricity network, a water supply and modern sewers were built. He became known above all for his role in the city's development and the expansion of the Rotterdam harbours.

name: Jan de Jonghstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1912-1945), born in Amsterdam and shot dead there.

name: Jan de Louterpad
en: Legal scholar (1847-1932), professor in Amsterdam and Utrecht, who taught international and constitutional law.

name: Jan de Louterstraat
en: Legal scholar (1847-1932), professor in Amsterdam and Utrecht, who taught international and constitutional law.

name: Jan den Haenstraat
en: One of the naval heroes of the Battle of Solebay in 1672. He was killed fighting the French off Palermo in 1676.

name: Jan Eisenloeffelstraat
en: Pseudonym of Johannes Wigbold (1876-1957), silversmith, who set up his own workshop in 1911. A representative of Dutch Art Nouveau and Art Deco.

name: Jan Evertsenbrug
en: Johan Evertsen (1600-1666), of a Zeeland family of naval heroes. As admiral he took part in several naval battles, including the Battle of the Downs (1639). He was killed in the Second Anglo-Dutch War.

name: Jan Evertsenstraat
en: Johan Evertsen (1600-1666), of a Zeeland family of naval heroes. As admiral he took part in several naval battles, including the Battle of the Downs (1639). He was killed in the Second Anglo-Dutch War.

name: Jan Goeverneurhof
en: Man of letters (1809-1889), known above all as a children's poet, who wrote under the pseudonym Jan de Rijmer. Founder and for many years editor of the family magazine 'De Huisvriend'.

name: Jan Goldschmedingstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1921-1944), involved in organising the clandestine paper 'Trouw'.

name: Jan Hanzenstraat
en: A landowner who in 1564 bought a piece of land on condition that he maintain a path running along it, which was therefore called the Jan Hanzenpad. The path lay partly in Nieuwer-Amstel and ran from the Singel to the Kostverlorenwetering. Later its remnants were called Jan Hanzenstraat and Jan Hanzenkade. In 1904 the quay was renamed Agatha Dekenstraat.

name: Jan Haringstraat
en: A Sea Beggar from Hoorn who in 1573 held the Diemerzeedijk between the IJ and the Diemermeer (Watergraafsmeer) alone against the Spanish for a time.

name: Jan Janzenstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1919-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in The Hague.

name: Jan Kiststraat
en: A skipper (died 1740) who sailed a transport barge for the Dutch East India Company (VOC).

name: Jan Lelimanhof
en: Architect (1829-1910) whose buildings include 'Arti et Amicitiae', the Prinsengracht hospital, several bread factories and some workers' housing (among others in the Valckenierstraat).

name: Jan Lievensstraat
en: Painter (1607-1674), a pupil of Rembrandt. His work includes murals in the city hall on the Dam.

name: Jan Ligthartstraat
en: Gerard Jan Ligthart (1859-1916), educator. With H. Scheepstra he wrote the once very well-known reading books for schoolchildren, 'Ot en Sien'.

name: Jan Luijkenstraat
en: Poet and engraver (1649-1712), popular above all for 'Het menselyk bedryf' (the human occupations), which he made with his son Caspar. By council decision of 27 February 1895 the street name was extended over a longer stretch, which was reversed by council decision of 3 April 1912.

name: Jan Maijenstraat
en: The Dutch navigator Jan Cornelisz May, who in 1611 discovered the Jan Mayen island named after him, between Spitsbergen and Iceland.

name: Jan Mankesstraat
en: Painter and etcher (1889-1920), mainly of animals.

name: Jan Massensloot
en: It is not known how this ditch got its name.

name: Jan Mensplein
en: Jan Mens (Amsterdam, 18 September 1897 - Amsterdam, 31 October 1967) was a Dutch writer. In 1935 he came into contact with the former schoolmaster Theo Thijssen, who gave him recommendations and feedback. In 1938 he won the Komso first-work prize for his manuscript Mensen zonder geld (people without money), which was his breakthrough. In the early 1960s he was the best-selling writer in the Netherlands, known for De kleine waarheid (the little truth), a picture of the life of the 'ordinary' Amsterdammer.

name: Jan Moretuspad
en: Jan Moretus (1543-1610) was the son-in-law of Christoffel Plantijn and worked in his bookshop for a long time. After Plantijn's death Jan Moretus carried on the bookshop and its printing works until his own death in 1610.

name: Jan Muschstraat
en: Johannes Petrus Musch (1875-1960), actor, a brilliant interpreter of Shakespeare and Vondel, who played a long series of great roles (Lucifer, De wijze kater, Nathan the Wise, Molière's Miser). In 1952 he celebrated 60 years on the stage.

name: Jan Nautahof
en: Resistance fighter (1917-1944), born in Almelo, died in Vught camp. Nauta worked for the clandestine paper 'Trouw'.

name: Jan Olphert Vaillantlaan
en: Naval officer (1751-1800) in the service of the Admiralty of Amsterdam, an expert on finding longitude at sea by lunar distances. In 1784 he published 'Verhandeling van de stuurmanskunst' (treatise on navigation).

name: Jan Oudegeeststraat
en: One of the founders of the Dutch trade union movement (1870-1950). Chairman of the NVV from 1909 to 1919 and secretary of the International Federation of Trade Unions from 1919 to 1926. He was also a member of Amsterdam's city council and of the Senate and the House of Representatives.

name: Jan Peppinkstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1918-1942) involved in many clandestine activities, who led the espionage group 'Nederland Vrij'.

name: Jan Pieter Heijestraat
en: Amsterdam physician and poet (1809-1876). He founded the Society for Nursing in 1844, was for thirty years director of Toonkunst, and promoted community singing. He wrote the popular children's songs 'De Zilvervloot' (the silver fleet), 'Kabels los' and 'Vlaggelied'.

name: Jan Postmahof
en: Resistance fighter (1895-1944), active in the labour movement, born in Amsterdam and, as a leader of the clandestine Communist Party, executed by firing squad in Vught.

name: Jan Poytstraat
en: Jan Poyt (years of birth and death unknown), a sixteenth-century designer, designed the striking tower of Ransdorp, which dates from the early sixteenth century. For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Jan Puntstraat
en: An eighteenth-century actor, much admired in his day and later fiercely criticised. Punt was also a skilled engraver.

name: Jan Rebelstraat
en: Jan Rebel was an islet in the old IJ. The name appears on old maps; how the islet got it is unknown.

name: Jan Ringelstraat
en: The Sea Beggar from Oostzaan who in 1576 sailed through the chain across the harbour of Muiden, so that Sonoy could sail in with his fleet.

name: Jan Schaeferbrug
en: Johannes Lodewijk Nicolaas Schaefer (1940-1994), politician for the Labour Party (PvdA). He sat in the House of Representatives from 1971, was state secretary for urban renewal at the Ministry of Housing and Spatial Planning in the Den Uyl cabinet from 1973 to 1977, and alderman in Amsterdam from 1978 to 1986 (housing, urban renewal, building control, land company). His are the winged words 'In gelul kan je niet wonen' (you can't live in hot air). He gave an enormous boost to urban renewal and housebuilding in Amsterdam.

name: Jan Schaeferpad
en: Johannes Lodewijk Nicolaas Schaefer (1940-1994), politician for the Labour Party (PvdA). He sat in the House of Representatives from 1971, was state secretary for urban renewal at the Ministry of Housing and Spatial Planning in the Den Uyl cabinet from 1973 to 1977, and alderman in Amsterdam from 1978 to 1986 (housing, urban renewal, building control, land company). His are the winged words 'In gelul kan je niet wonen' (you can't live in hot air). He gave an enormous boost to urban renewal and housebuilding in Amsterdam.

name: Jan Sluijtersstraat
en: Painter (1881-1957) who developed an entirely personal style in his portraits, still lifes and genre pieces.

name: Jan Smitstraat
en: Johannes Wilhelmus Smit (1851-1940), founder of the Roman Catholic Volksbond (people's league), who worked above all among the workers on the Eastern Islands.

name: Jan Somerhof
en: Jan Egbert W.H. Somer (1905-1945), resistance fighter and printer by trade, who for a long time printed the clandestine paper 'Het Parool'. Born in Hoorn, he was executed by firing squad in Zutphen on 13 April 1945.

name: Jan Springerhof
en: Jan L. Springer (1850-1915), architect, who with J.B. Springer and A.L. van Gendt built the Stadsschouwburg (completed 1894). He was also director of the Hague Academy of Fine Arts.

name: Jan Swammerdambrug
en: Jan Swammerdam (1637-1680), anatomist and naturalist, who made important microscopic studies, preserved in his 'Bybel der natuure' (Bible of nature).

name: Jan Theuniszhof
en: Linguist (1569-1638), specialising in Arabic.

name: Jan Thoméepad
en: Physician and football pioneer known far beyond the borders (1886-1954). Until his death he was medical attendant to the Dutch national football team.

name: Jan Tooropstraat
en: Painter and draughtsman (1858-1928), who developed an entirely personal style full of symbolism, later imbued with a religious mood. Fresco in the Beurs on the Damrak.

name: Jan van Beersstraat
en: Flemish man of letters (1821-1888), poet of Flemish everyday life.

name: Jan van Boendalestraat
en: Flemish poet (c. 1280 - c. 1365), town clerk of Antwerp and a renowned didactic poet.

name: Jan van der Neuthof
en: Jan Tijmen van der Neut (1921-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, died in Siegburg prison (Germany). In 1941 he was arrested by the occupiers for distributing the clandestine paper 'Vrij Nederland'.

name: Jan van Duivenvoordestraat
en: Lord of Warmond (1547-1610), who fought on the side of the Sea Beggars and defeated the Spanish in the harbour of Cádiz (1596).

name: Jan van Eijckstraat
en: Southern Netherlandish painter (1386-1440), court painter to John of Bavaria and later to Philip of Burgundy. He used oil paint in a way entirely new for the time.

name: Jan van Galenstraat
en: Fleet commander (1604-1653), killed in the Battle of Livorno against the English.

name: Jan van Goyenkade
en: Painter (1596-1656), mainly of landscapes.

name: Jan van Houthof
en: Man of letters (1542-1609), the first scholarly archivist, who wrote the first Dutch alexandrines.

name: Jan van Riebeeckhaven
en: Jan Anthonie van Riebeeck or Riebeek (1618-1708), who in 1652, in the service of the Dutch East India Company, founded the Cape Colony at the Cape of Good Hope.

name: Jan van Riebeekstraat
en: Jan Anthonie van Riebeeck or Riebeek (1618-1708), who in 1652, in the service of the Dutch East India Company, founded the Cape Colony at the Cape of Good Hope.

name: Jan van Schaffelaarplantsoen
en: A cavalry captain in the struggle between the Hooks and the Cods, who jumped from the tower of Barneveld to save the lives of his men. The main character of 'De Schaapherder', a historical novel by J.F. Oltmans.

name: Jan van Zutphenplantsoen
en: Amsterdam diamond worker (1863-1958), who in 1894 founded the General Dutch Diamond Workers' Union (ANDB) with Henri Polak, and later did important social and humanitarian work.

name: Jan van Zutphenstraat
en: Amsterdam diamond worker (1863-1958), who in 1894 founded the General Dutch Diamond Workers' Union (ANDB) with Henri Polak, and later did important social and humanitarian work.

name: Jan Vethstraat
en: Painter and draughtsman (1864-1925), and also an art historian, who campaigned to preserve the beauty of Amsterdam.

name: Jan Voermanstraat
en: Painter of landscapes and flowers (1857-1944), who illustrated many Verkade albums.

name: Jan Vrijmanstraat
en: Jan Hulsebos (1925-1997), journalist and filmmaker, who changed his name to Jan Vrijman during the Second World War. He was involved in the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid', and co-founded and co-directed the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA).

name: Jan Vroegopsingel
en: Amsterdam police sergeant (1877-1946), co-founder and from 1917 to 1946 chairman of the Allotment Holders' League (Bond van Volkstuinders).

name: Jan Willem Brouwersstraat
en: Joannes Wilhelmus Brouwers (1831-1893), Roman Catholic priest, journalist and writer, co-editor of the daily 'De Tijd' from 1863 to 1870 and parish priest in Bovenkerk from 1870.

name: Jan Wilsbrug
en: Named after Jan Wils (1891-1972), architect of the Olympic Stadium and the two Citroën buildings on the Stadionplein. He also designed the City Theatre on the Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen.

name: Jan Witheijnstraat
en: Shipbuilder (1610-1662). In 1656 he was the first to be leased a shipyard on the island of Wittenburg.

name: Jan Zijvertszstraat
en: A Beggar captain, known for the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

name: Jan Zwanenburghof
en: Resistance fighter (1921-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

name: Janna van der Weglaan
en: Janna Rinske van der Weg (1893-1974), skater. In 1917 she was the first woman ever to finish the Elfstedentocht, and the second woman in the event's history to take part. In daily life she was a domestic servant.

name: Janusz Korczakstraat
en: Polish-Jewish doctor (1878-1942), educator, children's author and director of an orphanage. On 6 August 1942 he was deported with two hundred children from the orphanage to the Treblinka extermination camp and murdered there together with the children.

name: Jarasingel
en: Víctor Jara (1938-1973), Chilean singer, who on international tours represented the voice of the opposition. For Chilean television he made programmes about the horrors of civil war and fascism. He was murdered by the junta in 1973.

name: Jarmuiden
en: The English port of Yarmouth, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Jasmijnstraat
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Jasonstraat
en: A figure from Greek mythology, leader of the Argonauts around 1350 BC.

name: Jasper Leijnsenstraat
en: The heroic sailor in a naval battle against the Spanish near Reimerswaal in 1574.

name: Jasper Warnerstraat
en: A pioneer of football (1870-1924), who in 1897 succeeded Pim Mulier as chairman of the Dutch Football Association.

name: Javakade
en: The island (Java), one of the Greater Sunda Islands (Indonesia). For many years the premises of the Stoomvaart Maatschappij Nederland stood on this quay; the company handled a large share of shipping to the former Dutch East Indies.

name: Javaplantsoen
en: The island (Java), one of the Greater Sunda Islands (Indonesia). For many years the premises of the Stoomvaart Maatschappij Nederland stood on this quay; the company handled a large share of shipping to the former Dutch East Indies.

name: Javaplein
en: The island (Java), one of the Greater Sunda Islands (Indonesia). For many years the premises of the Stoomvaart Maatschappij Nederland stood on this quay; the company handled a large share of shipping to the former Dutch East Indies.

name: Javastraat
en: The island (Java), one of the Greater Sunda Islands (Indonesia). For many years the premises of the Stoomvaart Maatschappij Nederland stood on this quay; the company handled a large share of shipping to the former Dutch East Indies.

name: Jean Desmetstraat
en: Film distributor and cinema owner (1875-1956), who began as a fairground and travelling cinema operator. By bringing foreign films to the Netherlands he contributed substantially to the radical changes in the film industry between 1907 and 1916.

name: Jekerstraat
en: A small river that flows into the Maas at Maastricht.

name: Jelle Posthumapad
en: Resistance fighter (1906-1943), born in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad in Scheveningen in 1943. He was active in distributing the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid'.

name: Jeltje de Bosch Kemperpad
en: Jonkvrouw de Bosch Kemper (1836-1916), the driving force behind several associations that organised nursing courses, and co-founder of the Tesselschade association. She promoted, among other things, the founding of the Amsterdam School of Domestic Science and the drawing school for girls.

name: Jennerstraat
en: Edward Jenner (1749-1823), English physician, who improved cowpox inoculation against smallpox so that it could be used on a mass scale. The street's name was earlier set as Emmalaan (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 15 March 1904).

name: Jephtastraat
en: A tragedy by Vondel, dating from 1659. By council decision of 6 October 1948 the street name was extended southwards, but on 18 February 1970 that stretch was added to the Gulden Winckelplantsoen.

name: Jeroenensteeg
en: Probably named after the former Sint Jeroenentoren, one of the small towers on the fifteenth-century city wall, to which the little street led. Jeroen was parish priest of Noordwijk and was killed by the Norsemen in the ninth century; he was later canonised.

name: Jisperveldstraat
en: A nature reserve near the Noord-Holland village of Jisp, a botanically important peat area.

name: Joan Melchior Kemperstraat
en: Legal scholar (1776-1824), professor in Amsterdam and Leiden, who campaigned against the rule of the regents and for constitutional government.

name: Joan Muyskenweg
en: Amsterdam industrialist (1866-1928), director of Werkspoor, who played an important part in the company's development.

name: Joannes de Swaefhof
en: A seventeenth-century schoolmaster from Middelburg, whose treatise on upbringing is considered the first complete work of pedagogy published in the Netherlands.

name: Joannes Reddingiusstraat
en: Poet (1873-1944), part of the late flowering of the Tachtigers (the Movement of the Eighties).

name: Jodenbreestraat
en: This street, laid out on part of the Sint Antoniesdijk, was part of the Sint Antoniesbreestraat until the second half of the seventeenth century. At that time the Jewish population began to grow considerably, and this part of the Breestraat became the main street of the 'Jodenbuurt' (Jewish quarter). From then on the name Jodenbreestraat came into use. After the occupiers had deported the Jewish residents in the war years 1940-1945, and much of the odd-numbered side had been demolished (and burnt in stoves), the rest of that row of façades was demolished in the 1960s.

name: Joep Langebrug
en: Joep Lange was a professor of infectious diseases and an AIDS expert, one of the most influential AIDS scientists in the world. He was killed on 17 July 2014 in the MH17 air disaster.

name: Joes Kloppenburgbrug
en: Joes Kloppenburg (1970-1996) was beaten to death by Richard L. on 17 August 1996 when he intervened in a street fight in the Voetboogsteeg with the words 'Kappen nou!' (stop it now!). This bridge is fairly close to where he died and is meant as a symbol against senseless violence.

name: Joh.M. Coenenstraat
en: Johannes Meinardus Coenen (1825-1899), musician, who composed choral works, ballets and operas, and conducted concerts in Felix Meritis and the Paleis voor Volksvlijt.

name: Johan Braakensiekhof
en: Illustrator and caricaturist (1858-1940), who for many years drew a weekly cartoon for 'De Groene Amsterdammer'. Also an illustrator of children's books.

name: Johan Broedeletstraat
en: Novelist and playwright (1877-1947), and also a critic for 'De Haagsche Post'.

name: Johan Coltermanpad
en: A Beggar captain of the Eighty Years' War and delegate of the Prince of Orange, who fought at Enkhuizen and Haarlem in 1572.

name: Johan Cruijff Boulevard
en: Johan Cruijff, born 25 April 1947 in Amsterdam, died 24 March 2016 in Barcelona. Forward for Ajax 1964-1973.

name: Johan Cruijffbrug
en: Johan Cruijff, born 25 April 1947 in Amsterdam, died 24 March 2016 in Barcelona. Forward for Ajax 1964-1973.

name: Johan de Meesterstraat
en: Man of letters (1860-1931), novelist, editor of 'De Nieuwe Gids' and contributor to the 'Nieuwe Rotterdamsche Courant'.

name: Johan Greivestraat
en: Johan Conrad Greive (Amsterdam, 2 April 1837 - Amsterdam, 14 May 1891) was a Dutch artist, known above all for his realist views of distant landscapes. During his career he was a member of the artists' society Arti et Amicitiae and taught at the Rijksakademie. His work can be seen in the Rijksmuseum and the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam, among other places.

name: Johan Herman Doornstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1910-1944), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Ede.

name: Johan Hofmanstraat
en: Probably named after J. Hofman, chairman of the Dutch Christian Typographers' Union (NCTB) and editor of its journal. He wrote several articles in Eltheto and Stemmen des Tijds, and the memorial book for the NCTB's jubilee is his work. In 1945 Hofman became second chairman of the re-founded CNV executive.

name: Johan Huijsenstraat
en: Photographer (1877-1959), a versatile portrait photographer who also made townscapes.

name: Johan Huizingalaan
en: Historian (1874-1945), professor at Groningen and Leiden, with many publications to his name, including 'Herfsttij der Middeleeuwen' (The Waning of the Middle Ages).

name: Johan Jongkindstraat
en: Landscape painter and engraver (1819-1891), who lived most of his life in France. A representative of impressionism.

name: Johan Kernstraat
en: Linguist (1833-1917), professor of Sanskrit at Leiden, and an expert on Indian and Malayo-Polynesian languages and literatures.

name: Johan Limpersstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1915-1944), a sculptor by profession (Prix de Rome 1940), born in Haarlem, executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

name: Johan Lulofsstraat
en: Professor of astronomy, mathematics and philosophy at Leiden (1711-1768), an expert on the chronometer method and as such an adviser to the States of Holland and the States General. In 1750 he published his 'Inleiding tot eene natuur- en wiskundige beschouwing des aardkloots' (introduction to a physical and mathematical study of the globe).

name: Johan Neeskensbrug
en: Johan Neeskens, born 15 September 1951 in Heemstede. Midfielder for Ajax 1970-1974, with 124 league matches. Three times Dutch champion, three times KNVB Cup winner, three times winner of the European Cup, once winner of the Cup Winners' Cup, once winner of the Intercontinental Cup, twice winner of the European Super Cup; 49 caps and two World Cup finals. In 1969 Ajax became the first Dutch club to reach the final of the prestigious European Cup, today's Champions League. Ajax lost that final, but two years later, in 1971, won the most important prize in football after all. In the two following years Ajax retained the title, confirming itself as the standard-bearer of Dutch football. Not only the titles but the way they were won, with modern, attacking football, made Ajax an international sensation. Coach Rinus Michels moulded this rare concentration of talent into a legendary team that was both untouchable and trend-setting at home and abroad.

name: Johan Ramaerstraat
en: Hydraulic engineer (1852-1932) who built the Merwedekanaal.

name: Johan Rijnjastraat
en: Architect (1870-1941) whose designs include the first buildings in Noord, between 1911 and 1915.

name: Johan Schamppad
en: Johan Frederik Jeremias Schamp (1899-1943), resistance fighter, active in distributing the clandestine paper 'Vrij Nederland'. He died in Amsterdam after being mistreated by the occupiers.

name: Johan Schippersplantsoen
en: Johan Godefridus Schippers (1923-1945), resistance fighter, born and executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

name: Johan van der Keukenstraat
en: Photographer and filmmaker (1938-2001). He trained in film in Paris and became famous in the Netherlands at a young age with his photo book 'Wij zijn 17' (we are 17). From the 1960s he worked mainly as a filmmaker, making dozens of short and longer films that won many awards at home and abroad.

name: Johan van Hasseltkade
en: He lived from 1850 to 1916 and was director of Public Works from 1900 to 1907, and before that director of the Waterworks.

name: Johan van Hasseltkanaal-Oost
en: He lived from 1850 to 1916 and was director of Public Works from 1900 to 1907, and before that director of the Waterworks. He had a large part in organising the ENTOS shipping exhibition of 1913. In 1900 Van Hasselt drew up a design for developing Amsterdam-Noord, with housing districts and a canal. An eastern and a western part of this canal were dug in 1919 and named after him. When a road was built on the undug part, it was named after him too.

name: Johan van Hasseltweg
en: He lived from 1850 to 1916 and was director of Public Works from 1900 to 1907, and before that director of the Waterworks.

name: Johan van Kuyckstraat
en: A Beggar captain who fought the Spanish near Vlissingen in 1572.

name: Johann Keplerstraat
en: German astronomer (1571-1630), who worked in Prague for many years;, one of the founders of modern astronomy, who discovered the laws governing the motion of the planets. A forerunner of Newton.

name: Johann Siegerstraat
en: Johann Gerhard Wilhelm Sieger (1856-1942), founder of the Amsterdam Quinine Factory.

name: Johanna Borskibrug
en: Johanna Borski (1764-1846) was called 'the financier of the Netherlands' because she invested in visionary projects such as De Nederlandsche Bank, the Nederlandsche Handel-Maatschappij and the Hollandsche IJzeren Spoorweg-Maatschappij (railway company). She twice saved the Dutch state from bankruptcy. She was born Johanna van der Velde on the Vijzelstraat and had her office on the Keizersgracht near the Spiegelstraat. This bridge looks out on the building of the Nederlandsche Handel-Maatschappij, which she helped found and twice saved from ruin.

name: Johanna Naberstraat
en: Feminist (1859-1941), co-founder of the International Archive for the Women's Movement, secretary of the Association for Women's Suffrage, board member of the International Woman Suffrage Alliance and member of Amsterdam's city council. Besides studies of feminism she wrote historical works.

name: Johanna Schouten-Elsenhoutstraat
en: Johanna Isidoro Eugenia Schouten-Elsenhout (1910-1992) was a Surinamese poet.

name: Johanna Westerdijkstraat
en: Botanist (1883-1961), from 1906 director of the Willie Commelin Scholten phytopathology laboratory in Amsterdam. In 1917 she became the first woman in the Netherlands to be appointed professor. The universities of Uppsala and Giessen gave her honorary doctorates.

name: Johannes de Bekahof
en: A fourteenth-century chronicler, whose works include the 'Great Chronicle of the Bishops of Utrecht'.

name: Johannes Hilverdinkstraat
en: Painter (1813-1902), mainly of landscapes.

name: Johannes J. Glasweg
en: Johannes Jacob Glas (1917-1942), resistance fighter. He kept up the links between the Waarheid resistance groups in the factories of Amsterdam-Noord, made explosives and had a part in the February Strike (1941). He was arrested in 1941 and executed by firing squad at Soesterberg on 19 November 1942.

name: Johannes Jelgerhuishof
en: Actor, draughtsman and painter (1770-1836), who excelled as a character actor.

name: Johannes Meewisstraat
en: Johannes Adriaan Meewis (1905-1948), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, died in Davos as a result of his imprisonment.

name: Johannes Poststraat
en: Resistance fighter (1906-1944), a farmer by trade, born in Hoogeveen, who played a leading role in the resistance, especially in the national knokploegen (armed squads). After a failed raid on the remand prison in Amsterdam he was executed by firing squad in Bloemendaal in 1944.

name: Johannes van der Steurstraat
en: Philanthropist (1865-1945), head of a children's home in Magelang (Indonesia) and a campaigner for child protection in the former Dutch East Indies, widely known as 'Pa van der Steur'.

name: Johannes van der Waalsstraat
en: Formerly Van der Waalsstraat. Physicist (1837-1923), professor in Amsterdam, who made a special study of the properties of gases and improved the Boyle-Gay-Lussac law. In 1910 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics. The name was changed in 1955 because of confusion with the Waalstraat in the Rivierenbuurt.

name: Johannes van Meurshof
en: Historian (1579-1639), professor of history and Greek at Leiden, who wrote important historical works on the Netherlands and Denmark.

name: Johannes Verhulststraat
en: Composer and conductor (1816-1891) of masses, overtures and songs. Conductor of the Caecilia concerts and of Felix Meritis, and around 1870 the undisputed leader of Amsterdam's musical life.

name: Johannes Vermeerplein
en: Painter (1632-1675), mainly of domestic interiors.

name: Johannes Vermeerstraat
en: Painter (1632-1675), mainly of landscapes and interiors.

name: Johannes Worpstraat
en: Organist and composer (1821-1891), author of the textbook 'Muziekleer' (music theory).

name: Johannis de Rijkestraat
en: Hydraulic engineer (1842-1913). In 1865 he was overseer in the building of the Oranjesluizen at Schellingwoude, and in 1872 he went to Japan, where in government service he improved harbours and major waterworks. From 1891 to 1903 he was a kind of state secretary at the Japanese Ministry of Transport and Water Management. He was knighted for his work in both the Netherlands and Japan.

name: John Blankensteinstraat
en: Football referee (1949-2006), one of the few openly gay people in the football world, who campaigned for gay emancipation.

name: John Campbellstraat
en: An eighteenth-century English captain, commander of the yacht Chatham, who in 1757 designed the sextant, a measuring instrument for finding position at sea.

name: John Coltranestraat
en: John William Coltrane (1926-1967), American jazz saxophonist, inspired by Indian and Arabic music.

name: John Fernhouthof
en: Photographer, cameraman and director (1913-1987), trained by the filmmaker Joris Ivens. Like Ivens he made several politically committed left-wing films. His most famous film is 'Sky over Holland' (1967), which shows the kinship between Dutch art and the Dutch landscape.

name: John Franklinstraat
en: English naval officer (1786-1847) who explored the Northwest Passage, but whose expedition perished in the polar ice.

name: John Hadleystraat
en: English physicist and mathematician (1682-1744), inventor of the octant, an angle-measuring instrument for finding position at sea.

name: John Lockehof
en: English philosopher (1632-1704), founder of a new approach to education and a forerunner of Kant.

name: John M. Keynesplein
en: John Maynard Keynes (1883-1946), British economist, known for his book 'The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money', which argues that government should play an active role in the economy and counter economic stagnation through investment. The book is often seen as the foundation of modern macroeconomics.

name: John Motleyhof
en: John Lothrop Motley (1814-1877), American historian of the Netherlands, whose works include 'The Rise of the Dutch Republic' (1856) and 'The Life and Death of John of Barneveld' (1875).

name: John Napierstraat
en: Scottish scholar (1550-1617), inventor of calculation with logarithms and so a pioneer of modern astronomy. His invention was of great importance for navigation.

name: John Rädeckerbrug
en: John Rädecker (1885-1956, born and died in Amsterdam) drew, painted, made prints and carved wooden sculptures. His first sculptures were of brick, such as the Worker for De Dageraad in Amsterdam. He became best known as designer of the sculptures on the National Monument on the Dam.

name: Johnny & Jonesbrug
en: Johnny & Jones was an Amsterdam jazz duo, in which Nol van Wesel (1918-1945) was Johnny and Max Kannewasser (1916-1945) Jones. Because they were Jewish they were interned in the Westerbork transit camp in 1943. Even so they managed to return briefly to Amsterdam to make some recordings, including the 'Westerbork Serenade'. On 4 September they were put on a transport to Germany, where they died of exhaustion in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp shortly before the liberation. Their most famous song was 'Meneer Dinges, weet niet wat swing is' (Mr Thingummy doesn't know what swing is).

name: Joke Smitstraat
en: Campaigner for women's emancipation (1933-1981), critic and writer. She founded the movement 'Man Vrouw Maatschappij' and was a member of the Emancipation Committee. From 1970 to 1971 she sat on Amsterdam's city council for the PvdA. She floated the idea of a political party of women's own.

name: Jolicoeurstraat
en: One of the leaders of the uprising of enslaved people in Suriname. The escaped enslaved people, also called Maroons, waged a guerrilla war against their oppressors, plundering the plantations and dealing heavy blows to the economy.

name: Jollenpad
en: A jol (dinghy) is a small keelboat.

name: Jonagoldstraat
en: An apple variety from the United States, known for its good taste and its equally good keeping qualities.

name: Jonas Daniël Meijerplein
en: Secretary of the committee that drafted the constitution of 1813 (1780-1834). The square was made by filling in parts of the Houtgracht and the Muidergracht. The name was given to this square between the synagogues because in 1810 J.D. Meijer, as peacemaker, drew up the concordat between the two Jewish congregations.

name: Jonathanhof
en: An apple, also known as the Ulster Seedling, the parent of the Jonagold and from the United States.

name: Joop Eijlstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1896-1941), a warehouseman by trade, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in The Hague.

name: Joop Gerritzestraat
en: Resistance fighter (1913-1942), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad at Soest.

name: Joop IJisbergstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1900-1942), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad at Soest.

name: Joop van Weezelhof
en: Joseph Jacques van Weezel, resistance fighter (1909-1945), active in the CPN from 1930. In 1941 he was arrested by the Nazis on suspicion of organising the February Strike. He died in the Dachau concentration camp in 1945.

name: Joos Banckersplantsoen
en: Fleet commander (1599-1647), who had a part in the capture of the Silver Fleet under Piet Hein and in the Battle of the Downs under Cornelis Tromp.

name: Joos Banckersweg
en: Fleet commander (1599-1647), who had a part in the capture of the Silver Fleet under Piet Hein and in the Battle of the Downs under Cornelis Tromp.

name: Joos de Moorstraat
en: Vice-admiral of Zeeland (1548-1618), known from the Eighty Years' War, who fought the Dunkirk privateers.

name: Joost Bilhamerstraat
en: Architect (1541-1590), also a surveyor and cartographer. His works include the tower of the Oude Kerk. His map of 1575 is one of the oldest known maps of Holland.

name: Joris Ivensplein
en: Filmmaker (1898-1989), one of the most important documentary makers in film history. He became known for avant-garde documentaries such as 'De brug' (the bridge, 1928) and 'Regen' (rain, 1929), in which he experimented with movement and rhythm. Later he became more and more interested in social issues and a convinced communist, and made films commissioned by various communist regimes. Because of his films about the 'police actions' in Indonesia he became persona non grata in the Netherlands. He received countless awards for his films.

name: Joris Ivensstraat
en: Filmmaker (1898-1989), one of the most important documentary makers in film history. He became known for avant-garde documentaries such as 'De brug' (the bridge, 1928) and 'Regen' (rain, 1929), in which he experimented with movement and rhythm. Later he became more and more interested in social issues and a convinced communist, and made films commissioned by various communist regimes. Because of his films about the 'police actions' in Indonesia he became persona non grata in the Netherlands. He received countless awards for his films.

name: Joris van Andringastraat
en: A seventeenth-century naval commander, died 1676, and secretary to Admiral Michiel de Ruyter.

name: Joris van den Berghweg
en: Sports journalist (1882-1953), especially of cycling.

name: Joseph Haydnpad
en: Joseph Haydn (1732-1809), Austrian composer.

name: Joseph Scaligerstraat
en: Joseph Justus Scaliger (1540-1609), classical philologist and professor in Geneva. As a Huguenot he fled after the St Bartholomew's Day Massacre and later came to Holland, where he became a professor at Leiden. He taught Hugo de Groot and founded the Leiden school of philology.

name: Joseph Schumpeterstraat
en: Joseph Alois Schumpeter (1883-1950), Austrian economist, who fled to America because of the rise of the Nazis. Known for his theory of 'creative destruction': old ways of working and old structures are constantly replaced by new ones.

name: Josephus Jittastraat
en: Abraham Carel Josephus Jitta (1887-1958) was a Dutch legal scholar and professor at the Technische Hogeschool in Delft.

name: Joubertstraat
en: Petrus Joubert (1831-1900), commander-in-chief of the Boers in the Transvaal wars of independence.

name: Jouke Zietsmastraat
en: Jouke Zietsma (1893-1962) was involved in Tuindorp Nieuwendam, a high point of the rural variant of the Amsterdam School. For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Jozef Israëlskade
en: Painter (1824-1911), a pupil of J.W. Pieneman and J.H. Kruseman, who became known for his socially engaged scenes, among them scenes from the lives of poor fishermen.

name: Juliana van Stolbergstraat
en: Juliana of Stolberg (1506-1580), wife of William of Nassau and mother of Prince William of Orange. Princess Juliana is named after her.

name: Julianaplein
en: Juliana Louise Emma Marie Wilhelmina, born 30 April 1909, married in 1937 to Prince Bernhard of Lippe-Biesterfeld, Queen of the Kingdom of the Netherlands from 1948 to 1980.

name: Julius Pergerstraat
en: Photographer (1840-1924), a contemporary of Pieter Oosterhuis, who like Oosterhuis photographed engineering works, including bridges and railways.

name: Jungfrau
en: A mountain peak in Switzerland, 4158 metres high.

name: Jupiterstraat
en: The largest planet in our solar system.

name: Justus Halbertsmastraat
en: Frisian writer, philologist and historian (1789-1869).

name: Justus Lipsiusstraat
en: Linguist (1547-1606), professor at Leiden and later at Leuven.

name: Justus van Maurikstraat
en: Amsterdam cigar manufacturer (1846-1904), who became very popular as a writer about the life of ordinary Amsterdammers. He was co-editor of 'De Groene Amsterdammer'.

name: Juttepeerpad
en: An old Dutch pear variety. The street lies on the former De Bongerd allotment complex.

name: Kaapstadweg
en: With Bloemfontein and Pretoria, one of the capitals of South Africa (Cape Town).

name: Kaasjeskruidstraat
en: A plant family (mallows) named for its fruit, shaped somewhat like a little cheese. The common mallow, which also grows in the Netherlands, was used in classical antiquity against all sorts of ailments, from bowel and womb complaints to wasp and scorpion stings.

name: Kabelgaststraat
en: A trade name: someone who splices and joins cables. The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Kabelweg
en: The insulated bundle of wires carrying electricity under water or underground (a cable). The road follows the strip of land along which, around 1950, the high-voltage cables were laid from the Hemweg power station to the western garden cities then being built, to supply them with power.

name: Kabouterbrug
en: The Kabouterbrug is named after the Kabouter movement (1969-1974), a playful protest movement and local political party.

name: Kadijksplein
en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

name: Kadoelenbrug
en: The name of the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was added to Amsterdam on 1 August 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) appears as early as 1375. In 1429 the manors of Landsmeer and Quadolen are mentioned, which then shared one lord. Old maps show Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterland sea dike (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1 August 1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed because of confusion with the Zuideinde (formerly Oostzaan).

name: Kadoelenpad
en: The name of the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was added to Amsterdam on 1 August 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) appears as early as 1375. In 1429 the manors of Landsmeer and Quadolen are mentioned, which then shared one lord. Old maps show Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterland sea dike (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1 August 1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed because of confusion with the Zuideinde (formerly Oostzaan).

name: Kadoelenweg
en: The name of the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was added to Amsterdam on 1 August 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) appears as early as 1375. In 1429 the manors of Landsmeer and Quadolen are mentioned, which then shared one lord. Old maps show Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterland sea dike (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1 August 1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed because of confusion with the Zuideinde (formerly Oostzaan).

name: Kadoelerbreek
en: The name of the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was added to Amsterdam on 1 August 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) appears as early as 1375. In 1429 the manors of Landsmeer and Quadolen are mentioned, which then shared one lord. Old maps show Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterland sea dike (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1 August 1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed because of confusion with the Zuideinde (formerly Oostzaan).

name: Kagelinkkade
en: The name of an old farm east of Diepenheim (Overijssel), by the Kagelink wood.

name: Kajuitpad
en: A part of a ship (the cabin).

name: Kajuitweg
en: A part of a ship (the cabin).

name: Kalfjeslaan
en: The former eighteenth-century inn on the Amsteldijk (demolished 1967), later the café-restaurant Het Kalfje.

name: Kalkmarkt
en: The lime market (kalkmarkt) was held on this quay from about 1663 until the end of the eighteenth century. The quay was made when the Nieuwe Waalseiland was filled in with earth in 1644.

name: Kalkoenstraat
en: The game bird (the pheasant).

name: Kalmoesstraat
en: A water plant (sweet flag).

name: Kalverstraat
en: After the calf market (kalvermarkt) held here until the seventeenth century. The name already occurs as such in 1393. However, no proof has been found that a cattle market was really held here, only that there was a calf market on the Dam in 1586. When it came inside the city, the stretch between the Spui and the Munt was called Byndewyck, that is, Binnenwijk (inner quarter). This southern part had the cattle market from 1486 to 1629 and was also called Ossemarkt (ox market). After that the name Kalverstraat spread over the whole street.

name: Kamerlingh Onneslaan
en: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes (1853-1926), physicist and professor at Leiden, who liquefied helium. In 1913 he won the Nobel Prize in Physics.

name: Kamerpalmhof
en: A kind of palm related to the succulents, with thick, leathery leaves (aspidistra).

name: Kamillestraat
en: A strongly scented meadow plant (camomile) of the daisy family, found not only in meadows but also often on waste ground.

name: Kamperfoelieweg
en: The climbing shrub (honeysuckle).

name: Kampervenuspad
en: An old Dutch pear variety. The street lies on the former De Bongerd allotment complex.

name: Kampina
en: A nature reserve east of Oisterwijk (Noord-Brabant), made up of fens, the Kampina heath and the valley of the Beerze stream.

name: Kanaaldijk West
en: Named after the Kanaaldijk: the west side of the dike.

name: Kanaalpost
en: Named after the Kanaaldijk.

name: Kanaalstraat
en: The kanaal (canal) meant here is the nearby Jacob van Lennepkanaal.

name: Kanariestraat
en: The songbird (the canary).

name: Kaneelappelstraat
en: A tropical fruit (sugar apple), originally from South America. Its skin is usually green, and its very soft flesh is white, with a sweet, aromatic taste.

name: Kanteel
en: The raised part of a crenellated defensive wall, with arrow slits (a merlon). The name refers to the rectangular shape of the neighbouring buildings.

name: Kantershof
en: The name of a farm in Bunde (Limburg).

name: Kantershofpad
en: The name of a farm in Bunde (Limburg).

name: Kantershofstraat
en: The name of a farm in Bunde (Limburg).

name: Kapkarpad
en: The very first type of caravan (a hooded cart). The street name refers to the caravan site here.

name: Kapoeasweg
en: A navigable river in Indonesia, on Kalimantan (Borneo).

name: Kapteynstraat
en: Jacobus Cornelis Kapteyn (1851-1922), astronomer and professor at Groningen, known for his research on star streams. He also lectured in the United States and South Africa.

name: Karel Doormanstraat
en: Karel Willem Frederik Marie Doorman (1889-1942), naval officer. During the Second World War he was rear admiral in the Dutch East Indies. In 1942 he was given the impossible task of preventing the Japanese from landing on Java, and was killed in this famous Battle of the Java Sea. The street came onto Amsterdam territory in 1921 under the name Houtmanstraat (council decision of Sloten, 8 March 1910), and by council decision of 22 March 1922 was named Zeven Provinciënstraat, after Admiral De Ruyter's flagship. After some changes to its boundaries (council decisions of 27 April 1933 and 10 June 1936), its present name was set in 1946.

name: Karel du Jardinstraat
en: Painter of landscapes and animals (1622-1678).

name: Karel Klinkenbergstraat
en: Painter of townscapes (1852-1924).

name: Karel van de Woestijnestraat
en: Flemish man of letters (1878-1929), professor at Ghent from 1921, one of the greatest Flemish poets after Guido Gezelle, and also known as a critic.

name: Karel van het Revebrug
en: Karel van het Reve (1921-1999) was a professor of Russian literature and a man of letters, widely regarded as one of the most important non-fiction writers in the Netherlands.

name: Karimatastraat
en: An Indonesian island group off the west coast of Kalimantan (Borneo).

name: Karl Grögersingel
en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), one of the nine involved in the attack on the Amsterdam population register on 27 March 1943. He was also involved in the attack on the railway near Sloterdijk and in founding the seditious magazine 'Rattenkruid' (rat poison).

name: Karl Marxpad
en: Karl Heinrich Marx (1818-1883), German philosopher and economist, who believed that capitalism would necessarily perish through its own development. Founder of Marxism, in which class struggle and the overthrow of the ruling class are central.

name: Karlskrona-eiland
en: A Swedish port on the Baltic from which much potash, timber and iron used to be shipped to Amsterdam.

name: Karnstraat
en: A dairy implement for making butter from milk (a churn).

name: Karpatastraat
en: Karpata, nicknamed Bastian, one of the leaders of the slave revolt that broke out on Curaçao in August 1795. He was captured in September that year and executed.

name: Karperstraat
en: The freshwater fish (the carp).

name: Karperweg
en: The freshwater fish (the carp).

name: Karspeldreef
en: The name recalls the former municipality of Weesperkarspel. Karspel or kerspel is an old word for a rural municipality, and earlier still for a church village or parish.

name: Karthuizersdwarsstraat
en: The streets were laid out where the monastery of the 'Carthuysers ter saliger havene' (Carthusians of the blessed haven) stood from 1394 to 1578. Until 1892 the cross street was called Blindemansteeg, but the name was changed because of confusion with the other Blindemansteeg. The path and playground are on the site of the monastery's former graveyard, which is why the park was called Karthuizer Kerkhof until 1889.

name: Karthuizersplantsoen
en: The streets were laid out where the monastery of the 'Carthuysers ter saliger havene' (Carthusians of the blessed haven) stood from 1394 to 1578. Until 1892 the cross street was called Blindemansteeg, but the name was changed because of confusion with the other Blindemansteeg. The path and playground are on the site of the monastery's former graveyard, which is why the park was called Karthuizer Kerkhof until 1889.

name: Karthuizersstraat
en: The streets were laid out where the monastery of the 'Carthuysers ter saliger havene' (Carthusians of the blessed haven) stood from 1394 to 1578. Until 1892 the cross street was called Blindemansteeg, but the name was changed because of confusion with the other Blindemansteeg. The path and playground are on the site of the monastery's former graveyard, which is why the park was called Karthuizer Kerkhof until 1889.

name: Karveelstraat
en: A fast sailing ship (caravel), carrying mainly a mainsail. The type dates from the late Middle Ages: two of Columbus's three ships in 1492, the Niña and the Pinta, were caravels.

name: Kastanjeplein
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Kastanjeweg
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Kastelenstraat
en: The name was given because the street runs right through the neighbourhood of castle names. The last stretch of the Kastelenstraat was renamed Zwaansvliet on 3 February 1965.

name: Kasterleepark
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Kastrupstraat
en: The name of Copenhagen's airport.

name: Katrijpstraat
en: A hamlet, also spelt Catrijp, at the foot of the dunes near Schoorl (Noord-Holland).

name: Kattenburgerbrug
en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

name: Kattenburgergracht
en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

name: Kattenburgerhof
en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

name: Kattenburgerkade
en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

name: Kattenburgerkruisstraat
en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

name: Kattenburgerplein
en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

name: Kattenburgerstraat
en: One of the three eastern islands, with Wittenburg and Oostenburg. It was already called Kattenburg before it was diked and built on in the second half of the seventeenth century. No explanation for the name has been found so far. There was a house called 'de Cat', but that name is only recorded in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had been demolished during the occupation, the rest were demolished in 1965-1968. Rebuilding then began on a new street plan. The Kattenburgerplein is the only thing that still recalls the old buildings.

name: Kattenburgervaart
en: A canal named after Kattenburg, the westernmost of the three Eastern Islands in Amsterdam.

name: Kattengat
en: Originally this was a narrow little canal running from the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal (now the Spuistraat) to the Singel. There is no agreement about the origin of the name. A narrow passage used to be called, figuratively, a kattegat: a gap so narrow that not even a cat could get through. The name may also come from the old nature of the ground: marshy land where catmint grows. The little canal was filled in during the second half of the nineteenth century. Part of it is now called Koggestraat. The remaining little street was widened considerably by demolition in 1936.

name: Kattenlaan
en: The origin and age of the name are unknown. The street came over under the same name from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel in 1896.

name: Kattensloot
en: This name probably refers to the animal (cats).

name: Kattenslootbrug
en: The name of the ditch beneath it.

name: Katwijkstraat
en: The Zuid-Holland fishing village and seaside resort.

name: Kazernestraat
en: After the Oranje-Nassau barracks (kazerne), built in 1811.

name: Kea Boumanstraat
en: Kornelia Bouman (1903-1998), tennis player. Until 1996 she was the only Dutch Grand Slam winner (French Championships, 1927). She won bronze in the mixed doubles at the 1924 Olympic Games.

name: Keerpunt
en: The name came out of conversations with residents: a keerpunt (turning point) in the city council's thinking, to build homes instead of office buildings, the result of the neighbourhood's participation.

name: Keerwal
en: A place where you can go no further and have to turn back (keren). The buildings on the Keerwal screen the homes by the railway in the Funenpark.

name: Kees Abspoelstraat
en: Kees Abspoel (1899-1970) was Shell's in-house architect, and as such designed Shell's Great Laboratory in Amsterdam-Noord, on the Overhoeks site.

name: Kees Boekestraat
en: For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Kees Broekmanstraat
en: Cornelis Broekman (1927-1992), speed skater. In 1952 he was the first Dutchman to win a Winter Olympics medal, silver in the 5000 metres. He was also second in the 10 km.

name: Kees Fensbrug
en: Kees Fens (1929-2008) was an Amsterdam literary critic, essayist and man of letters. He received the P.C. Hooft Prize in 1990 and an honorary doctorate from the University of Amsterdam in 2004. From his house he looked out on this bridge, and in 2008 he published the book 'Het geluk van de brug' (the happiness of the bridge).

name: Kees Schererhof
en: Christoffel Johannes Scherer (1920-1993), photographer, who made his breakthrough with reportage on the North Sea flood of 1953, among other things. Two years later he co-founded World Press Photo. He portrayed Amsterdam poetically.

name: Keienbergweg
en: The name of a hill in Gelderland, between Velp and Beekhuizen.

name: Keizersbrug
en: It takes its name from the nearby Keizersstraat.

name: Keizersgracht
en: After Emperor Maximilian, Archduke of Austria, who in 1489 granted Amsterdam the privilege of bearing the imperial crown on its coat of arms.

name: Keizersstraat
en: On the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

name: Kelbergen
en: The name of a manor house in Brummen (Gelderland).

name: Kelbergenpad
en: The name of a manor house in Brummen (Gelderland).

name: Kemangiestraat
en: A herb, also called lemon basil or Thai basil.

name: Kemiriestraat
en: A nut. A kemiri (candlenut) is a kind of almond with a very strong taste.

name: Kemminkhorstweg
en: Named after the old farm Kemminckhorst near Dalfsen (Overijssel).

name: Kempenlaan
en: The border region of Belgian and Dutch Brabant (the Kempen).

name: Kempering
en: The name of a farm at Reutum, in Tubbergen (Overijssel).

name: Ken Saro-Wiwastraat
en: Nigerian writer (1941-1995), politician and businessman. As leader of MOSOP, the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People founded in 1990, he campaigned for more autonomy for the Ogoni. In 1995 he was sentenced to death after a show trial by the dictatorial regime, and on 10 November 1995 he was hanged together with eight other Ogoni activists.

name: Kennemerduinstraat
en: The Kennemerduinen national park, a nature reserve north of the Bloemendaalse Zeeweg.

name: Keratellastraat
en: A microscopic water creature (a rotifer) with two fast-spinning crowns of cilia and strong chewing parts for grinding its food. The keratella lives in a small case marked by spines.

name: Kerdijkhof
en: Arnoldus Polak Kerdijk (1846-1905), politician and journalist, who as a progressive liberal worked for the emancipation of workers. He was also a director of the Rijkspostspaarbank (post office savings bank).

name: Kerkepad
en: The Kerkepad is named after its position and purpose: the path from the dike village of Nieuwendam to the village church.

name: Kerklaan Zunderdorp
en: The main street of Zunderdorp, leading towards the village church.

name: Kerkstraat
en: The Kerkstraat was laid out in 1665 and named for the plan to link four churches (kerken) with it: the Amstelkerk, the Oosterkerk and two others that were never built, one by the Molenpad and one by the Weesperstraat. Later the street got various names: Kerkstraat (to the Amstel), Nieuwe Kerkstraat (to the Roetersstraat), Plantage Kerklaan (in the Plantage) and Korte Kerkstraat, which was renamed Tussen Kadijken in 1943.

name: Kermispad
en: The fair (kermis) with its attractions. The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

name: Kerriestraat
en: A spice mix (curry), originally from India, where the word 'kari' means sauce. The English corrupted 'kari' into 'curry'. Kerrie came to the Netherlands by way of Indonesia.

name: Kersenstraat
en: The fruit of the cherry tree.

name: Kerstomaatplantsoen
en: A kind of tomato, also called cocktail or cherry tomato.

name: Kervelplantsoen
en: A herb (chervil). In the Middle Ages the plant was often found in monastery gardens.

name: Ketelhuisplein
en: The very striking boiler house of the former Wilhelmina Gasthuis.

name: Ketelmakerij
en: The street lies on the site of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij. Ketelmakerij (boilerworks) refers to one of the workshops that were here.

name: Ketelmakerstraat
en: This trade name (boilermaker) recalls the old boilerworks that was here.

name: Ketelstraat
en: The machine part, the steam boiler (ketel): a closed vessel in which water is turned into steam by heating.

name: Keurenplein
en: Keuren are the ordinances of any public authority before 1795. The name is linked to the verb 'keuren' in the sense of 'choosing': originally these were the rules to be observed, or laid down, on the day new officials were chosen.

name: Keverberg
en: A castle in Kessel (Limburg), also called Kessel castle, built on the foundations of an eleventh-century stronghold and destroyed by German troops in 1944.

name: Kiefskamp
en: One of the best-preserved eighteenth-century country houses, from about 1770, near Vorden (Gelderland).

name: Kiekstraat
en: Israël David Kiek (1811-1899), photography pioneer. In the Netherlands his surname has become a byword for the unpretentious, off-the-cuff photo: the kiekje (snapshot). He had a photo studio in Leiden and photographed Leiden student life.

name: Kierkegaardstraat
en: Søren Kierkegaard (1813-1855), Danish preacher and philosopher, whose work centres on his personal view of life. He rejected the state church and institutional Christianity.

name: Kievitstraat
en: The meadow bird (the lapwing).

name: Kijkduinstraat
en: The former fort south of Huisduinen near Den Helder, known for the naval battle of 1673 in which Admiral De Ruyter defeated the combined Anglo-French fleet.

name: Kikkenstein
en: The name of a patrician house in Loenen (Utrecht).

name: Kikkensteinhof
en: The name of a patrician house in Loenen (Utrecht).

name: Kikkensteinstraat
en: The name of a patrician house in Loenen (Utrecht).

name: Kimpoweg
en: The name of the airport of Seoul, South Korea.

name: Kinderdijkstraat
en: The river dike along the Noord, in the Alblasserwaard (Zuid-Holland).

name: King's Cross
en: A major railway station in north London.

name: Kingsfordweg
en: The name of the airport of Sydney, Australia.

name: Kinkerbrug
en: This bascule bridge is named after Johannes Kinker (1764-1845), poet and lawyer in Amsterdam and The Hague, who later became a professor at Liège.

name: Kinkerstraat
en: He translated work by Shakespeare and Schiller.

name: Kinrooistraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Kinselmeer
en: A lake north of Durgerdam.

name: Klaas Geertsplantsoen
en: Klaas Geerts (1932-2002) founded the architectural practice INBO. He played an important part in the post-war reconstruction of the Netherlands and designed the Molenwijk. For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Klaas Katerstraat
en: Amsterdam bricklayer (1833-1906), who in 1876 founded the Christian association Patrimonium in Amsterdam and chaired it until 1899. From 1880 to 1900 he led the Christian Workers' League.

name: Klaas Wannen
en: Named after the ditch between the Twiske and the Gouw, probably named after a farmer. It disappeared when the Twiske was turned into a polder and laid out as woodland.

name: Klapmutsenveem
en: A veem is a company that stores goods in its warehouses and delivers them out again. Each veem had its own badge, after which it was named. These could be hats of different colours and shapes (Klapmutsen, Blauwhoeden and others). Some took their name from where their workmen came from (Vriesseveem, Zeeuwse Veem and others).

name: Klaprozenweg
en: The klaproos (corn poppy), a plant of the poppy family.

name: Klarenburg
en: The former farm Karenburg on the Uitweg, demolished to build the Osdorp garden city. The l in the street name is therefore a mistake, but the burgomaster and aldermen later judged the difference not important enough to change the council decision.

name: Klaroenstraat
en: A leaf vegetable with red-flamed leaves, also known as amaranth or Chinese spinach.

name: Klaverbladstraat
en: The name refers to the leaf of the native edible plants of the pea family (clover).

name: Kleefkruidstraat
en: An edible plant of the bedstraw family (cleavers), which owes its stickiness to the many little hooks that cover it.

name: Kleiburg
en: A former farm in the Bijlmermeer, on the Weespertrekvaart.

name: Kleine Beerstraat
en: A constellation (the Dolphin).

name: Kleine Bickersstraat
en: These streets are on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr Johan Bicker (1591-1653), a shipbuilder and merchant, and a schepen (magistrate) and burgomaster of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets later laid out on the island automatically took the name of its founder.

name: Kleine Diestraat
en: The nearby waters of the Kleine Die and the Grote Die. 'Die' is a contraction of 'de' (the) and 'ie'. 'Ie' in turn is a Noord-Holland variant of 'aa', meaning water, which in Frisian-speaking areas is written 'ee'. The spelling 'IJ' is actually incorrect.

name: Kleine Houtstraat
en: Recalls the timber trade that used to be concentrated around the Haarlemmer Houttuinen. (The Grote Houtstraat was abolished in 1973.)

name: Kleine Pimpernelstraat
en: A perennial with edible leaves (salad burnet). Its round flower head carries small greenish-purple flowers.

name: Kleine Wetering
en: A wetering is a dug watercourse. Called Kleine (little) Wetering because of its size.

name: Kleine Wittenburgerstraat
en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

name: Kleine Zonneplein
en: The central body of the planetary system to which the Earth belongs (the sun).

name: Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen
en: Maria Johanna Kleine née Gartman (1818-1885), actress. As the first woman teacher at the Drama School she trained many actors and directors. Before it was named in 1915, the square was part of the Lijnbaansgracht and the Weteringschans.

name: Klieverink
en: Het Klieverink or Klievering, the name of a farm in Losser (Overijssel).

name: Klieverinkweg
en: Het Klieverink or Klievering, the name of a farm in Losser (Overijssel).

name: Klimopbrug
en: The climbing shrub (ivy).

name: Klimopstraatje
en: The climbing shrub (ivy).

name: Klimopweg
en: The climbing shrub (honeysuckle).

name: Klinkerweg
en: A metalworker who fastens iron parts together with rivets (a riveter). The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Klipperstraat
en: A long, narrow, fast-sailing three-master (a clipper).

name: Kloekhorststraat
en: The name of an old farm in the hamlet of Klein Dochteren, in Lochem (Gelderland).

name: Klokkenbergweg
en: The name of a hill near Nijmegen.

name: Klönne plein
en: The gasholder specialists August Klönne built the Westergasfabriek's new telescopic gasholder in 1902. The gasholder is the landmark of the former works site.

name: Kloveniersburgwal
en: The Kloveniersburgwal owes its name to a part of the civic guard called kloveniers, after the firearm its men used, a culverin.

name: Klovenierssteeg
en: After the Kloveniersdoelen, the meeting place of the old civic guard, where the Doelen Hotel now stands. The old civic guard originally used the crossbow, but in 1522 the guardsmen were given guns, or kloveren, and were named kloveniers after them. Until the end of the sixteenth century this burgwal was the outermost city moat. Before 1909 the alley was called Watersteeg, but this caused confusion with the Watersteeg by the Rokin.

name: Kneppelhoutstraat
en: Johannes Kneppelhout (1814-1885), pseudonym Klikspaan, writer of realistic, humorous sketches and stories.

name: Kneppelweg
en: The name of an old farm near Eefde (Gelderland).

name: Knokkestraat
en: A Belgian coastal town in the province of West Flanders (West-Vlaanderen).

name: Knollendamstraat
en: A village in the Zaan region. The street was originally named Derde Spaarndammerdwarsstraat (council decision of 30 March 1881).

name: KNSM-laan
en: The Koninklijke Nederlandsche Stoomboot-Maatschappij (Royal Netherlands Steamship Company), founded in 1856 and one of the largest Dutch shipping companies. It ran scheduled services to the West Indies, Central America, the west and north coasts of South America, the Levant and European ports, and also sailed between North and South America. In 1981 the KNSM was absorbed into the Koninklijke Nedlloyd group.

name: Koekjesbrug
en: There are four possible explanations for the name of this fixed bridge. It may be named after a popular biscuit (koekjes) seller who was pushed into the mud here by jostling youths. There also used to be a small cocoa mill here where cocoa biscuits were sold. The name may also go back to the market gardener Pannenkoek, who once owned land next to the bridge. A fourth possibility is that it is named after a policeman called Koek, who just before the bridge opened walked across it demonstratively after a quarrel with the ferryman. The ferryman is then said to have written on the bridge railing 'Deze brug is gedoopt Koekjesbrug' (this bridge is christened Koekjesbrug).

name: Koekoeksplein
en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

name: Koekoeksstraat
en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

name: Koen Limpergstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1908-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Haarlem.

name: Koenenkade
en: After a former resident.

name: Koerierstersplein
en: Girls who were active in the resistance in the Second World War. They handed out ration cards, false papers and money, and escorted Jewish children by bicycle or train. The street name is also a tribute to the couriers Miep Gies and Elly Voskuijl, who looked after the people hiding in the Secret Annex, among them Anne Frank.

name: Koestraat
en: The street ran along the cowshed (koestal) of the former Bethany convent, which stretched between this street and the Bethaniënstraat.

name: Koffieweg
en: The ground powder of roasted coffee beans. Coffee is handled in the port of Amsterdam.

name: Kofschipstraat
en: A round-built two-master with a broad stern (a kof), a slow sailer.

name: Kogeldistelstraat
en: An akkerdistel (creeping thistle) is a species of thistle.

name: Koggestraat
en: An old type of ship (the cog), after which the traditional Amsterdam Koggeschip is named. Before it was filled in in the nineteenth century, the water was part of the Kattengat.

name: Koivistokade
en: A large Russian oil port on the Baltic, today known as Primorsk. Koivisto, Finnish for 'birch grove', belonged to Finland from 1918 to 1944.

name: Kokmeeuwpad
en: A bird of the gull family (the black-headed gull).

name: Kokospalmhof
en: A kind of palm. The inside of the fruit of this palm looks like the face of a monkey, which in Portuguese is called 'coco'.

name: Kolbergbrug
en: Kolberg was the German name for the Polish Baltic port of Kołobrzeg. The names in the Houthavens are taken from places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Kolberggracht
en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

name: Kolfschotenstraat
en: An estate with a house near Scherpenzeel (Utrecht).

name: Kolibristraat
en: A very small tropical bird (the hummingbird).

name: Kolksluis
en: Bridge 302 lies in the Zeedijk over the Oudezijdskolk. The kolk of a lock is the chamber between its two pairs of gates. This was where the Oudezijds Voorburgwal and Achterburgwal drained into the IJ. The lock dates from the early fifteenth century.

name: Kolksteeg
en: This was where the Oudezijds Voorburgwal and Achterburgwal drained into the IJ. The lock dates from the early fifteenth century.

name: Kollenbergweg
en: The name of a hill east of Sittard (Limburg).

name: Kölpinstraat
en: The lake, the Kölpinsee, in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, northern Germany.

name: Kombuisweg
en: A kombuis is a ship's kitchen (galley).

name: Kometensingel
en: Small celestial bodies made of ice, gas and dust (comets).

name: Komijnstraat
en: A culinary herb (cumin) of the carrot family, native to the Middle East and India.

name: Kompasweg
en: Named after the navigational instrument (the compass).

name: Konijnenstraat
en: The rodent (the rabbit). The name arose from the trade in hides and skins carried on in this part of the city.

name: Koningin Wilhelminaplein
en: Wilhelmina Helena Pauline Maria, Princess of Orange-Nassau (1880-1962), daughter of King William III and Queen Emma, Queen of the Netherlands from 1898 to 1948.

name: Koninginneweg
en: Named after the queen of the time, Queen Emma.

name: Koningsbergenbrug
en: Koningsbergen was the Dutch name for Königsberg, now the Russian Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad. The names in the Houthavens are taken from places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Koningsbergengracht
en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

name: Koningslaan
en: After the kings of the House of Orange-Nassau.

name: Koningspalmplein
en: A kind of palm, considered by many the most beautiful palm in the world, hence the name royal palm.

name: Koningsplein
en: In the first years of the seventeenth century part of the Singel was called Koningsgracht, in honour of the allied King Henry IV of France. The square on this Koningsgracht was therefore named Koningsplein. The name Koningsgracht did not last, but the name of the square survived.

name: Koningsstraat
en: The streets lie on the old Lastage and were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

name: Koogstraat
en: The village of Koog aan de Zaan (Noord-Holland).

name: Koolpalmhof
en: A tree, also called cabbage tree or grass palm. Although its shape recalls a palm tree, it does not belong to the palm family. Its young, soft leaves used to be eaten instead of cabbage (kool).

name: Koolrabistraat
en: A vegetable (kohlrabi), probably from northern Europe, whose swollen stem is eaten.

name: Koopvaardersplantsoen
en: A collective name for former merchant ships.

name: Koornhorst
en: The name of a farm in Bergh-Montferland (Gelderland).

name: Koos Vorrinkweg
en: Jacobus Johannes Vorrink (1891-1955), teacher and politician, founder and leader of the AJC (Workers' Youth Federation), chairman of the SDAP and member of parliament. He played an active part in founding the Labour Party (PvdA).

name: Koperslagerij
en: The street lies on the site of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij. Koperslagerij (coppersmithy) refers to one of the workshops that were here.

name: Kopjachtplein
en: A sailing yacht with a high stem.

name: Koppelingpad
en: A machine part (the coupling or clutch).

name: Koppenburglaan
en: The name of an old farm in Lathum, in the municipality of Angerlo (Gelderland).

name: Kopraweg
en: Copra is the dried flesh of the coconut. Copra used to be made by traders who travelled from port to port in the Pacific.

name: Korenbloemstraat
en: The plant (cornflower), of the daisy family.

name: Korfbalstraat
en: Named after the korfball that was played here on the former sports ground.

name: Korianderstraat
en: A plant (coriander) of the carrot family, also called ketumbar, from the Mediterranean and the Middle East.

name: Kormelinkweg
en: An old farm south-west of Eibergen (Gelderland).

name: Korrelbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after the Korrel family, who ran a dairy shop at Eerste Jan Steenstraat 4 from 1947 to 1985. The bridge is also meant as a tribute to the many small shopkeepers of the 1950s, 60s and 70s who have disappeared, a time when you could still buy on tick.

name: Kors van Bennekombrug
en: Kors van Bennekom (Lodewijk, 13 July 1933 - Amsterdam, 4 October 2016) was an Amsterdam photographer and holder of the City of Amsterdam's Frans Banninck Cocq medal.

name: Korsjespoortsteeg
en: After the timber merchant Corsgen Jacobszoon, who in the fifteenth century had an orchard on the Singel, outside the city. The bridge over the Singel was therefore called the Korsjesbrug. Later the name passed to the gate and to the street leading to it. In the sixteenth century a new, longer alley was laid out in line with the first. Both were then called Korsjespoortsteeg, but the older one was given the prefix 'Korte' (short).

name: Korte 's-Gravesandestraat
en: Willem Jan van 's-Gravesande (1688-1742), professor of mathematics and astronomy at Leiden. He was the first follower of Newton in the Netherlands.

name: Korte Amstelstraat
en: The Korte Amstelstraat was made around 1670 by partly filling in the Nieuwe Achtergracht. A church was planned in the middle of the Amstelveld, so in 1669 a temporary church was built in a corner. The church was never built; the temporary church still stands.

name: Korte Blekersstraat
en: Called Korte Blekerspad before 1911, after the bleaching fields (blekerijen) there in the eighteenth century, along the Blekerssloot.

name: Korte De Wittenstraat
en: The brothers Cornelis de Witt (1623-1672), burgomaster of Dordrecht, and Johan de Witt (1625-1672), Grand Pensionary of Holland, both murdered by the mob in The Hague on a false accusation. One side of the quay was first called Maljapenkade.

name: Korte Dijkstraat
