en: The street was laid out as a dike at the end of the sixteenth century, after which the surroundings (long a marsh) were filled in with earth (aangeplempt).

name: Korte Distelstraat
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Korte Geuzenstraat
en: At first meant as a term of abuse (geuzen: beggars), but taken as a title of honour by the allied nobles in the fight against Spain. Later the fighting name of all opponents of Spain in the Eighty Years' War. The Korte Geuzenstraat was earlier part of the Geuzenstraat.

name: Korte Keizersdwarsstraat
en: On the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

name: Korte Keizersstraat
en: On the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

name: Korte Kolksteeg
en: Originally the water from the peatland behind, which came by way of the now filled-in Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal, flowed through this kolk (basin) into the Damrak. Around 1350 the Martelaarsgracht was dug and this outlet fell out of use. The kolk was filled in towards the end of the fifteenth century.

name: Korte Koningsdwarsstraat
en: On the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

name: Korte Koningsstraat
en: The streets lie on the old Lastage and were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

name: Korte Korsjespoortsteeg
en: After the timber merchant Corsgen Jacobszoon, who in the fifteenth century had an orchard on the Singel, outside the city. The bridge over the Singel was therefore called the Korsjesbrug. Later the name passed to the gate and to the street leading to it. In the sixteenth century a new, longer alley was laid out in line with the first. Both were then called Korsjespoortsteeg, but the older one was given the prefix 'Korte' (short).

name: Korte Leidsedwarsstraat
en: The city of Leiden.

name: Korte Lijnbaanssteeg
en: The ropewalks (lijnbanen) of the ropemakers. The Lijnbaanssteeg dates from the fifteenth century, when the Singel was the outermost canal. A ropemaker needed a fairly large site for his trade, which could only be found on the edge of the city. The ropewalks lay on the city side of the moat, so inside the rampart. The Lijnbaansgracht ran right round the city. It has since been filled in in several places and there has taken other names, such as Leidseplein, Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen, Frederiksplein, Maarten Jansz. Kosterstraat, Valckenierstraat and Plantage Muidergracht.

name: Korte Marnixkade
en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

name: Korte Marnixstraat
en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

name: Korte Meerhuizenstraat
en: A former country house on the Amstel, where the Amstelkade now meets the Amsteldijk, demolished around 1914. In the seventeenth century the poet Hendrik Laurensz Spiegel lived here.

name: Korte Niezel
en: The name is a corruption of liesdel, a del or dale where lies (irises) grow. It was marshy land north of the higher ground on which the Oude Kerk was built. In the second half of the fourteenth century this hollow was raised and built on. In one of the streets the old name Liesdel lived on. In later centuries it became Niesdel, and in the eighteenth century officially Niezel. In the sixteenth century a little street was laid out in line with it, which after various other names finally became Korte (short) Niezel, while the oldest part was given the prefix Lange (long).

name: Korte Ouderkerkerbrug
en: Named after the village of Ouderkerk aan de Amstel, to which these roads lead. The prefix Korte (short) dates from 1956, after the dike was cut through for the industrial estate.

name: Korte Ouderkerkerdijk
en: The name of the dike in which this bridge lies.

name: Korte Papaverweg
en: The plant (poppy), wild and cultivated, also called klaproos.

name: Korte Prinsengracht
en: After 'the princely title', meaning that of the Princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and the plainest in the character of its buildings. It was dug in the expansion of 1612 and built up from the Brouwersgracht to the Leidsegracht. In the expansion of 1658 this canal too was extended across the Amstel (as far as the Entrepotdok). The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for today's Noordermarkt never caught on with the citizens.

name: Korte Reguliersdwarsstraat
en: All these names recall the Reguliers monastery (of the Canons Regular), which stood from 1394 to 1532 outside the city gate of the time, where the Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now cross. The city gate, of which the Munttoren is a remnant, was once called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht then ended at that gate. Parts of it were filled in in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Before 1909 the Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

name: Korte Schimmelstraat
en: Hendrik Jan Schimmel (1825-1906), bank director, known as a novelist and playwright and also editor of 'De Gids'. These streets came into Amsterdam in 1896 with the names set by Nieuwer-Amstel, Van Speyckstraat and Van Speyckdwarsstraat, but were renamed in 1922, after the annexation of Sloten brought a second Van Speyckstraat within the city boundary.

name: Korte Spinhuissteeg
en: After the nearby Spinhuis (spinning house), a house of correction for women founded in 1596. From 1833 to 1941 the building housed the police headquarters.

name: Korte Stormsteeg
en: Because this part of the city lay on its outermost edge until the sixteenth century, it took the full brunt of storms. The alley's name probably arose from this.

name: Korte Tolstraat
en: After the toll gate (tol) on the corner of today's Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was levied from about 1780 until the area was annexed in 1896, for the upkeep of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 11 February 1886).

name: Korte Van Eeghenstraat
en: Like the Van Eeghenstraat, named after Christiaan Pieter van Eeghen (1816-1889), Amsterdam merchant, president-commissioner of De Nederlandsche Bank and the man behind the Vondelpark. When the street was laid out, the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel named it Heemskerkstraat on 7 February 1896 (after the minister J. Heemskerk Az.). After the annexation of 1896 the name was changed to Van Eeghendwarsstraat, because Amsterdam already had a Van Heemskerckstraat (council decision of 13 June 1896). The residents and owners, however, asked for the name to be changed: in their view 'dwarsstraat' (cross street) lowered the tone. The city council then set the present name.

name: Korte Vogelstraat
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Korte Water
en: A historical name from old Sloten/Osdorp. According to Jan Dou's map of 1687, the Korte Water lay south of the Ookmeertje.

name: Korte Zoutkeetsgracht
en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the salt works (zoutketen) stood on both sides of this canal. These were sheds where coarse salt was refined for household use.

name: Kortenaerstraat
en: Egbert M. Kortenaer, lieutenant-admiral, who took part in the naval battles of Ter Heijde (1653) and the Sound (1658). He was killed in 1665 in the Battle of Lowestoft against the English.

name: Kortenakenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Korteweghof
en: Diederik Johannes Korteweg (1848-1941), mathematician and astronomer, professor in Amsterdam, who edited the complete works of Christiaan Huygens.

name: Kortrijk
en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

name: Kortvoort
en: A hamlet and house near Oss (Noord-Brabant). A voort or voorde is a ford.

name: Kortwoudepad
en: Kortwoude is a hamlet in the Dutch province of Friesland, in the municipality of Achtkarspelen.

name: Kostverlorenstraat
en: After the Kostverlorenwetering, dug in 1413 to give a shorter waterway to the Haarlem and Leiden lakes. According to some, the name Kostverloren (cost lost) comes from the heavy legal costs of this channel, which was a bone of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609. The name Kostverloren occurs in several places in the Netherlands.

name: Kostverlorenvaart
en: After the Kostverlorenwetering, dug in 1413 to give a shorter waterway to the Haarlem and Leiden lakes. According to some, the name Kostverloren (cost lost) comes from the heavy legal costs of this channel, which was a bone of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609. The name Kostverloren occurs in several places in the Netherlands.

name: Kotteraarstraat
en: The metalworker who works with the kotter, a tool for reaming holes and making them cylindrical (a borer). The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Kotterspad
en: A fast-sailing ship (cutter), used among other things for coastal shipping and fishing. Derived from the English 'to cut'.

name: Kousenbandstraat
en: A pod up to 90 centimetres long (yardlong bean), probably from tropical Africa, grown in South America and tropical Asia.

name: Kouterstraat
en: A kouter is the blade of a plough (coulter).

name: Kouwenoord
en: The name of several farms, among them one in Kesteren (Gelderland).

name: Kouwenoordweg
en: The name of several farms, among them one in Kesteren (Gelderland).

name: Koxhorn
en: An old country estate in Wassenaar (Zuid-Holland).

name: Kraaiennest
en: The name of a house and fort in Breukelen-Sint Pieter (Utrecht) and of a farm in Harmelen (Utrecht).

name: Kraaiennestpad
en: The name of a house and fort in Breukelen-Sint Pieter (Utrecht) and of a farm in Harmelen (Utrecht).

name: Kraaienplein
en: The bird (the crow).

name: Kraailookstraat
en: A plant, a rare wild garlic (crow garlic).

name: Kraaipanstraat
en: The place in the Transvaal (South Africa) where fighting against the British took place in the Boer War (1899-1902).

name: Kraandrijverstraat
en: The crane driver or crane operator works the crane that moves loads horizontally and vertically. The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Kraansluis
en: The name of this fixed bridge recalls the Grote Kraan (great crane), which stood on the IJ from 1643 to 1841 and was used to step masts into ships and to unload blocks of stone and guns.

name: Kraanspoor
en: The name comes from the 1952 concrete structure (a crane track) on which the offices are built. Two large cranes used to stand here, hoisting cargo from the land onto the ships.

name: Krabbendamstraat
en: A village in the Kop van Noord-Holland (the northern tip of Noord-Holland).

name: Kraijenhoffstraat
en: Cornelis R.Th. Baron van Kraijenhoff (1758-1840), hydraulic engineer and Minister of War under King Louis Napoleon, who strengthened the fortifications around the city in 1815.

name: Kramatplantsoen
en: A suburb of Batavia (now Jakarta). Kramat is an Islamic term for something sacred (a grave, animal or object) to which miraculous power is attributed.

name: Kramatweg
en: A suburb of Batavia (now Jakarta). Kramat is an Islamic term for something sacred (a grave, animal or object) to which miraculous power is attributed.

name: Krammerstraat
en: The waterway between Overflakkee and Sint Philipsland.

name: Kranenburg
en: A former knightly manor on the Rottemeren, in Bleiswijk.

name: Krasseurstraat
en: A workman in a construction shop who scribes the working drawings onto metal plates. The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Kratontuin
en: After the fortified, walled palace of Javanese rulers, the centre of political power and culture, which often formed a city within a city. Each dynasty founded a new kraton, where sometimes several thousand people lived. The most famous kraton on Java is that of Yogyakarta, founded in 1757.

name: Kreeftstraat
en: A constellation (Cancer, the Crab), also a sign of the zodiac.

name: Krelis Louwenstraat
en: A comedy by Pieter Langendijk, often performed with success.

name: Kretaweg
en: A Greek island (Crete).

name: Kribbestraat
en: A stone dam built across part of a river to guide the current (a groyne).

name: Krijn Breurstraat
en: Krijn Martinus Breur (1917-1943), resistance fighter, born in Dordrecht, executed by firing squad in Leusden.

name: Krijn Taconiskade
en: Photojournalist (1918-1979), who during the Second World War joined the photographers' group 'De Ondergedoken Camera' (the camera in hiding), which photographed clandestinely during the Hunger Winter. After the liberation he worked in international photojournalism, including a reportage on a famine in Haiti. He was a member of the famous photographers' collective Magnum.

name: Krijtbergbrug
en: Named after the nearby Krijtberg, or St Francis Xavier church (sometimes also called the Rijtjeskerk), on the Singel. Consecrated in 1883, the church replaced the former clandestine church in the house de Crijtberg, served by the Jesuits.

name: Krimpertplein
en: The name of a farm on the Verwolde estate near Laren (Gelderland).

name: Krom Boomssloot
en: A side canal of the Recht Boomssloot, hence the prefix krom (crooked).

name: Krom Boomssloot
en: Named after the sixteenth-century master shipbuilder Cornelis Pietersz. Boom. To connect his yard on the Lastage with the surrounding water he had a canal and a side canal dug.

name: Krombekstraat
en: One of the few surviving varieties of the Dutch white bean.

name: Kromme Distelstraat
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Kromme Leimuidenstraat
en: A village between the Westeinder Plassen and the Braassemermeer in Zuid-Holland. The prefix Kromme (crooked) refers to the shape of the street.

name: Kromme Palmstraat
en: The tree (palm). The Palmgracht was filled in in 1895.

name: Kromme Waal
en: The walen were once (early seventeenth century) inlets of the IJ on the old side (Oude Waal) and the new side (Nieuwe Waal), where seagoing ships were laid up in winter. The Oude Waal silted up and became too shallow, and the Waalseiland was built up there in 1646. The quay on the city side kept the names Oude Waal and Kromme Waal (after its shape); on the Waalseiland came the names Binnenkant and Buitenkant (now Prins Hendrikkade). The Nieuwe Waal disappeared when the Westelijk Entrepotdok was built. Before 1912 the Waalsteeg was called Schippersstraatje; the name was changed because of confusion with the Schippersstraat.

name: Kromme-Mijdrechtstraat
en: The river in Zuid-Holland. Where it joins the Drecht, the Amstel begins. That the street is curved is a coincidence, or a joke by whoever named it.

name: Krommehoekstraat
en: Krommehoek, the name of a vanished farm.

name: Krommeniestraat
en: The village in the Zaan region. Because of building and demolition the street was shortened in 1978 and part of it was added to the Spaarndammerplantsoen.

name: Krommertstraat
en: The winding little canal the Krommert, already partly filled in before 1930. The rest was filled in in the 1950s.

name: Kromwijkdreef
en: The name of several patrician houses, among them ones in Tienhoven (Utrecht) and Maarsseveen (Utrecht).

name: Kronstadtbrug
en: Kronstadt is a Russian port on the Gulf of Finland near Saint Petersburg. The names in the Houthavens are taken from places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Kroonweg
en: The currency (crown) of Sweden, Denmark, Norway and the Czech Republic.

name: Krooswijkhof
en: Krooswijk or Crooswijk is a former sixteenth-century country estate on the Rotte, now a district of Rotterdam by the Crooswijk cemetery. This court was laid out, with other streets, on the route once planned for the Rotterdamseweg.

name: Krootstraat
en: The kroot or beetroot is a root crop, of the same family as the sugar beet.

name: Kropaarstraat
en: A grass (cock's-foot) found in Europe, Asia and North Africa.

name: Krugerplein
en: Johannes Stephanus Paulus Kruger, better known as Paul Kruger (1825-1904), president of the Transvaal from 1883. He sought support in Europe for his country's struggle against British rule, in vain, and died in Switzerland.

name: Krugerstraat
en: Johannes Stephanus Paulus Kruger, better known as Paul Kruger (1825-1904), president of the Transvaal from 1883. He sought support in Europe for his country's struggle against British rule, in vain, and died in Switzerland.

name: Kruisbessenstraat
en: The fruit of the shrub of the same name (gooseberry).

name: Kruisherenpad
en: In the early years of the garden city (around 1955) this path was the regular route of the fathers of the Roman Catholic church to their presbytery. They belonged to the order of the Crosiers (Kruisheren), so the path soon got this name.

name: Kruislaan
en: After its position: the road crosses (kruist) the Middenweg.

name: Kruitberg
en: An old patrician house near Santpoort (Noord-Holland), which in the seventeenth century belonged to Stadtholder William III.

name: Kruitberghof
en: An old patrician house near Santpoort (Noord-Holland), which in the seventeenth century belonged to Stadtholder William III.

name: Kruitbergstraat
en: An old patrician house near Santpoort (Noord-Holland), which in the seventeenth century belonged to Stadtholder William III.

name: Kruithuisstraat
en: A powder house (kruithuis) was built on this site in the seventeenth century. After some decades of use it was pulled down because the city's buildings were closing in on it.

name: Kruldistelstraat
en: An akkerdistel (creeping thistle) is a species of thistle.

name: Krulslaplantsoen
en: A variety of ordinary head lettuce with slightly curled leaves.

name: Kruysweerstraat
en: A former country house on the Amstel.

name: ks. Ibisplantsoen
en: The crane ship Ibis, built in 1982 at the NSM yard (the successor of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij). This crane ship, with a lifting capacity of 1600 tonnes, was used for hydraulic engineering works in the Persian Gulf.

name: ks. Ibisweg
en: The crane ship Ibis, built in 1982 at the NSM yard (the successor of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij) for Ballast-Nedam. This crane ship, with a lifting capacity of 1600 tonnes, was used for hydraulic engineering works in the Persian Gulf.

name: Kuilsenhofweg
en: The name of a farm at Beek near Nijmegen (Gelderland).

name: Kuinderstraat
en: A small river in Friesland, which once flowed into the IJsselmeer at Kuinre.

name: Kuiperbergweg
en: A hill near Ootmarsum, the top of the eastern push moraine of Overijssel.

name: Kuiperssteeg
en: After the cooperage (kuiperij) here in the seventeenth century. Before that the alley appears as St. Clarensteeg, after the former St Clare convent.

name: Kuipersstraat
en: Named after the former Kuiperspad, which already existed in the seventeenth century and on which the street was laid out. Until 1896 the street belonged, under the same name, to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

name: Kurk
en: A corrupted spelling of the Irish port of Cork, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Kustvaarderstraat
en: A ship built for coastal trade, usually of 500 tonnes at most, better known as a coaster.

name: Kwadijkerstraat
en: The village of Kwadijk, north of Purmerend.

name: Kwadrantweg
en: An instrument for measuring the altitude of celestial bodies, used in navigation (the quadrant).

name: Kwakersplein
en: After the former Kwakerspoel and Kwakerseiland, names first recorded here around 1680. The name probably comes from the sect of the Quakers (kwakers). Followers of this sect, whose principles were first preached in Amsterdam around 1656, were expelled from the city, so they met at this remote spot outside the city boundary. In 1674 they were allowed to meet in a house on the Keizersgracht. The name de Bijkerk (the side church), borne by one of the mills that stood here, also supports this explanation. Another explanation is the old word 'kwakel', the name for a high, narrow wooden bridge that still survives in Noord-Holland. The Kwakerseiland would then have been linked to the surrounding land by little wooden bridges of this kind.

name: Kwakersstraat
en: After the former Kwakerspoel and Kwakerseiland, names first recorded here around 1680. The name probably comes from the sect of the Quakers (kwakers). Followers of this sect, whose principles were first preached in Amsterdam around 1656, were expelled from the city, so they met at this remote spot outside the city boundary. In 1674 they were allowed to meet in a house on the Keizersgracht. The name de Bijkerk (the side church), borne by one of the mills that stood here, also supports this explanation. Another explanation is the old word 'kwakel', the name for a high, narrow wooden bridge that still survives in Noord-Holland. The Kwakerseiland would then have been linked to the surrounding land by little wooden bridges of this kind.

name: Kwartelstraat
en: A bird of the fowl family (the quail).

name: Kwartiermeesterstraat
en: An officer responsible for quarters and supplies (the quartermaster).

name: Kwekerijlaan
en: A place where plants are grown (a nursery). The street lies on the former De Bongerd allotment complex.

name: Kwelderweg
en: Vegetated land built up outside the dike, which usually no longer floods at high water (a salt marsh).

name: Kwintsheulstraat
en: A village in the Westland (Zuid-Holland).

name: L. van Sonsbeeckstraat
en: Lodewijk Hendrik van Sonsbeeck (1831-1903), burgomaster of Sloten from 1864 to 1868, and then of Vlagtwedde.

name: L.H. Sarlouisbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after Louis Hartog Sarlouis (1884-1942), founder of the Jewish secondary school (H.B.S.) and chief rabbi of Amsterdam from 1936 to 1942, the year he was deported to Auschwitz, where he died.

name: L.J.M. Beelstraat
en: Louis Jozef Maria Beel (1902-1977), statesman of the KVP (Catholic People's Party). In 1945 he became Minister of the Interior and in 1946 prime minister. From 1951 to 1956 he was again Minister of the Interior, and then prime minister once more in 1958-1959. He was also, among other things, a Minister of State.

name: La Guardiaweg
en: The name of one of New York's airports.

name: La Meye
en: A mountain peak in France (La Meije), 3987 metres high.

name: Laagte Kadijk
en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

name: Laan der Hesperiden
en: Figures from Greek mythology: seven nymphs who guard the tree with the golden apples in the land of Hesperia.

name: Laan van Spartaan
en: The grounds of the Amsterdam football club VVA/Spartaan, founded in 1901, are on this avenue.

name: Laan van Vlaanderen
en: The usual name for the Dutch-speaking part of Belgium, north of the language border (Flanders). Named after the former county, which takes its name from a Carolingian district, the pagus Flandrensis.

name: Laanweg
en: Originally this was a tree-lined road (laan). When the Buiksloterham was drained in 1851, three roads were made here: the 'weg' (along the canal), the 'dijk' (the former sea dike) and this 'laan'. The Laanweg disappeared around 1970 when its buildings were demolished and this little polder was raised. The old name has now been given to part of the service road of the Ranonkelkade and the Meidoornweg.

name: Laarderhoogtweg
en: The name of a hill near Laren (Noord-Holland).

name: Laboratoriumstraat
en: After the nearby Aeronautical Laboratory (Luchtvaartlaboratorium), where scientific experiments and observations are made for aviation.

name: Ladogameerhof
en: Lake Ladoga (Ladozhskoye ozero), in northern Russia near the Finnish border.

name: Laing's Nekstraat
en: A mountain pass in South Africa, also called Langenek, known for Joubert's victory over the British in the First Boer War. The oldest part of the street (by the Ringvaart) has had various names over the years. Before 1896 it was Tweede Ringkadedwarsstraat, as named by Nieuwer-Amstel. By council decision of 16 October 1901 that name was changed to Meerstraat, and in 1912 this stretch was added to the Laing's Nekstraat.

name: Lakenhalstraat
en: The Stedelijk Museum De Lakenhal in Leiden, in a 1640 building by the city architect Arent van 's-Gravesande (originally the cloth hall). It opened as a museum in 1874 and is known for its historical collection of silver, glass, pewter and tiles, and for paintings by famous people of Leiden.

name: Lamarckhof
en: Jean de Monet de Lamarck (1744-1827), French biologist, who set out the first modern theory of evolution. A forerunner of Darwin.

name: Lambert Rimastraat
en: Lambert Gregoire Rima (1907-1943), resistance fighter, born in The Hague, executed by firing squad in Leusden. Rima was connected with the clandestine paper 'Het Parool'.

name: Lamonggracht
en: A river on the Indonesian island of Java.

name: Lampenistenstraat
en: A trade name: someone responsible for lighting and maintaining lamps (a lamplighter), for example on board a ship or at a station.

name: Lampongstraat
en: Under Dutch rule over Indonesia this was a residency in the south of Sumatra.

name: Land van Cocagneplein
en: Luilekkerland (the land of Cockaigne): a medieval tale of a land with food and drink in abundance, where no one has to work.

name: Landbouwstraat
en: The growing of plant products for human and animal use (agriculture).

name: Landskroon
en: A former seventeenth-century country house with a hunting lodge and falconry, on the Vecht near Muiden. It was demolished long ago; a farm of the same name now stands on the site.

name: Landsmeerderdijk
en: After the village of Landsmeer. Until 1966 this part of the Waterland sea dike belonged to the municipality of Landsmeer.

name: Landsteinerstraat
en: Karl Landsteiner (1868-1943), Austrian, later American, pathologist, who discovered the blood groups and the rhesus factor, which made blood transfusion possible. He won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1930.

name: Langbroekdreef
en: A village in the province of Utrecht.

name: Langbroekpad
en: A village in the province of Utrecht.

name: Lange Distelstraat
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Lange Leidsedwarsstraat
en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date from the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got its name because it led to the Leidsepoort (Leiden gate). It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

name: Lange Niezel
en: The name is a corruption of liesdel, a del or dale where lies (irises) grow. It was marshy land north of the higher ground on which the Oude Kerk was built. In the second half of the fourteenth century this hollow was raised and built on. In one of the streets the old name Liesdel lived on. In later centuries it became Niesdel, and in the eighteenth century officially Niezel. In the sixteenth century a little street was laid out in line with it, which after various other names finally became Korte (short) Niezel, while the oldest part was given the prefix Lange (long).

name: Lange Stammerdijk
en: The road came over under this name from the municipality of Weesperkarspel.

name: Lange Vogelstraat
en: The streets lie in the district where the streets are named after birds (vogels). The little neighbourhood of these twelve streets is sometimes called the Vogeldorp (bird village).

name: Lange Vonder
en: Named after a long wooden bridge near Broek in Waterland over the arm of the Kerk Ee river leading to the Havenrak. A vonder is a narrow wooden crossing over water.

name: Langebrugsteeg
en: Compared with the other streets laid out here between the canals, this one was exceptionally long.

name: Langestraat
en: Compared with the other streets laid out here between the canals, this one was exceptionally long.

name: Langkatstraat
en: A region on the east coast of the island of Sumatra (Indonesia).

name: Langsom
en: The name of a former mill ditch in the Riekerpolder.

name: Langswater
en: An old Rijnland name, found on Floris Balthasar van Berckenrode's map of 1610. Langswater was a drainage ditch from old Osdorp to the IJ, level with Spieringhorn.

name: Lanseloetstraat
en: One of the main characters of the abel spel (secular play) 'Lanseloet van Denemerken' ('Lanseloet ende Sanderijn', from about 1400).

name: Lanzarotestraat
en: A Spanish island off the north-west coast of Africa, one of the Canary Islands.

name: Laplacestraat
en: Pierre-Simon, Marquis de Laplace (1749-1827), French mathematician and astronomer, who put forward the hypothesis that the solar system formed from a rotating ball of gas.

name: Larikslaan
en: A tree of the conifer group (larch) that sheds its needles in winter. In the Netherlands the Japanese variety is the most common.

name: Lascarpad
en: Lascar is the most active stratovolcano in the Andes (in Chile), 5,592 m high.

name: Lassusstraat
en: Orlando di Lasso (1532-1594), in French Roland de Lassus, born in Hainaut, choirmaster in Rome, Antwerp and Munich, who wrote sacred and secular music. He is called the prince of music.

name: Lastageweg
en: The Lastage was originally the land built up by the sea outside the sea dike, stretching between the Nieuwmarkt and the later Oudeschans. The name appears as early as 1342 and remained in use until the eighteenth century. At first shipyards, warehouses and ropewalks were set up here, and everything needed for ballasting, unloading and loading ships (lasten) was made here. In the second half of the sixteenth century houses and streets began to be built, and in 1593 the area officially came within the city. The Lastageweg was named in 1931 after the slum clearance of the Jonker and Ridder neighbourhood, and was made by widening the Tweede Jonkerdwarsstraat and the Tweede Ridderdwarsstraat.

name: Latexweg
en: A tropical product, the raw material of rubber, that was handled in the port of Amsterdam.

name: Latherusstraat
en: The little climbing plant, also called lathyrus (sweet pea), of the pea family.

name: Lau Mazirelbrug
en: Laura Carola Mazirel (1907-1974), lawyer and solicitor in Amsterdam, who stood up for groups isolated in society: before the Second World War German refugees, after the war Gypsies and homosexuals. During the war she was involved both with the crèche of the Hollandsche Schouwburg, where the Jewish population was gathered before deportation, and with the resistance group around Gerrit van der Veen.

name: Lau Mazirelstraat
en: Laura Carola Mazirel (1907-1974), lawyer and solicitor in Amsterdam, who stood up for groups isolated in society: before the Second World War German refugees, after the war Gypsies and homosexuals. During the war she was involved both with the crèche of the Hollandsche Schouwburg, where the Jewish population was gathered before deportation, and with the resistance group around Gerrit van der Veen.

name: Lauernessestraat
en: After the 1840 novel by Bosboom-Toussaint, 'Het huis Lauernesse' (the house of Lauernesse).

name: Lauriergracht
en: The southern European ornamental tree (the laurel).

name: Laurierstraat
en: The southern European ornamental tree (laurel). (The canal was dug on the site of the old Kaatsbaanpad.)

name: Lavendelstraat
en: A subshrub, an aromatic herb (lavender) used in the perfume industry.

name: Lavoisierstraat
en: Antoine L. Lavoisier (1743-1794), French chemist and one of the founders of modern chemistry.

name: Le Mairegracht
en: Jacob le Maire (1585-1616), explorer, who with Willem Schouten discovered the strait at the southern tip of South America named after him, and the cape they called Cape Horn, after Schouten's home town of Hoorn. A Le Mairestraat had been planned and named elsewhere on 20 November 1878, but that council decision was withdrawn on 19 August 1905.

name: Le Mairekade
en: Jacob le Maire (1585-1616), explorer, who discovered the strait at the southern tip of South America named after him, and the cape, which he called Cape Horn after his home town of Hoorn. A Le Mairestraat had been planned and named elsewhere on 20 November 1878, but that council decision was withdrawn on 19 August 1905.

name: Le Mairestraat
en: Jacob le Maire (1585-1616), explorer, who discovered the strait at the southern tip of South America named after him, and the cape, which he called Cape Horn after his home town of Hoorn. A Le Mairestraat had been planned and named elsewhere on 20 November 1878, but that council decision was withdrawn on 19 August 1905.

name: Le Tourmalet
en: A mountain peak in France (the Col du Tourmalet), 2114 metres high.

name: Lederambachtstraat
en: Land near the Biesbosch drowned in the St Elizabeth's flood of 1421.

name: Lee Millerbrug
en: Lee Miller (1907-1977) was an American photographer and model, known as a war correspondent in the Second World War. She went on to become a renowned fashion and art photographer.

name: Leen Jongewaardkade
en: Leendert (Leen) Jongewaard (Amsterdam, 30 March 1927 - Nice, 4 June 1996) was a Dutch actor and singer, known above all for his parts in the television series Ja zuster, nee zuster, 't Schaep met de 5 pooten and Citroentje met suiker, and for his performances of songs such as In een rijtuigje, Op een mooie Pinksterdag and M'n opa.

name: Leendert Schijveschuurderstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1917-1941), involved in many clandestine activities and a participant in the February Strike of 1941.

name: Leendert Valstarhof
en: Resistance fighter (1896-1942), born in Delft, died in the Buchenwald concentration camp (Germany).

name: Leenhofstraat
en: Ferdinand Leenhoff (1841-1914), sculptor, whose works include the statue of Thorbecke (1876) on the Thorbeckeplein and that of Jan Pieterszoon Coen in Hoorn. He spent most of his life in France, where much of his sculpture is found.

name: Leerdamhof
en: A town on the Linge in Zuid-Holland, known above all for its glass industry.

name: Leeuwarderweg
en: The arterial road north, leading over the Afsluitdijk to Leeuwarden. Before 1936 the Leeuwarderweg was part of the Buiksloterdijk. The Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg was built when the IJ tunnel was completed.

name: Leeuwendalersweg
en: A pastoral play by Vondel ('Leeuwendalers'), written to celebrate the peace with Spain and performed in the Amsterdam Schouwburg in 1648.

name: Leeuwenhoekstraat
en: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (1632-1723), correspondent of the Royal Society, who with the microscopes he built himself was the first to see bacteria.

name: Leeuwenputbrug
en: In the first half of the seventeenth century the gallows field was embellished with a stone well with three tall columns topped by lions' heads, as though what took place there were a venerable ceremony. In time the remains of the bodies fell into the well. When the IJ froze over in winter, which then happened regularly, people crossed the ice on skates or sledges to take a look. The fun on the ice around the gallows well could take bizarre forms, as a print by Reinier Vinkeles from around 1780 shows. Close to the well stand two busy stalls selling snacks and hot drinks. A man relieves himself against the well, apparently to show his disgust. Onlookers, among them a father explaining things to his children, cheerfully discuss everything there is to see. It is known that bodies stayed hanging or lying on the gallows field for years, and the idling visitors could gape at every stage of decay. Swarms of crows and countless rats picked the skeletons clean.

name: Leeuwenwerf
en: The former shipyard 'De Gouden Leeuw' (the golden lion), which lay here along the canal.

name: Leeuwerikstraat
en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

name: Leghornstraat
en: A white breed of chicken that makes up a large part of the Dutch poultry stock. Leghorn is the English name for Livorno, and the breed is indeed of Italian origin.

name: Legmeerplein
en: A former peat lake, now a polder between Aalsmeer and Amstelveen, drained in 1874.

name: Legmeerstraat
en: A former peat lake, now a polder between Aalsmeer and Amstelveen, drained in 1874.

name: Leibnizstraat
en: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1646-1716), German philosopher and statesman, an important seventeenth-century thinker, who tried to bring the scholars of all countries into contact with one another. As a natural philosopher he invented the differential calculus independently of Newton.

name: Leidekkerssteeg
en: After a former resident, Heinrich de Leydecker, who lived here in 1550. Before that the alley appears as Graefmakerssteeg, which suggests that a gravedigger once lived here too.

name: Leidsebrug
en: The city of Leiden.

name: Leidsegracht
en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date from the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got its name because it led to the Leidsepoort (Leiden gate). It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

name: Leidsekade
en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date from the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got its name because it led to the Leidsepoort (Leiden gate). It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

name: Leidsekruisstraat
en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date from the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got its name because it led to the Leidsepoort (Leiden gate). It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

name: Leidseplein
en: The city of Leiden.

name: Leidsestraat
en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date from the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got its name because it led to the Leidsepoort (Leiden gate). It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

name: Leiduinstraat
en: An estate near Heemstede (Noord-Holland).

name: Leimuidenstraat
en: A village between the Westeinder Plassen and the Braassemermeer in Zuid-Holland. The prefix Kromme (crooked) refers to the shape of the street.

name: Lekkeresluis
en: There used to be stalls by this fixed bridge where, among other things, a 'pannenkoek van de Lekkeresluis' (pancake of the tasty lock) was baked.

name: Leksmondhof
en: The village of Lexmond or Leksmond on the Lek (Zuid-Holland), already mentioned in the twelfth century.

name: Lekstraat
en: The part of the Rhine between Wijk bij Duurstede and Krimpen.

name: Leliegracht
en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

name: Leliendaalstraat
en: Named after the historical ship the Leliëndaal, which carried enslaved people in the eighteenth century.

name: Leliesluis
en: The name of this fixed bridge comes from the canal it lies on. That canal in turn is named after the Oude Leliestraat, mentioned as early as 1560, which took its name from the house 'In de Witte Lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel by the Torensluis.

name: Lemelerbergweg
en: The name of a hill near Lemele (Overijssel).

name: Lemoenpad
en: The gear by which a horse was hitched to a caravan (the shafts). The street name refers to the caravan site here.

name: Lentestraat
en: The spring season (lente). The street came in 1966, under the name Merwedestraat, from the then abolished municipality of Weesperkarspel (council decision of Weesperkarspel, 29 November 1957).

name: Leo Frijdahof
en: Resistance fighter (1923-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Bloemendaal.

name: Leo Heijdenrijkstraat
en: Leonardus Justinus Heijdenrijk (1932-1999) was a Dutch architect.

name: Leo Hornstraat
en: Leopold Silvain Horn (1916-1995), football referee, who officiated at international level between 1951 and 1966. Horn was Jewish and a resistance fighter in the Second World War, and later a successful businessman.

name: Leo Smitstraat
en: Dutch composer of Portuguese-Jewish descent (1900-1943), who studied at the Amsterdam Conservatory. He left a small but rich body of work, influenced by Ravel and Stravinsky. On 27 April 1943 he was put on a transport to the Sobibor extermination camp, where he was murdered on 30 April.

name: Leonard Bernsteinstraat
en: American conductor and composer (1917-1989), who became famous for his musicals, among them 'West Side Story'. He also composed operas, symphonies and concertos, and conducted all the great orchestras of the world.

name: Leonard Springerbrug
en: Leonard Antonij Springer (Amsterdam, 24 January 1855 - Haarlem, 28 September 1940) was a landscape architect who designed and laid out more than 600 gardens large and small, city parks, country estates and cemeteries. In Amsterdam they include the Oosterpark, part of Park Frankendael and De Nieuwe Ooster cemetery.

name: Leonardostraat
en: Leonardo da Vinci (1452-1519), Italian painter, sculptor and architect, an artist of great genius, who painted 'The Last Supper' and the 'Mona Lisa'.

name: Leopoldstraat
en: Jan Hendrik Leopold (1865-1925), poet and writer of literary studies, whose verse bears witness to great loneliness.

name: Lepelkruisstraat
en: Nothing certain can be said about the origin of the name; it probably comes from a gable stone. The Lepelstraat was originally a short side street of the Weesperstraat and officially the Weesperdwarsstraat until the middle of the eighteenth century. At the end of the nineteenth century the Lepelstraat was extended in both directions over the sites of the Veemarkt and the Stadswerf. Because of new building along the Weesperstraat only the western part remains. The eastern part was renamed Lepelkruisstraat and Korte Lepelstraat in 1980.

name: Lepelstraat
en: Nothing certain can be said about the origin of the name; it probably comes from a gable stone. The Lepelstraat was originally a short side street of the Weesperstraat and officially the Weesperdwarsstraat until the middle of the eighteenth century. At the end of the nineteenth century the Lepelstraat was extended in both directions over the sites of the Veemarkt and the Stadswerf. Because of new building along the Weesperstraat only the western part remains. The eastern part was renamed Lepelkruisstraat and Korte Lepelstraat in 1980.

name: Lesbosstraat
en: A Greek island in the Aegean Sea, off the coast of Turkey.

name: Letelierstraat
en: Orlando Letelier (1932-1976), Chilean foreign minister under President Allende. He was imprisoned in Pinochet's coup of 1973. After his release he led the Chileans in exile, and his contacts with influential politicians in the United States made him a danger to the regime. He was murdered by the Chilean secret police.

name: Leusdenhof
en: A municipality in the province of Utrecht, known for the De Treek estate and the Leusderheide.

name: Leuvenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Levantkade
en: After the region of the Levant (the coasts of Asia Minor, Syria, Egypt, Lebanon and Israel), to which the former KNSM ran a scheduled service.

name: Levantplein
en: After the region of the Levant (the coasts of Asia Minor, Syria, Egypt, Lebanon and Israel), to which the former KNSM ran a scheduled service.

name: Lex Althoffstraat
en: Resistance hero and journalist (1904-1941), born in Haarlem, executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

name: Lex van Deldenbrug
en: Alexander Zwaap (1919-1988), composer. Van Delden was the name he used from his time in hiding and in the resistance. In 1982 he received the City of Amsterdam's Pin of Merit.

name: Lia Doranastraat
en: Lia Dorana, pseudonym of Beppy van Werven (1918-2010), was a Dutch cabaret artist, singer and actress.

name: Libau-eiland
en: The old German name for Liepāja, now a Latvian port, from which much timber used to be shipped to Amsterdam.

name: Lichterstraat
en: An inland vessel without its own propulsion, used for carrying goods (a lighter).

name: Lidewijdepad
en: A novel by Busken Huet from 1868.

name: Lidostraat
en: A long island in the Venetian lagoon, where large-scale renovation took place around 2012.

name: Liefdesbruggetje
en: This bridge is called the Liefdesbruggetje (little bridge of love) because it is a favourite spot for wedding photos. From here you can look out over the park and the pond without seeing any buildings.

name: Liendenhof
en: Named after the village near Elst in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

name: Liergouw
en: The name de Liere already occurs here in the seventeenth century, as a map by Gerrit Drogeham shows. Lier is a water name, also found in the Westland and south of Zwolle, among other places. Its precise meaning is unknown.

name: Lies Bakhuyzenlaan
en: Lies Bakhuyzen (1923-1997), secretary of the Sloten-Oud Osdorp village council, worked for the Dutch Reformed congregation and for almost twenty years was a member of the Order of St John, which offers spiritual support to people in need. The little lane, running from the Sloterweg to the Ringvaartdijk, is close to her former home.

name: Liesdelsluis
en: The Liesdel in the name of this fixed bridge means 'low land overgrown with irises'.

name: Lieven de Keystraat
en: Flemish architect (1560-1627), in Haarlem from 1591, whose buildings include the Vleeshal (meat hall) and the Waag (weigh house) in Haarlem.

name: Lieven Keersemakerstraat
en: A Beggar leader (1528-1613) in the revolt against Spanish rule in Veere.

name: Ligusterhof
en: A plant genus (privet) of the olive family, much used in hedges. Wild privet is native to the Netherlands.

name: Lijnbaansbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after the Lijnbaanssteeg, in which it lies. The alley dates from the fifteenth century, when the Singel was the outermost canal and the ropewalks (lijnbanen) of the ropemakers were here, on a kind of industrial estate.

name: Lijnbaansgracht
en: The ropewalks (lijnbanen) of the ropemakers. The Lijnbaanssteeg dates from the fifteenth century, when the Singel was the outermost canal. A ropemaker needed a fairly large site for his trade, which could only be found on the edge of the city. The ropewalks lay on the city side of the moat, so inside the rampart. The Lijnbaansgracht ran right round the city. It has since been filled in in several places and there has taken other names, such as Leidseplein, Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen, Frederiksplein, Maarten Jansz. Kosterstraat, Valckenierstraat and Plantage Muidergracht.

name: Lijndenstraat
en: Frederik Baron van Lijnden van Hemmen (1761-1845), fortification and hydraulic engineer and member of parliament, who wrote a treatise (in 1821) on draining the Haarlemmermeer.

name: Lijnoliestraat
en: A reference to the Vettewinkel paint factory, later Sigma, on the Cruquius site from 1934 to 2008. Lijnolie, short for lijnzaadolie (linseed oil), is an ingredient of paints and a base for varnish.

name: Lijsterweg
en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

name: Lijzijde
en: A nautical term: the side of the ship turned away from the wind (the lee side).

name: Limburghof
en: The province. The nearby streets are named after Limburg castles.

name: Limmenstraat
en: A village in the Noord-Kennemerland region of Noord-Holland.

name: Limmerick
en: A corrupted spelling of the Irish port of Limerick, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Lindekersstraat
en: An old cherry variety, also known as Early Rivers, that flowers early.

name: Lindengracht
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Lindenhoevestraat
en: A former eighteenth-century country estate by the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, which lay roughly on this spot.

name: Lindenhoeveweg
en: A former eighteenth-century country estate by the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, which lay roughly on this spot.

name: Lindenstraat
en: The broadleaf tree (the lime or linden).

name: Linnaeusdwarsstraat
en: Carl Linné or Linnaeus (1707-1778), Swedish botanist, who took his doctorate at the University of Harderwijk in 1735. He was one of the first to devise a system for classifying plants and animals. Until 1878 the Linnaeusstraat was called Oetewalerweg; earlier still it was known as the Geldeloze pad. As late as 1886 the Linnaeusdwarsstraat was called Ipsenstraat, after J. Ipsen, who had the first house in this little street built.

en: Carl Linné or Linnaeus (1707-1778), Swedish botanist, who took his doctorate at the University of Harderwijk in 1735. name: Linterhof
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Lipariweg
en: A volcanic island north-east of Sicily, which gives its name to the island group that includes Stromboli.

name: Lippijnstraat
en: A medieval farce (sotternie).

name: Lirestraat
en: The currency of Italy before the euro (the lira).

name: Lisdoddelaan
en: A water plant (bulrush) that grows along the banks of streams, lakes and ponds.

name: Lise Meitnerpad
en: Elise Meitner (1878-1968), Austrian-Swedish physicist, whose specialities were radioactivity and nuclear physics. With the German chemist Otto Hahn (1879-1968) she led research into nuclear fission in uranium, for which Meitner supplied the theoretical basis in 1939. Hahn received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1944; Meitner's part was not recognised. She was later rehabilitated, among other things when element 109, discovered in 1982, was named meitnerium.

name: Litasweg
en: The currency of Lithuania before the euro (the litas).

name: Livornostraat
en: The Italian city off which the Dutch naval officer Jan van Galen defeated the English fleet in a naval battle in 1653.

name: Lizzy Ansinghstraat
en: Maria Elisabeth Georgine (Lizzy) Ansingh (1875-1959), painter, known above all for her scenes with dolls. She was one of the 'Amsterdamse Joffers' (Amsterdam young ladies).

name: Lloydplein
en: Refers to the adjoining Lloyd Hotel.

name: Lobo-Braakensiekstraat
en: Greta Lobo-Braakensiek (1882-1926) and David Jessurun Lobo (1884-1926) were celebrated stage actors. David was also a director and translated several plays. The couple were killed in a railway accident near Leiden.

name: Locomotiefstraat
en: From 1913 to 2002 this area was home to the firm Orenstein & Koppel, which made railway equipment. A locomotive is used to drive trains or for shunting. With hauled trains the locomotive pulls the train and can also push it.

name: Lodewijk Boisotstraat
en: Admiral of Zeeland (1530-1576) under William of Orange, who in 1574 relieved Leiden from the Spanish siege. He drowned trying to relieve Zierikzee.

name: Lodewijk Tripstraat
en: Amsterdam merchant (1605-1684), several times burgomaster of Amsterdam, who in 1665 had the 'Trippenhuis' built on the Kloveniersburgwal together with his brother Hendrik.

name: Lodewijk van Duurenstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1917-1944), involved in organising the clandestine paper 'Trouw'.

name: Loefzijde
en: A nautical term: the side of the ship the wind blows on (the windward side).

name: Loenendreef
en: The village on the Vecht (Utrecht).

name: Loenermark
en: With the Loenense Bos, an extensive nature area on the Veluwe.

name: Loenermarkbrug
en: With the Loenense Bos, an extensive nature area on the Veluwe.

name: Loet C. Barnstijnstraat
en: Born Lodewijk Cohen (1880-1953), he called himself Loet C. Barnstijn after his mother, to distinguish himself from others named Cohen. Film distributor and producer, he started with a cinema in The Hague in 1912 and founded the famous Filmstad studios.

name: Loevestein
en: An old castle where the Maas and the Waal meet, at Poederoijen (Gelderland), founded by Dirc Loef. It was never lived in by a noble family. In the seventeenth century it was a prison that held many well-known figures, among them Hugo de Groot, and the castle was nicknamed the Dutch Tower (of London).

name: Loggerhof
en: A fast-sailing fishing vessel with a sharp bow (a lugger).

name: Lohuis
en: A nature reserve south-east of Aalten (Gelderland), made up of woods with a heath pool.

name: Lokerenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of East Flanders.

name: Lomanstraat
en: Abraham Dirk Loman (1823-1897), theologian and writer, who arranged the old Dutch songs collected by Valerius.

name: Lombokstraat
en: One of the Lesser Sunda Islands (Indonesia).

name: Lommelstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Lomondlaan
en: The lake, Loch Lomond, on the border of the Central and Strathclyde regions in western Scotland.

name: Lontarpalmstraat
en: A kind of palm. Lontar comes from 'rontal', a compound of two Old Javanese words, ron (leaf) and tal (tree). Because its leaves spread out like a fan, the rontal tree is also called the fan palm.

name: Loodskotterhof
en: A vessel lying off the coast that takes the pilot to and from seagoing ships (a pilot cutter).

name: Looiersgracht
en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

name: Loosdrechtdreef
en: The villages of Oud- and Nieuw-Loosdrecht (Utrecht).

name: Loosduinenstraat
en: A village in Zuid-Holland south of The Hague, added to The Hague in 1923.

name: Lootsstraat
en: Cornelis Loots (1765-1834), Amsterdam broker who devoted himself to poetry. His poems were collected and published after his death.

name: Loowaard
en: A manor (havezate) near Duiven (Gelderland), dating from about 1550.

name: Lopikhof
en: A village in the Lopikerwaard (Utrecht), between the Lek and the Hollandse IJssel. It takes its name from a peat stream originally called Lobeke.

name: Lord Kelvinstraat
en: Sir William Thomson, alias Lord Kelvin (1824-1907), British physicist, born in Belfast and for 53 years professor at Glasgow, a founder of thermodynamics. He designed many electrical measuring instruments.

name: Lorentzlaan
en: Hendrik Antoon Lorentz (1853-1928), physicist, founder of the electron theory, who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1902.

name: Lorreinenstraat
en: A Frankish chivalric romance of the twelfth or thirteenth century (the Roman der Lorreinen): a rhymed tale set in the time of Charlemagne.

name: Lou Jansenplein
en: Resistance fighter (1900-1943), an office clerk by trade, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in The Hague.

name: Louis Apolstraat
en: Painter (1850-1936), known for his winter scenes.

name: Louis Armstrongstraat
en: Louis Daniel Armstrong (1900-1971), American trumpeter, singer and jazz bandleader, one of the most important figures in the history of jazz.

name: Louis Bouwmeesterstraat
en: Louis Frederik Johannes Bouwmeester (1841-1925), actor. For many years with the Vereeniging Het Nederlandsch Tooneel, he founded the Haarlemsch Tooneel in 1903. He excelled above all in the classical repertoire.

name: Louis Chrispijnstraat
en: The father, Louis Chrispijn Sr (1854-1926), a gifted actor and director, and the son, Louis Chrispijn Jr (1878-1931), an actor who excelled above all in comedy.

name: Louis Couperusstraat
en: Louis Marie Anne Couperus (1863-1923), man of letters, who wrote many psychological and historical novels and a great number of essays, letters and journalism. Known for his dandyism, aestheticism and fatalism.

name: Louis Davidsstraat
en: Stage name of Simon David (1883-1939), revue artist and chansonnier, known for his sentimental songs. He also wrote revues in which his sister Henriëtte (Heintje) Davids (died 1975) performed.

name: Louis de Visserstraat
en: Louis Leonardus Hendrikus de Visser (1878-1945), politician, originally of the SDAP and later a communist. He was chairman of the Communist Party from 1925 to 1935 and a member of the House of Representatives from 1925 to 1940. In 1941 he was arrested and deported to the Neuengamme concentration camp, where he died shortly before the liberation.

name: Louis J. Welterbrug
en: Mr Louis J. Welter (1910-1943), under the alias 'Kriek', was active in the Javanese resistance during the Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies (1942-1945). He compiled a report of military information that could hasten an Allied invasion, and helped build a clandestine transmitter near Bandung. It was almost ready when he was arrested in September 1942. In May 1943 he was sentenced to death and beheaded.

name: Louis Moorhof
en: Louis Barth. Joh. Moor (1856-1937), actor, who played above all in the French comedy company. He was also well known as a director and as a translator of foreign plays.

name: Louis Naarstigstraat
en: Aloysius Christiaan Naarstig (1895-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam and executed by firing squad there.

name: Louis Raemaekersstraat
en: Draughtsman of political cartoons (1869-1956), for many years the regular illustrator of the daily 'De Telegraaf'.

name: Louis Schottingstraat
en: Journalist (1870-1957), a reporter for the 'Algemeen Handelsblad'. For many years he was the doyen of Amsterdam's city council reporters.

name: Louise de Colignystraat
en: Fourth wife of Prince William of Orange (1555-1620) and mother of Prince Frederik Hendrik.

name: Louise Marie Loeberplantsoen
en: Painter (1894-1983), who attended the Rijksakademie between 1915 and 1918 in Amsterdam, her home town, and worked in an abstract-figurative and non-figurative style.

name: Louise Wentstraat
en: Louise Went (1865-1951), one of the founders of the Vereniging Amsterdams Bouwfonds (Amsterdam building fund association). In 1895 she carried out a survey of living conditions in the Jordaan for the Bouwonderneming Jordaan.

name: Louvrelaan
en: The Palais, later the Musée du Louvre, in Paris. Various architects worked on the building, begun in the sixteenth century, for centuries. The collection began with the art treasures of the French kings, above all Francis I and Louis XIV, and the royal collection was greatly enlarged by Napoleon. France's most important museum.

name: Louweshoek
en: Stefan Louwes (1889-1953), agricultural adviser and head of food supply during the Second World War. By council decision of 8 June 1960 the road was shortened somewhat.

name: Louwesweg
en: Stefan Louwes (1889-1953), agricultural adviser and head of food supply during the Second World War. By council decision of 8 June 1960 the road was shortened somewhat.

name: Lozingskanaal
en: A canal running to the Zeeburg pumping station (the name means discharge canal).

name: Lübeckbrug
en: Lübeck is a Hanseatic city in the German state of Schleswig-Holstein. The names in the Houthavens are taken from places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Lübeckgracht
en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

name: Lucellestraat
en: A play by Bredero from 1616, dedicated to Maria Tesselschade.

name: Luchtvaartstraat
en: Traffic by means of air transport (aviation). The name was given because of the nearby Aeronautical Laboratory.

name: Lucien Gaudinstraat
en: French fencer who won a gold medal at the 1924 Olympic Games in Paris.

name: Ludovicus Imminkpad
en: Ludovicus Immink (1822-1869) designed mainly for the Zaan region, but in Amsterdam is known for the Nieuwendammerkerk. For this neighbourhood the chosen category was the names of Dutch architects involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Luiksingel
en: A Belgian city (Liège), in the province of Liège.

name: Lumeijstraat
en: Willem van Lumey (1542-1576), leader of the Sea Beggars before Den Briel in 1572. William of Orange then appointed him his lieutenant and governor of Holland, but he was finally dismissed for his cruelties. The municipality of Sloten named the street Emmastraat (council decision of Sloten, 28 June 1911), but this and other names were changed after the annexation of 1921 because they already existed elsewhere in Amsterdam.

name: Lumièrestraat
en: Auguste Marie Louis Nicolas Lumière (1862-1954) and Louis Jean Lumière (1864-1948), French film pioneers. With their invention of the cinématographe, a camera and projector in one, the Lumière brothers were among the founders of cinema.

name: Lupineplein
en: The plant (lupin), used as an ornamental and grown as green manure for sandy soil because of its nitrogen-fixing root nodules.

name: Lupinestraat
en: The plant (lupin), used as an ornamental and grown as green manure for sandy soil because of its nitrogen-fixing root nodules.

name: Luthuliplein
en: The South African Albert John Luthuli (1898-1967), former president of the African National Congress (ANC), and until the 1950s the principal spokesman of the non-violent resistance to apartheid. In 1960 he received the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Lutkemeerweg
en: Named after the Lutkemeer, drained here in 1865 (lutke = little).

name: Lutmastraat
en: Janus Lutma (1588-1669), gold- and silversmith. Part of this street came over in 1896 from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel as the Ruyterstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 30 September 1890), while another part was called Lutmaplein until 1924 (council decision of 6 June 1917).

name: Luttenbergweg
en: The name of a hill near Raalte (Overijssel).

name: Luvernes
en: The Scottish port of Inverness, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Luyendijkje
en: The path was laid on a low summer dike that has long had this name and continues under the same name in the municipality of Landsmeer. The name 'luyendijk' is the same as 'looidijk' and was given to a back embankment meant to stop water seeping in from the neighbouring area. Here it is an embankment along the border with Oostzaan, built at the end of the sixteenth century.

name: Luzacstraat
en: Lodewijk Caspar Luzac (1786-1861), statesman and Minister of the Interior, who helped prepare the constitutional revision of 1848.

name: Lyceumbrug
en: The name of this bridge refers to the nearby Amsterdams Lyceum (a secondary school).

name: M. Berdenis van Berlekomstraat
en: Mathilde Wibaut-Berdenis van Berlekom (1862-1952), socialist and feminist, who in 1895 founded a Middelburg branch of the Association for Women's Suffrage and campaigned for universal women's suffrage. She was married to the alderman F.M. Wibaut, with whom she wrote the book 'Wordend huwelijk' (marriage in the making).

name: M. Gandhilaan
en: Mohandas (Mahatma) Karamchand Gandhi (1869-1948), leader of the non-violent resistance in India that led to the country's independence in 1947. Besides opposing British rule, he called for a boycott of imported goods. He was often imprisoned for his actions, and was murdered shortly after independence.

name: M. Hanenbergstraat
en: Matthijs Abel Joannes Hanenberg (1781-1838), from 1815 first schout (sheriff) and then, until 1837, burgomaster of the municipality of Sloten, Sloterdijk, Osdorp and De Vrije Geer.

name: M. Justbrug
en: Named after Chief Rabbi Meir Just (1908-2010), who served in Buitenveldert. He lived in Soetendael and so often walked over this bridge to the Jewish Cultural Centre on the Van der Boechorststraat.

name: M.C. Addicksstraat
en: Martinus Casimir Addicks (1887-1941), born in Amersfoort, one of the first victims among the resistance during the German occupation, executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

name: M.J. Granpré Molièreplein
en: Marinus Jan Granpré Molière (1883-1972), architect, founder of the 'Delft School', which sought to join traditional and modern architecture. He drew up expansion plans for many Dutch towns and built, among other things, the town halls of Naaldwijk, Zwijndrecht and Uithoorn. He also designed the church on this square.

name: M.J.E. Lippitsstraat
en: Meinardus Johannes Elias Lippits (1869-1941), architect, who designed housing blocks in Amsterdam-Noord on the garden-city model. He was also involved in building the Hotel Schiller on the Rembrandtplein.

name: M.S. Vaz Diasbrug
en: This bascule bridge is named after Mozes Salomon Vaz Dias (1882-1963), founder of the press agency M.S. Vaz Dias, which in 1934 merged into the Algemeen Nederlands Persbureau (ANP), which he co-founded.

name: Ma Braunpad
en: Mrs M.J. Braun-Voorwinde (1883-1956), a Rotterdam swimming instructor, who lives on as Ma Braun, one of the pioneers of swimming in the Netherlands. She trained the first Dutch women to compete successfully at the Olympic Games, from 1924.

name: Maagdenpalmstraat
en: A plant family (periwinkle) of mainly warm, but sometimes temperate, regions. The Madagascar periwinkle contains substances used in cancer drugs. An infusion of the lesser periwinkle, native to the Netherlands, can be used as a gargle and against diarrhoea.

name: Maanhof
en: The celestial body (the moon) that moves around the earth in an elliptical orbit.

name: Maanstraat
en: The celestial body (the moon) that moves around the earth in an elliptical orbit.

name: Maarkedalpad
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Maarsenhof
en: A village on the Vecht (Utrecht).

name: Maarten Harpertszoon Trompstraat
en: Dutch admiral (1597-1653), who defeated the Spanish fleet at the Downs in 1639. He was killed fighting the English in the naval battle of Ter Heijde.

name: Maarten Jansz. Kosterstraat
en: He lived from about 1520 to 1592. From 1567 to 1576 he was personal physician to Frederik II, King of Denmark and Norway. In 1578 he was one of the leading figures of the Alteration (the quiet revolution in Amsterdam in which the pro-Spanish burgomasters were put outside the city walls). From that year Koster was several times burgomaster of Amsterdam, and throughout he kept up his medical practice. He gave the first public lessons in anatomy. Before 1872 the street was called the Amstelgrachtje, filled in in 1866; earlier still it was part of the Lijnbaansgracht.

name: Maasdrielhof
en: A village on the Maas in Gelderland.

name: Maaseikpad
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Maaseikstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Maaslandstraat
en: A Zuid-Holland village in the municipality of Midden-Delfland.

name: Maassluisstraat
en: A town on the Nieuwe Waterweg (Zuid-Holland).

name: Maasstraat
en: The river (Meuse) that rises in France and flows through the Netherlands from Maastricht.

name: Machineslootbrug
en: This bridge keeps alive the memory of one of the former names of today's Admiralengracht.

name: Machinetocht
en: A canal in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Madagascarhaven
en: An African island, the fourth largest island in the world, south-east of Africa.

name: Madelievenstraat
en: The little wild flower (the daisy), of the daisy family.

name: Madibabrug
en: Nickname of Nelson Mandela.

name: Madurastraat
en: An island north of Java (Indonesia).

name: Magalhaensplein
en: Fernão de Magalhães or Magellan (1480-1521), Portuguese navigator, who in 1520 discovered the strait between South America and Tierra del Fuego named after him, and from there was the first to cross the Pacific Ocean, to the Philippines.

name: Magalhaensstraat
en: Fernão de Magalhães or Magellan (1480-1521), Portuguese navigator, who in 1520 discovered the strait between South America and Tierra del Fuego named after him, and from there was the first to cross the Pacific Ocean, to the Philippines.

name: Magere Brug
en: Around 1670 a drawbridge was laid over the Amstel so narrow that it was only fit for pedestrians. Although officially called the Kerkstraatbrug (after the Lange Kerkstraat), people stubbornly called it the 'Magere brug' (skinny bridge), and the city council then adopted the name. The story of the Mager sisters, who lived nearby, belongs to the realm of fables. Old pictures show that the old bridge was a simple wooden structure: the deck of the fixed part lay on simple wooden trestles, while the movable middle was a drawbridge with a single leaf. In 1772 it was given a double leaf, and in 1871 the bridge was demolished entirely and replaced by one with nine spans.

name: Magersfonteinstraat
en: A place in South Africa (Orange Free State), known for the Boer victory over the British in the Boer War (1899-1902).

name: Magneetstraat
en: The electromagnet is meant: an iron circuit that is not entirely closed, with windings through which direct current is passed.

name: Magnoliastraat
en: An ornamental tree that flowers before its leaves appear.

name: Mainhaven
en: A tributary of the Rhine, on which the city of Mainz lies (the Main).

name: Mainhavenweg
en: A tributary of the Rhine, on which the city of Mainz lies (the Main).

name: Majanggracht
en: A river on the Indonesian island of Java.

name: Majoie Hajarystraat
en: Majoie Hajary (Paramaribo, 16 August 1921 - Neuilly-sur-Seine, 25 August 2017) was a composer from a multicultural family, who won fame with music that conveyed, among other things, the value of a diverse society.

name: Majoor Bosshardtbrug
en: Alida Margaretha Bosshardt (1913-2007) became known for her work for the Salvation Army, most of which took place right around this bridge. Here on the Wallen she also founded the Goodwill Centre. In 2009 she was voted 'Greatest Amsterdammer of all time'. The 'Major' (who was actually a lieutenant-colonel) was a true bridge-builder between different groups, which is why a bridge was chosen for her rather than a street.

name: Majoor Fransweg
en: The name of Bosboom-Toussaint's epistolary novel of 1874.

name: Majubastraat
en: Amajuba or Majuba, Zulu for 'dovecote', was a mountain top in Natal, on the border with the Transvaal, known from the First Boer War (1880-1881).

name: Makassarplein
en: An Indonesian port on the island of Sulawesi (Celebes), called Ujung Pandang from 1971 to 1999.

name: Makassarstraat
en: An Indonesian port on the island of Sulawesi (Celebes), now called Ujung Pandang.

name: Makersstraat
en: Refers to an area of Strandeiland where many creative businesses in manufacturing (makers) can set up.

name: Maldenhof
en: The village on the Maas-Waal canal (Gelderland).

name: Maliebaan
en: The name recalls the 'Maliebaen' that once lay near the Schagerlaan. A maliebaan is a ground for a game like kolf (pall-mall), played with long iron mallets and wooden balls.

name: Maltaweg
en: An island in the Mediterranean.

name: Malvastraat
en: A plant genus, better known as mallow.

name: Mandarijnenstraat
en: The fruit.

name: Mandenmakerspad
en: Basket-making was originally a typical travelling trade. The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

name: Manegestraat
en: After the French riding school (manège) that stood here from 1761 to 1881.

name: Manenburgstraat
en: A former eighteenth-century country estate on the Kruislaan, on the site of today's Nieuwe Ooster cemetery.

name: Manna de Wijs-Moutonhof
en: Writer of cabaret songs (1873-1947), who also performed in cabaret herself, singing her own songs.

name: Maputoweg
en: A port and the capital of Mozambique. The street is near the Afrikahaven in the Western Port Area.

name: Marathonweg
en: Originally a village on the east coast of Attica (Greece), where the Persians were defeated in 490 BC. A messenger, by tradition Pheidippides, ran with the news to Athens (42 km), and the marathon race is named after this event.

name: Marcantilaan
en: Marcanti was the former name of the 'De Hoeksteen' conference centre next to the entrance of the Centrale Markt, opposite this avenue. Marcanti is a contraction of MarktCantine (market canteen), the original function of the 1933 building.

name: Marcellus Emantsstraat
en: Poet, novelist and playwright (1848-1923), a forerunner of the Tachtigers, whose work is deeply sombre in tone.

name: Marchanthof
en: Hendrik Pieter (Henri) Marchant (1869-1956), statesman, one of the founders of the Vrijzinnig-Democratische Bond (Liberal Democratic League) and, among other posts, Minister of Education, Arts and Sciences under Prime Minister Colijn. The Nieuwe Spelling (new spelling) of 1933 is named after him.

name: Marco Polostraat
en: Venetian traveller (1254-1323), who spent a quarter of a century among the Chinese and is known for his travel accounts.

name: Marconistraat
en: The Italian engineer Guglielmo Marconi (1874-1937), who invented wireless telegraphy in 1896. In 1909 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics.

name: Marcusstraat
en: Balthazar Jan Fred. Marcus (1806-1865), burgomaster of the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel, to which this street belonged until 1896.

name: Marga Klompélaan
en: Margaretha Albertina Maria Klompé (1912-1986), politician of the KVP. She became the first woman minister in the Netherlands when she was made Minister of Social Work in 1956, and with a break of three years remained so until 1971. That year she was appointed a Minister of State.

name: Margaret Bourke-Whitebrug
en: Margaret Bourke-White (1904-1971) was the first war correspondent accredited to the US Army and a photographer for the US Air Force.

name: Marguerite Yourcenarstraat
en: Pseudonym of the French writer Marguerite Cleenewerck de Crayencour (1903-1987). She taught French literature in the United States from 1942 to 1950 and from 1952 to 1953, and finally settled there. Yourcenar wrote in every literary genre and was also an excellent translator.

name: Maria Austriastraat
en: Professional name of the Czech-Jewish photographer Marie Karoline Oestreicher (1915-1975), who settled in Amsterdam before the war and was active in the resistance during it. In 1945 she co-founded the photo agency Particam (Partisan Camera). She is known for her theatre photographs and her portraits of musicians, actors, dancers, directors and writers.

name: Maria Beshof
en: Maria Elisabeth Bes was the first woman student at the Polytechnic School in Delft (today's TU Delft) and the first woman chemical engineer.

name: Maria Montessoristraat
en: Italian doctor (1870-1952), who became famous as an educator for her teaching method, based on the child's free individual development.

name: Maria Snelplantsoen
en: Maria Dina Snel (1890-1941), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, died in Scheveningen prison. She had a part in distributing the clandestine paper 'Vrij Nederland'.

name: Maria Ulfahstraat
en: Maria Ulfah Santoso (Serang 1911 - Jakarta 1988), who after her husband's execution by Dutch troops in February 1949 remarried and was known as Maria Ulfah Soebadio. From an aristocratic family, she was the first Indonesian woman to complete a law degree in the Netherlands (1929-1933). She worked for the emancipation of Indonesian women on many boards, among others as chair of the Indonesian women's federation Kowani. She was the first woman to hold a ministerial post, Social Affairs in the second and third Sjahrir cabinets (1946-1947).

name: Mariadistelkade
en: The milk thistle (Silybum marianum) is an annual or biennial plant of the daisy family (Asteraceae).

name: Marianellastraat
en: Marianella García Villas (1949-1983), president of the Human Rights Commission of El Salvador from its founding in 1973. The regime regarded her as a terrorist and she had to leave the country, continuing her work from Mexico. In 1983 she was captured and murdered by the army.

name: Marianne Hilaridesplantsoen
en: Marianne Hilarides was a Dutch ballet dancer. A pupil of Sonia Gaskell, she made her debut in 1950 with the Ballet Recital, where she was given solo roles, among them the pas de deux of Le Cygne Noir (the Black Swan).

name: Marianne Philipsstraat
en: Marianne Goudeket née Philips (1866-1950), novelist, whose books include 'Bruiloft in Europa' (wedding in Europe) and 'De biecht' (the confession).

name: Marie Altelaarplein
en: Neighbourhood activist, feminist and communist (1917-2005), nicknamed Tante (Aunt) Marie, the driving force behind a fifteen-year campaign against high rents on the Eastern Islands in the 1970s and 1980s.

name: Marie Baronlaan
en: Marie Baron competed as a swimmer at the age of 16 in the modern Olympic Games of 1924 in Paris.

name: Marie Heinekenplein
en: Painter (1844-1930), mainly of flowers and still lifes, who held several exhibitions in Amsterdam between 1883 and 1899. She was a member of the Amsterdam artists' society 'Arti et Amicitiae'.

name: Marie van Westerhovenstraat
en: Actress (1857-1946), married to Louis Chrispijn, who was on the stage for more than sixty years and also performed in operetta for many years.

name: Marieken van Nimwegenstraat
en: The name of a fifteenth-century miracle play (Mariken van Nieumeghen).

name: Mariëndaal
en: An estate with a nineteenth-century country house and a nature area, between Arnhem and Oosterbeek.

name: Marifoonweg
en: A mobile radio telephone for use on the water (marine VHF).

name: Mariniersbrug
en: After the nearby Marines barracks.

name: Marinierskade
en: After the nearby Marines barracks.

name: Mariotteplein
en: Edme Mariotte (1620-1684), French physicist, who discovered the coloured rings around the sun and moon and the blind spot in the eye.

name: Mariottestraat
en: Edme Mariotte (1620-1684), French physicist, who discovered the coloured rings around the sun and moon and the blind spot in the eye. Marisplein, Jacob Oud-Zuid council decision 26 January 1922 15: m 9

name: Maritzstraat
en: Gerrit Maritz (1797-1839), one of the leaders of the Great Trek of the Boers in South Africa in 1835 and the years after. He defeated the Matabele in 1837. The boys' book Pieter Maritz and the place name Pietermaritzburg do not refer to a historical figure of that name: it is a contraction of the two Voortrekkers Gerrit Maritz and Piet Retief.

name: Marius Bauerplantsoen
en: Marius A.J. Bauer (1867-1932), painter and etcher, whose many journeys to the East give his etchings their striking oriental fantasy.

name: Marius Bauerstraat
en: Marius A.J. Bauer (1867-1932), painter and etcher, whose many journeys to the East give his etchings their striking oriental fantasy.

name: Marius Meijboomstraat
en: Photographer (1911-1998), who had a famous photo studio in Amsterdam and made mainly portraits and fashion and advertising photographs. He was known for his photographs of the royal family.
