During the war he belonged to the group of photographers later known as 'De Ondergedoken Camera' (the camera in hiding).

name: Marius van Bouwdijk Bastiaansestraat
en: Marius A. van Bouwdijk Bastiaanse (1886-1964), gynaecologist at the Wilhelmina Gasthuis and professor at the University of Amsterdam.

name: Marjoleinstraat
en: The shrubby plant used as a herb (marjoram).

name: Markelerbergpad
en: Refers to the Markelerberg, a hill of 66 metres in the municipality of Hof van Twente.

name: Markengouw
en: The village and former island of that name, Marken (Noord-Holland).

name: Markerveld
en: A polder near Uitgeest (Noord-Holland), created in 1637.

name: Markiespad
en: The cloth awning over the door of a caravan. The street name refers to the caravan site here.

name: Markonstraat
en: This was probably a former country estate on the Amstel.

name: Marksingel
en: The currency of Germany and Finland before the euro (the mark).

name: Marmolada
en: A mountain peak in Italy, 3354 metres high.

name: Marnixkade
en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

name: Marnixplein
en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

name: Marnixstraat
en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

name: Maroastraat
en: A volcano in New Zealand.

name: Marowijnestraat
en: A river in Suriname, on the border with French Guiana.

name: Marquette
en: A castle in Heemskerk, so called since 1612 after Daniel de Hertaing, Lord of Marquette. The castle dates from the fourteenth century and was then a stronghold of the Cods. Its present form dates largely from 1741.

name: Marskramerstraat
en: Originally a typical travelling trade: a street trader who carries his wares in a basket on his back (a pedlar). The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

name: Marsmanstraat
en: Hendrik Marsman (1899-1940), poet. In 1940 he fled to England, but the ship struck a mine and Marsman was among the victims.

name: Marssloot
en: A ditch in Amsterdam-Noord, near the Kadoelen.

name: Marsstraat
en: The planet (Mars).

name: Martelaarsgracht
en: Probably named after a house with the sign of 'the martyr'. Before it was filled in, the water of the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and Achterburgwal drained into the IJ here. There was then a quay only on the even-numbered side. The bridge in the Nieuwendijk over this canal was called the Martelaarsbrug.

name: Marten Corverhof
en: Actor and theatre reformer (1727-1794).

name: Marten Toonderbrug
en: Marten Toonder (Rotterdam, 2 May 1912 - Laren, 27 July 2005) was a Dutch comics author. Besides his great role in literature, Toonder also put his talents to use during the Second World War.

name: Martien Coppenshof
en: Martinus Franciscus Josephus Coppens (1908-1986), photographer, known above all for his photographs of Brabant farming families. Besides people he also photographed churches, cathedrals and landscapes.

name: Martin Cortesstraat
en: Spanish teacher of navigation (1532-1589), who in 1551 wrote the navigation handbook 'Breve Compendio de la Sphera y de la Arte de Navegar', published in English in 1561 as 'The Arte of Navigation' and popular with English seamen.

name: Martin Ennalsplein
en: Human rights defender (1927-1991), secretary-general of Amnesty International in the 1970s and involved in founding many other human rights organisations. Under his leadership Amnesty's work was extended to campaigns against torture, the death penalty, extrajudicial executions and disappearances.

name: Martin Ennalsstraat
en: Human rights defender (1927-1991), secretary-general of Amnesty International in the 1970s and involved in founding many other human rights organisations. Under his leadership Amnesty's work was extended to campaigns against torture, the death penalty, extrajudicial executions and disappearances.

name: Martin Luther Kingpark
en: American preacher (1929-1968), known internationally for his struggle against poverty and discrimination, murdered in Memphis (USA) on 4 April 1968. Before 1968 the park was called Amstelpark (council decision of 19 October 1949), a name later given to another park. The name was changed at the request of the Pacifist Socialist Party (PSP).

name: Martin Niemöllerstraat
en: German pastor (1892-1984) and peace activist. The 'Bekennende Kirche' (Confessing Church) he founded openly opposed Hitler. He was arrested in 1937 and held in concentration camps as Hitler's 'personal prisoner' until 1945. After the war he argued for international reconciliation and against rearmament.

name: Martin Vlaarkade
en: Martinus Vlaar (1904-1975), one of the organisers of the February Strike of 1941, was arrested soon after and freed by American troops in 1945. Afterwards he was very active in the Spaarndammerbuurt.

name: Martini van Geffenstraat
en: Jhr. Frans Willem H.P.J. Martini van Geffen (1832-1883), burgomaster of the municipality of Sloten from 1881 to 1883.

name: Martinus Jan Langeveldstraat
en: Educationalist (1905-1989), a pupil of Philip Kohnstamm among others. Langeveld is regarded as one of the most important educationalists of the second half of the twentieth century.

name: Martinus Nijhoffstraat
en: Poet and essayist (1894-1953), a well-known critic and editor of 'De Gids', one of the great figures of his generation.

name: Mary van der Sluisstraat
en: Mary Meijer-van der Sluis (1917-1994), fencer, Dutch champion in 1937 and 1947 and a competitor at the 1948 Olympic Games. She had to suspend her sporting career during the war because she was Jewish.

name: Mary Zeldenruststraat
en: Mary Zeldenrust-Noordanus (1928-1984), psychologist, who worked for sexual emancipation and women's emancipation. She founded the Institute for Psychological Market Research.

name: Mastbos
en: A nature reserve near Breda.

name: Masthof
en: An anker (anchor) is the ship's part.

name: Mata Harihof
en: Stage name of the Frisian Margaretha Geertruida Zelle (1876-1917). Mata Hari is Malay for 'eye of the day' (the sun). An oriental dancer, in Paris among other places, and a spy during the First World War. Convicted by the French of spying for Germany, she was executed in 1917. Five films about her life were made in various countries.

name: Mataramstraat
en: A region on the island of Java (Indonesia) under Dutch rule. It was originally a separate kingdom on Java. It was also the name of a principality on the island of Lombok that existed until 1894.

name: Matenesse-hof
en: A thirteenth-century castle on the Schie in the old manor of Mathenesse, now a district of Rotterdam.

name: Mathurastraat
en: One of the three most important fighters who resisted the oppressive system on the plantations of Suriname through the so-called 'Fonale Sankties'.

name: Matrozenhof
en: Refers to the nearby shipping training institute (matrozen = sailors).

name: Mattenbiesstraat
en: A kind of reed (bulrush) that grows on the banks of fresh and brackish waters.

name: Matterhorn
en: A mountain in Switzerland and Italy, 4477 metres high.

name: Mattheus Sladushof
en: Linguist (1569-1629), specialising in Hebrew and Arabic.

name: Maurice Peeterspad
en: Mauritius Prosper Peeters (1882-1957), cyclist, who became the Netherlands' first Olympic cycling champion by winning the sprint in 1920 in Antwerp. Four years later in Paris he won bronze in the tandem.

name: Maurice Ravellaan
en: Joseph Maurice Ravel (1875-1937), French composer, conductor and pianist of Swiss and Basque descent. With his contemporary Claude Debussy (1862-1918) he is seen as the leading impressionist composer. His most famous work is the ballet 'Boléro' (1928).

name: Mauritiushaven
en: An island east of Madagascar, colonised from 1598 by Dutch seamen and later taken over by the French and the English, among others. It is named after Stadtholder Prince Maurits, Count of Nassau.

name: Maurits Kannstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1894-1942), a lawyer by profession, born in The Hague, died in the Sachsenhausen concentration camp.

name: Maurits Sabbehof
en: Flemish man of letters (1873-1938), writer of novels, literary criticism and plays, who in 1923 became a professor at Brussels and curator of the Plantin Museum in Antwerp.

name: Mauritskade
en: Maurits, Prince of Orange (1567-1625), stadtholder of Holland and Zeeland from 1585, and later of all seven provinces. The quay was originally part of the Buitensingel.

name: Mauritsstraat
en: There was once a Mauritsstraat here too (council decision of 10 June 1880), which then ran as far as the Rhijnspoorplein (Weesperpoort station). It was added to the Swammerdamstraat in 1970, and the old name has now returned. The name honours Maurits, Prince of Orange.

name: Mauvestraat
en: Anton Mauve (1838-1888), landscape painter.

name: Max de Haasstraat
en: Max de Haas (1898-1983), journalist, director and screenwriter. When the Germans invaded the Netherlands in May 1940, De Haas, a politically aware Jew with few illusions about the Nazis' plans, fled to England with his Viennese wife Gretl.

name: Max Euweplein
en: Machgielis Euwe (1901-1981), mathematician, chess grandmaster and theorist. From 1921 to 1958 he was almost continuously Dutch champion, and in 1935 he won the world title. In 1981 he was awarded the Silver Medal of the City of Amsterdam.

name: Max Planckstraat
en: German physicist (1858-1947), professor at Kiel and Berlin, the founder of quantum theory,, who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1918.

name: Maxwellstraat
en: The Scottish physicist James Clerk Maxwell (1831-1879), originator of the electromagnetic theory of light.

name: Maya Angeloustraat
en: Maya Angelou (1928-2014), born Marguerite Johnson, was an American writer and poet.

name: Mechelensingel
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Medemblikstraat
en: A town in Noord-Holland, formerly an important Zuiderzee town.

name: Meentstraat
en: Meent is an old Dutch word for common pasture. Here it is a historical Rijnland name: land east of Heemstede lost to flooding.

name: Meer en Vaart
en: A former farmstead on the Sloterdijkermeerweg near the Haarlemmerweg, demolished to build Bos en Lommer. It was the official residence of the burgomaster of the municipality of Sloten, abolished in 1921.

name: Meerbrug
en: The name of this fixed bridge in Kadoelen comes from the surrounding hamlet called 't Meertje (the little lake), which belonged to Landsmeer before the annexation of 1921.

name: Meerhuizenplein
en: A former country house on the Amstel, where the Amstelkade now meets the Amsteldijk, demolished around 1914. In the seventeenth century the poet Hendrik Laurensz Spiegel lived here.

name: Meerhuizenstraat
en: A former country house on the Amstel, where the Amstelkade now meets the Amsteldijk, demolished around 1914. In the seventeenth century the poet Hendrik Laurensz Spiegel lived here.

name: Meerkerkdreef
en: The village of Meerkerk on the Merwedekanaal (Zuid-Holland), between Vianen and Gorinchem.

name: Meerluchtlaan
en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

name: Meermontkade
en: Former country house on the Amstel.

name: Meernhof
en: A village west of Utrecht (De Meern).

name: Meerpad
en: This means the former Buikslotermeer, to which the path led.

name: Meeuwenlaan
en: The bird family (the gulls).

name: Meeuwenplein
en: The bird family (the gulls).

name: Meibergdreef
en: A hill south of Berg en Dal/Groesbeek (Gelderland).

name: Meibergpad
en: A hill south of Berg en Dal/Groesbeek (Gelderland).

name: Meidoornplein
en: The tree or shrub (hawthorn) of the apple family.

name: Meidoornweg
en: The tree or shrub (hawthorn) of the apple family.

name: Meimorgenstraat
en: The poem of the same name ('May morning') by Jacqueline E. van der Waals (1868-1922), in the collection 'Nieuwe Verzen' (1909).

name: Mekongweg
en: A river more than four thousand kilometres long that flows through China, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam.

name: Melis Stokehof
en: A thirteenth-century Dutch poet, known for his 'Rijmkroniek' (rhymed chronicle), regarded as a follower of Jacob van Maerlant.

name: Melkdistelstraat
en: An akkerdistel (creeping thistle) is a species of thistle.

name: Melkweg
en: The Milky Way is the faintly shining band across the sky, caused by the light of the millions of stars of the galaxy our sun belongs to. The road was earlier called Ringweg.

name: Meloenenstraat
en: The fruit.

name: Melsbroekhof
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Memeleiland
en: An old Prussian town, called Klaipėda since 1945 and part of Lithuania. In the second half of the eighteenth century it was important for supplying timber to Amsterdam.

name: Memlingstraat
en: Hans Memling (1430-1494), Southern Netherlandish painter of altarpieces and portraits. A number of his works are brought together in Bruges.

name: Menadostraat
en: A town on the Indonesian island of Sulawesi (Celebes).

name: Mendelhof
en: Gregor Mendel (1822-1884), Austrian biologist who discovered the laws of heredity in plants.

name: Mendes da Costahof
en: Jozef Mendes da Costa (1863-1939), sculptor, whose work can be seen among other places in the boardroom of the Stock Exchange.

name: Menno ter Braakstraat
en: Essayist and critic (1902-1940), who fiercely opposed the rise of National Socialism.

name: Mensinge
en: An old Drenthe manor (havezate), partly surrounded by water, near Roden. It dates originally from 1381 and was rebuilt in 1728.

name: Mercatorplein
en: Flemish geographer and cartographer whose real name was Gerard Kremer (1512-1594), who drew the first world map in cylindrical projection.

name: Mercatorstraat
en: Flemish geographer and cartographer whose real name was Gerard Kremer (1512-1594), who drew the first world map in cylindrical projection.

name: Merckenburg
en: An eighteenth-century building in Heukelum (Zuid-Holland) with a fourteenth-century square tower in the middle of its façade, the remnant of the original castle.

name: Mercuriushaven
en: In Roman mythology, the god of trade (Mercury).

name: Mercuriusplein
en: The smallest planet (Mercury), closest to the sun.

name: Mercuriusstraat
en: The smallest planet (Mercury), closest to the sun.

name: Merdekagracht
en: Merdeka means free or independent. Already in colonial times it was the forbidden rallying cry of the nationalist movement, and after the proclamation of the Republic of Indonesia on 17 August 1945 it became the characteristic battle cry of the independence fighters.

name: Merelstraat
en: The songbird (the blackbird).

name: Merenburgstraat
en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

name: Merlijnstraat
en: The name of a Celtic romance (Merlin), adapted by Jacob van Maerlant in 1260.

name: Merwedeplein
en: The river formed where the Maas and the Waal flow together.

name: Mesdagstraat
en: Hendrik Mesdag (1831-1915), painter of seascapes.

name: Messchaertstraat
en: Johannes Martinus Messchaert (1857-1922), baritone, who in 1884 founded the Amsterdam Conservatory with Daniël de Lange, Frans Coenen and Julius Röntgen.

name: Messinastraat
en: An Italian port on Sicily, to which the former KNSM ran a scheduled service.

name: Metaalbewerkerweg
en: The trade: a collective name for workers in the metal industry.

name: Meteorensingel
en: Meteors are 'shooting stars', probably fragments of former comets.

name: Meteorenweg
en: Meteors are 'shooting stars', probably fragments of former comets.

name: Methaanweg
en: The gas (methane), a colourless and odourless firedamp and marsh gas.

name: Metselstraat
en: A reference to the concrete company Albeton, on the Cruquius site between 1977 and 2014 (metselen = to lay bricks).

name: Mezenstraat
en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

name: Mezquitalaan
en: An Islamic building in Córdoba, fortress-like in appearance, founded in 785 by Emir Abd al-Rahman. Over the centuries Christian elements were added, the most important being the sixteenth-century cathedral in the middle of the complex.

name: Michel de Klerkhof
en: Architect (1884-1923), who built several housing complexes in Amsterdam, including in the Spaarndammerbuurt (Amsterdam School style).

name: Michelangelostraat
en: Michelangelo Buonarroti (1475-1564), Italian sculptor, painter, architect and poet, the greatest artist of his time (the dome of St Peter's and the paintings in the Sistine Chapel in Rome).

name: Michiel de Ruijtertunnel
en: Michiel Adriaansz. de Ruyter (1607-1676), the renowned admiral of Holland and West Friesland. He was born in Vlissingen. In Amsterdam he lived on what is now the Prins Hendrikkade.

name: Middelhoffstraat
en: A former pleasure garden on the east side of the Schagerlaan.

name: Middeliestraat
en: A village north-west of Edam (Noord-Holland).

name: Middelveldstraat
en: After the Middelveldsche Akerpolder, in which this neighbourhood lies.

name: Middenlaan Zunderdorp
en: The street was officially named in 1953, following the local name it had long had. It does not run through the middle of the village, but it is the central road in relation to the village and the nearby hamlets.

name: Middenmeerpad
en: After the former farmstead Midden-Meer, which stood on the corner of the Middenweg and the Kruislaan until 1809.

name: Middenweg
en: Named after its position: the road was laid right across (through the middle of) the drained Watergraafsmeer.

name: Midscheeps
en: A term for everything in the middle of a ship (amidships).

name: Midwoudpad
en: A village in Noord-Holland, in the West-Friesland region.

name: Mien Labbertonstraat
en: Writer of books for young people (1883-1966), whose works include 'Jonge Harten' (young hearts, 1938) and 'Lentebloesem' (spring blossom, verse, 1926).

name: Mien Ruysbrug
en: Wilhelmina Jacoba (Mien) Moussault-Ruys, better known by her maiden name Mien Ruys (Dedemsvaart, 12 April 1904 - Deventer, 9 January 1999), was an internationally known Dutch garden architect. In the Netherlands she was nicknamed Bielzen Mien (Sleeper Mien) because she pioneered the use of railway sleepers in gardens, which was especially popular in the 1970s. She liked to work with straight forms: rectangles, squares and clean lines. She was one of the first in the Netherlands to take small town gardens seriously as a garden architect. Her work lives on in the Mien Ruys Gardens Foundation, which maintains 30 gardens in her style in Dedemsvaart (the Tuinen van Mien Ruys), open to visitors from April to October. In 1954 she and her husband, the publisher Theo Moussault, founded the quarterly Onze Eigen Tuin (our own garden). In 1958-1959 she designed, for and with Gerrit Rietveld, the gardens around his factory building for the De Ploeg weaving mill in Bergeijk, which is still well preserved today as a 'village garden'. The same goes for the garden of the Rosa Spier Huis for elderly artists in Laren. She also designed, among other things, the greenery between the home zones of Tuindorp Frankendael.

name: Mijehof
en: A small village on the little river of the same name in Zuid-Holland (the Meije), which flows into the Oude Rijn at Zwammerdam.

name: Mijndenhof
en: The little village on the Vecht opposite Loenen (Utrecht).

name: Milletstraat
en: Jean-François Millet (1815-1875), French landscape painter.

name: Millingenhof
en: The village on the Rhine (Gelderland).

name: Milovan Djilasplein
en: Yugoslav politician and human rights activist (1911-1995). In 1941 he co-founded the Partisan army, and in 1946 became deputy prime minister under Marshal Tito. He fell from favour through his struggle for more democracy.

name: Milovan Djilasstraat
en: Yugoslav writer and human rights activist (1911-1995), one of Josip Tito's closest associates and a leading figure in the Yugoslav Communist Party. He spoke openly of his disappointment with communism, broke with Tito and was imprisoned several times.

name: Minahassastraat
en: A region on the island of Sulawesi (Indonesia).

name: Minckelersstraat
en: Jan Pieter Minckelers (1748-1824), physicist, who discovered that coal gas could be used for lighting.

name: Minervahaven
en: In Roman mythology, the goddess of wisdom (Minerva).

name: Minervahavenweg
en: In Roman mythology, the goddess of wisdom (Minerva).

name: Minervalaan
en: In Roman mythology, the goddess of wisdom (Minerva).

name: Minervaplein
en: In Roman mythology, the goddess of wisdom (Minerva).

name: Minnemoersstraat
en: The name arose at the end of the seventeenth century and probably comes from a gable stone or shop sign. Before that the little street appears as Bickersdwarsstraat. A minnemoer or minnemoeder was a woman who took on the mothering of a baby, nursing and/or swaddling it (a wet nurse).

name: Miraplein
en: A star in the constellation Cetus (the Whale).

name: Modelmakerstraat
en: A trade name: someone who makes models, for example for casting moulds (a pattern maker). The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Modemstraat
en: A device that converts computer signals for the telephone network. As a counterpart to the street names recalling Amsterdam-Noord's former shipbuilding industry, this name refers to modern information technology.

name: Moeder Alacoquebrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after Mother Alacoque (1892-1956), a Dutch nun who helped many prisoners during the Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies (1942-1945). She was mother superior of the Charitas Hospital in Palembang on Sumatra, whose patients included several people involved in spreading war news and smuggling money and medicines into the prison camps in Palembang.

name: Moederkruidstraat
en: A medicinal plant (feverfew).

name: Moerbeienstraat
en: The fruit of the mulberry tree, whose leaves are used to rear silkworms.

name: Moerdijkstraat
en: A spot on the Hollandsch Diep where Johan Willem Friso drowned in 1711. The Moerdijk railway bridge (2530 m) was built here between 1868 and 1872, and the road bridge in 1936.

name: Moermanskkade
en: A Russian port and naval base on the Barents Sea (Murmansk), founded in 1915.

name: Moermond
en: A picturesque castle in Renesse (Zeeland), badly damaged by the water in the flood of 1953. During its restoration the foundations of a large early medieval castle came to light.

name: Moestuinlaan
en: A vegetable garden. The street lies on the former De Bongerd allotment complex.

name: Moezelhaven
en: A tributary (the Moselle) that flows into the Rhine at Koblenz (Germany), an important river for the industries and mines of the Saar region.

name: Moezelhavenweg
en: A tributary (the Moselle) that flows into the Rhine at Koblenz (Germany), an important river for the industries and mines of the Saar region.

name: Mokerstraat
en: A heavy smith's hammer or sledgehammer.

name: Molen 't Haasjepad
en: A polder mill, an octagonal ground-sailer, which kept the Wilmkebreek dry from its reclamation in 1633. The mill was badly damaged in the flood of 1916, after which it was replaced by an electric pumping station. It was demolished in 1924.

name: Molenaarsweg
en: The miller is the person who works a mill. The road runs along the Molenwijk park. Before 1976 the road was part of the Stellingweg.

name: Molenbeekstraat
en: The name of several Dutch watercourses, among them ones in Limburg and along the Veluwezoom.

name: Molengouw
en: After the mill that stood level with today's Nibbixwoudstraat, to which this street once led as a path.

name: Molenpad
en: In the sixteenth century this path lay outside the city and led to a mill (molen) level with today's Raamplein (until the seventeenth century the Raamstraat was also called Molenpad). The Molenpad is in fact the only one of the many outer paths to have kept the name 'pad' when it came inside the walls after 1612.

name: Molenslootpad
en: The name for a main drainage ditch leading to the polder mill.

name: Molensteeg
en: The alley dates from the early fourteenth century, when the Count of Holland had a mill built on the Zeedijk. The mill had gone before 1357, but the alley has kept the name to this day. In the sixteenth century it was also called Minderbroederssteeg.

name: Molenwerf
en: This name was set in 1956, but had existed for a long time. A molenwerf is the plot of ground a mill stands on; here, the site of the mill in the old village of Sloterdijk.

name: Molenwijk
en: This is the name of a park. The residential blocks built in it form a number of windmill sails in plan and bear the names of types of mill.

name: Molsteeg
en: The name of this alley first appears in 1557 and refers to the house 'De Mol' (the mole), mentioned as early as 1533, which stood on the ground now occupied by the alley.

name: Molukkenstraat
en: An island group in Indonesia between Sulawesi and New Guinea, which includes the islands of Ambon, Ceram and Halmahera (Indonesian name: Maluku).

name: Mondlanestraat
en: Eduardo Mondlane (1920-1969), leader of the Frelimo liberation movement in Mozambique, murdered in 1969. Mozambique did not become independent of Portugal until 1975.

name: Monitorstraat
en: A display screen. As a counterpart to the street names recalling Amsterdam-Noord's former shipbuilding industry, this name refers to modern information technology.

name: Monnikendammerplantsoen
en: The town in Noord-Holland, once a flourishing Zuiderzee town.

name: Monnikendammerweg
en: The town in Noord-Holland, once a flourishing Zuiderzee town.

name: Monnikendwarsstraat
en: Named after the Franciscan or Grey Friars' monastery, founded in 1464 and destroyed in 1578. The street's oldest name is Grauwemonnikenstraat (1581).

name: Monnikenstraat
en: Named after the Franciscan or Grey Friars' monastery, founded in 1464 and destroyed in 1578. The street's oldest name is Grauwemonnikenstraat (1581).

name: Monnikskapstraat
en: A plant genus (monkshood) of the buttercup family, flowering yellow, purple, blue, pink or white. The name comes from the strikingly shaped upper petal. Monkshood grows mainly in mountain meadows in the northern hemisphere. Of the more than 250 species, only the yellow monkshood is native to the Netherlands.

name: Monte Adi
en: A mountain peak in Spain, 1453 metres high.

name: Monte Perdido
en: A mountain peak in Spain, 3355 metres high.

name: Monte Viso
en: A mountain peak in Italy, 3841 metres high.

name: Montelbaanstraat
en: Named after the Montelbaanstoren, built in the sixteenth century. The street was laid out after the slum clearance of the Jonker and Ridder neighbourhood around 1930. Where the name Montelbaan comes from, we are in the dark.

name: Montferlandstraat
en: The hilly country near 's-Heerenberg and Zeddam (Gelderland).

name: Montfoorthof
en: The town on the Hollandse IJssel (Utrecht).

name: Moreelsestraat
en: Paulus Moreelse (1571-1638), painter, influenced by Titian, whose works include the civic guardsmen of the Kloveniersdoelen.

name: Morellenstraat
en: The fruit, a kind of cherry (morello).

name: Morsestraat
en: The North American Samuel Morse (1791-1872), who devised a system of signs from combinations of dots and dashes (Morse code).

name: Mortelstraat
en: A reference to the concrete company Albeton, on the Cruquius site between 1977 and 2014 (metselen = to lay bricks).

name: Mosplein
en: The little plants (mosses), spore plants found all over the world.

name: Mosstraat
en: The little plants (mosses), spore plants found all over the world.

name: Mosveld
en: The little plants (mosses), spore plants found all over the world.

name: Motorkade
en: A motor is an engine that supplies motive power, driven by electricity, gases or heat.

name: Motorwal
en: A motor is an engine that supplies motive power, driven by electricity, gases or heat.

name: Mozartkade
en: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756-1791), Austrian composer of church music, operas, symphonies, piano concertos, songs and chamber music, the greatest composer of the classical period.

name: Mozes en Aäronstraat
en: After the two Old Testament figures Moses, leader of the exodus from Egypt, and Aaron, head of the priesthood. The street runs between the former city hall (secular authority, Moses) and the Nieuwe Kerk (spiritual authority, Aaron).

name: Mr. P.N. Arntzeniusweg
en: Pieter N. Arntzenius (1745-1799), lawyer and poet, secretary of the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer.

name: ms. Oslofjordweg
en: The motor ship Oslofjord, a passenger ship built at the yard of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM) for a Norwegian shipping line, for service between Norway and North America. At its launch in 1948 the ship was christened by the Queen of Norway.

name: ms. Tarnweg
en: The motor ship (ms) Tarn, built at the yard of the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (later NDSM).

name: ms. van Riemsdijkweg
en: The motor ship Van Riemsdijk, a cargo and passenger ship built in 1939 at the yard of the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (later NDSM) for the Koninklijke Paketvaart Maatschappij (KPM), for service in Indonesia. When war broke out in May 1940 the ship was not yet finished. Towards the end of the war the occupiers sank it in the Noordzeekanaal; after the war it was raised and completed.

name: mt. Lincolnweg
en: The turbine tanker Esso Lincoln was built in 1961 at the yard of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM) for Esso. It was the hundredth ship launched there after 1945, on 15 December 1962.

name: mt. Ondinaweg
en: A motor tanker of 6341 tonnes, built in 1939 at the yard of the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (later NDSM) for the Anglo Saxon Petroleum Co.

name: Muiderbergbrug
en: After the village of Muiderberg.

name: Muiderlaan
en: It runs towards Muiden, like the Muiderstraat and the Plantage Muidergracht.

name: Muiderstraat
en: The street runs towards the town of Muiden (as does the Plantage Muidergracht). Most of the north side of the street was demolished in the Hunger Winter of 1944-45 and the rest in the years after, and the street was then widened to 37 metres.

name: Muntbergweg
en: A hill west of Groesbeek (Gelderland).

name: Muntendamstraat
en: Pieter Muntendam (1901-1986), professor of social medicine at Leiden from 1953. For sixty years he worked intensively on public health in the Netherlands, among other things as director-general and as state secretary. He held progressive views on euthanasia and abortion. Among his many posts was the chairmanship of the State Commission on alternative medicine.

name: Muntplein
en: Amsterdammers simply call it the Munt. In the building next to the Munttoren (the remnant of the Regulierspoort) coins were minted (munt) for a time in the seventeenth century, and the name Munt has stuck to it ever since. The official name Muntplein dates from 1917. From 25 January 1877 to 1917 the square was called Sophiaplein, and before 1877 Schapenplein (sheep square).

name: Muntsluis
en: Amsterdammers simply call it the Munt. In the building next to the Munttoren (the remnant of the Regulierspoort) coins were minted (munt) for a time in the seventeenth century, and the name Munt has stuck to it ever since.

name: Murdoch Mackenziestraat
en: Scottish cartographer (1712-1797), whose maps include those of the Orkney Islands. The sea atlas of the Orkneys that the VOC issued to its ships after 1753 was a translation of Mackenzie's work.

name: Murillostraat
en: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo (1618-1682), Spanish Baroque painter (Madonnas and saints).

name: Museumbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after the nearby Rijksmuseum, built in 1883 by Pierre Cuypers.

name: Museumplein
en: After the nearby Rijksmuseum, built in 1883 by Pierre Cuypers. Large exhibitions were held on the Museumplein in 1883, 1887 and 1895, and after that, until about 1940, it was an ice club's ground.

name: Museumstraat
en: After the nearby Rijksmuseum, built in 1883 by Pierre Cuypers. Large exhibitions were held on the Museumplein in 1883, 1887 and 1895, and after that, until about 1940, it was an ice club's ground.

name: Mussenstraat
en: The birds (sparrows), related to the finches.

name: Muurbloemstraat
en: The plant (wallflower), of the cabbage family.

name: Muzenplein
en: In Greek mythology the Muses (daughters of Zeus) are the goddesses of the arts and sciences.

name: N. Lansdorpstraat
en: Nicolaas Lansdorp (1885-1968), architect, who designed the church on the Mosstraat. In Amsterdam he built 2000 homes and 160 schools, such as the Vossius Gymnasium.

name: Na Druk Gelukbrug
en: Named after Dirk Beukeboom's farm at what was then Oude Amstelveenseweg 255, which had to make way for the Olympic Stadium and the Olympic neighbourhood.

name: Naaldwijkstraat
en: The name of a village in the Westland (Zuid-Holland).

name: Naardermeerstraat
en: The nature reserve west of Naarden. In 1905 a plan by the municipality of Amsterdam to buy the area as a rubbish dump was rejected by the city council. This led to the founding of the Society for the Preservation of Nature Monuments in the Netherlands (Natuurmonumenten), which bought the Naardermeer in 1906.

name: Nachtegaalstraat
en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

name: Nachtwachtlaan
en: Rembrandt's famous painting of the militia company of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq (1642). The painting got the name Nachtwacht (Night Watch) by mistake, because its paint had darkened.

name: Nadezjda Mandelstamstraat
en: Wife of the dissident Russian writer Osip Mandelstam. Nadezhda Mandelstam (1899-1980) risked her own life to get her husband's poetry published; he died in 1938 while interned.

name: Nadia en Lili Boulangerplantsoen
en: Nadia (Paris, 16 September 1887 - Paris, 22 October 1979) and Lili (Paris, 1893 - Mézy-sur-Seine, 1918) Boulanger were sisters and both composers. They meant a great deal to classical music in the early twentieth century, known above all in their native France but eventually abroad too. Nadia Boulanger's musical work is closely linked with the American Conservatory at Fontainebleau, which she directed from 1949 until the end of her life, training more than 600 pupils. Lili Boulanger was the first woman to win the Prix de Rome. After that she was constantly ill, and died aged only 24.

name: Nadirstraat
en: A term in astronomy: the imaginary point on the celestial sphere directly beneath the observer (the opposite of the zenith).

name: Nadorststeeg
en: Old registers show that in 1557 an inn with the sign 'Nadorst' (after-thirst) stood on the corner of the Nes and this alley.

name: Nageljongenstraat
en: A trade name: a young worker who heats the rivets red-hot and hands them to the riveter. The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Namenhof
en: A Belgian town (Namur), in the province of Namur.

name: Nannie van Wehlstraat
en: Pseudonym of Susanne J.A. Reys (1880-1944), writer of books for young people, who wrote not only girls' books but also essays on educational and feminist questions.

name: Nannoplein
en: The name of an idyll by the writer Carel Vosmaer (1882).

name: Naritaweg
en: The name of one of Tokyo's airports.

name: Narva-eiland
en: A town in Estonia on the Russian border, which mattered to Amsterdam as a historical timber-exporting port.

name: Narwalstraat
en: A cetacean (the narwhal), grey with brown spots on its back, with only a few teeth in its upper jaw, no more than five metres long. It lives in the Arctic.

name: Nassaukade
en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. Before it was named in 1879, the quay was called Buitensingel.

name: Nassauplein
en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. Before it was named in 1879, the quay was called Buitensingel.

name: Nathan F. Israëlweg
en: Nathan Frederik Israël (1904-1944), resistance fighter, who was involved in preparing the February Strike of 1941, took part in the armed resistance and produced the clandestine paper 'De Waarheid' in Amsterdam-Noord. He was killed in a gunfight on 15 August 1944.

name: Navigatiepad
en: Finding position at sea. The streets around here relate to shipping and navigation.

name: NDSM-kade
en: The Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, formed in 1946 by merging the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). It lay along the north bank of the IJ and built cargo ships, among others, and carried out repairs and conversions. The newbuilding yard closed in 1979; the repair side (a second NSM) went bankrupt in 1984.

name: NDSM-pier
en: The Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, formed in 1946 by merging the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). It lay along the north bank of the IJ and built cargo ships, among others, and carried out repairs and conversions. The newbuilding yard closed in 1979.

name: NDSM-plein
en: The Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, formed in 1946 by merging the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). It lay along the north bank of the IJ and built cargo ships, among others, and carried out repairs and conversions. The newbuilding yard closed in 1979.

name: NDSM-straat
en: The Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, formed in 1946 by merging the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). It lay along the north bank of the IJ and built cargo ships, among others, and carried out repairs and conversions. The newbuilding yard closed in 1979.

name: Nederhoven
en: A small moated castle in Beegden (Limburg), with the date 1614 in its wall anchors.

name: Nedersticht
en: The old name for today's province of Utrecht, as opposed to the Oversticht, which comprised today's provinces of Overijssel and Drenthe together with Oost- and Weststellingwerf and the city of Groningen.

name: Neerkanne
en: Originally a medieval castle at Canne near Maastricht, repeatedly destroyed. Its present form dates from 1700, restored in 1955. It is also called Agimont castle.

name: Neerlandiaplein
en: The name of the building put up in 1888 by the Diaconate of the Reformed congregation as a home for elderly married couples, part of the Amstelhof complex for elderly people in need of care. Today it is part of the Hermitage.

name: Nellesteinpad
en: The name of a house near Maarn (Utrecht). Since 1976 the name Nellestein has been used for a residential area by the Gaasperplas metro station.

name: Nellie Bodenheimstraat
en: Writer of books for young people (1874-1951), known above all for her illustrations for children's books.

name: Nelson Mandelapark
en: Nelson Rolihlahla 'Madiba' Mandela (1918-2013), South African anti-apartheid fighter and politician, regarded in his own country as the Father of the Nation. As leader of the ANC's military wing he was sentenced to life imprisonment in 1964, but was freed in 1990. In 1993 he received the Nobel Peace Prize with President F.W. de Klerk for their efforts to end the apartheid regime. In the first free elections of 1994 he was elected president, an office he held for five years.

name: Neptunushaven
en: In Roman mythology, the god of the sea (Neptune).

name: Neptunusplein
en: A planet of our solar system (Neptune).

name: Neptunusstraat
en: A planet of our solar system (Neptune).

name: Nepveustraat
en: Jan Nepveu (1719-1779), governor of Suriname.

name: Nes
en: The place name nes means a low-lying spit of land along water. The name Nes, originally Nesse, shows that the land here was once marshy. Until the seventeenth century the northern part was still called Gansoord. The word oord means much the same as nes, but occurs mainly along the larger rivers.

name: Nesciobrug
en: Nescio was the pseudonym of the Amsterdam writer J.H.F. Grönloh, known for novellas such as De Uitvreter (the sponger) and Titaantjes (little titans). He liked to walk around the nearby Diemerzeedijk and the Buiten-IJ.

name: Nesserhoek
en: Named after the right-angled bend in the Waterland sea dike, now the Buiksloterdijk, that stood out into the IJ, exposed to westerly winds and waves.

name: Nesserland
en: Named after the spit of land, the Nes, that jutted out into the IJ from the Buiksloot sea dike.

name: Nesserton
en: Named after the end of the Nes, a spit of land in the IJ on the north-west side of the Buiksloterham, marked by a barrel (ton) on a pole. It disappeared when the Noordzeekanaal was built.

name: Netwerkweg
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Newtonstraat
en: Isaac Newton (1642-1727), English mathematician and physicist, who discovered important laws of gravitation.

name: Niasstraat
en: An island group off the west coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

name: Nibbixwoudstraat
en: A village between Hoorn and Medemblik (Noord-Holland).

name: Nic. de Roeverstraat
en: Nicolaas de Roever (1850-1893), Amsterdam city archivist and historian, author of 'In de oude Amstelstad' (in the old city on the Amstel).

name: Nickeriestraat
en: A river in Suriname.

name: Nico Broekhuysenweg
en: Nicolaas Broekhuysen (1876-1958), initiator and pioneer of korfball in the Netherlands.

name: Nico Jessekade
en: Photographer (1911-1976), who began as a doctor with his own general practice. Known for his loose way of photographing, marked by blur and the use of flash. His most famous book is 'Vrouwen van Parijs' (women of Paris), published in several countries.

name: Nico Snijdersstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

name: Nico van Suchtelenhof
en: Man of letters (1878-1949), who wrote poetry at first and later novels, and was for many years director of the Wereldbibliotheek publishing house in Amsterdam.

name: Nicolaas Anslijnstraat
en: Nicolaas Anslijn, education reformer (1778-1838), writer of school readers, including 'De Brave Hendrik' (good Henry). Born in Leiden, died in Alkmaar.

name: Nicolaas Beetsplantsoen
en: Man of letters and writer (1814-1903), who as a student wrote the celebrated 'Camera Obscura' under the pseudonym Hildebrand.

name: Nicolaas Beetsstraat
en: Man of letters and writer (1814-1903), who as a student wrote the celebrated 'Camera Obscura' under the pseudonym Hildebrand.

name: Nicolaas Berchemstraat
en: Painter (1620-1683), mainly of landscapes.

name: Nicolaas Hennemanhof
en: Photographer (1813-1898), who settled in London around 1847, was for years assistant to the famous English photographer William Henry Fox Talbot, and was appointed court photographer to Queen Victoria.

name: Nicolaas Japiksestraat
en: Historian (1872-1944), director of the Queen's Royal House Archive, who wrote historical studies including 'Geschiedenis van het Huis van Oranje-Nassau' (history of the House of Orange-Nassau).

name: Nicolaas Maesstraat
en: Painter (1634-1693) of history pieces and portraits, a pupil of Rembrandt.

name: Nicolaas Ruychaverstraat
en: A Beggar captain at the capture of Den Briel and the siege of Alkmaar. He was killed in 1577 in a failed raid on Amsterdam meant to bring the city over to the Prince's side.

name: Nicolaas Tetterodestraat
en: Amsterdam industrialist (1816-1894), founder of the 'Amsterdam' type foundry.

name: Nicolaas Witsenkade
en: Shipbuilder, cartographer and writer, who lived from 1641 to 1717. He studied law at Leiden and was an adviser to Tsar Peter the Great. His 1671 book on shipping is one of the important sources on Dutch shipbuilding in the seventeenth century. Between 1682 and 1705 he was many times burgomaster of Amsterdam.

name: Nicolaas Witsenstraat
en: Shipbuilder, cartographer and writer, who lived from 1641 to 1717. He studied law at Leiden and was an adviser to Tsar Peter the Great. His 1671 book on shipping is one of the important sources on Dutch shipbuilding in the seventeenth century. Between 1682 and 1705 he was many times burgomaster of Amsterdam.

name: Nida Senffstraat
en: Dina Willemina Jacoba Senff (1920-1995), swimmer, who won gold in the 100 metres backstroke at the 1936 Olympic Games in Berlin. At the turn she forgot to touch the wall, swam back, and still won.

name: Niek Engelschmanbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after Niek Engelschman (1914-1988), who also called himself Bob Angelo. He was very active in the struggle for gay emancipation and founded the COC.

name: Nienke van Hichtumstraat
en: Pseudonym of Sjoukje Maria Diederika Troelstra-Bokma de Boer (1860-1939), wife of the SDAP politician P.J. Troelstra. A writer of books for young people, she became known above all for 'Afke's tiental' (Afke's ten), which described the poverty and social ills around the turn of the century.

name: Nierkerkestraat
en: A village near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland, drowned in 1530.

name: Niersstraat
en: A river in Limburg that flows into the Maas at Gennep.

name: Nieuw Herlaer
en: A former castle in Sint-Michielsgestel, where a convent of that name was later built. A tower with a spire remains of the original castle.

name: Nieuw-Zeelandweg
en: A road east of the Australiëweg; geographically, New Zealand lies east of Australia.

name: Nieuwe Achtergracht
en: This canal was dug around 1660 behind (achter) the four main canals, hence the name. It connected the Reguliersgracht with the Amstel. In 1870 most of it was filled in.

name: Nieuwe Achtergracht
en: Dug at the same time as the Achtergracht, but on the other (new) side of the Amstel. Around 1670 part of it was filled in, creating the Korte Amstelstraat.

name: Nieuwe Akerweg
en: Named after the Akerpolder in the former municipality of Sloten. Aker and Akerwatering are historical names that already appear on a 1687 map of Rijnland by Jan Dou.

name: Nieuwe Amstelbrug
en: When this double bascule bridge, designed partly by Berlage, was completed in 1903, it was the newest bridge over the Amstel. The Hoge Sluis was also called the Amstelbrug, but this bridge was newer, hence the Nieuwe (new) Amstelbrug.

name: Nieuwe Amstelstraat
en: The river.

name: Nieuwe Batavierstraat
en: The name is thought to come from a gable stone or shop sign in the former Batavierstraat. Batavier is most probably a corruption of Batavia. The Nieuwe Batavierstraat was created when the island of Uilenburg was rebuilt.

name: Nieuwe Diep
en: When the Zuiderzee broke through the Diemerdijk in 1422, the new lake formed below the Bovendiep lake.

name: Nieuwe Doelenstraat
en: The doelen were the places where the civic guard companies met and practised shooting at a target (doel). The Oude Doelenstraat was laid out on the site of the oldest doelen, from the fifteenth century. The Nieuwe Doelenstraat takes its name from the Kloveniersdoelen, which from 1522 stood where the Doelen Hotel is today.

name: Nieuwe Egelantiersstraat
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Nieuwe Foeliestraat
en: One of the products, important at the time, brought from the East Indies and stored here in the East India Company's warehouses (foelie is mace).

name: Nieuwe Gietersstraat
en: Named after 't Giethuis, the city's gun and bell foundry, which stood here from 1614 to 1821. The street name first came into use in the eighteenth century.

name: Nieuwe Gouw
en: Gouw is a Waterland word for road. The addition Nieuwe (new) shows that this road is a little younger than the other Waterland roads, though it already appears on Covens's 1749 map of Amstelland and surroundings. In 1957 the name was officially confirmed again.

name: Nieuwe Gouwsloot
en: A gouw is a Waterland word for road.

name: Nieuwe Haagseweg
en: The main road to The Hague. The old Haagseweg now has a secondary role.

name: Nieuwe Hemweg
en: After a former islet, the Hem, in the old IJ. The Hem was first a spit of land that only later became an island through erosion of its banks. The word is the same as 'ham', now known only in 'inham' (inlet). A last stretch of the Hemweg still exists; the road originally began at the Spaarndammerbuurt. In 1947 it was cut through to build several harbours, and parts of it are now called Coenhavenweg and Archangelweg. The Nieuwe Hemweg was built to replace the Hemweg.

name: Nieuwe Herengracht
en: After the Heren Regeerders (the lords who governed the city; in the old days the city was not administered but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch when in 1612 it was widened into today's canal, the first of the three main canals. The stretch beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658, as does the Nieuwe Herengracht.

name: Nieuwe Hoogstraat
en: These streets lie slightly higher (hoog) than those around them. The Oude Hoogstraat was laid out around 1490, the Nieuwe Hoogstraat a century later.

name: Nieuwe Houthaven
en: A storage harbour for the timber trade (houthaven), built in 1873 and enlarged in 1878.

name: Nieuwe Jonkerstraat
en: The Jonker, Ridder, Koning and Keizer streets (squire, knight, king and emperor) were laid out in the second half of the sixteenth century on land originally built up by silt outside the Zeedijk, and officially brought within the city in 1593 (see Lastage). Although the origin of the names is unknown, it seems obvious that the four groups of names were chosen by the city government of the time. The Jonker and Ridder neighbourhood was cleared in 1928, when the Lastageweg was also laid out. The Nieuwe Jonkerstraat is a remnant of the former Jonkerstraat.

name: Nieuwe Keizersgracht
en: After Emperor Maximilian, Archduke of Austria, who in 1489 granted Amsterdam the privilege of bearing the imperial crown on its coat of arms.

name: Nieuwe Kerkstraat
en: The Kerkstraat was laid out in 1665 and named for the plan to link four churches (kerken) with it: the Amstelkerk, the Oosterkerk and two others that were never built, one by the Molenpad and one by the Weesperstraat. Later the street got various names: Kerkstraat (to the Amstel), Nieuwe Kerkstraat (to the Roetersstraat), Plantage Kerklaan (in the Plantage) and Korte Kerkstraat, which was renamed Tussen Kadijken in 1943.

name: Nieuwe Laan
en: A former road in the Sloter Middelveldsche Polder, linking the Uitweg and the Sloterdijkermeerweg. A map of 1650 calls this old road Nieuwelaan; later maps give the name Malleweg. When the present Nieuwe Laan was built in 1958 it was named Malleweg (council decision of 16 January 1958), but because of objections the name was changed to Nieuwe Laan in 1967.

name: Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg
en: The arterial road north, leading over the Afsluitdijk to Leeuwarden. Before 1936 the Leeuwarderweg was part of the Buiksloterdijk. The Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg was built when the IJ tunnel was completed.

name: Nieuwe Leliestraat
en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

name: Nieuwe Looiersdwarsstraat
en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

name: Nieuwe Looiersstraat
en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

name: Nieuwe Maanstraat
en: The celestial body (the moon) that moves around the earth in an elliptical orbit.

name: Nieuwe Meer
en: The lake was given this name to distinguish it from the Oude Meer (old lake). From the 1950s the Nieuwe Meer was enlarged with part of the Riekerpolder and dredged to a depth of thirty metres for sand for the western garden cities.

name: Nieuwe Meerpad
en: The lake was given this name to distinguish it from the Oude Meer (old lake). From the 1950s the Nieuwe Meer was enlarged with part of the Riekerpolder and dredged to a depth of thirty metres for sand for the western garden cities.

name: Nieuwe Nieuwstraat
en: By a council resolution of 1550 it was decided to lay out a new street by the Korsjespoort, which was simply called the 'nieuwe straat' (new street). Thirty years later the St Gertrude convent and the Onze Lieve Vrouwengasthuis, which stood between the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and the Nieuwendijk, were pulled down, and one of the streets laid out there was also called the 'nieuwe straat'. To tell the two new streets apart, in the first half of the seventeenth century their names were given the prefixes 'Oude' (old) and 'Nieuwe' (new), which they have kept to this day. The Nieuwe Nieuwstraat was at first also called Nieuwe Herenstraat.

name: Nieuwe Oostenburgerdwarsstraat
en: Oostenburg was the easternmost of the three islands (with Kattenburg and Wittenburg) brought within the city in the expansion of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. At first there were three streets from the canal, named after their position Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat (front, middle and back streets). In the first half of the twentieth century the Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic for the expansion of the Werkspoor company, and it was abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985; the Compagniestraat now runs there. The disappearance of several shipyards freed land on which the Nieuwe Oostenburgerstraat and -dwarsstraat were laid out.

name: Nieuwe Oostenburgerstraat
en: Oostenburg was the easternmost of the three islands (with Kattenburg and Wittenburg) brought within the city in the expansion of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. At first there were three streets from the canal, named after their position Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat (front, middle and back streets). In the first half of the twentieth century the Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic for the expansion of the Werkspoor company, and it was abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985; the Compagniestraat now runs there. The disappearance of several shipyards freed land on which the Nieuwe Oostenburgerstraat and -dwarsstraat were laid out.

name: Nieuwe Osdorpergracht
en: After the hamlet of Osdorp, shown on old maps as Oostdorp. Building of the Osdorp garden city began in 1957 and was practically complete by 1973. The Osdorperweg was long called Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

name: Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat
en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

name: Nieuwe Prinsengracht
en: After 'the princely title', meaning that of the Princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and the plainest in the character of its buildings. It was dug in the expansion of 1612 and built up from the Brouwersgracht to the Leidsegracht. In the expansion of 1658 this canal too was extended across the Amstel (as far as the Entrepotdok). The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for today's Noordermarkt never caught on with the citizens.

name: Nieuwe Purmerweg
en: The polder (the Purmer), created by draining the lake near Purmerend between 1618 and 1622.

name: Nieuwe Ridderstraat
en: The Jonker, Ridder, Koning and Keizer streets (squire, knight, king and emperor) were laid out in the second half of the sixteenth century on land originally built up by silt outside the Zeedijk, and officially brought within the city in 1593 (see Lastage). Although the origin of the names is unknown, it seems obvious that the four groups of names were chosen by the city government of the time. The Jonker and Ridder neighbourhood was cleared in 1928, when the Lastageweg was also laid out. The Nieuwe Jonkerstraat is a remnant of the former Jonkerstraat.

name: Nieuwe Schermerstraat
en: A lake in Noord-Holland (the Schermer), drained between 1631 and 1635.

name: Nieuwe Spiegelstraat
en: After a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers who ran soap works. In the corner house of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel lived Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' in 1564 and Pieter Lourens Spiegel in 1608; the house was still called Hertspiegel in 1738. Building on the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat began in 1665, and here too a resident of the Spiegel family probably gave the name.

name: Nieuwe Teertuinen
en: When the old tar yards (teertuinen, now the Prins Hendrikkade) moved to the Sloterdijksgracht, which became the storage place of the tar merchants, the quay there soon came to be called Nieuwe (new) Teertuinen.

name: Nieuwe Tuinstraat
en: Tuin (garden) here means a yard or enclosed space. The street name comes from the Stadstimmertuin (the city's carpentry yard, the Stadswerf), which lay here from 1612 to 1660 (by the Lijnbaansgracht) and to which the street led.

name: Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat
en: The island of Uilenburg, which came within the city in 1593 together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known for certain, but it probably comes from the marshland here, called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was formed by joining the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

name: Nieuwe Utrechtseweg
en: After the city of Utrecht. The street comes out on the Frederiksplein, where the Utrechtsepoort (Utrecht gate) once stood (demolished in 1860). The Nieuwe Utrechtseweg is the new arterial road to Utrecht; the old road ran by way of Duivendrecht and Abcoude.

name: Nieuwe Vaart
en: Named after the Nieuwe Vaart, dug around 1650 to link the IJ and the Oosterdok by the shortest possible route with the mouth of the IJ at Zeeburg.

name: Nieuwe Vijzelstraat
en: The name probably comes from the former residents Cornelis Arents Vijselaar (around 1600) and Jan Vijselaar (around 1632). The Vijzelstraat was then a short street running as far as today's Reguliersdwarsstraat. When the street was extended, the name passed to the extension too, and until the eighteenth century people spoke of the Oude and Nieuwe Vijzelstraat. The Vijzelgracht, dug between 1660 and 1670, was filled in in 1934.

name: Nieuwe Wagenstraat
en: There was also a wagon square by the Haarlemmerpoort, and a Wagenstraat there too. Because of confusion, the latter was renamed Nieuwe Wagenstraat in 1909. At the same time and for the same reason the Schapensteeg was renamed Korte Wagenstraat.

name: Nieuwe Westerdokstraat
en: The closing dike, built between 1830 and 1834, that turned the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to the Station Island at the end of the 1880s, part of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 when the Haarlemmer Houttuinen were widened.

name: Nieuwe Willemsstraat
en: This is the continuation of the Willemsstraat. This name too was originally set with a single s.

name: Nieuwe Zonneweg
en: The central body of the planetary system to which the Earth belongs (the sun).

name: Nieuwe-Wercksbrug
en: Named after the original name of today's Jordaan (the Nieuwe Werck, the new works).

name: Nieuwebrugsteeg
en: After the bridge the alley leads to. The first wooden bridge over the northern part of the Damrak was built between 1402 and 1421. When it was later replaced by a stone bridge, this was named the Nieuwebrug (new bridge). Old documents also give the name Uiterstebrug (outermost bridge).

name: Nieuwegeinlaan
en: A town south of Utrecht.

name: Nieuwegrachtje
en: In the early nineteenth century a public street was laid out on the former timber rampart along the Rapenburgergracht, and it was named 't Nieuwe grachtje (the new little canal).

name: Nieuwendammer Sluispad
en: Named after the nearby little lock (sluis). An old local name was made official.

name: Nieuwendammerdijk
en: The part of the Waterland sea dike that lay in the former municipality of Nieuwendam until 1 January 1921. The name Nieuwendam arose when a new dike or dam was built here after a dike breach in 1516, and passed to the dike village that grew up afterwards.

name: Nieuwendammerkade
en: Named after the former village of Nieuwendam, whose name arose when a new dike or dam was built here after a dike breach in 1516.

name: Nieuwendammerstraat
en: After the former village of Nieuwendam. The first part of the street came onto Amsterdam territory under the name Nieuwstraat at the annexation of 1 January 1921.

name: Nieuwendijk
en: The Nieuwendijk probably owes its name to a partial re-diking along the mouth of the Amstel, in which the Amsteldam mentioned in 1275 was also a link.

name: Nieuwenhuysenstraat
en: Frederik Nieuwenhuysen (1905-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Haarlem.

name: Nieuwerhoek
en: A seventeenth-century country estate near Loenen aan de Vecht, one of the three 'hoek' houses (Ouderhoek, Middelhoek and Nieuwerhoek) founded by the Amsterdam Van Hoek family. Ouderhoek was demolished in 1838.

name: Nieuwersluishof
en: A village on the Vecht (Utrecht).

name: Nieuwevaart
en: After the Nieuwe Vaart, dug around 1650 to link the IJ and the Oosterdok by the shortest possible route with the mouth of the IJ at Zeeburg.

name: Nieuwevaartkade
en: After the Nieuwe Vaart, dug around 1650 to link the IJ and the Oosterdok by the shortest possible route with the mouth of the IJ at Zeeburg.

name: Nieuwevaartweg
en: After the Nieuwe Vaart, dug around 1650 to link the IJ and the Oosterdok by the shortest possible route with the mouth of the IJ at Zeeburg.

name: Nieuwezijds Armsteeg
en: Arm here means bend. The alley leads to the bend in the Warmoesstraat.

name: Nieuwezijds Kolk
en: Originally the water from the peatland behind, which came by way of the now filled-in Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal, flowed through this kolk (basin) into the Damrak. Around 1350 the Martelaarsgracht was dug and this outlet fell out of use. The kolk was filled in towards the end of the fifteenth century.

name: Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal
en: The name, like that of the Oudezijds Voorburgwal, marks the canal in front of (voor) the town wall (burgwal) on the new side (Nieuwezijds) of the city. The Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal was filled in in 1884. Before that some stretches carried unofficial names from the markets held there: Pijpenmarkt, Boommarkt, Bloemmarkt and Postzegelmarkt (pipe, tree, flower and stamp markets).

name: Nieuwlandhof
en: The name of the village in the Neder-Betuwe, west of Leerdam (Zuid-Holland).

name: Nieuwmarkt
en: Created in 1614 by filling in and vaulting over part of the Kloveniersburgwal. The square that thus arose around the Waag was at first called Sint Antoniesmarkt, and later Nieuwmarkt (new market).

name: Nieuwpoortkade
en: The place in Belgium where Prince Maurits defeated the Spanish in 1600.

name: Nieuwpoortstraat
en: The place in Belgium where Prince Maurits defeated the Spanish in 1600.

name: Niftrikhof
en: After the village of that name in the Land van Maas en Waal (Gelderland).

name: Nigellestraat
en: A garden plant of the buttercup family, better known as love-in-a-mist (juffertje in 't groen).

name: Nigtevechthof
en: The village south of Weesp, between the Vecht and the Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal (Utrecht).

name: Nijenburg
en: One of the five thirteenth-century castles with which Floris V meant to subdue the West Frisians. The castle, destroyed in 1491, whose foundations can still be seen, lies just east of Alkmaar near Oudorp (Noord-Holland).

name: Nijlpaardenbrug
en: Refers to the hippopotamuses (nijlpaarden) in Artis.

name: Nilda Pintostraat
en: Nilda Maria Geerding Jessurun Pinto (1918-1954), Curaçao writer, known above all for the lively way she recorded Curaçao folk tales in Papiamentu.

name: Nirwana
en: In Buddhism, the highest spiritual state a person can reach, in which the soul is freed from craving, aversion and delusion and comes, as it were, to rest.

name: Nisserstraat
en: Lake Nisser (Nisservatn), in Telemark, southern Norway.

name: Nobelweg
en: Alfred Nobel (1833-1896), Swedish industrialist and chemist, inventor of dynamite. After his death his fortune went to a fund from which, since 1901, Nobel Prizes have been awarded each year for outstanding achievement in physics, chemistry, medicine, literature and peace; a prize in economics was added in 1969.

name: Nolensstraat
en: Willem Hubertus Nolens (1860-1931), Roman Catholic priest and politician, for many years after Schaepman's death leader of the Roman Catholic State Party and a member of parliament. From 1909 he was professor of labour law in Amsterdam.

name: Nooit Dorstraat
en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

name: Noord-Bevelandstraat
en: A Zeeland island.

name: Noordbrabantstraat
en: The province (Noord-Brabant). The street lies among streets named after castles in this province.

name: Noorder Amstelkanaal
en: A canal linking the Amstel and the Schinkel.

name: Noorder IJdijk
en: The north side of the IJ.

name: Noorder Valdeur
en: Named after the outlet between the Twiske and the Haal, which probably had a wooden sluice. Its boards were raised with a rope running over a block in a frame. It disappeared when the Twiske was turned into a polder.

name: Noorderakerweg
en: The name comes from the Akerpolder, which the road runs through. The addition Noorder (northern) distinguishes it from the other road, the Zuiderakerweg. The road came over under the name Noorderakerweg in 1921 from the then abolished municipality of Sloten.

name: Noorderbreedte
en: The distance in degrees of a place north of the equator (northern latitude).

name: Noorderdwarsstraat
en: The names come from the Noordse Bos, in the seventeenth century a neighbourhood of gardens crossed by paths and ditches, stretching from the Reguliersgracht to the Spiegelgracht. In 1670 the city gave the land to three charitable institutions, which built homes on it.

name: Noorderhaakspad
en: A sandbank near Texel (the Noorderhaaks), whose western part serves as a resting area for birds and seals. It is also called the Razende Bol.

name: Noorderkerkstraat
en: The Noorderkerk, a Protestant cruciform church built in 1623 by Cornelis Danckertsz.

name: Noorderkroonstraat
en: The constellation (the Great Bear).

name: Noordermarkt
en: After the Noorderkerk. Until 1655 the square was largely taken up by the church's graveyard. In that year and the following ones the graveyards were moved to a site outside the city. The market square was officially first named Prinsenmarkt (after the Prinsengracht), but that name did not last.

name: Noorderpark
en: Created in 2014 by joining the Florapark and the Volewijkspark, two green areas on either side of the Noordhollandsch Kanaal. The park owes its name to its position in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Noorderstraat
en: The names come from the Noordse Bos, in the seventeenth century a neighbourhood of gardens crossed by paths and ditches, stretching from the Reguliersgracht to the Spiegelgracht. In 1670 the city gave the land to three charitable institutions, which built homes on it.

name: Noordhollandsch Kanaal
en: A canal running from Amsterdam-Noord by way of Purmerend and Alkmaar to Den Helder.

name: Noordhollandschkanaaldijk
en: The canal between Amsterdam and Den Helder, dug in 1818-1824 to a design by Jan Blanken, because the port of Amsterdam was becoming unreachable through the sandbanks at the mouth of the IJ. (The Willemssluizen are named after King William I, who encouraged the building of the canal.)

name: Noordhollandstraat
en: The province (Noord-Holland). The surrounding streets are named after castles in this province.

name: Noordkaapstraat
en: The high rock formation (the North Cape), known as the northernmost point of Norway and of Europe.

name: Noordkaperweg
en: A whale (the right whale), black, sometimes with a white belly, reaching 15 metres in length. It lives in the temperate zones of the Atlantic and Pacific and around the Southern Ocean.

name: Noordplein
en: The area around Noord metro station forms the high-density centre of Amsterdam-Noord. The name Noordplein tells of its geographical position in the city. The square is the heart of Noord and links Noord with Zuid through the metro line and the Zuidplein there.

name: Noordsche Compagniebrug
en: Named after the Noordsche or Groenlandsche Compagnie (Northern or Greenland Company), which had its warehouses at Keizersgracht 40-44, the so-called Groenlandsche pakhuizen.

name: Noordwal
en: After its position, the north bank of the IJ.

name: Noordzeekanaal
en: The canal gives Amsterdam a direct link to the North Sea. It was made by reclaiming the IJ and cutting through the dunes at Velsen, dug to a design by Willem Antonie Froger, and opened on 1 November 1876. Canal and polders were built and run by the Kanaalmaatschappij (canal company), whose property passed to the state after its dissolution in 1884. Before it was named in 1978, the road was part of the Basisweg and the Zuiderweg in the Grote IJpolder.

name: Noordzeekanaalweg
en: A road named after the North Sea.

name: Noordzeeweg
en: A marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean (the North Sea).

name: Noordzijde
en: Named after its position relative to the Sloterplas (the north side).

name: Notarisappelstraat
en: An apple variety first grown in 1890 by the notary J.H.Th.W. van den Ham in Lunteren.

name: Notenstraat
en: The fruit of the nut tree.

name: Notweg
en: A former road between the Sloterdijkermeerweg and the Haarlemmerweg, which disappeared when the Bos en Lommer neighbourhood was built. A notweg is a country road for carrying the harvest from the fields; the Frisian word 'not' means 'harvest'. The term is common in Noord-Holland north of the IJ, also as notsloot for a waterway with the same purpose.

name: Nova Zemblastraat
en: An island in the Arctic Ocean (Novaya Zemlya). Barentsz and Heemskerck wintered there in 1596-1597 in their failed attempt to reach the Indies by the northern route. This street was first part of the Roggeveenstraat (council decision of 20 November 1878).

name: NSM-brug
en: Refers to the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, which was here until 1946. After merging with the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM) it continued as the NDSM.

name: Nuldernauwpad
en: A Veluwe border lake between Gelderland and Flevoland.

name: Nydia Ecuryhof
en: Nydia Maria Enrica Ecury (Oranjestad, 1926 - Willemstad, 2012) was a teacher, writer, translator and actress. She studied English and journalism in Canada. In 1957 she settled on Curaçao, where she taught at the Martinus-Mavo and the Nilda Pinto domestic science school, and also gave private lessons in Papiamentu. In 1967 she was one of the founders of the theatre group Thalia. She made her debut as a poet in 1972 and went on to publish several collections. In 1986 she also acted in the film Almacita di desolato. She received the Pierre Lauffer Prize in 1995 and the Cola Debrot Prize in 2007, as well as the Theatre Festival Award of Aruba and the prize of the Island Department of Cultural Affairs. Nydia Ecury was the sister of the resistance hero Boy Ecury, already honoured with a street name in Amsterdam.

name: Nydia Ecurystraat
en: Nydia Maria Enrica Ecury (Oranjestad, 1926 - Willemstad, 2012) was a teacher, writer, translator and actress. She studied English and journalism in Canada. In 1957 she settled on Curaçao, where she taught at the Martinus-Mavo and the Nilda Pinto domestic science school, and also gave private lessons in Papiamentu. In 1967 she was one of the founders of the theatre group Thalia. She made her debut as a poet in 1972 and went on to publish several collections. In 1986 she also acted in the film Almacita di desolato. She received the Pierre Lauffer Prize in 1995 and the Cola Debrot Prize in 2007, as well as the Theatre Festival Award of Aruba and the prize of the Island Department of Cultural Affairs. Nydia Ecury was the sister of the resistance hero Boy Ecury, already honoured with a street name in Amsterdam.

name: Obiplein
en: An island group in Indonesia, part of the Moluccas. The square was made in 1980 on the site of the former Obistraat (council decision of 26 January 1923).

name: Oceanenweg
en: The great oceans of the world: the Atlantic, the Indian and the Pacific.

name: Ochtenhof
en: A small village on the Waal in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

name: Octaanweg
en: A hydrocarbon (octane), a petroleum derivative.

name: Oderweg
en: The river on the border of Poland and Germany.

name: Oermilla Tewariestraat
en: Oermilla S. Radjaram Tewarie-Manichand (1922-1990), the first Hindustani woman to chair the women's organisation of the Sanatan Dharm, an important religious movement among Hindustani Surinamese. Between 1944 and 1968 she gave various religious and cultural lectures in Suriname.

name: Oesjesduiker
en: The name of this culvert comes from the sign 't Osje (the little ox) that once hung at a butcher's on the corner of the Oostenburgergracht.

name: Oetewalerbrug
en: This 1924 bridge is named after the village of Oetewaal, or Outewaal or Houtewaal, which once lay on the Zeedijk level with today's Muiderpoort. The village, mentioned as early as 1387, was burnt down by the Spanish in 1575 and ravaged by a storm flood in 1651, but rebuilt each time. In 1658 it was annexed by the municipality of Amsterdam. Before 1878 the Linnaeusstraat was called Oetewalerweg and was the road from Oetewaal to the Watergraafsmeer. The Oetewalerbrug is popularly also called the Hemabrug because the Hema store is nearby.

name: Oetewalerpad
en: The village of Oetewaal, or Outewaal or Houtewaal, which once lay on the Zeedijk level with today's Muiderpoort. The village, mentioned as early as 1387, was burnt down by the Spanish in 1575 and ravaged by a storm flood in 1651, but rebuilt each time. In 1658 Amsterdam annexed it in the fourth expansion. Before 1878 the Linnaeusstraat was called Oetewalerweg and was the road from Oetewaal to the Diemermeer (Watergraafsmeer). Today's Oetewalerstraat came within Amsterdam in the annexation of 1896 under the name Noordstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 16 June 1884).

name: Oetewalerstraat
en: The village of Oetewaal, or Outewaal or Houtewaal, which once lay on the Zeedijk level with today's Muiderpoort. The village, mentioned as early as 1387, was burnt down by the Spanish in 1575 and ravaged by a storm flood in 1651, but rebuilt each time. In 1658 Amsterdam annexed it in the fourth expansion. Before 1878 the Linnaeusstraat was called Oetewalerweg and was the road from Oetewaal to the Diemermeer (Watergraafsmeer). Today's Oetewalerstraat came within Amsterdam in the annexation of 1896 under the name Noordstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 16 June 1884).

name: Oetgensdwarsstraat
en: Frans Hendriks Oetgens (1559-1625), the city's master of works and several times burgomaster of Amsterdam, owned the land here around 1600. The former street names Oetgenspad (now Eerste Oosterparkstraat) and Oetgensachterpad also recall him. The new streets laid out in 1980 are on the site where the Royal Bavarian Brewery was built in 1864, in operation until 1927. Some of its buildings served as business premises until about 1955.

name: Oetgensstraat
en: Frans Hendriks Oetgens (1559-1625), the city's master of works and several times burgomaster of Amsterdam, owned the land here around 1600. The former street names Oetgenspad (now Eerste Oosterparkstraat) and Oetgensachterpad also recall him. The new streets laid out in 1980 are on the site where the Royal Bavarian Brewery was built in 1864, in operation until 1927. Some of its buildings served as business premises until about 1955.

name: Oeverlandenweg
en: A resident proposed naming a still unnamed space Oeverlandenweg. The Oeverlandenweg runs from the Adam Smithplein to the Oeverlanden (the riverbank lands) and is therefore seen as a fitting name for it.

name: Oeverpad
en: After its position: along and towards the bank (oever) of the Sloterplas.

name: Oeverparklaan
en: Refers to the Oeverpark, which this avenue runs along for its whole length.

name: Oeverzeggestraat
en: A kind of reed (sedge) that grows at the edge of ponds and in slow-flowing water.

name: Ogentrooststraat
en: A plant (eyebright) of the figwort family.

name: Ohmstraat
en: Georg S. Ohm (1787-1854), German physicist, who formulated the law of the strength of electric current (the ohm is a unit of electrical resistance).

name: Okeghemstraat
en: Johannes Ockeghem (1430-1495), Flemish composer, regarded as the chief master of the Netherlands School. He wrote masses, motets and chansons and is thought to have taught Obrecht.

name: Oldambtstraat
en: The eastern part of the province of Groningen. 'Old' is the northern and eastern Dutch form of 'oud' (old); 'ambt' or 'ambacht' means administrative district.

name: Oldenaller
en: A country house near Nijkerk (Gelderland), built in 1655 probably to a design by Jacob van Campen, on the site of an earlier castle. It was remodelled around 1850 by K.G. Zocher.

name: Oldengaarde
en: A Drenthe manor (havezate) near Dwingeloo, from 1717.

name: Oleanderstraat
en: The ornamental shrub.

name: Olga de Haasstraat
en: Olga de Haas was a Dutch ballet dancer.

name: Oliepalmstraat
en: A kind of palm. The oil palm yields palm oil, used among other things in margarine, soap, biscuits and as fuel.

name: Olifantswerf
en: After the former shipyard 'De Olyphant' (the elephant) that was here on Kattenburg.

name: Olmenweg
en: The broadleaf tree (elm), better known as iep.

name: Olof Palmeplein
en: Sven Olof Joachim Palme (1927-1986), Swedish politician of international stature, founder and chairman of the Palme Commission on disarmament and security. He fought hard against the apartheid regime in South Africa, and in the 1960s and 1970s campaigned with others against American action in Vietnam. He was murdered in 1986.
