name: Oltmansstraat
en: Jan Frederik Oltmans (1806-1854), writer of historical novels, among them 'De Schaapherder' (the shepherd).

name: Olympiakade
en: The sacred site in ancient Greece where the Olympic Games were first held, in 776 BC.

name: Olympiakanaal
en: The sacred site in ancient Greece where the Olympic Games were first held, in 776 BC.

name: Olympiaplein
en: The sacred site in ancient Greece where the Olympic Games were first held, in 776 BC.

name: Olympiastraat
en: The sacred site in ancient Greece where the Olympic Games were first held, in 776 BC.

name: Olympiaweg
en: The sacred site in ancient Greece where the Olympic Games were first held, in 776 BC.

name: Olympisch Stadion
en: The sacred site in ancient Greece where the Olympic Games were first held, in 776 BC.

name: Ombilinstraat
en: A river in central Sumatra, Indonesia.

name: Ommerenhof
en: A village in the Neder-Betuwe (Gelderland).

name: Omval
en: A spit of land between the Amstel and the ring canal of the Watergraafsmeer, so called since the seventeenth century or earlier after an 'omval' that stood there, that is, a tumbledown building or ruin. The name came over when this part of the municipality of Ouder-Amstel was transferred on 1 January 1921.

name: Omvalbrug
en: A spit of land between the Amstel and the ring canal of the Watergraafsmeer, so called since the seventeenth century or earlier after an 'omval' that stood there, that is, a tumbledown building or ruin. The name came over when this part of the municipality of Ouder-Amstel was transferred on 1 January 1921.

name: Onbekendegracht
en: The Onbekendegracht originally gave the former city carpentry yard access to the Amstel. A notarial deed of 1800 calls the canal 'het Onbekende of Amstelgragtje' (the unknown or Amstel little canal).

name: Onbekendegracht
en: The canal was dug to divert the Nieuwe Achtergracht. The name (unknown canal) is said to have arisen because the diversion meant the Nieuwe Achtergracht could no longer be seen from the Amstel. In 1948 one of the residents asked the burgomaster and aldermen to change the name, as people found it somewhat strange. Fortunately the request was not granted.

name: Onderlangs
en: Named after its position (below and along) relative to the ring dike of the Watergraafsmeer (here the Gooiseweg).

name: Onkelboerensteeg
en: After a seventeenth-century resident, Dirk Honckelboer; the oldest spelling is Onckelboerssteegje. Before that the alley was called Pleytstraat and Kijffstraat.

name: Onsenoort
en: A fourteenth-century castle at Nieuwkuijk near Vlijmen (Noord-Brabant), of which only a massive rectangular tower remains.

name: Onstein
en: A moated country house from 1711 near Vorden (Gelderland).

name: Oogststraat
en: The yield of the field crops (the harvest).

name: Ooievaarsweg
en: The bird (the crow).

name: Ookmeerweg
en: After the former polder, a drained lake north of the hamlet of Osdorp.

name: Oossaander Hoop
en: A ship of the Oostzaan shipowner Pieter Swan, which went whaling from 1769 to 1775 under the command of his brother Cornelis.

name: Oost-Indische Huisbrug
en: Named after the nearby Oost-Indisch Huis (East India House), on the corner of the Kloveniersburgwal and the Oude Hoogstraat.

name: Oostakkerstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of East Flanders.

name: Oosteinde
en: The name refers to its position relative to the Utrechtsepoort (Utrecht gate), which stood in the middle of the Frederiksplein, where the Paleis voor Volksvlijt was later built. The street ran along the east side at the end of the city (outside the gate, inside the city moat). The street on the other side was then named Westeinde.

name: Oostelijk Marktkanaal
en: It lies on the east side of the Central Market Halls.

name: Oostelijke Handelskade
en: The eastern harbour basin owed its existence to trade (handel). The road was built in 1875-1883. In 1919 part of it was renamed Piet Heinkade (council decision of 18 July 1919). Why the word Oostelijke (eastern) was added to the name does not appear from the correspondence that led to the naming; before it was named in 1883 the road was already called Handelskade. It was originally a quay along the closing dike of the Oosterdok.

name: Oostenburgerdwarsstraat
en: Oostenburg was the easternmost of the three islands (with Kattenburg and Wittenburg) brought within the city in the expansion of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. At first there were three streets from the canal, named after their position Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat (front, middle and back streets). In the first half of the twentieth century the Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to public traffic for the expansion of the Werkspoor company, and it was abolished in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abolished in 1985; the Compagniestraat now runs there. The disappearance of several shipyards freed land on which the Nieuwe Oostenburgerstraat and -dwarsstraat were laid out.

name: Oostenburgerdwarsvaart
en: Oostenburg was the easternmost of the three islands (with Kattenburg and Wittenburg) brought within the city in the expansion of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. en: Oostenburg was the easternmost of the three islands (with Kattenburg and Wittenburg) brought within the city in the expansion of 1658. Laying out the streets and building began in 1664. name: Ooster Ringdijk
en: After its position relative to the Watergraafsmeer. Before the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was annexed, the Ooster Ringdijk was called Noorder- and Zuider-Ringdijk. The Eerste Ringdijkstraat was then called Schoollaan, and earlier still the name Dielemanstraat seems to have been used. A Tweede Ringdijkstraat (formerly Dijklaan) has since disappeared entirely through demolition.

name: Oosterbeerbrug
en: Oosterbeer is a former bastion on which the De Gooyer mill stood for some time.

name: Oosterdok
en: The Oosterdok was created by a closing dike on the east side of the city, completed in 1832. The quay on and along this dike was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

name: Oosterdoksdoorgang
en: The water passage by the Oosterdokskade, which gives it its name.

name: Oosterdoksdraaibrug
en: This swing bridge is by the Oosterdok, hence the name.

name: Oosterdokskade
en: The Oosterdok was created by a closing dike on the east side of the city, completed in 1832. The quay on and along this dike was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

name: Oosterdoksstraat
en: The Oosterdok was created by a closing dike on the east side of the city, completed in 1832. The quay on and along this dike was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

name: Oosterendstraat
en: A village on the island of Texel.

name: Oosterlengte
en: The distance of a place in degrees east of the meridian taken as the first (eastern longitude).

name: Oostermeerstraat
en: A former country house on the Amstel.

name: Oosterpark
en: After its position in the eastern part of the city. The name at first applied only to the park, laid out from 1887 onwards. The road along the park was only named so in 1895 and was previously called Eerste Parkstraat.

name: Oostersekade
en: The origin of this name is unknown. Since the description 'east side of the Oudeschans' also occurs, the explanation may be that Oosterse was used for eastern. (The Oosterkerk was also called the Oosterse kerk.) Another suggestion is that there may have been a mooring here for ships in the Baltic (Oosterse) trade (compare the Texelse kade and the Gelderse kade).

name: Oosterspoorplein
en: The Oosterspoorweg (Eastern Railway), the line from Amsterdam to Amersfoort, opened in 1874 and extended to Zutphen in 1876, completing the connection with northern Germany.

name: Oostertocht
en: A tocht is a ditch connecting the polder ditches with the main polder canal.

name: Oostertoegang
en: The eastern entrance from the Oosterdok to the IJ.

name: Oosthuizenstraat
en: A village north-east of the Beemster (Noord-Holland).

name: Oostoever
en: After its position relative to the Sloterplas (the east bank).

name: Oostzaanstraat
en: The village of Oostzaan, east of the Zaan.

name: Oostzanerdijk
en: The part of the Waterland sea dike that originally belonged to the municipality of Oostzaan.

name: Opdijkstraat
en: A dike thrown up 'higher up' as a kind of second line of defence against the water.

name: Open Havenfront
en: A former open waterfront, filled in to build Centraal Station.

name: Openhartsteeg
en: Named after a gable stone showing an open heart with an orange. As early as the sixteenth century this was a sign of loyalty to the House of Orange. The alley was once also called Pottenbakkerssteeg (potters' alley).

name: Ophemerthof
en: A village on the Waal, south-west of Tiel (Gelderland).

name: Opheusdenhof
en: A village in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

name: Opijnenhof
en: A village in the Tielerwaard on the Waal, north-west of Zaltbommel (Gelderland).

name: Opmerkzaam
en: The group of women who regularly hold their silent march on the Plaza de Mayo in Buenos Aires (Argentina), wanting the truth about the fate of their husbands and children who disappeared under the generals' regime. Against the weapons of violence and empty talk, they show through their solidarity and persistence their struggle for truth, freedom and justice. Several streets around this square are named after the virtues they stand for (opmerkzaam = attentive).

name: Opveld
en: A castle in Heer (Limburg).

name: Oranje Nassaulaan
en: The House of Orange-Nassau is a branch of the House of Nassau.

name: Oranje-Vrijstaatkade
en: The Boer republic founded in 1854, which in 1899 allied itself with the Transvaal in the struggle against the British. The Orange Free State is today a province of the Republic of South Africa.

name: Oranje-Vrijstaatplein
en: The Boer republic founded in 1842, which in 1899 allied itself with the Transvaal in the struggle against the British. The Orange Free State is today a province of the Republic of South Africa.

name: Oranjebrug
en: This drawbridge takes its name from the street it lies in. The origin of the street name is uncertain; it may refer to the house 'de Prins van Oranje' that once stood here near the Haarlemmerdijk.

name: Oranjesluizen
en: After the House of Orange-Nassau, to which the royal family belongs. The first stone of the Oranjesluizen was laid by the then king, William III, on 29 April 1870.

name: Orcastraat
en: Also called killer whale, black with a white underside. It can grow to six metres long, with a dorsal fin of two metres.

name: Örehof
en: The öre is worth 1/100 of the standard currency of Sweden, Norway and Denmark (the krona or krone).

name: Orgeldraaierspad
en: Basket-making was originally a typical travelling trade. The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

name: Orionplantsoen
en: Orion is a conspicuous constellation on the celestial equator. In Greek mythology Orion was a hunter who pursued the Pleiades, was accidentally killed by Artemis and was then raised to the stars.

name: Orionstraat
en: A constellation (the Dolphin).

name: Orlyplein
en: The name of Paris's airport.

name: Ornsteinstraat
en: Leonard Salomon Ornstein (1880-1941), physicist, professor at Utrecht from 1915.

name: Orteliuskade
en: Abraham Ortelius (1527-1598), Flemish geographer, maker of a famous atlas.

name: Orteliuspad
en: Abraham Ortelius (1527-1598), Flemish geographer, maker of a famous atlas.

name: Orteliusstraat
en: Abraham Ortelius (1527-1598), Flemish geographer, maker of a famous atlas.

name: Ortler
en: A mountain peak in Italy, 3899 metres high.

name: Osdorper Ban
en: After the hamlet of Osdorp, shown on old maps as Oostdorp. Building of the Osdorp garden city began in 1957 and was practically complete by 1973. A ban is another word for a governor (landvoogd).

name: Osdorpergracht
en: After the hamlet of Osdorp, shown on old maps as Oostdorp. Building of the Osdorp garden city began in 1957 and was practically complete by 1973. The Osdorperweg was long called Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

name: Osdorperweg
en: After the hamlet of Osdorp, shown on old maps as Oostdorp. Building of the Osdorp garden city began in 1957 and was practically complete by 1973. The Osdorperweg was long called Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

name: Osdorperwegbrug
en: After the hamlet of Osdorp, shown on old maps as Oostdorp. Building of the Osdorp garden city began in 1957 and was practically complete by 1973. The Osdorperweg was long called Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

name: Osdorpplein
en: After the hamlet of Osdorp, shown on old maps as Oostdorp. Building of the Osdorp garden city began in 1957 and was practically complete by 1973. The Osdorperweg was long called Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

name: Ostwaldstraat
en: Wilhelm Ostwald (1853-1932), German chemist, who made important discoveries in colour theory. In 1909 he received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

name: Oterleekstraat
en: A village east of Alkmaar (Noord-Holland).

name: Otopeniweg
en: The name of Bucharest's airport.

name: Ottho Heldringstraat
en: Preacher (1804-1876), founder of a refuge for 'fallen women' and of the homes for neglected young people named after him.

name: Oturia
en: A mountain peak in Spain, 1920 metres high.

name: Ouborg
en: A fourteenth-century castle on the Swalm near Swalmen (Limburg), of which only the ruin of a massive octagonal tower remains.

name: Oud-Ehrenstein
en: Once a strong castle, of which medieval parts survive, on the road from Heerlen to Kerkrade (Limburg). Before 1363 this stein (fortified stone house) came into the possession of the noble Van Ederen family. The name passed to the castle and was shortened to Ehrenstein.

name: Oudaen
en: A knightly manor near Breukelen, on the right bank of the Vecht, partly still medieval and rebuilt in the seventeenth century. It is one of the few castles that escaped being burnt by French troops in 1672.

name: Oude Doelenstraat
en: The doelen were the places where the civic guard companies met and practised shooting at a target (doel). The Oude Doelenstraat was laid out on the site of the oldest doelen, from the fifteenth century. The Nieuwe Doelenstraat takes its name from the Kloveniersdoelen, which from 1522 stood where the Doelen Hotel is today.

name: Oude Haagsebrug
en: This bridge, now used as a bus lane, is named after the road it lies on. The road once led to The Hague as part of the former Rijksweg 4; since this has no longer been the case since 1966, the road is called the Oude (old) Haagseweg.

name: Oude Haagseweg
en: The main road to The Hague. The old Haagseweg now has a secondary role.

name: Oude Hoogstraat
en: These streets lie slightly higher (hoog) than those around them. The Oude Hoogstraat was laid out around 1490, the Nieuwe Hoogstraat a century later.

name: Oude Houthaven
en: Dug in 1876 for handling and storing timber.

name: Oude Kinkerbrug
en: Johannes Kinker (1764-1845) was a Dutch poet, philosopher and lawyer.

name: Oude Leliestraat
en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

name: Oude Looiersstraat
en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

name: Oude Meerhof
en: Named after the former Oude Meer (old lake), which lay in line with the still existing Nieuwe Meer.

name: Oude Nieuwstraat
en: By a council resolution of 1550 it was decided to lay out a new street by the Korsjespoort, which was simply called the 'nieuwe straat' (new street). Thirty years later the St Gertrude convent and the Onze Lieve Vrouwengasthuis, which stood between the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and the Nieuwendijk, were pulled down, and one of the streets laid out there was also called the 'nieuwe straat'. To tell the two new streets apart, in the first half of the seventeenth century their names were given the prefixes 'Oude' (old) and 'Nieuwe' (new), which they have kept to this day. The Nieuwe Nieuwstraat was at first also called Nieuwe Herenstraat.

name: Oude Spiegelstraat
en: After a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers who ran soap works. In the corner house of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel lived Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' in 1564 and Pieter Lourens Spiegel in 1608; the house was still called Hertspiegel in 1738. Building on the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat began in 1665, and here too a resident of the Spiegel family probably gave the name.

name: Oude Turfmarkt
en: The peat market (turfmarkt), held on this part of the former bank of the Amstel from 1564 to 1642. In 1913 the name was abolished and the quay added to the Rokin; in 1946 it got its historical name back.

name: Oude Waal
en: The walen were once (early seventeenth century) inlets of the IJ on the old side (Oude Waal) and the new side (Nieuwe Waal), where seagoing ships were laid up in winter. The Oude Waal silted up and became too shallow, and the Waalseiland was built up there in 1646. The quay on the city side kept the names Oude Waal and Kromme Waal (after its shape); on the Waalseiland came the names Binnenkant and Buitenkant (now Prins Hendrikkade). The Nieuwe Waal disappeared when the Westelijk Entrepotdok was built. Before 1912 the Waalsteeg was called Schippersstraatje; the name was changed because of confusion with the Schippersstraat.

name: Oude-IJselstraat
en: The Oude IJssel is a tributary of the IJssel.

name: Oudebrugsteeg
en: The alley led to the oldest bridge, laid over the Damrak in the early fourteenth century to link the old and new sides. The bridge went when this part of the Damrak was filled in; the two alleys still mark where it stood.

name: Oudekennissteeg
en: Since the older spelling is Oudekerksteeg, this is clearly a corruption of the name, dating from the eighteenth century. The alley is named after the nearby Oude Kerk. It was originally called Barvoetsbroeders-, Minderbroeders- or Grauwmonnikensteeg (Barefoot Friars', Friars Minor or Grey Friars' alley).

name: Oudekerksbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after the nearby Oude Kerk, the oldest church in Amsterdam, which probably dates from 1306 and is dedicated to St Nicholas.

name: Oudekerksplein
en: After the Oude Kerk here. The square was largely created by clearing the graveyard around the church, which was replaced in 1655 by a cemetery outside the city wall. The Oude Kerk is the oldest church in Amsterdam, probably dating from 1306, and dedicated to St Nicholas. The present tower dates from 1566, built by Joost Bilhamer.

name: Oudemanshof
en: Corneille A.J.A. Oudemans (1825-1906), botanist, professor in Amsterdam from 1859, whose works include the 'Flora van Nederland'.

name: Oudenaardeplantsoen
en: A Belgian town in the province of East Flanders.

name: Oudenrijnlaan
en: A village west of Utrecht.

name: Ouderkerkerdijk
en: Named after the village of Ouderkerk aan de Amstel, to which these roads lead. The prefix Korte (short) dates from 1956, after the dike was cut through for the industrial estate.

name: Oudeschans
en: A schans is an earthen rampart, and the Oudeschans was built as such around 1516 for defence against the Guelders. The rampart itself has long gone, but the water and quay have kept the name. The addition 'Oude' (old) was probably given when a new rampart was built around the enlarged city in the following century.

name: Oudezijds Achterburgwal
en: The canal behind (achter) the Voorburgwal on the old side. The little square in front of the Oude Waalse Kerk, until then part of this burgwal, was named Walenpleintje on 22 March 1978.

name: Oudezijds Achterburgwal
en: The canal behind (achter) the Voorburgwal on the old side.

name: Oudezijds Armsteeg
en: Arm here means bend. The alley leads to the bend in the Warmoesstraat.

name: Oudezijds Kolk
en: The basin (kolk) through which the Oudezijds Voorburgwal and Achterburgwal drained into the IJ.

name: Oudezijds Voorburgwal
en: The name, like that of the Oudezijds Voorburgwal, marks the canal in front of (voor) the town wall (burgwal) on the new side (Nieuwezijds) of the city. The Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal was filled in in 1884. Before that some stretches carried unofficial names from the markets held there: Pijpenmarkt, Boommarkt, Bloemmarkt and Postzegelmarkt (pipe, tree, flower and stamp markets).

name: Oudezijds Voorburgwal
en: Before 1385 the Amstel divided the city into two roughly equal parts, the old side (with the Oude Kerk) and the new side (with the Nieuwe Kerk). Each side was bounded by a burgwal (town moat). When new burgwallen were dug behind these around 1385, the existing one became the Voorburgwal (front) and the new one the Achterburgwal (back), on both the Oudezijde and the Nieuwezijde. After the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal was filled in in 1867 its name was changed to Spuistraat. The terms Oude- and Nieuwezijds date from the fifteenth century; before that people spoke of the Kerkzijde (church side) and the Windmolenzijde (windmill side). Parts of the Oudezijds Voorburgwal also had other unofficial names: by the Oudekerksplein was the Bierkaai (beer quay), and the east side was long called the Fluwelenburgwal (velvet burgwal).

name: Oudorperstraat
en: The Noord-Holland village of Oudorp.

name: Ouwerdingenpad
en: An area on Zuid-Beveland drowned in 1532.

name: Overamstelstraat
en: Named after the Overamstelsche Polder, which lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896; seen from the heart of that municipality, the polder lay on the other side (over) of the Amstel. The street originally ran as far as the Linnaeusstraat and was called Korte and Lange Overamstelstraat. When only the Korte Overamstelstraat remained after the Transvaalbuurt was built, the prefix 'Korte' was abolished in 1913.

name: Overbrakerpad
en: Named after the Overbraker Binnenpolder. From 1943 to about 1960 there was also an Overbrakerweg (in the Overbraker Buitenpolder), but it disappeared when the Sloterdijk industrial estate was built.

name: Overdam
en: Once a noble house, later a farm, on the Vecht between Weesp and Nigtevecht (Utrecht).

name: Overflakkeestraat
en: Part of the Zuid-Holland island of Goeree-Overflakkee.

name: Overhaalsgang
en: Originally an alley (waaigat) off the Hoogte Kadijk, which in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries gave access to the ferry (overhaal) across the Nieuwe Vaart, abolished around 1877 when a railway was built along the Wittenburgergracht. There is now a fixed crossing where the old ferry was.

name: Overhaalstraat
en: In traffic terms an overhaal is a ferry.

name: Overhoeksparklaan
en: On this site stands the high office tower of the same name that Arthur Staal designed for Shell in 1966. The term 'overhoeks', meaning 'set diagonally', refers to the building's orientation to the city and the water.

name: Overhoeksplein
en: On this site stands the high office tower of the same name that Arthur Staal designed for Shell in 1966. The term 'overhoeks', meaning 'set diagonally', refers to the building's orientation to the city and the water.

name: Overijsselweg
en: The province (Overijssel). Several streets nearby are named after castles in Overijssel.

name: Overleg
en: Consultation (overleg) with parties inside and outside the collective: one of the virtues of the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo, after which the streets around the Dwaze Moedersplein are named.

name: Overpeltstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Overschiebrug-Noord
en: The former village in Zuid-Holland (Overschie), part of Rotterdam since 1941.

name: Overschiebrug-Zuid
en: The former village in Zuid-Holland (Overschie), part of Rotterdam since 1941.

name: Overschiestraat
en: The former village in Zuid-Holland (Overschie), part of Rotterdam since 1941.

name: Overslag
en: The transfer of goods from seagoing ships to inland vessels and vice versa (transhipment).

name: Overslaghof
en: The transfer of goods from seagoing ships to inland vessels and vice versa (transhipment).

name: Overtoom
en: Named after the overtoom (a dam over which boats were hauled) built in the Schinkel in the fourteenth century. Until it was filled in in 1904 the Overtoom was a canal, the Heiligewegse or Overtoomse vaart. The southern quay, as far as it lay in Amsterdam, was called Vondelkade (council decision of 29 September 1875). The north side (the quiet side) has always been called Overtoom.

name: Overveenstraat
en: A village near Haarlem (Noord-Holland).

name: Overvoorde
en: An old noble house near Rijswijk (Zuid-Holland).

name: Overzichtweg
en: A former country estate on the Schagerlaan, built around 1701 by Jacob Pauw, who named it Groenhoven. A later owner changed the name to Oversigt (overview). The estate was demolished in 1804. The Pauwenlaan that once lay west of the Schagerlaan was named after this Jacob Pauw.

name: P. Dijkstraplein
en: P. Dijkstra (1891-1957), director of the Koninklijke Nederlandsche Stoomboot-Maatschappij and, from 1945 to 1955, director of the Holland Afrika Lijn.

name: P. Hans Frankfurthersingel
en: P. Hans Frankfurther (1932-1996) worked for more than thirty years for the village of Sloten and the Sloten-Oud Osdorp village council. Thanks partly to his efforts the Sloten windmill returned to the district in 1991. In 1994 and 1995 he successfully coordinated the referendum campaign to save the Vrije Geer meadow.

name: P. Lieftinckstraat
en: Pieter Lieftinck (1902-1987), economist and politician of the Labour Party (PvdA), Minister of Finance from 1945 to 1952, famous for his currency reform in the summer of 1945. The street was at first mistakenly named P. Lieftingstraat; the error was corrected by council decision of 13 June 1990.

name: P.E. Tegelbergplein
en: Petrus Emelius Tegelberg (1838-1917), appointed co-director of the Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland' in 1873, board member of the Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij and treasurer of the Amsterdam Chamber of Commerce.

name: P.J. Oudstraat
en: Pieter Jacob Oud (1886-1968), liberal statesman, Minister of Finance in Colijn's extra-parliamentary crisis cabinets, known for his austerity policy. In 1948 he co-founded the VVD and chaired its group in the House of Representatives. He was burgomaster of Rotterdam in 1938-1941 and 1945-1952.

name: P.L. Marnettestraat
en: Pieter Lucas Marnette (1888-1948), Amsterdam architect, much of whose work, such as the school on the Schermerstraat, belongs to the Amsterdam School. At the Public Works department he designed street furniture.

name: Paalbergweg
en: The name of a hill between Ermelo and Speulde (Gelderland).

name: Paardekraalstraat
en: A place in the Transvaal (South Africa) where in 1880 the Transvaal Boers held a people's assembly and resolved to resist the threat of British rule. The stretch between the Transvaalkade and the Transvaalstraat was named Eerste Ringkadedwarsstraat by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 22 August 1890), changed to Polderstraat on 16 October 1901, and added to the Paardekraalstraat in 1912.

name: Paardenstraat
en: In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries this street and the nearby Wagenstraat were home to carters, livery-stable keepers and coachmen. They lie near the Rembrandtplein, where markets used to be held, and earlier there was a wagon square near the Regulierspoort (Muntplein).

name: Paasbergpad
en: Refers to the Paasberg, a hill 80 metres high in the Twente municipality of Losser.

name: Paasheuvelweg
en: A hill near Vierhouten (Gelderland).

name: Pablo Nerudalaan
en: Chilean poet (1904-1973), who received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971.

name: Pacayastraat
en: A mountain (volcano) in Guatemala.

name: Padangstraat
en: A port on the west coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

name: Paerlduiker
en: Takes its name from the brewery 'De Paerl' (the pearl), built on Wittenburg in the middle of the seventeenth century by Reinst and Grootenhuizen.

name: Pakingehof
en: A church village drowned in 1377 in the Braakman, an inlet of the Westerschelde (Zeeuws-Vlaanderen) that has since been reclaimed.

name: Paladruhof
en: The lake, Lac de Paladru, in south-east France, in the Isère department.

name: Palamedesstraat
en: 'Palamedes, of vermoorde onnooselheyt' (Palamedes, or murdered innocence), a tragedy by Vondel about Van Oldenbarnevelt, written in 1626 after Maurits's death. The part of the Overtoom off which this street runs was formerly called Vondelkade. Until 1890 the Palamedesstraat was a private street, named by the builder; when the municipality took it over, the name was kept.

name: Paleis voor Volksvlijtbrug
en: This bridge is named after the Paleis voor Volksvlijt (Palace of Industry), which burnt down in 1929 and stood where De Nederlandsche Bank is now.

name: Paleisstraat
en: Takes its name from the City Hall built in 1648, the Royal Palace since 1808. Before 1875 the street was called Gasthuisstraat, after the city's oldest hospital, from the fourteenth century, and Stilsteeg (for which no explanation can be given). Another part was called Korte Gasthuismolensteeg before 1875.

name: Palembangstraat
en: A city on Sumatra (Indonesia).

name: Palestrinastraat
en: Giovanni Palestrina (1525-1594), Italian composer of sacred music, organist and choirmaster.

name: Paletstraat
en: A painter's tool: the little board on which the painter mixes colours (the palette).

name: Palmdwarsstraat
en: Refers to the palm tree.

name: Palmgracht
en: Refers to the palm tree.

name: Palmstraat
en: Refers to the palm tree.

name: Pamirstraat
en: Mountains in Tajikistan and Afghanistan.

name: Pampuslaan
en: The name of an artificial island in the IJsselmeer east of Amsterdam. At low water ships often had to wait a long time until the water was high enough to sail over the sandbank to Amsterdam; the expression 'voor Pampus liggen' (lying before Pampus, meaning dead to the world) comes from this.

name: Panamakade
en: After the Panama Canal, dug between 1900 and 1914 through the Isthmus of Panama (Central America).

name: Panamalaan
en: After the Panama Canal, dug between 1900 and 1914 through the Isthmus of Panama (Central America).

name: Panchulisteeg
en: Panchuli is a mountain range in the Himalayas.

name: Pancrasstraat
en: Gerbrand Claesz Pancras (1591-1649), Amsterdam soap-boiler, burgomaster of the city from 1639 to 1649. When it was laid out the name was set as Pancraskade (council decision of 15 November 1876); after the canal was filled in in 1908 the name was adjusted.

name: Pandimsteeg
en: Pandim is a mountain range in India.

name: Pandorinastraat
en: A microscopic water plant: a colony-forming green alga enclosed in a jelly sheath, which thanks to its chlorophyll can assimilate carbon dioxide.

name: Pannerdenstraat
en: A village on the Rhine (Gelderland).

name: Papa Koendersstraat
en: Julius Gustaaf Arnout Koenders, better known as Papa Koenders (Paramaribo, 1886 - Paramaribo, 1957), was a teacher and a campaigner for Sranantongo. He was, in his own words, 'the grandson of grandparents who were slaves'. With his association Pohama, founded in 1944, he promoted Sranan and Creole culture, and he founded the monthly Foetoe-boi, published from 1946 to 1956. In 1943 he published Foe memre wi afo, 1 juli 1863-1943 (to remember our ancestors), in 1944 60 moi en bekentie singie na Sranantongo (60 beautiful and well-known songs in Sranan), and in 1945 Aksie mie, mie sa piekie joe foe wie skien (ask me, I will answer you about the human body). Koenders had a great influence on other well-known Surinamese writers such as Eddy Bruma, Trefossa and Michaël Slory.

name: Papaverhoek
en: The plant (poppy), wild and cultivated, also called klaproos.

name: Papaverkanaal
en: The plant (poppy), wild and cultivated, also called klaproos.

name: Papaverweg
en: The plant (poppy), wild and cultivated, also called klaproos.

name: Papenbrugsteeg
en: After the Papenbrug, which crossed the Damrak here before it was partly filled in and was built shortly before 1475. According to a sixteenth-century story an old, decayed bridge lay here over the Damrak, which some clergymen (papen) set on fire one Shrove Tuesday; the repaired or rebuilt bridge was therefore called the Papenbrug.

name: Papendrechtstraat
en: A village on the Beneden-Merwede, opposite Dordrecht (Zuid-Holland).

name: Papiermolensluis
en: The name of this fixed bridge comes from the sign 'De Papiermolen' (the paper mill) on the corner house, where a paper seller lived.

name: Papierweg
en: The product (paper), which is handled in the port of Amsterdam.

name: Paradijsappelstraat
en: A very old apple from the northern Netherlands, mainly red in colour.

name: Paradijsplein
en: The word (paradise), of Old Persian origin, means 'surrounded by a wall'. It often means a garden, but first of all it is a world where existence is peaceful and timeless.

name: Paramariboplein
en: The capital of Suriname.

name: Paramaribostraat
en: The capital of Suriname.

name: Parelstraat
en: Named after the former Parelbrug between the Kattenburgergracht and the Wittenburgergracht, and after the seventeenth-century brewery De Parel (the pearl).

name: Parkhof
en: The green area around the court.

name: Parlevinker
en: A parlevinker is a trader who sells goods from a small boat to the ships.

name: Parlevinkerpad
en: A parlevinker is a trader who sells goods from a small boat to the ships.

name: Parmenidesstraat
en: Greek philosopher (540-460 BC), the leading figure of the Eleatic school, which taught the unity of all nature.

name: Parnassusweg
en: A mountain in Greece, in Greek mythology the home of Apollo and the Muses. Today used figuratively for the realm of poetry.

name: Parosstraat
en: A Greek island in the Aegean Sea, part of the Cyclades group. All the Cyclades lie in a circle (Ancient Greek: kyklos) around Delos, an important Greek sanctuary in antiquity.

name: Parthenonhof
en: The great Doric temple on the Acropolis of Athens, built in 447-432 BC in honour of the city goddess Athena, the high point of Greek architecture for its unsurpassed harmonious proportions.

name: Pascalstraat
en: Blaise Pascal (1623-1662), French philosopher, mathematician and physicist. Hydraulics rests on Pascal's law.

name: Passeerdersgracht
en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

name: Passeerdersstraat
en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

name: Passtukkenpad
en: Probably named after the spacer piece (passtuk) used to fill or measure gaps between objects.

name: Pastelstraat
en: A colour crayon (pastel); the name is also given to the finished work, the crayon drawing.

name: Pasteurstraat
en: Louis Pasteur (1822-1895), French chemist, who proved that various diseases are caused by bacteria, developed a vaccine against rabies and a method of killing bacteria (pasteurisation). Before 1922 this was the Prins Hendrikstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 31 January 1902).

name: Pastoorsbrug
en: The origin of this fixed bridge's name (pastor's bridge) is not known for certain. Perhaps the former Roman Catholic clandestine church 'De Zaaier' at Keizersgracht 22 had something to do with it.

name: Pasubio
en: A mountain peak in Italy, 2236 metres high.

name: Paterslaan
en: According to old deeds of sale, the name of a meadow along the Wijkergouw in Schellingwoude.

name: Patrice Lumumbastraat
en: The first prime minister of Congo, who took office on 23 June 1960; barely a week later the former Belgian colony was an independent republic. Lumumba was hated in Belgium and Congo for his fierce speech about the injustices of colonial rule. He held office only until 5 September 1960, and was murdered on 17 January 1961.

name: Patroclosstraat
en: A Greek hero of the Trojan War (Patroclus), sung by Homer.

name: Paul Christiaan Fluhof
en: Paul Christiaan Flu (Paramaribo, 1884 - Leiden, 1945) was a physician, professor of tropical hygiene and rector magnificus of Leiden University. Highly gifted, he qualified as a doctor at twenty at the Medical School in Paramaribo and then went to the Netherlands to train further. He worked in Suriname, the Netherlands and Indonesia. In Suriname too he achieved a great deal: he laid the foundation of the water supply network and helped many people through his great knowledge of tropical diseases. His pioneering work was noticed, and in 1911 he was made a Knight of the Order of Orange-Nassau. He then worked in Indonesia, where he and his family, despite their dark skin, belonged to the European elite. In 1921 he became professor of Tropical Hygiene at Leiden and director of the newly founded Institute of Tropical Medicine, and in 1938 rector magnificus of Leiden University. During the German occupation in the Second World War he stood up for the university's freedom. In August 1942 Flu was placed under house arrest, and in January 1944 taken to a concentration camp. In the same period the occupiers murdered his eldest son. When Flu was able to return he was badly weakened by physical hardship, and above all broken by his son's death. He died on 19 December 1945, a few months after Leiden University reopened, aged 61.

name: Paul Christiaan Flustraat
en: Paul Christiaan Flu (Paramaribo, 1884 - Leiden, 1945) was a physician, professor of tropical hygiene and rector magnificus of Leiden University. Highly gifted, he qualified as a doctor at twenty at the Medical School in Paramaribo and then went to the Netherlands to train further. He worked in Suriname, the Netherlands and Indonesia. In Suriname too he achieved a great deal: he laid the foundation of the water supply network and helped many people through his great knowledge of tropical diseases. His pioneering work was noticed, and in 1911 he was made a Knight of the Order of Orange-Nassau. He then worked in Indonesia, where he and his family, despite their dark skin, belonged to the European elite. In 1921 he became professor of Tropical Hygiene at Leiden and director of the newly founded Institute of Tropical Medicine, and in 1938 rector magnificus of Leiden University. During the German occupation in the Second World War he stood up for the university's freedom. In August 1942 Flu was placed under house arrest, and in January 1944 taken to a concentration camp. In the same period the occupiers murdered his eldest son. When Flu was able to return he was badly weakened by physical hardship, and above all broken by his son's death. He died on 19 December 1945, a few months after Leiden University reopened, aged 61.

name: Paul Hufkade
en: Photographer (1924-2002), famous for his staged studio pictures, glamour portraits, advertising campaigns and glossy fashion features.

name: Paul Scholtenstraat
en: Legal scholar (1875-1946), professor at the University of Amsterdam from 1907, known for his editions of the law of persons and the law of property.

name: Paul Schuitemahof
en: Graphic designer and photographer (1897-1973), known for his powerful typographic designs. After 1926 he brought photographic elements into his designs, and was among the first designers to use photomontage in industrial design. A representative of the New Photography.

name: Paul van Vlissingenstraat
en: Paul Fentener van Vlissingen was a Dutch entrepreneur, columnist, writer, conservationist and philanthropist, a scion of the patrician Van Vlissingen family.

name: Paulus Potterstraat
en: Painter (1625-1654), mainly of landscapes and animals.

name: Paulus van Hemertstraat
en: Theologian and philosopher (1756-1825), who resigned as a preacher because of objections to the doctrine of predestination and afterwards devoted himself mainly to the philosophy of Kant.

name: Pauwels-Van Bienestraat
en: The artist couple Désiré Pauwels (1861-1942) and Sophie van Biene (1854-1907). Pauwels was a famous singer, first at the French Opera in The Hague and later at the Dutch Opera; Sophie van Biene was an actress with the Nederlandsch Tooneel.

name: Pauwenpad
en: The Pauwenlaan once ran roughly here, named after Jacob Pauw, who built a country estate nearby around 1701. The Pauwenlaan disappeared when the railway to Utrecht was built.

name: Pazzanistraat
en: Julius Pazzani, engineer, director of the Imperial Continental Gas Association, responsible for the technical fitting-out of the Westergasfabriek buildings. The street lies on the site of this former gasworks.

name: Pedro de Medinalaan
en: Spanish cosmographer (1493-1567), who in 1545 published the book 'Arte de Navegar'. A Dutch translation appeared in 1580 as 'De zeevaert oft conste van ter zee te varen' (seafaring, or the art of sailing at sea).

name: Pedro Nunesstraat
en: Portuguese mathematician (1502-1578), royal cosmographer from 1529, who published on the graduated arc; his findings were of practical use in navigation.

name: Peelstraat
en: A region on the border of Noord-Brabant and Limburg, originally a poor area of heath and peat, now entirely cultivated. The last bit of the Peel survives as a nature reserve, the Grote Peel.

name: Pegasusstraat
en: A constellation (the Dolphin).

name: Pekelharingstraat
en: Cornelis Adrianus Pekelharing (1848-1922), physician, professor at Utrecht from 1881, known among other things for his research on beriberi.

name: Pekkendam
en: A former estate near Diepenheim (Overijssel).

name: Pelerin
en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of Le Pellerin, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Pelikaanbrug
en: After the nearby warehouse d'Peliekaan (the pelican) at Hoogte Kadijk 51.

name: Pelikaanstraat
en: The bird (the crow).

name: Pelistersteeg
en: Pelister is a mountain range in North Macedonia.

name: Penninkshof
en: A historical Rijnland name, still found in Penningsveer on the Liede (between Haarlem and Spaarnwoude).

name: Pennyhof
en: The penny is worth 1/100 of the standard currency of Great Britain (the pound sterling).

name: Penseelstraat
en: A painting and drawing tool, a thin brush.

name: Peperstraat
en: After the Peperwerf (pepper yard), which lay where the Peperstraat is now and belonged to the warehouses of the Dutch East India Company, where imported spices among other things were stored.

name: Pereboomsloot
en: The fruit of the pear tree.

name: Perenpad
en: The fruit of the pear tree.

name: Pernaubrug
en: Pernau was the German name for the Estonian port of Pärnu on the Gulf of Riga. The names in the Houthavens are taken from places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Pernaugracht
en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

name: Perseusstraat
en: A constellation in the northern Milky Way.

name: Persijn
en: A sixteenth-century castle near Wassenaar (Zuid-Holland), demolished in the eighteenth century, named after the Hague branch of the Persijn family.

name: Persstraat
en: A reference to the waste-paper company (pers = press) on the Cruquius site until the area was redeveloped in the twenty-first century.

name: Perzikstraat
en: The fruit of the peach tree.

name: Pesetalaan
en: The currency of Spain before the euro (the peseta).

name: Pestalozzihof
en: Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi (1746-1827), Swiss educator influenced by Rousseau, who renewed the methods of elementary education.

name: Pesthuysbrug
en: Named after the old pest house, built in 1635 in the Stads- or Godshuispolder, at first only for plague sufferers and later also for patients with dysentery and typhus and the insane. After much rebuilding it became the Wilhelmina Gasthuis in 1891. The last part of the old pest house was demolished in 1925.

name: Petemayenbrug
en: The name of this double drawbridge is probably a corruption of Petemoeienbrug. A petemoei is a (god)aunt, and the word was once also used for a little old woman.

name: Peter Martensstraat
en: Photographer (1937-1992), a socially engaged photojournalist who photographed above all human misery, with form subordinate to content. A photo had to shock.

name: Peter Postbrug
en: Peter Post (1933-2011). In 1949 this born-and-bred Amsterdammer won his first cycling title, at the Amsterdam butcher's boys' championship, and went on as a track cyclist to become the undisputed 'Emperor of the Six-Day Races'. As a road cyclist he won Paris-Roubaix in 1964. As team manager he led Joop Zoetemelk to overall victory in the Tour de France in 1980.

name: Peter Schatstraat
en: Composer (1935-2003) of operas and orchestral and choral works, regarded as the greatest talent of his generation for the development of Dutch music. In 1973 he received the prestigious Matthijs Vermeulen Prize.

name: Peter van Anrooystraat
en: Conductor and composer (1879-1954), who conducted several orchestras and is known as a composer for his Piet Hein Rhapsody. A pioneer of youth concerts.

name: Peter Wotkehof
en: Austrian photographer (1800-1870), who settled in Rotterdam in 1854 and as one of the first practitioners in the Netherlands made daguerreotypes, above all of musicians, and panoramas of Rotterdam.

name: Petroleumhaven
en: After the harbour here for unloading oil tankers and the sites for storing petroleum products. The harbour came into use in 1888. The first part of the road was earlier named Vlothavenweg (council decision of 21 January 1953).

name: Petroleumhavenweg
en: After the harbour here for unloading oil tankers and the sites for storing petroleum products. The harbour came into use in 1888. The first part of the road was earlier named Vlothavenweg (council decision of 21 January 1953).

name: Petrus Blokhof
en: Historian (1855-1929), professor at Leiden, author of 'Geschiedenis van het Nederlandsche volk' (history of the Dutch people) and of a social history of Leiden.

name: Pettenstraat
en: A village at the northern end of the Hondsbossche Zeewering (Noord-Holland).

name: Peursumstraat
en: A village in the Alblasserwaard on the little river Giessen (Zuid-Holland).

name: Philip Vingboonsstraat
en: Architect (c. 1607-1678), who used the raised neck gable and pilasters. His buildings include many fine canal houses on the Herengracht and Keizersgracht, the Rokin and the Singel.

name: Pia Beckbrug
en: Pieternella (Pia) Beck (1926-2009) was a Dutch jazz pianist, whom her colleague Oscar Peterson called the best woman jazz pianist in the world. She was one of the first artists to be open about being a lesbian. In the Park Haagseweg all the streets are named after famous jazz musicians.

name: Piarcoplein
en: The name of the airport of Port of Spain, Trinidad.

name: Pienemanstraat
en: Nicolaas Pieneman (1810-1860), history and portrait painter, who succeeded his father J.W. Pieneman as chairman of the society of artists and art lovers 'Maatschappij Arti et Amicitiae', founded in 1839.

name: Pier Afrika
en: The continent.

name: Pier Azië
en: The largest of the continents.

name: Pier Europa
en: The continent.

name: Pier Panderstraat
en: Frisian sculptor (1864-1919). Part of his work is collected in the Pier Pander Temple in Leeuwarden.

name: Pierre Cuypershof
en: Petrus J. Cuypers (1827-1921), architect and creator of Dutch Gothic Revival. His buildings include the Rijksmuseum (1885), Centraal Station (1889) and the Vondelkerk (1878).

name: Pierre Lallementstraat
en: French mechanic (1843-1891). Lallement, a maker of prams, saw a running machine pass by in 1862 and had the idea of adding pedals to the front wheel, an invention he patented four years later. He is therefore sometimes seen as the inventor of the pedal bicycle.

name: Pierre Laufferstraat
en: Pierre A. Lauffer (Curaçao, 1920 - Curaçao, 1981) was a writer, poet and cultural campaigner for the preservation of his mother tongue, Papiamentu. He wrote stories from an early age and remained active as an author. His first collection of poems, entirely in Papiamentu, Patria (fatherland), appeared in 1944; in language and subject it was a turning point in the literature. Lauffer is sometimes called the national poet of Curaçao because he worked hard to preserve the folklore and history of his island. He saw Papiamentu as the bearer of culture, with a fundamental role in Curaçao's search for autonomy. In 1969 he was awarded the Cola Debrot Prize for his literary achievement.

name: Piet Bakkerbrug
en: Piet Bakker was a writer and journalist. Besides his love of De Pijp, he also put his love of Amsterdam into words in books such as 'Amsterdam zoals het leeft en werkt' (Amsterdam as it lives and works, 1933) and 'Gids voor Amsterdam' (guide to Amsterdam, 1937). But above all he gave Amsterdam its most iconic 'little darling' in Ciske de Rat, to whom two successful films and a musical have been devoted.

name: Piet Dickentmanbrug
en: Pieter Casper Johan Dickentman (1879-1950) was an Amsterdam cyclist, the first professional stayer (motor-paced rider) in the Netherlands, and world champion in 1903.

name: Piet Gijzenbrugstraat
en: A bridge over the Leidse Trekvaart near Noordwijkerhout. The name Piet Gijzenbrug passed to the hamlet around the bridge.

name: Piet Heinkade
en: Pieter Pieterszoon Heyn (1577-1629), vice-admiral in the service of the West India Company, known for capturing the Spanish silver fleet in 1628 in the bay of Matanzas (Cuba).

name: Piet Heintunnel
en: Pieter Pieterszoon Heyn (1577-1629), vice-admiral in the service of the West India Company, known for capturing the Spanish silver fleet in 1628 in the bay of Matanzas (Cuba).

name: Piet Keizerbrug
en: Piet Keizer, born 14 June 1943 in Amsterdam, died 10 February 2017 in Amsterdam. Forward for Ajax 1961-1974, with 365 league matches (146 goals). Six times Dutch champion, five times KNVB Cup winner, three times winner of the European Cup, twice winner of the European Super Cup, once winner of the Intertoto Cup and once of the Intercontinental Cup. Piet Keizer won 34 caps and never played for any club but Ajax. In 1969 Ajax became the first Dutch club to reach the final of the prestigious European Cup, today's Champions League. Ajax lost that final, but two years later, in 1971, won the most important prize in football after all. In the two following years Ajax retained the title, confirming itself as the standard-bearer of Dutch football. Not only the titles but the way they were won, with modern, attacking football, made Ajax an international sensation. Coach Rinus Michels moulded this rare concentration of talent into a legendary team that was both untouchable and trend-setting at home and abroad.

name: Piet Kranenbergpad
en: Ajax 1961-1974, 365 league matches (146 goals). Six times Dutch champion, five times KNVB Cup winner, three times winner of the European Cup, twice winner of the European Super Cup, once winner of the Intertoto Cup and once of the Intercontinental Cup. Piet Keizer won 34 caps and never played for any club but Ajax. In 1969 Ajax became the first Dutch club to reach the final of the prestigious European Cup, today's Champions League. Ajax lost that final, but two years later, in 1971, won the most important prize in football after all. In the two following years Ajax retained the title, confirming itself as the standard-bearer of Dutch football. Not only the titles but the way they were won, with modern, attacking football, made Ajax an international sensation. Coach Rinus Michels moulded this rare concentration of talent into a legendary team that was both untouchable and trend-setting at home and abroad.

name: Piet Meerburgbrug
en: This bridge is named after Piet Meerburg, born in De Bilt in 1919 and died in Amsterdam in 2010. During the Second World War he was involved in rescuing Jewish children, for which he received the Yad Vashem distinction; one of those children was the later burgomaster Ed van Thijn. With Lau Mazirel and Walter Süskind, among others, he rescued many adults and children during the German occupation from the Hollandsche Schouwburg and the crèche opposite it. He was also one of the founders of the nearby Kriterion cinema, which is run by students of the University of Amsterdam. He was also a prominent theatre impresario in Amsterdam, for many years director of the Nieuwe de la Mar theatre, and producer of the musical My Fair Lady.

name: Piet Moeskopspad
en: Pieter Daniel Moeskops (1893-1964), cyclist, five times world sprint champion in the 1920s.

name: Piet Mondriaanplein
en: Painter (1872-1944), who lived in the United States after 1940. A pioneer of abstract art and leader of Neo-Plasticism.

name: Piet Mondriaanstraat
en: Painter (1872-1944), who lived in the United States after 1940. A pioneer of abstract art and leader of Neo-Plasticism.

name: Piet Nakstraat
en: Pieter Frederik Willem Nak (1906-1996), who worked for the city cleansing department and was a central figure in the clandestine Communist Party. With his colleague Willem Kraan he initiated the February Strike of 1941. In the 1960s he managed to broaden the Vietnam movement, which led to general rejection of American action there.

name: Piet Peelenbrug
en: This bridge is named after Piet Peelen (1922-1978), who worked in the Bridges department. He worked to improve the quality of life in Osdorp, especially in matters of traffic.

name: Piet Wiedijkstraat
en: especially in matters of traffic.

name: Piet Zwarthof
en: Photographer, typographer and industrial designer (1885-1977), a pioneer of the 'New Photography' and modern typography. He rejected traditional typographic rules and used the basic principles of Constructivism instead. His work is recognisable by its primary colours, geometric shapes, repeated word patterns, taut diagonal lettering and early use of photomontage.

name: Pieter A. van Heijningestraat
en: Pieter Adrianus van Heijninge (1903-1942), resistance fighter, who distributed clandestine material, raised money for the resistance and helped instigate the February Strike of 1941. He was arrested in 1941 and executed by firing squad in Woudenberg on 16 October 1942.

name: Pieter Aertszstraat
en: Painter (1508-1575) of genre pieces and church interiors. Before 1919 the street was called Nieuwe Tolstraat.

name: Pieter Baststraat
en: Pieter Bast (c. 1550-1605), Dutch engraver and draughtsman, a child of the well-known Plantin printing family.

name: Pieter Boorsmapad
en: Amateur historian (1871-1951), interested in the history of the Zaan region, who laid the foundation for the systematic study of the history of the Zaan windmills.

name: Pieter Borstraat
en: Pieter Christiaanszoon Bor (1559-1635), historian and Receiver of Holland, author of 'De Nederlandsche oorlogen' (the Netherlands wars).

name: Pieter Buyskensstraat
en: A Beggar captain in the revolt of Enkhuizen (1534-1606).

name: Pieter Calandlaan
en: Hydraulic engineer (1826-1902), whose name is linked above all with building the Nieuwe Waterweg from Rotterdam to Hoek van Holland (1866-1872).

name: Pieter Cornelisz. Hooftstraat
en: One of the great men of letters of the seventeenth century (1581-1647), who wrote poetry and plays, among them 'Granida' and 'Warenar'. Prince Maurits appointed him Drost (bailiff) of Muiden, and for many years the Muiderslot was then the gathering place of literary figures.

name: Pieter de Hoochstraat
en: Painter (1629-after 1679), especially of domestic interiors.

name: Pieter Goemansbrug
en: On this fixed bridge Pieter Goemans (Peter Shott), who lived from 1925 to 2000, found the inspiration in the 1950s for his song 'Aan de Amsterdamse grachten' (on the Amsterdam canals). A plaque on the bridge recalls this.

name: Pieter Goosstraat
en: Mapmaker (c. 1616-1675) in the service of the VOC, whose work included small-scale sea charts on which the course to the Dutch East Indies could be plotted.

name: Pieter Holmplein
en: Swedish seaman (c. 1686-1776) and teacher of navigation, who settled in Amsterdam, first in the Korsjespoortsteeg and later in the Kattegat. He was an expert in calculating course and distance, and in 1748 published his well-known 'Stuurmans zeemeeter' (navigator's sea-measurer).

name: Pieter Holmstraat
en: Swedish seaman (c. 1686-1776) and teacher of navigation, who settled in Amsterdam, first in the Korsjespoortsteeg and later in the Kattegat. He was an expert in calculating course and distance, and in 1748 published his well-known 'Stuurmans zeemeeter' (navigator's sea-measurer).

name: Pieter Jacobszdwarsstraat
en: A landowner who lived here in the late fourteenth and early fifteenth centuries. The little street was then called Gasthuissteeg, but was later named after him.

name: Pieter Jacobszstraat
en: A landowner who lived here in the late fourteenth and early fifteenth centuries. The little street was then called Gasthuissteeg, but was later named after him.

name: Pieter Langendijkstraat
en: Man of letters and playwright (1683-1756), whose works include 'Het wederzijds huwelijksbedrog' (mutual marriage deceit) and 'Krelis Louwen'. The street was first named without the first name (1900), but people sometimes corrupted that into Lange Dijkstraat.

name: Pieter Lastmankade
en: Amsterdam painter (1583-1633), among other things of biblical scenes, and teacher of Rembrandt. By council decision of 10 January 1923 part of the quay was renamed Jan van Goyenkade.

name: Pieter Lodewijk Takstraat
en: Journalist and politician (1848-1907), one of the leaders of the SDAP and editor-in-chief of Het Volk. He was one of the founders of the general workers' cooperative De Dageraad.

name: Pieter Nieuwlandstraat
en: Poet, mathematician and astronomer (1764-1794), professor of astronomy and navigation in Amsterdam and Leiden. At the age of 19 he was already recommended for a professorship in Latin. This street was first called Derde Van Swindenstraat (council decision of 15 November 1882).

name: Pieter Oosterhuisstraat
en: Photographer (1816-1885), originally a painter. He began with a portrait studio, later made stereo photographs and cartes de visite of townscapes, which he sold in large editions, and is known for his industrial photographs recording the building of railways, bridges, harbours and canals.

name: Pieter Oosterleehof
en: Educationalist and writer (1863-1930), director of the Christian teacher training college De Klokkenberg in Nijmegen and a well-known figure in education. His works include a history of Christian education.

name: Pieter Pauwstraat
en: Pieter Adriaensz Pauw (1552-1611), councillor and alderman of Amsterdam. His brother Reynier Pauw was burgomaster.

name: Pieter Postpad
en: Architect (1608-1669), who had a part in building the city hall on the Dam. His other buildings include the Mauritshuis and Huis ten Bosch in The Hague and the city hall of Maastricht.

name: Pieter Postsingel
en: Architect (1608-1669), who had a part in building the city hall on the Dam. His other buildings include the Mauritshuis and Huis ten Bosch in The Hague and the city hall of Maastricht.

name: Pieter van den Heuvelpad
en: Resistance fighter (1915-1942), who distributed clandestine material, was involved in preparing the February Strike of 1941 and belonged to a sabotage group in the Fokker factory in Amsterdam-Noord, where he worked. He was executed by firing squad at Soesterberg on 19 November 1942.

name: Pieter van der Doesstraat
en: Commander of the Holland fleet in the struggle against the Spanish (1562-1599).

name: Pieter van der Meulenhof
en: Resistance fighter (1912-1944), born in The Hague in 1912, died in Scheveningen prison. Van der Meulen was active as a printer in producing the clandestine paper 'Het Parool'.

name: Pieter van der Werfstraat
en: Burgomaster of Leiden, who distinguished himself by his perseverance during the siege of Leiden in 1573-1574.

name: Pieter Vlamingstraat
en: Historian (1686-1733), who wrote a 'Beschrijvinge van Amsterdam' (description of Amsterdam), left unfinished by his sudden death and later used by the historian Jan Wagenaar.

name: Pieter Zeemanlaan
en: Physicist (1865-1943), professor in Amsterdam, known above all for his study of light (the Zeeman effect). In 1902 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics.

name: Pietersbergweg
en: Named after the Sint-Pietersberg in Maastricht.

name: Pigmentstraat
en: A reference to the Vettewinkel paint factory, later Sigma, on the Cruquius site from 1934 to 2008.

name: Pijlkruidstraat
en: A water plant (arrowhead), named for the shape of its leaves.

name: Pijnackerstraat
en: Adam Pijnacker (1622-1673), painter, especially of landscapes.

name: Pikoletstraat
en: A songbird of the finch family, found among other places in Suriname.

name: Pilatus
en: A mountain peak in Switzerland, 2129 metres high.

name: Pilotenstraat
en: A piloot is a steersman; here the pilot of an aircraft is meant.

name: Pina Bauschplein
en: Pina Bausch was a German dancer and choreographer, one of the founders of neo-expressionist modern dance (Tanztheater).

name: Pinasstraat
en: A seventeenth-century sailing ship with a square stern (a pinnace).

name: Pinatuboplein
en: A mountain (volcano) in the Philippines.

name: Pindosweg
en: Pindus is a mountain range in Greece.

name: Pinksterbloemstraat
en: The meadow plant (cuckooflower), of the cabbage family.

name: Piraeusplein
en: A Greek port, to which the former KNSM ran a scheduled service.

name: Piri Reisplein
en: Hadji Muhiddin Piri Ibn Hadji Mehmed, better known as Piri Reis ('Captain Piri'), Ottoman seafarer, navigator and cartographer of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, maker of the Piri Reis map, a detailed world map that appeared in 1513.

name: Pirinsteeg
en: Pirin is a mountain range in Bulgaria.

name: Pirolastraat
en: A plant (wintergreen), found mainly in the dunes.

name: Pisuissehof
en: Jean Louis Pisuisse (1880-1927), cabaret artist, a great figure in the world of cabaret and song.

name: Plaatwerkerstraat
en: A trade name: someone who works sheet metal. The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Planciusstraat
en: Petrus Plancius (1550-1622), preacher and navigation expert, who planned many voyages of discovery.

name: Planetenplein
en: Celestial bodies that move in elliptical orbits around the sun. The earth too is a planet.

name: Planetenstraat
en: Celestial bodies that move in elliptical orbits around the sun. The earth too is a planet.

name: Plantage Badlaan
en: After the bathhouse (badhuis) that stood here from 1797 to 1820.

name: Plantage Doklaan
en: In 1682 the city government decided to lay out a 'plantagie' on this land, which came within the city in 1658: a pleasure ground built up only with summer houses, gardens and a few inns. A grid of straight lines was laid out over the whole area. The avenue running the length of the new Plantage was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were added. The summer houses were gradually replaced by houses, so that today only the Wertheimpark recalls the area's former purpose.

name: Plantage Kerklaan
en: In 1682 the city government decided to lay out a 'plantagie' on this land, which came within the city in 1658: a pleasure ground built up only with summer houses, gardens and a few inns. A grid of straight lines was laid out over the whole area. The avenue running the length of the new Plantage was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were added. The summer houses were gradually replaced by houses, so that today only the Wertheimpark recalls the area's former purpose.

name: Plantage Lepellaan
en: In 1682 the city government decided to lay out a 'plantagie' on this land, which came within the city in 1658: a pleasure ground built up only with summer houses, gardens and a few inns. A grid of straight lines was laid out over the whole area. The avenue running the length of the new Plantage was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were added. The summer houses were gradually replaced by houses, so that today only the Wertheimpark recalls the area's former purpose.

name: Plantage Middenlaan
en: In 1682 the city government decided to lay out a 'plantagie' on this land, which came within the city in 1658: a pleasure ground built up only with summer houses, gardens and a few inns. A grid of straight lines was laid out over the whole area. The avenue running the length of the new Plantage was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were added. The summer houses were gradually replaced by houses, so that today only the Wertheimpark recalls the area's former purpose.

name: Plantage Muidergracht
en: The town of Muiden. The former Muidergracht began at the Leprozengracht. After it was filled in, one part became the Jonas Daniël Meijerplein, and the second part was later renamed Hortusplantsoen. The part of the Plantage Muidergracht parallel to the Sarphatistraat was called Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.

name: Plantage Parklaan
en: The avenue ran along the former 'Park', a broad strip of land along the Nieuwe Herengracht, of which the Wertheimpark is the remnant. Where the sports ground is now, a concert hall with a winter garden stood from 1849, and the Parkschouwburg theatre from 1883 to 1912.

name: Plantage Westermanlaan
en: The Nieuwe Prinsengracht originally ran as far as the Entrepotdok. In 1864 part of it was added to Artis (recognisable by the ponds). The rest was filled in and named Plantage Prinsenlaan by council decision of 19 November 1879. For the zoo's 125th anniversary the name was changed in 1963 to the present one, after Gerardus Frederik Westerman (1807-1890), the founder of 'Artis'.

name: Plantagekade
en: In 1682 the city government decided to lay out a 'plantagie' on this land, which came within the city in 1658: a pleasure ground built up only with summer houses, gardens and a few inns. A grid of straight lines was laid out over the whole area. The avenue running the length of the new Plantage was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were added. The summer houses were gradually replaced by houses, so that today only the Wertheimpark recalls the area's former purpose.

name: Platanenweg
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Platenwagenweg
en: The type of caravan (a flat wagon) in use around 1930. The street name refers to the caravan site here.

name: Platostraat
en: Athenian philosopher (427-347 BC), pupil of Socrates, one of the greatest thinkers in history, who founded a school of philosophy in Athens.

name: Pleimuiden
en: The English port of Plymouth, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Plein '40-'45
en: Recalls the years of the German occupation (Second World War). The liberation carillon stands on the square, which lies on the edge of the resistance heroes' neighbourhood.

name: Plein Spanje '36-'39
en: The name recalls the Spanish Civil War of 1936 to 1939, the vain struggle against Franco and his fascist regime. The name and the monument here honour a number of volunteers from the Netherlands who were killed in that struggle.

name: Plejadenplein
en: The star cluster, also known as the Seven Sisters (Zevengesternte).

name: Plejadenweg
en: The star cluster, also known as the Seven Sisters (Zevengesternte).

name: Plesmanlaan
en: Albert Plesman (1889-1953), aviation pioneer, who founded KLM in 1919 and was its director until his death.

name: Plesostraat
en: The name of the airport of Zagreb, Croatia.

name: Plimsollweg
en: The Plimsoll is the mark on a ship's hull showing how deep it may be loaded in various conditions (named after the Englishman S. Plimsoll).

name: Ploegstraat
en: A farm implement for loosening (ploughing) the soil of a field.

name: Plotterstraat
en: A drawing machine controlled by a computer. As a counterpart to the street names recalling Amsterdam-Noord's former shipbuilding industry, this name refers to modern information technology.

name: Plutarchusstraat
en: Greek philosopher and writer (50-120), who wrote biographies (Lives) of a number of famous Greeks and Romans and philosophical writings (Moralia).

name: Plutostraat
en: Pluto, long counted as the planet farthest from the sun; since 2006 it has been classed as a dwarf planet.

name: Pluvierplein
en: The bird (plover). In the Netherlands the Kentish plover is the best known.

name: Pluvierstraat
en: The bird (plover). In the Netherlands the Kentish plover is the best known.

name: Poederooienstraat
en: A village on the Maas in the Bommelerwaard.

name: Poeldijkstraat
en: A village in the Westland.

name: Poggenbeekstraat
en: Georg Jan Poggenbeek (1853-1903), painter, mainly of landscapes.

name: Polanenstraat
en: The former village of Houtrijk en Polanen, now called Halfweg.

name: Polderweg
en: After what used to be here: until about 1940 there was a small polder with the Tuinwijk allotment complex.

name: Polijsterweg
en: The trade name of someone who polishes, that is, grinds an uneven surface of metal or wood smooth.

name: Polluxplein
en: The star that, with the star Castor, forms the main stars of the constellation Gemini (the Twins).

name: Polluxstraat
en: The star that, with the star Castor, forms the main stars of the constellation Gemini (the Twins).

name: Polonceau-kade
en: Camille Polonceau (1813-1859), French railway engineer, known for his designs for roofs and trusses. The so-called Polonceau truss is one of the main features of the purifier house, the boiler house and the water-gas plant of the Westergasfabriek.

name: Polsbroekstraat
en: The ribbon village in the Lopikerwaard (Utrecht).

name: Polygoongracht
en: A film company founded in Haarlem in 1919, which produced commissioned films, documentaries and weekly cinema newsreels.

name: Pomonastraat
en: The Roman goddess of fruit trees.

name: Pompmanstraat
en: A trade name: someone responsible for the pumps in a ship's engine room.

name: Pond Sterlinglaan
en: The currency of Great Britain.

name: Ponserstraat
en: A trade name: someone who punches, pressing holes into metal for example with a machine. The street name refers to the shipbuilding that Amsterdam-Noord has lost.

name: Pontanusstraat
en: Johannes Isaac Pontanus (1571-1639), historian in the service of the King of Denmark and the States of Gelderland, who published a description of Amsterdam in 1611.

name: Pontplein
en: This square owes its name to the IJplein ferry (pont) that moors here.

name: Pontsteiger
en: The departure point of the Distelweg and Houthaven ferries.

name: Poolsterstraat
en: The star (Polaris) that lies exactly above the north and so stays in the same place for us.

name: Poolstraat
en: De Pool was the name of a former warehouse on the Prins Hendrikkade that housed the Roman Catholic clandestine church De Pool from 1719 until its demolition in 1878. The gable stone of that old warehouse was placed in its successor, the later Roman Catholic Annakerk on the Wittenburgergracht (since demolished too), and so the name went with it to Wittenburg.

name: Poortland
en: A corrupted spelling of the English port of Portland, as found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Poppendammergouw
en: One of the quarters of the former Banne Ransdorp; the others were Bloemendaal, Holysloot, Ransdorp and Durgerdam. The road came onto Amsterdam territory when the municipality of Ransdorp was annexed in 1921.

name: Populierenweg
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Portengenstraat
en: A village west of Breukelen (Utrecht).

name: Portsmuiden
en: The English port of Portsmouth, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Postjeskade
en: After the former Postjeswetering. A postje is a small freshwater fish.

name: Postjesweg
en: After the former Postjeswetering. A postje is a small freshwater fish.

name: Postjeswetering
en: After the former Postjeswetering. A postje is a small freshwater fish.

name: Potgieterstraat
en: Everardus Johannes Potgieter (1808-1875), merchant, writer, poet and critic, who became the centre of a literary circle. In 1837 he founded 'De Gids', which he edited for thirty years.

name: Potvisstraat
en: A cetacean (the sperm whale) with a round, thick head and large teeth, found all over the world.

name: Pracanalaan
en: The Pracana reservoir, in Portugal, in the Castelo Branco district.

name: Pradolaan
en: The Museo del Prado in Madrid, the national museum of Spain, opened in 1819. The basis of its rich collection was laid by the collection of Charles V, greatly enlarged by Philip II and Philip IV. It is famous for its paintings by Spanish, Italian and Southern Netherlandish artists.

name: Pramenpad
en: A small flat-bottomed inland boat (a pram), used mainly for carrying livestock and manure.

name: Praterlaan
en: A stadium in Vienna, where on 24 May 1995 Ajax won the Champions League final, Ajax v AC Milan (1-0).

name: Preangerstraat
en: A region near Bandung in western Java (Indonesia), known for growing coffee, tea and cinchona.

name: Presanella
en: A mountain peak in Italy, 3564 metres high.

name: President Allendelaan
en: Salvador Allende Gossens (1908-1973), president of the Republic of Chile from 1970, who died during a coup. Allende gave the Chilean republic a socialist government of Marxist stamp. Before 1974 the avenue was called Westoever (council decision of 6 October 1948).

name: President Brandstraat
en: Jan Hendrik Brand (1823-1888), president of the Orange Free State from 1864. His motto is well known: 'Alles sal reg kom, as ons almal ons plig doen' (all will come right if we all do our duty).

name: President Kennedylaan
en: John Fitzgerald Kennedy (1917-1963), 35th president of the United States from 1961, whose short term was marked by a firm approach, murdered in Texas on 22 November 1963. Before 1964 the avenue was called Rivierenlaan.

name: President Kennedyplantsoen
en: John Fitzgerald Kennedy (1917-1963), 35th president of the United States from 1961, whose short term was marked by a firm approach, murdered in Texas on 22 November 1963. Before 1964 the avenue was called Rivierenlaan.

name: President Steynplantsoen
en: Martinus Theunis Steyn (1857-1916), president of the Orange Free State (1896-1902), who took part in the Second Boer War (1899-1902).

name: President Steynstraat
en: Martinus Theunis Steyn (1857-1916), president of the Orange Free State (1896-1902), who took part in the Second Boer War (1899-1902).

name: Pretoriusstraat
en: Andries Pretorius (1799-1853), one of the Voortrekkers of the Transvaal Boers, who in 1838 defeated the Zulu king Dingane. The city of Pretoria is named after him.

name: Prins Bernhardplein
en: Named after His Highness Prince Bernhard Lucas Emmanuel of Orange-Nassau, van Vollenhoven (born 1969).

name: Prins Hendrikkade
en: The youngest son of King William II, Prince Willem Frederik Hendrik (1820-1879), who took a keen interest in trade and shipping. His bust, made in 1885 by Professor F. Stracke, stands opposite the Scheepvaarthuis. With the naming in 1879 a number of vivid names disappeared, and with them a piece of the city's memory. Counting from the Singel they were: the Haringpakkerij, after the herring trade here at the end of the sixteenth century, with the Haringpakkerstoren where the Haringpakkersbrug is now; the Tesselse kade, the mooring for ships from Texel; the Kampersteiger; the Oude Teertuinen, the tar merchants' place until 1643, when they moved to the Nieuwe Teertuinen; the Kamperhoofd, after the sixteenth-century bastion of that name; the Buitenkant, counterpart of the Binnenkant; and the IJgracht, the north side of the island of Rapenburg.

name: Prins Hendriklaan
en: Hendrik, Duke of Mecklenburg-Schwerin, Prince of the Netherlands (1876-1934), who married Queen Wilhelmina in 1901.

name: Prinseneiland
en: Probably named after the house 'De drie Prinsen' (the three princes), which must have stood here in the seventeenth century, with busts of Prince William I, Prince Maurits and Prince Frederik Hendrik. Where the house stood, however, is not known.

name: Prinseneilandsgracht
en: Probably named after the house 'De drie Prinsen' (the three princes), which must have stood here in the seventeenth century, with busts of Prince William I, Prince Maurits and Prince Frederik Hendrik. Where the house stood, however, is not known.

name: Prinsengracht
en: After 'the princely title', meaning that of the Princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and the plainest in the character of its buildings. It was dug in the expansion of 1612 and built up from the Brouwersgracht to the Leidsegracht. In the expansion of 1658 this canal too was extended across the Amstel (as far as the Entrepotdok). The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for today's Noordermarkt never caught on with the citizens.

name: Prinsenhofssteeg
en: After 1578 the former St Cecilia convent was fitted out as lodgings for royal visitors to the city, and so the building was called the Prinsenhof. When the Admiralty later met here, the name Admiraliteitshof came into use beside it. In 1808 the city hall on the Dam was converted into a palace and the Prinsenhof became the city hall, which it remained until 1988. In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries this was the Ceciliënsteeg.

name: Prinsensluis
en: This fixed bridge is named after the street it lies in and the canal it crosses. Prins here refers to the princely title, meaning that of the Princes of Orange.

name: Prinsenstraat
en: After 'the princely title', meaning that of the Princes of Orange.

name: Prinses Amaliaplein
en: Catharina-Amalia Beatrix Carmen Victoria of Orange-Nassau (born 7 December 2003), heir apparent with the title Princess of Orange, Princess of the Netherlands, Princess of Orange-Nassau, eldest daughter of King Willem-Alexander and Queen Máxima. She is known as Amalia.

name: Prinses Irenestraat
en: Irene Emma Elisabeth, second daughter of Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard, born 5 August 1939. In 1964 in Rome she married the French nobleman Prince Carlos Hugo of Bourbon-Parma. For traffic reasons the western part of the Prinses Irenestraat was renamed Fred. Roeskestraat by council decision of 27 April 1977.

name: Prinses Margrietstraat
en: Margriet Francisca, Princess of the Netherlands, born in Canada in 1943, third daughter of Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard, who married Pieter van Vollenhoven in 1967.

name: Prinses Marijkestraat
en: Maria Christina, Princess of the Netherlands, born 1947, fourth daughter of Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard. She was first called Princess Marijke, but has called herself Princess Christina since 1967.

name: Printerstraat
