en: A device for printing text and images stored in a computer. As a counterpart to the street names recalling Amsterdam-Noord's former shipbuilding industry, this name refers to modern information technology.

name: Processorstraat
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Prof. H. Bavinckstraat
en: Herman Bavinck (1854-1921), professor of theology at the Vrije Universiteit in Amsterdam, whose educational writings had a great influence on Christian schooling.

name: Prof. Ph. Kohnstammstraat
en: Philippus Abraham Kohnstamm (1875-1951), professor of education in Amsterdam and Utrecht, with great influence on education at home and abroad.

name: Prof. R. Casimirstraat
en: Rommert Casimir (1877-1957), educationalist, professor at Leiden and writer.

name: Prof. Tulpplein
en: Nicolaes Tulp (1593-1674), Amsterdam physician, lecturer to the surgeons' guild at the Athenaeum Illustre and several times burgomaster of the city. The title Professor was added to the street name in 1946, because many people tended to look for the street in the flower neighbourhood (tulp = tulip).

name: Prof. Tulpstraat
en: Nicolaes Tulp (1593-1674), Amsterdam physician, lecturer to the surgeons' guild at the Athenaeum Illustre and several times burgomaster of the city. The title Professor was added to the street name in 1946, because many people tended to look for the street in the flower neighbourhood (tulp = tulip).

name: Professor J.H. Gunningstraat
en: Professor Johannes Hermanus Gunning (1859-1951), educationalist, the first state-funded professor of education, who was the first in the Netherlands to argue for founding a lyceum.

name: Profiltigracht
en: A film company founded in The Hague in 1929, producer of (commissioned) films, documentaries and cinema newsreels, first the rival and later the partner of Polygoon.

name: Programmeurstraat
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Propaanweg
en: A petroleum derivative: a gas (propane) used as motor fuel.

name: Propellerstraat
en: The usual means of propelling aircraft before the rise of jet engines.

name: Provincialeweg
en: The name set by the municipality of Weesperkarspel for the road along the Weespertrekvaart and the Gaasp. The road was originally called the Weesperzandpad, laid out around 1640 by the cities of Amsterdam and Weesp, and managed until 1929 by the Commissioners of the Zandpad. In 1929 the Province took it over.

name: Pruimenstraat
en: The fruit of the plum tree.

name: Ptolemaeusstraat
en: Claudius Ptolemy (second century AD), Greek mathematician and astronomer, who first gave an overview of the geographical longitudes and latitudes of the main cities of antiquity. Ptolemy's theorem: in a cyclic quadrilateral the product of the diagonals equals the sum of the products of the opposite sides.

name: Puiflijkpad
en: A village in the Land van Maas en Waal (Gelderland).

name: Pumoriplein
en: Pumori is a mountain in the Himalayas.

name: Punterspad
en: An open, flat-bottomed boat (punter), used especially around Giethoorn.

name: Purmerhof
en: The polder (the Purmer), created by draining the lake near Purmerend between 1618 and 1622.

name: Purmerplein
en: The polder (the Purmer), created by draining the lake near Purmerend between 1618 and 1622.

name: Purmerweg
en: The polder (the Purmer), created by draining the lake near Purmerend between 1618 and 1622.

name: Purperhoedenveem
en: A veem is a company that stores goods in its warehouses and delivers them out again. Each veem had its own badge, after which it was named. These could be hats of different colours and shapes (Purperhoeden, Klapmutsen and others). Some took their name from where their workmen came from (Vriesseveem, Zeeuwse Veem and others).

name: Putterplantsoen
en: A songbird, also called goldfinch (distelvink), often kept as a cage bird.

name: Putterstraat
en: A songbird, also called goldfinch (distelvink), often kept as a cage bird.

name: Pybo Steenstrastraat
en: Scholar (died 1788), lecturer in mathematics, astronomy and navigation at the Athenaeum Illustre in Amsterdam, and examiner of navigators in the service of the VOC in Amsterdam. His publications include 'Grondbeginzels der Stuurmanskunst' (principles of navigation, 1766) and 'Openbare lessen over het vinden der lengte op zee' (public lectures on finding longitude at sea, 1770).

name: Pyreneeën
en: The mountain range in France and Spain.

name: Pythagorasstraat
en: Greek philosopher and mathematician (582-507 BC), known above all for the theorem named after him: the square of the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides. Before 1922 the street was called Mr. Cornelis van Lennepstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 15 March 1904).

name: Quashibastraat
en: Quashiba lived in slavery on Sint Maarten. In 1835 she and five fellow sufferers, among them her two children Sammy and Jane, escaped in a small boat to the nearby British island of Anguilla. Five years later her partner, Matthew Stancliff, dared to sail back to Sint Maarten to fetch Quashiba's sister Minny and her children, so that they too could live in freedom. Quashiba and her family thus stand for the struggle for freedom.

name: Quellijnstraat
en: Artus Quellijn or Quellinus (1609-1668), Southern Netherlandish sculptor, whose works include the sculpture for the city hall on the Dam.

name: Quinten Massijsstraat
en: Flemish painter and goldsmith (1466-1530). The name is also written Matsijs (Quentin Matsys).

name: R.J.H. Fortuynplein
en: R.J.H. Fortuyn (born 1916) was appointed director of the Koninklijke Hollandsche Lloyd in Amsterdam in 1956.

name: R.J.H. Fortuynstraat
en: R.J.H. Fortuyn (born 1916) was appointed director of the Koninklijke Hollandsche Lloyd in Amsterdam in 1956.

name: Raadhuisstraat
en: After the city hall (raadhuis), designed in the seventeenth century by Jacob van Campen and built by Daniël Stalpaert. In 1808 it was vacated on the orders of King Louis Napoleon and has since been used as the Royal Palace. The Raadhuisstraat was created in 1895 by widening the Huiszittensteeg and the Korte Huiszittensteeg, filling in the Warmoesgracht and breaking through the row of canal houses.

name: Raamdwarsstraat
en: The cloth frames (lakenramen), on which dyed cloth was hung to dry, had to stand outside the city. When the Kloveniersburgwal was still the city moat, these frames stood level with today's Raamgracht. The nearby Verversstraat (dyers' street) also recalls this old Amsterdam industry.

name: Raamgracht
en: The cloth frames (lakenramen), on which dyed cloth was hung to dry, had to stand outside the city. When the Kloveniersburgwal was still the city moat, these frames stood level with today's Raamgracht. The nearby Verversstraat (dyers' street) also recalls this old Amsterdam industry.

name: Raamplein
en: The cloth frames (lakenramen) moved here when the area between the Kloveniersburgwal and the Zwanenburgwal was brought within the city in the sixteenth-century expansions. The Raamplein was made by filling in a stretch of the Lijnbaansgracht.

name: Raampoort
en: This bridge is named after the Raampoort (gate), demolished in 1844.

name: Raamsteeg
en: The cloth frames (lakenramen) that stood outside the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. This is the oldest place whose name recalls the cloth dyers.

name: Raamstraat
en: The cloth frames (lakenramen) moved here when the area between the Kloveniersburgwal and the Zwanenburgwal was brought within the city in the sixteenth-century expansions. The Raamplein was made by filling in a stretch of the Lijnbaansgracht.

name: Raasdorperweg
en: The former hamlet of Raasdorp, on the edge of the Lutkemeer.

name: Rachel Ruyschbrug
en: Rachel Ruysch (The Hague, 1664 - Amsterdam, 1750) was one of the most successful still-life painters of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, world-famous for her colourful, lifelike flower paintings. As a married woman and mother of ten children she carried on her brilliant career undiminished.

name: Radarweg
en: The navigation aid for ships and aircraft at night and in poor visibility, based on the reflection of radio waves. Radar is short for Radio Detection and Ranging. The road was first named Gyroscoopweg.

name: Radboud
en: A square castle with round corner towers in Medemblik (Noord-Holland), founded by Floris V around 1289, partly demolished in the seventeenth century and rebuilt in 1890.

name: Rademakerstraat
en: Abraham Rademaker (1675/76-1735) was a Dutch engraver and draughtsman, famous for his prints of castles, towns and country estates in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. He made dozens of pictures of existing country estates, among others around Amsterdam.

name: Raden Adjeng Kartinistraat
en: Indonesian writer and campaigner (1879-1904), a champion of human rights and pioneer of the Indonesian feminist movement. Her manifesto 'Geef den Javaan opvoeding' (give the Javanese education) appeared in 1903, followed in 1911 by her letters. In 1964 she was declared a national heroine.

name: Raderbootstraat
en: A vessel driven by paddle wheels (a paddle steamer).

name: Radioweg
en: The transmission of sound and signals by electric waves, discovered by Hertz in 1888 and first applied by Marconi in 1900. When this street name was set, radio was one of the most important discoveries, through its use by the broadcasting associations.

name: Ramskooi
en: No explanation can be found for the name of this alley, which already existed around 1450. Some historians think of the name of a Norwegian timber merchant; another suggestion is that Jan Ran had a duck decoy (eendenkooi) here. In the sixteenth century the alley appears as Jan Ranskoy. It originally ran as far as the Prins Hendrikkade, which for that stretch was called Texelse kade until 1879, and earlier still Nieuwezijds Houttuinen.

name: Randwijkhof
en: A village in Gelderland, between Wageningen and Arnhem.

name: Rangeerderstraat
en: A railway worker responsible for coupling and uncoupling wagons and moving trains onto the various tracks (a shunter).

name: Ranonkelkade
en: The plant.

name: Ransdorper Die
en: A creek north of Ransdorp.

name: Raoul Wallenberghofje
en: Swedish diplomat (1912-unknown), who worked for peace and human rights. During the Second World War he saved tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews from deportation. In 1945 he was taken prisoner by Soviet troops. According to the Soviets he died of a heart attack in captivity in 1947, but his death has never been confirmed.

name: Raoul Wallenbergstraat
en: Swedish diplomat (1912-unknown), who worked for peace and human rights. During the Second World War he saved tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews from deportation. In 1945 he was taken prisoner by Soviet troops. According to the Soviets he died of a heart attack in captivity in 1947, but his death has never been confirmed.

name: Rapenburg
en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now the Oosterdok), the Oudeschans, the Rapenburgwal and the Schippersgrachtje. The main street took the island's name. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

name: Rapenburgerplein
en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now the Oosterdok), the Oudeschans, the Rapenburgwal and the Schippersgrachtje. The main street took the island's name. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

name: Rapenburgerstraat
en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now the Oosterdok), the Oudeschans, the Rapenburgwal and the Schippersgrachtje. The main street took the island's name. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

name: Rapenburgwal
en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now the Oosterdok), the Oudeschans, the Rapenburgwal and the Schippersgrachtje. The main street took the island's name. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

name: Raphael Lemkinstraat
en: Polish-Jewish lawyer (1901-1959), who fought in the Polish resistance in 1939 and fled to Sweden and later to the USA. He lost 49 relatives in the Holocaust. In 1944 he introduced the term genocide, and in 1948 he was the driving force behind the UN negotiations on the Genocide Convention.

name: Raphaëlplein
en: Raffaello Santi or Sanzio (1483-1520), Italian painter and a leading figure of the Renaissance, who painted many Madonnas, frescoes and portraits. He also worked as an architect on St Peter's in Rome.

name: Raphaëlstraat
en: Raffaëllo di Senti (1483-1520), Italian painter and a leading figure of the Renaissance, who painted many Madonnas, frescoes and portraits. He also worked as an architect on St Peter's in Rome.

name: Ravensteinplein
en: An old fortified town on the Maas (Noord-Brabant).

name: Ravensteinstraat
en: An old fortified town on the Maas (Noord-Brabant).

name: Ravenstraat
en: The street was laid out on the site of the shipyard 'De Raven', demolished in 1887, whose owner in 1692 is recorded as Marten Willems Raven.

name: Ravenswaaipad
en: A village in the municipality of Maurik in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

name: Ravenwerf
en: The shipyard 'De Zwarte Raaf' (the black raven), which once lay here between the Kattenburgerstraat and the Kattenburgergracht.

name: Realengracht
en: Reynier Reael, alderman of the city in 1633, who owned the whole of the Realeneiland.

name: Réaumurstraat
en: René Antoine Ferchault de Réaumur (1683-1757), French physicist, who in 1730 built the thermometer named after him, with an eighty-degree scale. The street's name was earlier set by the municipality of Watergraafsmeer as Bothastraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 31 October 1891).

name: Recht Boomssloot
en: The sixteenth-century master shipbuilder Cornelis Pietersz Boom. To connect his yard on the Lastage with the surrounding water he had a canal and a side canal dug, which were then named after him.

name: Reesluis
en: This fixed bridge is named after the Reestraat, in which it lies.

name: Reestraat
en: A kind of deer (ree = roe deer). The name recalls the trade in hides, concentrated in this neighbourhood before the street was laid out, and later in the nearby southern part of the Jordaan.

name: Reewijkplein
en: The Zuid-Holland village of Reeuwijk.

name: Reggestraat
en: A tributary of the Overijsselse Vecht.

name: Reguliersbreestraat
en: All these names recall the Reguliers monastery (of the Canons Regular), which stood from 1394 to 1532 outside the city gate of the time, where the Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now cross. The city gate, of which the Munttoren is a remnant, was once called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht then ended at that gate. Parts of it were filled in in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Before 1909 the Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

name: Reguliersdwarsstraat
en: All these names recall the Reguliers monastery (of the Canons Regular), which stood from 1394 to 1532 outside the city gate of the time, where the Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now cross. The city gate, of which the Munttoren is a remnant, was once called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht then ended at that gate. Parts of it were filled in in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Before 1909 the Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

name: Reguliersgracht
en: All these names recall the Reguliers monastery (of the Canons Regular), which stood from 1394 to 1532 outside the city gate of the time, where the Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now cross. The city gate, of which the Munttoren is a remnant, was once called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht then ended at that gate. Parts of it were filled in in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Before 1909 the Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

name: Reigersbos
en: The name of a farm that stood on the Abcouderstraatweg by the former Zwetskade.

name: Reigersbosachterom
en: The name of a farm that stood on the Abcouderstraatweg by the former Zwetskade.

name: Reigersbosdreef
en: The name of a farm that stood on the Abcouderstraatweg by the former Zwetskade.

name: Reigersbospad
en: The name of a farm that stood on the Abcouderstraatweg by the former Zwetskade.

name: Reigerweg
en: The bird (the crow).

name: Reijnier Vinkeleskade
en: Engraver and draughtsman (1741-1816), who made about three thousand prints, including many Amsterdam townscapes, so that his work also matters for the city's topography.

name: Reimersbeek
en: A castle in Nuth (Limburg), founded in the sixteenth century and partly demolished and rebuilt in the eighteenth. It is now a rectangular house of three wings with a seventeenth-century gatehouse and a farm from 1705.

name: Reimerswaalstraat
en: A place on Zuid-Beveland near Yerseke. The land of Reimerswaal was entirely swallowed by a storm flood in the seventeenth century.

name: Reina Prinsen Geerligsstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1922-1943), born in Semarang (Indonesia), died in the Oranienburg concentration camp (Germany).

name: Reinaert de Vosstraat
en: A medieval beast epic (Reynard the Fox), probably of French origin, adapted into Middle Dutch in 1260. Before 1939 this street was part of the Zeven Provinciënstraat (now Bestevâerstraat).

name: Reinhard Dozyhof
en: Historian (1820-1883), professor at Leiden and a renowned orientalist.

name: Reinier Claeszenplein
en: Dutch vice-admiral, who in 1606 was attacked by the Spanish fleet off Cape St Vincent (Portugal) and blew up his ship rather than surrender.

name: Reinier Claeszenstraat
en: Dutch vice-admiral, who in 1606 was attacked by the Spanish fleet off Cape St Vincent (Portugal) and blew up his ship rather than surrender.

name: Reinier Engelmanstraat
en: Actor (1795-1845), pupil and later partner of Andries Snoek.

name: Reinveen
en: A former farm on the Uitweg, demolished to build the garden city of Osdorp.

name: Reinwardtstraat
en: Caspar G.C. Reinwardt (1773-1854), professor of chemistry and pharmacy in Amsterdam and director of the Royal Cabinet of Natural History in Amsterdam, who organised the medical service on Java in 1817.

name: Reitdiepstraat
en: A canal between the city of Groningen and Zoutkamp.

name: Reitzstraat
en: Francis William Reitz (1844-1934), South African statesman and writer, president of the Orange Free State from 1889 to 1896, who took part in the Second Boer War (1899-1902).

name: Reizigersweg
en: Travelling people (reizigers). The name refers to the caravan site here.

name: Reling
en: The top rail of the railing round a ship's deck.

name: Rembrandtpark
en: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn (1606-1669), the greatest Dutch painter of the Golden Age.

name: Rembrandtplein
en: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn (1606-1669), the greatest Dutch painter of the Golden Age. In 1852 the cast-iron Rembrandt monument by Louis Royer was unveiled by King William III, placed first at the side of the square. In 1875 it was moved to the middle, which was the reason for renaming the square Rembrandtplein. Before that it was called Botermarkt, after the butter market held here every Monday morning from the seventeenth century.

name: Remijden
en: The historical name of a piece of land in old Sloten.

name: Remmerdenplein
en: A hamlet in the Gelderland municipality of Rheden.

name: Rengerskerkestraat
en: A village south of Schouwen (Zeeland), lost to a storm flood in the seventeenth century.

name: Renkumhof
en: A town on the Rhine (Gelderland).

name: Renooiplein
en: A village on the Linge in the Betuwe.

name: Renswoudestraat
en: A village in the Gelderse Vallei, with a seventeenth-century castle of the same name (Utrecht).

name: Resedastraat
en: The garden plant (mignonette), which grows wild in the dunes.

name: Retiefstraat
en: Piet Retief (1788-1838), leader of the South African Boers during the Great Trek of 1835 and the years after.

name: Retirobrug
en: A station in Buenos Aires.

name: Revaleiland
en: Now Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. In the seventeenth century Amsterdam was the largest buyer of its rye, grain and timber.

name: Reyer Anslostraat
en: Poet (1625-1669), whose works include a poem in praise of Amsterdam for the laying of the first stone of the new city hall in 1648. Before 1896 the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel called this street Parkstraat.

name: Rheastraat
en: A figure from Greek mythology, one of the Titans, wife of Cronus and mother of Hestia, Hera, Demeter, Poseidon, Hades and Zeus.

name: Rhenenhof
en: A town on the Rhine by the Grebbeberg (Utrecht).

name: Rhijnestein
en: A knightly manor at Cothen near Jutphaas on the Kromme Rijn, consisting of a residential tower and a gate from the sixteenth century; the second tower and the middle section date from around 1850.

name: Rhijnspoorplein
en: After the former Rhijnspoorweg-Maatschappij (Rhine Railway Company), which opened the Weesperpoort station here in 1843 and was later absorbed into the Dutch Railways.

name: Rhijnvis Feithstraat
en: Poet (1753-1824), a great innovator in both his poetry and his plays, and much admired in his lifetime. His evangelical New Year's Eve hymn is well known: 'Uren, dagen, maanden, jaren, vliegen als een schaduw heen' (hours, days, months, years fly past like a shadow).

name: Rhodosweg
en: A Greek island in the Mediterranean (Rhodes).

name: Rhôneweg
en: The river that rises in Switzerland and flows through Lake Geneva and France into the Mediterranean near Marseille.

name: Ribesstraat
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Richard Holstraat
en: Conductor, composer and teacher (1825-1904), who led the classical concerts in the Paleis voor Volksvlijt and taught Johan Wagenaar and Willem Mengelberg. He composed several symphonies.

name: Richard Wagnerstraat
en: German composer (1813-1883), creator of the nineteenth-century German music drama ('Lohengrin', 'Tannhäuser', 'Parsifal', the 'Ring of the Nibelung').

name: Ridderspoorweg
en: A plant (larkspur) with purple, blue, red, yellow or white flowers. Its scientific name, 'Delphinium', comes from the Latin word for dolphin, because the flower buds look somewhat like a dolphin.

name: Rie Beisenherzbrug
en: Maria Martha (Rie) Beisenherz (Amsterdam, 8 September 1901 - Bussum, 12 April 1992) was a Dutch swimmer and a pioneer of women's swimming. When at thirteen she wanted to join the swimming club HDZ she was turned down as too young, so with some other swimmers she founded the Amsterdamsche Dames Zwemclub (ADZ). Beisenherz represented the Netherlands once at the Olympic Games, Antwerp 1920, as the Netherlands' first woman competitor ever at the modern Olympics. She swam the 100 metres freestyle and reached the semi-finals in Antwerp, with a time of 1:22.6.

name: Rie Mastenbroekstraat
en: Hendrika Wilhelmina Kuypers-Mastenbroek (1919-2003), swimmer, who at the 1936 Olympic Games won three gold medals and one silver, an unprecedented haul for a woman swimmer.

name: Riekerweg
en: After the Riekerpolder here. The name comes from the former village of Rijk, which lay south of the village of Sloten.

name: Rietlandpark
en: Until about 1880 an undeveloped area, partly marshy and overgrown with reeds (riet). After trading sites and marshalling yards were laid out here at the end of the nineteenth century, the quays and roads were given their own names. The name Stads Rietlanden is still used for the marshalling yard.

name: Rietlandterras
en: Until about 1880 an undeveloped area, partly marshy and overgrown with reeds (riet). After trading sites and marshalling yards were laid out here at the end of the nineteenth century, the quays and roads were given their own names. The name Stads Rietlanden is still used for the marshalling yard.

name: Rietnesse
en: The former castle of Costijn van Sirixe in Zierikzee on Schouwen-Duiveland (Zeeland).

name: Rietveld Schröderpad
en: The Rietveld Schröder House museum in Utrecht. The architect Gerrit Rietveld (1888-1964) designed the house for Truus Schröder-Schräder, whose contribution largely shaped the final result. The house, its interior and its furniture follow the architectural principles of De Stijl. After Truus Schröder's death in 1985 the house was opened to the public.

name: Rietwijkerstraat
en: A hamlet near Amstelveen that disappeared when the Amsterdamse Bos was laid out. Originally a village further west, it was drowned in the Haarlemmermeer in the second half of the seventeenth century.

name: Rietzangerweg
en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

name: Rigakade
en: The seaport and capital of Latvia.

name: Rigelstraat
en: A star in the constellation Orion.

name: Rijgersborgh
en: A farm (also called Reigersbosch) on the Uitweg, demolished to build the Slotermeer district.

name: Rijnlandlaan
en: An area along the Oude Rijn from Katwijk aan Zee to Utrecht, mostly in today's province of Zuid-Holland.

name: Rijnsburgstraat
en: A town in Zuid-Holland. The street was originally part of the Sloterweg, but this stretch was renamed in 1973, because the city's expansion had split the Sloterweg in two.

name: Rijnstraat
en: The river (Rhine) that rises in Switzerland and enters the Netherlands at Lobith.

name: Rijsbesstraat
en: A blue-black berry (bog bilberry) of the heather family, a little more oval than the bilberry and rare in the Netherlands. It grows on peaty ground near woodland pools, tastes mildly sweet and is sometimes made into jam, jelly or juice.

name: Rijsdrechthof
en: An old Rijnland name: a stretch of water north of Leimuiden that disappeared when the Haarlemmermeer was drained.

name: Rijssenburghof
en: A drowned settlement between Leimuiden and Aalsmeer.

name: Rijswijkstraat
en: A town in Zuid-Holland on the edge of The Hague.

name: Rijtuigenhof
en: This court and its houses were laid out and built on a site occupied from 1910 to about 1980 by the buildings of the Amsterdamsche Rijtuig Maatschappij (carriage company).

name: Ringdijk
en: After its position relative to the Watergraafsmeer. Before the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was annexed, the Ooster Ringdijk was called Noorder- and Zuider-Ringdijk. The Eerste Ringdijkstraat was then called Schoollaan, and earlier still the name Dielemanstraat seems to have been used. A Tweede Ringdijkstraat (formerly Dijklaan) has since disappeared entirely through demolition.

name: Ringslangpad
en: A harmless snake (the grass snake) of the water snake family, native to Amsterdam. It can reach a length of one and a half metres. It is brown to olive green and owes its name to the yellow neck patches that can merge into a ring.

name: Ringsloot
en: A ring-shaped ditch.

name: Ringvaart
en: The water the path runs along. A ringvaart is the storage canal of a polder, into which surplus water from the polder is pumped.

name: Ringvaartdijk
en: The water the path runs along. A ringvaart is the storage canal of a polder, into which surplus water from the polder is pumped.

name: Ringweg-Noord
en: Named after the function of this national road (A10), whose parts are identified by adding the compass direction. The western part of the ring road was earlier named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten-IJ by a tunnel.

name: Ringweg-Oost
en: Named after the function of this national road (A10), whose parts are identified by adding the compass direction. The western part of the ring road was earlier named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten-IJ by a tunnel.

name: Ringweg-West
en: Named after the function of this national road (A10), whose parts are identified by adding the compass direction. The western part of the ring road was earlier named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten-IJ by a tunnel.

name: Ringweg-Zuid
en: Named after the function of this national road (A10), whose parts are identified by adding the compass direction. The western part of the ring road was earlier named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten-IJ by a tunnel.

name: Rini Ottehof
en: Sara Catharina Otte (1917-1991), film actress, who as a young girl caused a sensation in 1935 in the leading role of the film 'Jonge Harten' (young hearts). Her looks and her natural way of acting stood out above all.

name: Rinus Michelslaan
en: Marinus Jacobus Hendricus Michels (1928-2005), footballer and Ajax coach, who won the European Cup with Ajax in 1971. He went on to great success as coach of Barcelona and of the Dutch national team, at the 1974 World Cup (runners-up) and the 1988 European Championship (winners). Nicknamed 'the General', he was the founder of 'total football'.

name: Riouwstraat
en: The Riau Archipelago, an island group in Indonesia off the east coast of Sumatra.

name: Rita Reysbrug
en: Maria Everdina Reys (1924-2013), the best-known jazz singer of the Netherlands and perhaps of Europe, as her nickname 'Europe's First Lady of Jazz' attests. She was married to Wessel Ilcken, after whom a street near this bridge is named. In the Park Haagseweg all the streets are named after famous jazz musicians.

name: Ritzema Bosstraat
en: Jan Ritzema Bos (1850-1928), botanist, professor at Wageningen, founder of plant pathology and of state plant-health inspection in the Netherlands.

name: Robbert Cijferstraat
en: Resistance fighter (1919-1945), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad near the Zijpersluis (Noord-Holland).

name: Robert Doumastraat
en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

name: Robert Fruinlaan
en: Robert Jacobus Fruin (1823-1899), historian, professor at Leiden, who wrote many historical studies, among them 'Tien jaren uit den Tachtigjarigen Oorlog' (ten years of the Eighty Years' War).

name: Robert Kochplantsoen
en: German bacteriologist (1843-1910), discoverer of the cholera bacillus (1883) and of the tubercle bacillus (1882), who won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1905. Part of the Robert Kochplantsoen was laid out on the former Meerlaan (council decision of 10 January 1923).

name: Robert Scottstraat
en: English Antarctic explorer (1868-1912), who died on his second expedition, in which he reached the South Pole.

name: Robijnstraat
en: A hard, red gemstone (ruby).

name: Rochussenstraat
en: Jan Jacob Rochussen (1797-1871), statesman, successively Minister of Finance, Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies and Minister of the Colonies.

name: Rocketstraat
en: The name of the first English locomotive to run in a regular railway service (Stephenson's Rocket).

name: Rode Kruisstraat
en: The street was named to mark the centenary of the Netherlands Red Cross (founded 1867). The adjoining streets are named after people closely involved with it.

name: Rodenrijsstraat
en: A village north of Rotterdam.

name: Roebelkade
en: The currency of Russia (the rouble).

name: Roelantstraat
en: After the Song of Roland, the thirteenth-century epic about Roland, a knight of the Frankish ruler Charlemagne. Before 1939 this street was part of the De Rijpstraat.

name: Roelof Hartplein
en: Amsterdam physician and philanthropist (1837-1892).

name: Roelof Hartstraat
en: Amsterdam physician and philanthropist (1837-1892).

name: Roemer
en: Named after a ditch between the Twiske and De Gouw, which disappeared when the Twiske was laid out.

name: Roemer Visscherstraat
en: Amsterdam merchant and poet (1547-1620), host to the artists Vondel, Hooft, Huygens and Bredero in his house on the Geldersekade.

name: Roepie Kruizestraat
en: Jan Hendrik Kruize (1925-1992), hockey player, who won bronze with his team at the 1948 Olympic Games in London and silver four years later in Helsinki.

name: Roerdomppad
en: Name of the underlying path.

name: Roerstraat
en: A river (the Rur) that rises in the Eifel and flows into the Maas at Roermond.

name: Roeselarestraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

name: Roesiel
en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of La Rochelle, found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Roetersstraat
en: Hendrik Roeters (1617-1699), alderman of the city and owner of the land of the Roeterseiland named after him. The street was laid out on the Roetersburgwal, filled in in 1873.

name: Roffart
en: A seventeenth-century country house with a gate from 1629 in Baarlo (Limburg).

name: Roggeveenstraat
en: Jacob Roggeveen (1659-1729), navigator, who in 1721-1723 made a voyage to the East Indies around South America. On that voyage, at Easter 1722, he discovered the island that has since been called Easter Island.

name: Rokin
en: The long-held theory that the name derives from Rak-in (a reach inside the Dam, as the Damrak is outside it) must be thrown overboard. This part of the Amstel, now two-thirds filled in, originally had no quays: the houses on the Kalverstraat ran right down to the water. When in the sixteenth century the waterside façades of the first stretch from the Dam had to be set back, move in a little (inrukken), a quay was built here, recorded in 1559 as Ruck-in. A few years later this had become Rock-in, and as the quay was extended the whole of it took the name. Above the water on the Dam side stood the first Exchange (by Hendrick de Keyser) from 1611 to 1836. The stretch as far as the Spui was filled in in 1936.

name: Rollemanstraat
en: The street name refers to the caravan site here. Rolleman is Bargoens (Dutch cant) for a caravan dweller.

name: Rombout Hogerbeetsstraat
en: Pensionary of Leiden (1561-1626) and supporter of Hugo de Groot, imprisoned in 1619 but released in 1625 after the death of Prince Maurits. The street's name was earlier set as Eerste Hugo de Grootdwarsstraat (council decision of 13 October 1897).

name: Romeinsarmsteeg
en: After an old shop sign showing a hand holding a sword, the arm recognisably in the sleeve of Roman dress. A similar sign could be seen on a house on the Vijgendam until 1847. Before the seventeenth century this was the Nieuwe Kruissteeg.

name: Romerostraat
en: Óscar Arnulfo Romero (1917-1980), Archbishop of San Salvador, capital of El Salvador, who gave voice to the opposition. On 24 March 1980 he was murdered by right-wing paramilitaries on the steps of the cathedral.

name: Rondeel
en: A semicircular, usually brick bastion that formed part of the city walls in the early sixteenth century, lower and more heavily built than the older wall towers. Through its meaning and its first syllable, the name refers to the round shape of the new building.

name: Röntgenstraat
en: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen (1845-1923), German physicist, who discovered X-rays (Röntgen rays) in 1895, used in medicine to photograph the inside of the body. He won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901. The municipality of Watergraafsmeer named the street Wilhelminastraat when it was laid out (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 15 March 1904).

name: Roomolenstraat
en: Probably named after a gable stone. In the seventeenth century the little street was called Molensteeg, later Roomolensteeg, and in 1884 the city council changed that to Roomolenstraat. Perhaps the alley led to a (red) mill that stood here outside the city wall before 1600.

name: Roompotstraat
en: A channel in the mouth of the Oosterschelde, along the coast of Walcheren.

name: Roomtuintjes
en: An old pleasure garden on the Mauritskade, where the Pieter Vlamingstraat now begins, demolished between 1880 and 1884 to build the Dapperbuurt.

name: Rooseveltlaan
en: Franklin Delano Roosevelt (1882-1945), president of the United States from 1933, of a Dutch family that emigrated to America in 1649. Partly through his fierce opposition to American neutrality, he had a large share in the Allied victory in the Second World War. When the street was laid out it was named Zuider Amstellaan (council decision of 22 March 1922).

name: Roosje Vospad
en: Socialist trade union leader and politician (1860-1932, married to M. Stel), who fought for universal suffrage, one of the first women to try to integrate her feminist views into a socialist position.

name: Roosje Vosstraat
en: Socialist trade union leader and politician (1860-1932, married to M. Stel), who fought for universal suffrage, one of the first women to try to integrate her feminist views into a socialist position.

name: Rooswijck
en: An eighteenth-century country estate with towers added later, between Santpoort and Velsen (Noord-Holland).

name: Rosa Luxemburgstraat
en: German politician (1870-1919), representative of the radical Marxist current in social democracy. During the First World War she was imprisoned for anti-war agitation. In 1918 she was one of the leaders of the communist Spartacus League, which was soon turned into the Kommunistische Partei Deutschlands. She was murdered by officers.

name: Rosa Manusstraat
en: Rosette Suzanne (Rosa) Manus (1881-1943), feminist and pacifist, the linchpin of the congresses of the International Woman Suffrage Alliance, who gave much of her energy to the peace movement, internationally too. In 1941 she was arrested by the occupiers, and in 1943 she died in the Ravensbrück concentration camp.

name: Rosa Overbeekbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after Rosa Overbeek, a character in the novels of Theo Thijssen (1879-1943). She is the girlfriend of Kees de jongen (Kees the boy), after whom bridge 123 is named.

name: Roseboom
en: Also called 'De Witte Roseboom' (the white rose tree), a whaler that sailed from the Oostzanerwerf around 1726. The ship was named after its owner, the shipowner Cornelis Roos (1691-1757).

name: Rosendaalstraat
en: A seventeenth-century inn on the Ringdijk (between the Schagerlaan and the Pauwenlaan), demolished around 1809.

name: Rosmarijnsteeg
en: Rosmarijn or rozemarijn (rosemary) is an evergreen, fragrant shrub. The alley was originally called Raamsteeg, but already appears under its present name in 1616. The name probably comes from a gable stone on one of the corner houses showing a rosemary. An old note has been found mentioning the decorators who lived here and made flowers and other finery for christenings and weddings, which may have prompted the gable stone and the alley's name.

name: Rossinistraat
en: Gioachino Rossini (1792-1868), Italian opera composer.

name: Rostockbrug
en: Rostock is a port in north-eastern Germany. The names in the Houthavens are taken from places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Rosy Wertheimstraat
en: Composer (1888-1949), whose compositions show the influence of Stravinsky and Debussy, among others.

name: Rotterdammerbrug
en: After the city of Rotterdam.

name: Rousseaustraat
en: Jean-Jacques Rousseau (1712-1778), French philosopher of the Enlightenment, one of the forerunners of the French Revolution, a writer on education and a composer.

name: Rozenburglaan
en: A country estate between the Kruislaan and Betondorp, built in 1642 and demolished in 1914 to extend the Nieuwe Ooster cemetery. It was originally called 'Het Vischkaantje', but was later named 'Rozenburg' after one of its owners, David Rutgers van Rozenburg.

name: Rozengracht
en: The flower (the rose). The Rozengracht was filled in in 1895.

name: Rozenoordmetrobrug
en: A former nursery on the Amstel, between Zorgvlied and Het Kalfje, and also the landing stage of the boat service between Ouderkerk and Amsterdam.

name: Rozenoordpad
en: A former nursery on the Amstel, between Zorgvlied and Het Kalfje, and also the landing stage of the boat service between Ouderkerk and Amsterdam.

name: Rozenoordspoorbrug
en: A former nursery on the Amstel, between Zorgvlied and Het Kalfje, and also the landing stage of the boat service between Ouderkerk and Amsterdam.

name: Rozenstraat
en: The flower (the rose), like the nearby Rozengracht.

name: Rozijnenstraat
en: The fruit, dried grapes (raisins), from southern Europe, Asia Minor, California and Australia.

name: Rubensstraat
en: Peter Paul Rubens (1577-1640), Southern Netherlandish painter of biblical scenes and history pieces, known for his voluptuous female figures, and the teacher of Anthony van Dyck.

name: Rudi Bloemgartensingel
en: Jewish resistance fighter (1920-1943), one of the nine involved in the attack on the Amsterdam population register on 27 March 1943. He was also involved in the attack on the railway near Sloterdijk and in founding the seditious magazine 'Rattenkruid' (rat poison).

name: Rudi van Dantzigstraat
en: Rudi van Dantzig was a Dutch choreographer, ballet dancer and writer, for twenty years artistic director of the Dutch National Ballet.

name: Rudolf Agricolastraat
en: Philosopher (1443-1485), whose real name was Roelof Huisman, from the province of Groningen, a renowned humanist and professor at Heidelberg.

name: Rudolf Dieselstraat
en: German engineer (1858-1913), inventor of the diesel engine named after him.

name: Rudolf Nurejevstraat
en: Rudolf Nureyev was a Russian-Austrian ballet dancer and choreographer.

name: Ruigoord
en: A former islet in the IJ, which after reclamation became a rise in the Houtrakpolder, where the hamlet of the same name grew up (now largely demolished).

name: Ruijgoordweg
en: A former islet in the IJ, which after reclamation became a rise in the Houtrakpolder, where the hamlet of the same name grew up (now largely demolished).

name: Ruimzicht
en: A former farm on the Uitweg, demolished to build the garden city of Osdorp.

name: Ruisbeekhof
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Ruiseveenpad
en: Named after a hamlet near Veenendaal (Utrecht).

name: Ruisrietstraat
en: A kind of reed (common reed) that grows along the water's edge.

name: Rumbeke
en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

name: Rumphiusstraat
en: Georgius Everhardus Rumphius (1627-1702), born in Germany, who in 1652 sailed on a VOC ship. From 1662 he began systematic research into the flora and fauna of the Indonesian island of Ambon.

name: Runstraat
en: Finely ground oak bark (run), used for tanning leather.

name: Rupelmonde
en: One of the first country estates built by Amsterdam patricians near Loenen aan de Vecht in the seventeenth century, still in the style of an Amsterdam canal house.

name: Rusland
en: The oldest spelling, in a deed of 1403, is 'Willem Ruusschentuin' (Willem Ruussche's garden). The name was then corrupted through ''t Ruyssenlandt', ''t Russeland' and ''t Ruslant' into today's incomprehensible Rusland (Russia). The street is so wide because its left-hand part was a little canal dug in 1537 (the Raamsloot), which was filled in again that same century.

name: Rustenburgerdwarsstraat
en: The street was laid out in 1878 on the Rustenburgerpad, which recalls the former country estate Rustenburg, from 1620.

name: Rustenburgerstraat
en: The street was laid out in 1878 on the Rustenburgerpad, which recalls the former country estate Rustenburg, from 1620.

name: Rusthofstraat
en: A former farmstead on the Weesperzijde, level with the Fahrenheitsingel, originally called Voorzigt, renamed Rusthof in 1807 and pulled down around 1820.

name: Rutherfordstraat
en: Ernest Rutherford (1871-1937), New Zealand-born British physicist and chemist, known for his work on radioactivity, who received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1908.

name: Ruud Krolbrug
en: Ruud Krol, born 24 March 1949 in Amsterdam. Six times Dutch champion, four times KNVB Cup winner, three times winner of the European Cup, twice winner of the European Super Cup, once winner of the Intercontinental Cup. Krol played 339 league matches for Ajax and won 83 caps, playing in two World Cup finals, one of them as captain of the Netherlands. He was assistant coach at Ajax between 2002 and 2005. In 1969 Ajax became the first Dutch club to reach the final of the prestigious European Cup, today's Champions League. Ajax lost that final, but two years later, in 1971, won the most important prize in football after all. In the two following years Ajax retained the title, confirming itself as the standard-bearer of Dutch football. Not only the titles but the way they were won, with modern, attacking football, made Ajax an international sensation. Coach Rinus Michels moulded this rare concentration of talent into a legendary team that was both untouchable and trend-setting at home and abroad.

name: Ruys de Beerenbrouckstraat
en: Jhr. Charles Joseph Marie Ruijs de Beerenbrouck (1873-1936), Roman Catholic statesman, Minister of Justice and several times prime minister, holding the Interior portfolio.

name: Ruyschstraat
en: Frederik Ruysch (1638-1731), professor in Amsterdam, a famous anatomist, surgeon and botanist. The street was earlier called Derde Boerhaavestraat (council decision of 15 November 1882).

name: Ruysdaelkade
en: A seventeenth-century family of painters and engravers, the best known of whom was Jacob Isaacksz. van Ruisdael (1628-1682), landscape painter and teacher of Hobbema. The street already existed under this name in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1888.

name: Ruysdaelstraat
en: A seventeenth-century family of painters and engravers, the best known of whom was Jacob Isaacksz. van Ruisdael (1628-1682), landscape painter and teacher of Hobbema. The street already existed under this name in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1888.

name: S. F. van Ossstraat
en: S.F. van Oss (1868-1949), journalist, founder (1913) and editor-in-chief of the weekly 'De Haagsche Post', who wrote weekly humorous and satirical pieces under the pseudonym Jhr. Goeree d'Overflacque.

name: Saaftingestraat
en: A region in the north-east of Zeeuws-Vlaanderen (Saeftinghe), flooded in 1583 for strategic reasons (the defence of Antwerp) and never diked again.

name: Saenredamstraat
en: Pieter Jansz. Saenredam (1597-1665), painter, whose works include 'Interior of the St Bavo Church' and 'The Old City Hall on the Dam'.

name: Saffierstraat
en: A hard blue gemstone (sapphire).

name: Sagittahof
en: A constellation (Sagitta, the Arrow) in the northern sky.

name: Sallandstraat
en: One of the three quarters of Overijssel, between Gramsbergen and Deventer; the others are Twente and Vollenhove.

name: Saltetstraat
en: Rudolph Hendrik Saltet (1853-1927), hygienist and professor in Amsterdam, who did important work for public health.

name: Salzmannhof
en: Christian G. Salzmann (1744-1811), German educator of the Enlightenment.

name: Sam de Wolffstraat
en: Salomon de Wolff (1878-1960), economist and politician of Jewish descent, member of the Provincial States of Noord-Holland from 1909 to 1913 and private lecturer at the University of Amsterdam from 1930 to 1940. In 1943 he was arrested and deported to the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, from where he was allowed to go to Palestine (Israel).

name: Sam van Houtenstraat
en: Samuel van Houten (1837-1930), politician, at first liberal and later conservative, Minister of the Interior from 1894 to 1897. As a member of parliament he introduced a bill on child labour, the first social law, known as Van Houten's Kinderwetje (children's law, 1874).

name: Samosstraat
en: A Greek island in the eastern Aegean.

name: Sandenburch
en: A former castle near Veere, built in the thirteenth or fourteenth century by a member of the old knightly Van Sande family, and for many years home to the lords of Borssele. (Not to be confused with the still existing Sandenburg on the Langbroekerwetering.)

name: Sanderijnstraat
en: One of the main characters of the abel spel (secular play) 'Lanseloet van Denemerken' ('Lanseloet ende Sanderijn', from about 1400).

name: Sandhorst
en: A lost medieval castle in Wassenaar, demolished in 1818 after repeated rebuilding.

name: Sandinostraat
en: Augusto Sandino (1895-1934), resistance leader in Nicaragua, who from 1926 to 1934 fought with his guerrilla group in the mountains of Nicaragua against the American troops and the presidents they kept in power. He was arrested and murdered by the National Guard.

name: Sandwijk
en: The name of a country house with a large garden on the Oosterweg in the Purmer. It is now a farm called Abcoude.

name: Sanne Sanneshof
en: Photographer (1937-1967), whose central theme was 'woman'. He sought a new visual language and found it in combining photography and film. When he was killed in an accident at the age of thirty he was a leading photographer in the Netherlands, on the verge of an international breakthrough.

name: Santoriniweg
en: A Greek island in the Mediterranean (Rhodes).

name: Sape Kuiperplantsoen
en: Resistance fighter (1924-1943), born in Arnhem, executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

name: Sara Burgerhartstraat
en: Named after the heroine of the epistolary novel 'Historie van mejuffrouw Sara Burgerhart' (the history of Miss Sara Burgerhart) by Betje Wolff and Aagje Deken, of 1782.

name: Sarah Vaughanstraat
en: Sarah Lois Vaughan (1924-1990), regarded as one of the most important American jazz singers in history, known for her great vocal range, expressive voice and strong vibrato.

name: Sardiniëweg
en: The Italian island in the Mediterranean (Sardinia).

name: Sarphatikade
en: Samuel Sarphati (1813-1866), Amsterdam doctor and pharmacist with many connections in banking circles, who did much for the city. He drew up plans for extending the city around the Frederiksplein and beyond the Singelgracht, for which he founded the Nederlandsche Bouwmaatschappij in 1864. The societies and buildings that came about through him include the Society for Agriculture (1848), the Society for Industry (1852) with the Paleis voor Volksvlijt it built (1864), the School of Commerce, the National Mortgage Bank and the Amstel Hotel (1866). Before the Sarphatipark was named, the streets around it were parts of the Ceintuurbaan, Jan Steenstraat, Van der Helststraat and Sweelinckstraat. The Sarphatistraat originally appears under the name Schans.

name: Sarphatipark
en: Samuel Sarphati (1813-1866), Amsterdam doctor and pharmacist with many connections in banking circles, who did much for the city. He drew up plans for extending the city around the Frederiksplein and beyond the Singelgracht, for which he founded the Nederlandsche Bouwmaatschappij in 1864. The societies and buildings that came about through him include the Society for Agriculture (1848), the Society for Industry (1852) with the Paleis voor Volksvlijt it built (1864), the School of Commerce, the National Mortgage Bank and the Amstel Hotel (1866). Before the Sarphatipark was named, the streets around it were parts of the Ceintuurbaan, Jan Steenstraat, Van der Helststraat and Sweelinckstraat. The Sarphatistraat originally appears under the name Schans.

name: Sarphatistraat
en: Samuel Sarphati (1813-1866), Amsterdam doctor and pharmacist with many connections in banking circles, who did much for the city. He drew up plans for extending the city around the Frederiksplein and beyond the Singelgracht, for which he founded the Nederlandsche Bouwmaatschappij in 1864. The societies and buildings that came about through him include the Society for Agriculture (1848), the Society for Industry (1852) with the Paleis voor Volksvlijt it built (1864), the School of Commerce, the National Mortgage Bank and the Amstel Hotel (1866). Before the Sarphatipark was named, the streets around it were parts of the Ceintuurbaan, Jan Steenstraat, Van der Helststraat and Sweelinckstraat. The Sarphatistraat originally appears under the name Schans.

name: Saskia van Uijlenburgkade
en: Wife of Rembrandt van Rijn (1612-1642). She probably met Rembrandt through her uncle Hendrick, an art dealer. The couple married in 1634, and their son Titus was born in 1641. She is buried in the Oude Kerk.

name: Sassenheimstraat
en: The Zuid-Holland village between Lisse and Warmond.

name: Saturnusstraat
en: The planet (Saturn), one of the largest in our solar system.

name: Sausalitolaan
en: A town on San Francisco Bay, whose waterfront promenade is being renovated in the second decade of the twenty-first century.

name: Savelsbos
en: A nature reserve near Gronsveld (South Limburg), 174 ha in all: a hillside wood with rare fauna and flora and a prehistoric flint workshop.

name: Saxen-Weimarlaan
en: The German princely house (Saxe-Weimar), related by marriage to the Dutch royal house of Orange-Nassau.

name: Saxenburgerdwarsstraat
en: A former country estate, later a pottery, that stood here until 1879. The street came over under this name from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

name: Saxenburgerstraat
en: A former country estate, later a pottery, that stood here until 1879. The street came over under this name from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

name: Scannerstraat
en: A device with which a computer can read and store text and images. As a counterpart to the street names recalling Amsterdam-Noord's former shipbuilding industry, this name refers to modern information technology.

name: Schaafstraat
en: A carpenter's tool (the plane).

name: Schaarbeekstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Schaarsbergenstraat
en: A village on the edge of the Hoge Veluwe National Park (Gelderland).

name: Schaepmanstraat
en: Herman Johan A.M. Schaepman (1844-1903), Roman Catholic priest, statesman and poet, professor at the Rijsenburg seminary. A member of parliament from 1880 to 1903, he favoured wider suffrage and social legislation. He edited the daily 'De Tijd' and later 'Het Centrum'. As a poet he followed Bilderdijk and Da Costa.

name: Schagerlaan
en: Robert van Schager, occupant of the farmstead 't Roode Hart, the only farmstead on this avenue to survive the flood of 1651.

name: Schaikstraat
en: A village south of Ravenstein (Noord-Brabant).

name: Schakelstraat
en: The connection (switch), here of electric current.

name: Schalk Burgerstraat
en: Willem Schalk Burger (1852-1918), one of the popular leaders of the young South African Republic and a Boer general in the Second Boer War (1899-1902). After Paul Kruger left for Europe he was acting president of the Transvaal.

name: Schalkwijkpad
en: A village in the province of Utrecht, on the Utrecht-Culemborg railway.

name: Schapensteeg
en: Named after a former landowner, Jacob Schaap. From its oldest mention (1595) the alley appears as Jacob Schapensteeg; only in the course of the seventeenth century does the name appear as just Schapensteeg.

name: Scharenburg
en: The port of Scarborough on the east coast of England, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Scharenslijperspad
en: Basket-making was originally a typical travelling trade. The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

name: Scharrebiersluis
en: Scharrebier was the traditional drink of ordinary workmen. This 'thin' beer used to be sold on this drawbridge, because many working people were often gathered there.

name: Scharwouderstraat
en: This 'thin' beer used to be sold on this drawbridge, because many working people were often gathered there.

name: Scheepmakerskade
en: An unofficial name of this bridge is Rapenburgerschutsluis. The origin of the name Rapenburg is unknown.

name: Scheepsbouwkade
en: A reference to the NSM and later NDSM yard on the north side of the IJ, where ships were built between 1922 and 1978.

name: Scheepsbouwweg
en: The name recalls the shipyard, and especially the newbuilding yard, where many seagoing ships were built until the 1970s.

name: Scheepstimmermanstraat
en: The trade name for those who build ships in wood (ship's carpenter).

name: Scheldeplein
en: The river (Scheldt) that rises in France, enters the Netherlands beyond Antwerp and then flows into the sea through the Westerschelde.

name: Scheldestraat
en: The river (Scheldt) that rises in France, enters the Netherlands beyond Antwerp and then flows into the sea through the Westerschelde.

name: Schellingwouderbreek
en: The village of Schellingwoude.

name: Schellingwouderbrug
en: The village of Schellingwoude.

name: Schellingwouderdijk
en: The village (Schellingwoude). The dike is part of the Waterland sea dike.

name: Schelluinenstraat
en: The village north-west of Gorinchem (Zuid-Holland).

name: Schelvisch Hoofd
en: Named after the place where the Noord-Holland tram station stood, which was also the terminus of the ferry from the Noord-Zuidhollandsch Koffiehuis to Centraal Station.

name: Schepenbergweg
en: The name of a hill near Meerssen (Limburg).

name: Schepenlaan
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after types of ships and ship's parts.

name: Schermerstraat
en: A lake in Noord-Holland (the Schermer), drained between 1631 and 1635.

name: Scherpenzeelstraat
en: A village in the Gelderse Vallei (Gelderland).

name: Schielandplein
en: A place in Zuid-Holland.

name: Schiemanstraat
en: A naval trade name: the petty officer on board responsible for the rigging forward of the mast (the boatswain).

name: Schiermonnikoogstraat
en: A Wadden island (Friesland).

name: Schierstins
en: A fourteenth-century defensible tower house at Veenwouden (Friesland), restored in 1962. Before 1439 it came into the possession of the grey (schiere) monks of Klaarkamp Abbey.

name: Schillingdijk
en: The currency of Austria before the euro (the schilling).

name: Schimmelstraat
en: Hendrik Jan Schimmel (1825-1906), bank director, known as a novelist and playwright and also editor of 'De Gids'. These streets came into Amsterdam in 1896 with the names set by Nieuwer-Amstel, Van Speyckstraat and Van Speyckdwarsstraat, but were renamed in 1922, after the annexation of Sloten brought a second Van Speyckstraat within the city boundary.

name: Schinkel
en: A schinkel is a short connecting stretch between two weteringen (drainage channels), in this case the Nieuwe Meer and the Overtoom. It is thought the connection owes its name to its shape: 'schinkel' is a synonym of 'schenkel', the lower leg between foot and knee. The quay was earlier called Visserkade by Nieuwer-Amstel. The municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel had named the streets Visserstraat, Alexanderstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 20 October 1882) and Willemsparkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 30 January 1883), but in 1896 they were changed because of confusion with names that already existed in Amsterdam.

name: Schinkelhavenkade
en: The name recalls the old roadside inn Schinkelhaven. Before 1922 the street was part of the Schinkelkade.

name: Schinkelhavenstraat
en: The name recalls the old roadside inn Schinkelhaven. Before 1922 the street was part of the Schinkelkade.

name: Schinkelkade
en: A schinkel is a short connecting stretch between two weteringen (drainage channels), in this case the Nieuwe Meer and the Overtoom. It is thought the connection owes its name to its shape: 'schinkel' is a synonym of 'schenkel', the lower leg between foot and knee. The quay was earlier called Visserkade by Nieuwer-Amstel. The municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel had named the streets Visserstraat, Alexanderstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 20 October 1882) and Willemsparkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 30 January 1883), but in 1896 they were changed because of confusion with names that already existed in Amsterdam.

name: Schipbeekstraat
en: A shipping canal dug in the fifteenth century and extended in later centuries, on the border of Gelderland and Overijssel, which joins the IJssel at Deventer.

name: Schipluidenlaan
en: A village in the Westland, south of Delft.

name: Schippersgracht
en: In this neighbourhood, on the harbour side, skippers (schippers) and seamen made up most of the population, which gave the canal and the street their names.

name: Schippersstraat
en: In this neighbourhood, on the harbour side, skippers (schippers) and seamen made up most of the population, which gave the canal and the street their names.

name: Schoenerstraat
en: A small merchant ship with a sharp bow and two or more masts (a schooner).

name: Schoffelstraat
en: The garden tool (the hoe).

name: Schokkerjachtdijk
en: A ship, a fishing vessel related to the botter. The name probably comes from the island of Schokland. Schokkers were known for their great seaworthiness.

name: Schokkerspad
en: A small fishing boat, originally from Schokland.

name: Schoklandstraat
en: A former island in the Zuiderzee, now part of the Noordoostpolder.

name: Schollenbrug
en: After the inn that once stood here, named after the old Schollenbrug in the Weesperzijde that linked the Watergraafsmeer with the city. That bridge was earlier called the Schulpbrug, after the seventeenth-century inn de Schulp, which stood on the other side of the bridge, in the Watergraafsmeer (with a shell, schulp, on its façade).

name: Schollenbrugpad
en: After the inn that once stood here, named after the old Schollenbrug in the Weesperzijde that linked the Watergraafsmeer with the city. That bridge was earlier called the Schulpbrug, after the seventeenth-century inn de Schulp, which stood on the other side of the bridge, in the Watergraafsmeer (with a shell, schulp, on its façade).

name: Schollenbrugstraat
en: After the inn that once stood here, named after the old Schollenbrug in the Weesperzijde that linked the Watergraafsmeer with the city. That bridge was earlier called the Schulpbrug, after the seventeenth-century inn de Schulp, which stood on the other side of the bridge, in the Watergraafsmeer (with a shell, schulp, on its façade).

name: Schonerwoerdstraat
en: A village in the so-called Vijfheerenlanden (Zuid-Holland).

name: Schoolmeesterstraat
en: Named after the pseudonym 'De Schoolmeester' (the schoolmaster) of the Dutch poet Gerrit van de Linde (1808-1858).

name: Schoolstraat
en: After the old municipal school of Nieuwer-Amstel.

name: Schooltuinpad
en: Refers to the nearby school gardens.

name: Schoonboomstraat
en: A former church village on Zuid-Beveland, drowned by a storm flood in 1532.

name: Schoonhovendreef
en: A town on the Lek, on the border of Utrecht and Zuid-Holland.

name: Schoorlstraat
en: A village at the foot of the dunes, north of Alkmaar.

name: Schopenhauerhof
en: Arthur Schopenhauer (1788-1860), German philosopher, who denied the existence of a causally free will.

name: Schorpioenstraat
en: A constellation (Scorpius), a sign of the zodiac.

name: Schotse Hooglanden
en: The mountains of Scotland.

name: Schotse Huizenpad
en: The mountains of Scotland.

name: Schoutensteeg
en: After a former resident, Jan Arentsz Schouten; in the fifteenth century the alley's full name was Jan Arentszn Schoutensteeg. He was schout (sheriff) of Amsterdam from 1426 to 1430. Before that the name Willem Noirtsteeg was also used.

name: Schouwstraat
en: 't Schouw is a hamlet on the Noordhollandsch Kanaal, by Amsterdam's northern boundary.

name: Schovenstraat
en: Bundled stalks of corn (sheaves).

name: Schubertstraat
en: Franz Schubert (1797-1828), Austrian composer of symphonies, chamber music and songs, among them 'Die Forelle', 'Erlkönig' and the cycle 'Winterreise'.

name: Schuitenhuisstraat
en: A schuitenhuis is generally a shed for boats (now a boathouse). The name appears on a historical map of 1659 (by Stevijn and Van Broeckhuysen) near the inn 'De drie Baarsjes'.

name: Schurenbergweg
en: A hill near Hoensbroek (Limburg).

name: Schutterweg
en: The constellation of the Archer, Sagittarius, in the zodiac.

name: Schweigmannstraat
en: Antonius Petrus Paulus Schweigmann (1893-1945), resistance fighter, born in Leeuwarden, died in Sandbostel (Germany).

name: Science Park
en: A campus for international knowledge institutes in ICT, the exact sciences and natural science research.

name: Sean MacBridestraat
en: Irish politician (1904-1988). After the Second World War he was Minister for External Affairs and was actively involved in the making of the Geneva Conventions and the European Convention on Human Rights. In 1961 he was one of the founders of Amnesty International. He received both the Soviet (Lenin) Peace Prize and the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Seifertplein
en: Jaroslav Seifert (1901-1986), Czech writer. After the Soviet invasion his strongly anti-fascist and patriotic work could only circulate underground. In 1984 he received the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Seineweg
en: A river in France.

name: Seinwachterstraat
en: A railway official who works the signals from a signal box beside the line (signalman).

name: Seizoenenhof
en: The name matches the adjoining neighbourhood, whose streets are named after the four seasons.

name: Semarangstraat
en: A city on the island of Java (Indonesia).

name: Senecastraat
en: Roman philosopher and poet (4 BC - AD 65), tutor of Nero, who later forced him to commit suicide.

name: Senefelderstraat
en: Aloys Senefelder (1771-1834), Prague-born German actor and printer, inventor of lithography.

name: Seranggracht
en: A river on the Indonesian island of Java.

name: Serge Lifarsteeg
en: Serge Lifar was a Russian-French dancer, choreographer, ballet director and author.

name: Servaes Noutsstraat
en: Michiel Servaes Nouts (1630-1693), the first carillonneur of the city hall on the Dam.

name: Servetsteeg
en: This name already appears here in the seventeenth century, but the original name Revet- or Ravetsteeg was also used into the eighteenth century. A revet, ravet or rabat is a court for kaatsen, a handball game. This court stood on the corner of the alley and the burgwal, so it may be assumed that Servet (napkin) is a corruption of Revet.

name: Sextantweg
en: The navigation instrument, for measuring angles to fix a position at sea by the stars.

name: Shackletonstraat
en: Sir Ernest Henry Shackleton (1874-1922), Irish-born British Antarctic explorer, whose Nimrod expedition sent the first party to reach the South Magnetic Pole, in 1909.

name: Sibogastraat
en: Siboga or Sibolga is a town on the west coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

name: Sibrandus Stratinghstraat
en: Inventor and chemist (1785-1841), professor at Groningen, where he developed and tested motorised vehicles. In 1834 he was possibly the first person in the Netherlands to make a test drive in a steam carriage. He probably also built the world's first small electromagnetic vehicle.

name: Siciliëweg
en: An Italian island in the Mediterranean.

name: Siebren van der Baanhof
en: Resistance hero (1894-1944), sexton of the Reformed church on the Keizersgracht, where he hid weapons and other material of the resistance. When the occupiers discovered it in 1944 he was shot dead on the pavement in front of the building, together with the minister Ferwerda. Van der Baan was also active in distributing the underground paper 'Trouw'.

name: Sieg Vaz Diasstraat
en: Journalist (1904-1943) and resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

name: Sierenborch
en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of Cherbourg, found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Sierplein
en: Before houses were built on this square and it got an official name, it was popularly called Sierplein (ornamental square) because of its decorative paving.

name: Sieverdinkpad
en: The name of an old farm near Winterswijk.

name: Sijlhoff
en: A former castle in Leiderdorp, first built around 1292, destroyed in 1420, rebuilt in the Spanish period and finally demolished in the eighteenth century.

name: Sijpestein
en: A castle mentioned as early as 1288, destroyed and rebuilt several times. In 1911 the old foundations were uncovered and the castle was rebuilt in the old style. It lies near Loosdrecht.

name: Sijsjesbergweg
en: A hill near Huizen (Noord-Holland), north of the Tafelberg.

name: Sijsjesstraat
en: A songbird (the siskin).

name: Sikkelstraat
en: A farm tool for cutting corn stalks (the sickle).

name: Silenestraat
en: A plant (campion) of the carnation family, growing in the dunes and along verges.

name: Silodam
en: The breakwater in the IJ. From the end of the nineteenth century a large grain silo stood here, later joined by a second. Both silos are out of use and are being converted into homes.

name: Silvoldestraat
en: The Gelderland village on the Oude IJssel.

name: Silvretta
en: A mountain range on the border of Switzerland and Austria, whose highest peak, Piz Linard, is 3411 metres high.

name: Simon Carmiggeltstraat
en: Simon Johannes Carmiggelt (1913-1987), writer and journalist, best known for his newspaper columns ('Kronkels'), published under the pseudonym Kronkel in 'Het Parool'. In 1974 Carmiggelt received the P.C. Hooft Prize.

name: Simon Stevinstraat
en: Mathematician and engineer (1548-1620), head of the water authority and tutor of Prince Maurits, inventor of decimal fractions and of the sailing carriage. When it was laid out the street was named Kerklaan by the municipality of Watergraafsmeer (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 9 February 1901).

name: Simon van Gijnpad
en: The Museum Mr. Simon van Gijn in Dordrecht. In 1925 the former house, from 1729, of the banker and collector Simon van Gijn (1836-1922) was turned into a museum. Besides its authentic interiors, the museum is known for its collection of Dutch historical prints and its applied art and old toys.

name: Simon van Woerdenstraat
en: Simon van Woerden (1902-1998) designed the Bethelkerk around 1958.

name: Simone de Beauvoirstraat
en: French writer (1908-1986), who taught philosophy in Marseille, Rouen and Paris from 1931 to 1943. Her literary work is critical, sharp and steeped in her existentialist way of life.

name: Simonshavenstraat
en: A village on the Zuid-Holland island of Putten.

name: Simonskerkestraat
en: The village on Schouwen-Duiveland (Zeeland) drowned in 1484.

name: Simsonstraat
en: The hero of the Israelites in the Old Testament (Samson), a symbol of strength, whose beloved Delilah robbed him of his hair and so of his strength.

name: Sinaasappelstraat
en: The citrus fruit (the orange).

name: Sinderenstraat
en: A hamlet near Varsseveld (Gelderland).

name: Singel
en: A singel is a stretch of water or a road along the outer edge of a town. In Amsterdam the Singel (Amsterdammers say 'het Singel') formed the city boundary in the second half of the fifteenth century, inside which the walls and gates were built. At that time the moat was called 't Singel or the Stedegracht (now the Singel, Kloveniersburgwal and Geldersekade). Today's Singel has kept the old name. In the seventeenth century the city government did introduce the name Koningsgracht for it, but that name did not stick.

name: Singelgracht
en: A singel is a stretch of water or a road along the outer edge of a town. In Amsterdam the Singel (Amsterdammers say 'het Singel') formed the city boundary in the second half of the fifteenth century, inside which the walls and gates were built. At that time the moat was called 't Singel or the Stedegracht (now the Singel, Kloveniersburgwal and Geldersekade). Today's Singel has kept the old name. In the seventeenth century the city government did introduce the name Koningsgracht for it, but that name did not stick.

name: Singerstraat
en: The Singer Museum in Laren. The American painter W.H. Singer Jr. (1868-1943) came to Laren around 1900 and had a villa built in 1911. In 1956 a new wing of the building was opened as a museum. Its collection is based on that of the Singer couple: nineteenth- and twentieth-century works mainly by Dutch and French artists.

name: Sinjeur Semeynsstraat
en: After the book 'Sinjeur Semeyns' by H.J. Schimmel.

name: Sint Agnietenstraat
en: The St Agnes convent stood here, founded in 1397, destroyed in the great city fire of 1452 and rebuilt. Its surviving convent church, the Agnietenkapel, dates from 1470 and housed the Athenaeum from 1632 to 1862.

name: Sint Annendwarsstraat
en: Probably named after a small statue of a saint, depicting St Anne.

name: Sint Annenstraat
en: Probably named after a small statue of a saint, depicting St Anne.

name: Sint Antoniesbreestraat
en: Named after the Sint Antoniesdijk, the sea dike outside the city until the seventeenth century, which in turn took its name from the St Anthony's hospital or leper house.

name: Sint Antoniesluis
en: Named after the Sint Antoniesdijk, the sea dike outside the city until the seventeenth century, which in turn took its name from the St Anthony's hospital or leper house. Before 1976 the Sint Antoniesluis was part of the Zwanenburgwal.

name: Sint Jacobsdwarsstraat
en: Probably named after a statue of a saint, depicting the apostle James, on the façade of one of the corner houses. The St James's chapel will not have given the name, as it lay further north on the Nieuwendijk.

name: Sint Jacobsstraat
en: Probably named after a statue of a saint, depicting the apostle James, on the façade of one of the corner houses. The St James's chapel will not have given the name, as it lay further north on the Nieuwendijk.

name: Sint Jansstraat
en: Probably named after a small statue of a saint, depicting the apostle John, on the façade of one of the corner houses.

name: Sint Jorisstraat
en: After the St George's hospital that stood here, founded in the second half of the fourteenth century and demolished at the end of the sixteenth to extend the city.

name: Sint Luciënsteeg
en: The former St Lucy's convent, which after 1578 was taken into the complex of the Burgerweeshuis (the civic orphanage, now the Amsterdam Museum).

name: Sint Nicolaasbrug
en: St Nicholas of Myra is the patron saint of Amsterdam, and this bridge lies opposite the Basilica of St Nicholas (1887) on the Prins Hendrikkade.

name: Sint Nicolaasstraat
en: Probably named after a small statue of the saint, which must have stood on the façade at the corner of the street.

name: Sint Olofspoort
en: The Sint Olofspoort was one of the oldest city gates and stood here from before 1380 until 1618. It took its name from the adjoining St Olaf's chapel, which still stands and is one of the oldest surviving buildings in Amsterdam. Remains of the gate's foundations have been found. The Sint Olofssteeg was called Oudezijds Wijde Kapelsteeg until 1914.

name: Sint Olofssteeg
en: The Sint Olofspoort was one of the oldest city gates and stood here from before 1380 until 1618. It took its name from the adjoining St Olaf's chapel, which still stands and is one of the oldest surviving buildings in Amsterdam. Remains of the gate's foundations have been found. The Sint Olofssteeg was called Oudezijds Wijde Kapelsteeg until 1914.

name: Sint Pieterspoortsteeg
en: The gate is a remnant of the St Peter's hospital, which already stood here in the second half of the fourteenth century. In 1578 the hospital moved to the Binnengasthuis, and the buildings apart from the gate were pulled down and rebuilt as a bank.

name: Sint Willibrordusdwarsstraat
en: Named after the church of that name, dedicated to St Willibrord, the seventh-century Anglo-Saxon preacher and archbishop who brought Christianity to the whole of the Dutch lands. The church was demolished as unsafe in 1970. The street and the side street were taken over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel in 1896 under the names Kerkstraat, Hoedemakerskade (council decisions of Nieuwer-Amstel, 22 August 1890 and 28 August 1891) and Eerste Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 22 August 1890).

name: Sint Willibrordusstraat
en: Named after the church of that name, dedicated to St Willibrord, the seventh-century Anglo-Saxon preacher and archbishop who brought Christianity to the whole of the Dutch lands. The church was demolished as unsafe in 1970. The street and the side street were taken over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel in 1896 under the names Kerkstraat, Hoedemakerskade (council decisions of Nieuwer-Amstel, 22 August 1890 and 28 August 1891) and Eerste Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 22 August 1890).

name: Sint-Hubertpad
en: A Belgian town (Saint-Hubert) in the province of Luxembourg.

name: Sint-Truidenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Siriusstraat
en: One of the largest and brightest stars, in the constellation Canis Major (the Great Dog).

name: Sixhaven
en: Jonkheer Willem Six (1859-1919), chairman of the Royal Sailing and Rowing Club from 1898 to 1919 and a great promoter of digging the marina in Amsterdam-Noord. He died two months before the harbour was completed, after which it was named after him.

name: Sixhavenweg
en: Jonkheer Willem Six (1859-1919), chairman of the Royal Sailing and Rowing Club from 1898 to 1919 and a great promoter of digging the marina in Amsterdam-Noord. He died two months before the harbour was completed, after which it was named after him.

name: Sjai Agnonstraat
en: Shmuel Yosef Agnon (1887-1970) was the first writer in Hebrew to win the Nobel Prize in Literature. He is known by the acronym Shai as a first name.

name: Skûtsjespad
en: A traditional type of tjalk: a sailing vessel for sea and river work, with a round bow, a flat bottom and leeboards.

name: Slaakstraat
en: A stretch of water between Sint Philipsland and Noord-Brabant, dammed in 1884.

name: Slangenburg
en: A fifteenth-century castle near Doetinchem, rebuilt in the seventeenth century under General Van Baer van Slangenburg.

name: Slatuinenweg
en: This is what remains of the former Slatuinenpad, which until 1927 ran from the Baarsjesweg to the Haarlemmerweg past market gardens (slatuinen, where lettuce and vegetables were grown). It was a favourite walk for Amsterdammers.

name: Slauerhoffstraat
en: Jan Jacob Slauerhoff (1898-1936), doctor and poet, who roamed the whole world as a ship's doctor, which shows in the constant restlessness of his poetry.

name: Sleewijkstraat
en: The village of Sleeuwijk on the Merwede opposite Gorinchem (Noord-Brabant).

name: Slego
en: The old Dutch rendering of the port of Sligo, on the north-west coast of Ireland.

name: Sleutelbloemstraat
en: Also called primula (cowslip), a plant of meadows and old estates.

name: Sleutelbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after the seventeenth-century brewery 'De Sleutel' (the key), owned by Gerrit Bicker, which stood on the site of today's Binnengasthuis grounds.

name: Slibveldenweg
en: The road ends just past the Wijsentkade in a rectangular plot where the 'Slibvelden' (silt fields) were laid out at the end of the 1950s. The path is popularly known as the 'Slibveldenweg'.

name: Slichtenhorststraat
en: A hamlet and estate near Nijkerk (Gelderland).

name: Sliedrechtstraat
en: A town on the Beneden-Merwede, long known for its dredging firms and shipyards.

name: Slijkstraat
en: Named after the state of the ground (slijk = mud) in the sixteenth century. In the centre of Amsterdam several street names hint at the former marshy ground. At the time only the main streets were raised (such as the Zandstraat and the Dijkstraat).

name: Slijperweg
en: A metalworker who smooths the surface of metal objects (a grinder).

name: Slikkerveerstraat
en: A village on IJsselmonde, where the Lek and the Noord meet.

name: Slimmeweg
en: This is the former name of the Osdorperweg, as found on old maps of the area.

name: Slingerbeekstraat
en: A stream in the Gelderland Achterhoek that flows into the Oude IJssel at Doetinchem.

name: Slochterweg
en: The original name of the stretch of the Noordhollandsch Kanaal alongside, which linked the Buiksloter Meer with the Broeker Meer. Before this naming the road was part of the Kanaaldijk (Landsmeer until 1966) and the Leeuwarderweg.

name: Sloestraat
en: A former tidal channel between Walcheren and Zuid-Beveland, now entirely reclaimed.

name: Slootdorpstraat
en: The village in the Wieringermeer polder.

name: Slootstraat
