en: The street was laid out in 1660 on a filled-in ditch (sloot) by the former City Carpentry Yard.

name: Sloterdijkerbrug
en: The old dike village, of which the church and a small part remain. It belonged to the municipality of Sloten, joined to Amsterdam in 1921. The village was originally called Sloterdam and in earlier centuries had a harbour and a lock.

name: Sloterdijkerweg
en: The old dike village, of which the church and a small part remain. It belonged to the municipality of Sloten, joined to Amsterdam in 1921. The village was originally called Sloterdam and in earlier centuries had a harbour and a lock.

name: Sloterdijkstraat
en: Opinions differ about how this street got its name. Some say a house called Sloterdijk on the corner of the street gave it the name; others link it directly with the village of Sloterdijk, which could be seen from the street.

name: Sloterkade
en: After the village of Sloten, which until 1 January 1921 was the main village of the municipality of Sloten, which also included the village of Sloterdijk and the hamlet of Osdorp. The municipality stretched from the Haarlemmermeer to the North Sea Canal and from the Schinkel to Halfweg.

name: Slotermeerlaan
en: The name comes from the Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk which, after repeated drainings, was dug out again into water for sand extraction. This water is the Sloterplas.

name: Sloterparkbadsingel
en: The name comes from the Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk which, after repeated drainings, was dug out again into water for sand extraction. This water is the Sloterplas.

name: Sloterplas
en: The name comes from the Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk which, after repeated drainings, was dug out again into water for sand extraction. This water is the Sloterplas.

name: Slotervaart
en: The name comes from the Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk which, after repeated drainings, was dug out again into water for sand extraction. This water is the Sloterplas.

name: Sloterweg
en: After the village of Sloten, which until 1 January 1921 was the main village of the municipality of Sloten, which also included the village of Sloterdijk and the hamlet of Osdorp. The municipality stretched from the Haarlemmermeer to the North Sea Canal and from the Schinkel to Halfweg. The Sloterweg originally ran to (or began at) the Schinkel. Building the ring road removed part of it.

name: Slufter
en: A nature reserve on the island of Texel. The Slufter has several creeks still open to the sea, and is a breeding ground for seabirds and spoonbills.

name: Sluispad
en: The path runs along the lock (sluis) in the Gaasp here.

name: Sluisstraat
en: An artificial water barrier (a lock), in which opening and closing gates controls the connection between two waters.

name: Smaksteeg
en: The name already appears in the sixteenth century and comes from a gable stone on a corner house showing a smak, a kind of seagoing ship.

name: Smallepadsgracht
en: A ship, a flat-bottomed vessel of Frisian origin with leeboards and a gaff-rigged mast, well suited to shallow water. The smalschip was used to load goods and unload larger ships.

name: Smalschipstraat
en: A ship, a flat-bottomed vessel of Frisian origin with leeboards and a gaff-rigged mast, well suited to shallow water. The smalschip was used to load goods and unload larger ships.

name: Smaragdplein
en: These and other streets were laid out on the site of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM). To recall that former use, the names of the various workshops were used, in this case the shipyard's smithy.

name: Smaragdstraat
en: A grass-green gemstone (emerald).

name: Smederij
en: These and other streets were laid out on the site of the former Amsterdamsche Droogdok Maatschappij (ADM). To recall that former use, the names of the various workshops were used, in this case the shipyard's smithy.

name: Smederij Meisterbrug
en: A family business (the Meister smithy) in the Bellamybuurt, founded in 1909.

name: Smitstraat
en: Nicolaas Jacobus Smit, general in the Transvaal Boers' First War of Independence (1880-1881), in which he defeated the British at Ingogo. In 1883 he negotiated for the Boers in London.

name: Sneeuwbalstraat
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Sneeuwbalweg
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Snellerwaardgracht
en: A village on the Hollandse IJssel (Utrecht). The original spelling is Snelrewaard.

name: Snelleveldplein
en: A hamlet on the Waal near Waardenburg (Gelderland).

name: Snelleveldstraat
en: A hamlet on the Waal near Waardenburg (Gelderland).

name: Snelliusstraat
en: Willebrord Snellius (1580-1626), mathematician and physicist, professor at Leiden, known for the law of refraction named after him and for his triangulation of the Netherlands.

name: Snijdersbergweg
en: The name of a hill near Geulle (Limburg).

name: Snodenhoekpark
en: A hamlet near Elst in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

name: Snoekjesbrug
en: After a sixteenth-century resident, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike (snoek) depicted on the façade of his house. The name was originally Snoeksgracht/steeg.

name: Snoekjesgracht
en: After a sixteenth-century resident, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike (snoek) depicted on the façade of his house. The name was originally Snoeksgracht/steeg.

name: Snoekjessteeg
en: After a sixteenth-century resident, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike (snoek) depicted on the façade of his house. The name was originally Snoeksgracht/steeg.

name: Snorrenhoefstraat
en: A hamlet near Leusden (Utrecht).

name: Socratesstraat
en: Greek philosopher (469-399 BC), teacher of Plato, who was condemned as a freethinker to drink the cup of poison.

name: Soembawastraat
en: One of the Lesser Sunda Islands (Sumbawa, Indonesia).

name: Soendastraat
en: The island group (the Sunda Islands) that includes the main islands of Indonesia, divided into the Greater and the Lesser Sunda Islands. The Greater include Java, Sumatra, Kalimantan (Borneo) and Sulawesi (Celebes); the Lesser include Bali and the chain of islands east of Java. The Sundanese lands are in West Java.

name: Soerabajastraat
en: A port in East Java (Surabaya, Indonesia).

name: Soestdijkstraat
en: A village in the municipality of Soest. The royal palace of Soestdijk lies in the municipality of Baarn.

name: Soesterberghof
en: A village in the municipality of Soest, best known for the nearby military airfield.

name: Soetendaal
en: A former country estate near Maarssen on the Vecht.

name: Soewardistraat
en: Soewardi Soerjaningrat (Yogyakarta 1889 - Yogyakarta 1959), who later called himself Ki Hadjar Dewantoro. He was closely involved in the campaign of the multiracial Indische Partij, which sought an independent Indies, and for that was exiled to the Netherlands (1913-1919). After his return he worked mainly in education. In the first Indonesian cabinet he was Minister of Education and Culture (1945).

name: Softwareweg
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Solebaystraat
en: A place on the east coast of England. In the Battle of Solebay (1672) the Holland and Zeeland fleet under Admiral De Ruyter fought the English with success.

name: Solitudobrug
en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and in the Watergraafsmeer.

name: Solitudolaan
en: A former country estate by the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, roughly on this spot, mentioned as early as 1730 and still in existence in 1798.

name: Solitudolaanspoorbrug
en: A former country estate by the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, roughly on this spot, mentioned as early as 1730 and still in existence in 1798.

name: Solitudopad
en: A former country estate by the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, roughly on this spot, mentioned as early as 1730 and still in existence in 1798.

name: Solostraat
en: The largest river on the island of Java (Indonesia).

name: Somerlustpad
en: A former country estate on the Kruislaan, where the Nieuwe Ooster cemetery now is.

name: Sommelsdijkstraat
en: A village on the island of Overflakkee (Zuid-Holland).

name: Sonderbuur
en: The name of a demolished farm on the Haarlemmerweg near Halfweg.

name: Sonneveld
en: A medieval house of the Van Zonneveld family in Valkenburg (Limburg), demolished in 1789.

name: Sonthaven
en: The strait (the Sound, Øresund) between Denmark and Sweden, through which Amsterdam merchant ships sailed to the Baltic from the fourteenth century. In 1658 the Dutch fleet under Jacob van Wassenaer Obdam defeated the Swedish fleet here.

name: Sontvaarderstraat
en: A sontvaarder was a merchant ship that sailed through the Sound between the Netherlands and the Baltic.

name: Sophialaan
en: Queen Sophia Frederika Mathilda of Württemberg (1818-1877), the first wife of King William III.

name: Sophie Redmondplein
en: Jeanne Sophie Everdine Redmond (1907-1955), the first woman doctor in Suriname. She fought for the position of women and for preserving the heritage of Surinamese culture. Her nickname was Datra foe potisma, doctor for the poor. She wrote plays, collected in 1972.

name: Spaanse Brabanderstraat
en: After the comedy 'Spaanschen Brabander' (the Spanish Brabanter) by Gerbrand Adriaensz. Bredero, of 1617.

name: Spaarndammerdijk
en: The village of Spaarndam, north-east of Haarlem. The name comes from the dam in the Spaarne.

name: Spaarndammerplantsoen
en: The village of Spaarndam, north-east of Haarlem. The name comes from the dam in the Spaarne.

name: Spaarndammerstraat
en: The village of Spaarndam, north-east of Haarlem. The name comes from the dam in the Spaarne.

name: Spaarndammertunnel
en: The village of Spaarndam, north-east of Haarlem. The name comes from the dam in the Spaarne.

name: Spaarnwouderdijk
en: Named after the village of Spaarnwoude. The old Spaarnwouderdijk, which came to Amsterdam in 1921 with the annexation of the municipality of Sloten, has almost entirely disappeared, so the name was dropped. At the same time a newly built cycle path was given the old name Spaarnwouderdijk.

name: Spadinalaan
en: An area in south Toronto on Lake Ontario, being redeveloped since the start of the twenty-first century.

name: Spahof
en: A Belgian town (Spa) in the province of Liège.

name: Spakenburgstraat
en: A village on the Eemmeer (Utrecht).

name: Spaklerweg
en: The Spakler family, founders and owners of the sugar factory (a family business). Coenraad Hendrik Spakler (born around 1732 in Westphalia) owned a sugar refinery on the Rozengracht.

name: Spanderswoudstraat
en: A nature reserve: an old 's-Graveland country estate with woods, wooded banks and meadow.

name: Spangenhof
en: The former castle of Spangen, between Schiedam and Overschie. Spangen is now a district of Rotterdam.

name: Spankerenkade
en: A village near Dieren (Gelderland).

name: Sparrenweg
en: A conifer (the spruce).

name: Spechtstraat
en: The name of a bird family (the woodpeckers).

name: Speelmanstraat
en: Willem Pieter Speelman (1919-1945), resistance fighter, born in Vlagtwedde, executed by firing squad in Halfweg.

name: Speerdistelstraat
en: An akkerdistel (creeping thistle) is a species of thistle.

name: Speerstraat
en: The implement (spear, javelin) for javelin throwing, already practised by the ancient Greeks.

name: Spelderholt
en: A nature reserve north-east of Hoenderloo (Gelderland).

name: Spengenpad
en: A hamlet near Kockengen (Utrecht).

name: Sperwerlaan
en: A bird of prey (the sparrowhawk).

name: Speuldestraat
en: A hamlet near Ermelo (Gelderland).

name: Spicastraat
en: A star in the constellation Virgo.

name: Spiegelgracht
en: After a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers who ran soap works. In the corner house of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel lived Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' in 1564 and Pieter Lourens Spiegel in 1608; the house was still called Hertspiegel in 1738. Building on the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat began in 1665, and here too a resident of the Spiegel family probably gave the name.

name: Spijkerkade
en: The fastener, usually of metal, for joining wood (the nail).

name: Spijtellaantje
en: L.J. Spijdel (born 1844), who set up a small shipyard here in 1885. The lane came into Amsterdam with the annexation of Sloten and was popularly called by this name, which was made official in 1949.

name: Spinaker
en: A spinnaker is meant: a sail set when a ship sails dead before the wind.

name: Spinakerhof
en: A spinnaker is meant: a sail set when a ship sails dead before the wind.

name: Spinhuissteeg
en: After the nearby Spinhuis (spinning house), a house of correction for women founded in 1596. From 1833 to 1941 the building housed the police headquarters.

name: Spinozahof
en: Benedictus Spinoza (Baruch d'Espinoza) (1632-1677), Jewish philosopher who, after being banished from the Jewish community, lived by grinding spectacle lenses. One of the leading thinkers of the seventeenth century, he is known above all for his 'Ethics'. The Spinoza eye clinic stood on this street from 1874 to 1966. Part of the street was earlier called Andrieszkade, after the oldest known burgomaster of Amsterdam.

name: Spinozastraat
en: Benedictus Spinoza (Baruch d'Espinoza) (1632-1677), Jewish philosopher who, after being banished from the Jewish community, lived by grinding spectacle lenses. One of the leading thinkers of the seventeenth century, he is known above all for his 'Ethics'. The Spinoza eye clinic stood on this street from 1874 to 1966. Part of the street was earlier called Andrieszkade, after the oldest known burgomaster of Amsterdam.

name: Spitsbergenstraat
en: An island group in the Arctic Ocean, largely covered by a permanent ice cap, now part of Norway. Spitsbergen was discovered in 1596 by Willem Barentsz. The Dutch whaling station of Smeerenburg was built there in 1619.

name: Spitskopstraat
en: A mountain in South Africa where the Boers defeated the British in the First War of Independence (1880-1881).

name: Spooksteeg
en: The origin of the name (spook = ghost) is unknown. It does not appear on maps or in registers before 1800.

name: Spoorwegbassin
en: The Spoorwegbassin (railway basin) is a harbour; a bassin is a harbour basin.

name: Sporadenlaan
en: A Greek island group (the Sporades).

name: Sportpark De Weeren
en: A weer is a long strip of land between two boundary ditches; the ditch between two weren is sometimes called a werengouw. By council decision of 27 October 1971 part of the road was added to the Buikslotermeerplein.

name: Sportpark Kadoelen
en: The name of the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was added to Amsterdam on 1 August 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) appears as early as 1375. In 1429 the manors of Landsmeer and Quadolen are mentioned, which then shared one lord. Old maps show Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterland sea dike (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1 August 1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed because of confusion with the Zuideinde (formerly Oostzaan).

name: Sportpark Oostzanerwerf
en: After the Oostzanerwerf neighbourhood, in which the sports park lies. The neighbourhood takes its name from the municipality of Oostzaan, to which this area belonged until 1 August 1966.

name: Sportpark Sloten
en: After the village of Sloten, which until 1 January 1921 was the main village of the municipality of Sloten, which also included the village of Sloterdijk and the hamlet of Osdorp. The municipality stretched from the Haarlemmermeer to the North Sea Canal and from the Schinkel to Halfweg. The Sloterweg originally ran to (or began at) the Schinkel. Building the ring road removed part of it.

name: Sportpark Spieringhorn
en: The former polder inside the dike, which already existed before the IJ was reclaimed.

name: Sportparklaan
en: Refers to the former sports park.

name: Sportstraat
en: The street lies among streets named after the Greek games and after figures from antiquity famous for their strength.

name: Spreeuwenpark
en: The bird (the crow).

name: Spui
en: Until the end of the fourteenth century the water that formed the city's southern boundary. It was given a sluice when the Singel was dug, hence the name Spui (sluice). The Spui was filled in in 1882.

name: Spuistraat
en: Named after the Spui, into which the street runs. Before it was filled in in 1867 this was the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal, a canal dug around 1385, which can still be recognised in the street's straight course.

name: Spyridon Louisweg
en: Greek athlete (Spyridon Louis), who won the marathon at the 1896 Olympic Games in Athens.

name: Srefidensiplein
en: Srefidensi is an important concept in Surinamese history, meaning 'independence'. The word was coined by the Surinamese poet Henri Frans de Ziel, alias Trefossa (1916-1975): in Sranantongo 'srefi' means 'self' and 'densi' something like 'doing'. Trefossa also wrote the Surinamese national anthem.

name: Staalkade
en: After the Staalhof round the corner on the Groenburgwal, seat of the Staalmeesters (sampling officials), a board that supervised the products of the cloth industry in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. The Staalkade was only created around 1630 by land reclamation and was called Binnen-Amstel until 1913.

name: Staalmeestersbrug
en: The Staalhof stood in the Staalstraat, where the Staalmeesters (sampling officials) worked, made famous by Rembrandt.

name: Staalmeesterslaan
en: One of Rembrandt's best-known paintings (the Syndics of the Drapers' Guild).

name: Staalstraat
en: After the Staalhof round the corner on the Groenburgwal, seat of the Staalmeesters (sampling officials), a board that supervised the products of the cloth industry in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. The Staalkade was only created around 1630 by land reclamation and was called Binnen-Amstel until 1913.

name: Staatsliedenbrug
en: This bridge is named after the neighbourhood it lies in, the Staatsliedenbuurt.

name: Stade de Colombes
en: A stadium in Paris, where Ajax won the European Cup quarter-final on 5 March 1969.

name: Stadhouderskade
en: When this quay had to be named, it was two hundred years since Stadtholder William III had freed the country from the English, the French and the forces of Münster. Although Amsterdam was never very pro-stadtholder, this was reason enough to honour the stadtholders, alongside a Nassaukade and a Mauritskade: namely William II (1626-1650) and William III (1650-1702).

name: Stadiongracht
en: Refers to the neighbouring Olympic Stadium.

name: Stadionkade
en: Since the Greeks a stadium has been a sports ground with tiers of seats rising around it. The road runs past where the stadium stood when it was named in 1922 (level with today's Amazonestraat). The Olympic Stadium (on the square) was built for the 1928 Olympic Games.

name: Stadionplein
en: Since the Greeks a stadium has been a sports ground with tiers of seats rising around it. The road runs past where the stadium stood when it was named in 1922 (level with today's Amazonestraat). The Olympic Stadium (on the square) was built for the 1928 Olympic Games.

name: Stadionweg
en: Since the Greeks a stadium has been a sports ground with tiers of seats rising around it. The road runs past where the stadium stood when it was named in 1922 (level with today's Amazonestraat). The Olympic Stadium (on the square) was built for the 1928 Olympic Games.

name: Staghof
en: The part of a ship's rigging that supports the masts (the stays).

name: Stammerlandweg
en: The name recalls the Stammerlandpolder, an old polder name, now part of the Gemeenschapspolder.

name: Stapels
en: A corrupted spelling of the French port of Étaples, found on sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Staringplein
en: Antoni Christiaan Winand Staring (1767-1840), poet of nature poetry, who lived at the castle De Wildenborch near Vorden.

name: Staringstraat
en: Antoni Christiaan Winand Staring (1767-1840), poet of nature poetry, who lived at the castle De Wildenborch near Vorden.

name: Starrenboschstraat
en: The country estate Starre-Bosch, which stood on the Kruislaan from 1690 to about 1800, on the site of today's Oosterbegraafplaats.

name: Statenjachtstraat
en: The official name of the service vessel of the States assemblies of the Seven Provinces (the States yacht).

name: Stationsplein
en: After Centraal Station, completed in 1889 to a design by the architect Pierre Cuypers. The government of the day pushed through building the station here despite many objections from the city council and the Chamber of Commerce.

name: Staverdenplein
en: A hamlet in the municipality of Ermelo (Gelderland). Staverden castle, built around 1905 on medieval foundations, is also called Pauwenhof.

name: Steelvlietplein
en: A church village near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland, drowned by a storm flood in 1530.

name: Steenbokstraat
en: The constellation (Capricorn), also a sign of the zodiac.

name: Steenderenstraat
en: A village north of Doesburg (Gelderland). The municipality now also includes the historic little town of Bronkhorst.

name: Steengroevenpad
en: A country estate east of Winterswijk.

name: Steenhouwerijbrug
en: Named after the stonemasons who worked in the City Masonry Yard (Stads Metseltuin) on the Leidsegracht.

name: Steenhouwerssteeg
en: In 1557 the stonemason Jan Woutersz lived on the corner of the canal. Before that this was the Schoolsteegje, because the exit of the Oudezijds school was here.

name: Stekkenbergweg
en: The name of a hill north-west of Groesbeek (Gelderland).

name: Stellendamstraat
en: A fishing village on the island of Goeree-Overflakkee (Zuid-Holland).

name: Stellingweg
en: A stelling is the gallery on struts around a tall windmill, from which the miller turns the cap into the wind and takes in the sails. In 1976, for traffic reasons, part of the Stellingweg was renamed Molenaarsweg and another part was added to the Appelweg.

name: Stenen Beer
en: Named after a fortification in the defences of Amsterdam, between the Buitendijk and the Couhornerhoek, at the time of the Batavian Republic. It was demolished in 1825.

name: Stenendokweg
en: The excavated docks of the shipyard, closed by lock gates, used mainly by the repair yard (stone docks, as opposed to floating docks).

name: Stenghof
en: A steng is an extension of a ship's mast (a topmast).

name: Stentorstraat
en: A microscopic water creature (Stentor, the trumpet animalcule) that can attach itself to a surface, its body stretching greatly in length, with a funnel-shaped mouth at the end.

name: Stephensonstraat
en: George Stephenson (1781-1848), English engineer and railway pioneer, whose first locomotive ran in 1814.

name: Sterappelstraat
en: A variety of apple (star apple) that arose around 1830 in the southern Netherlands or Belgium, with fairly small, round, dark red fruit.

name: Sterkenburg
en: An old knightly manor at Driebergen (Utrecht), of which only the heavy round tower survived demolition in 1848, with a new house built against it.

name: Sterrenplein
en: The heavenly bodies: fixed stars, planets and comets. The square is the centre of the oldest part of the garden village of Oostzaan, where the streets are named after heavenly bodies.

name: Sterrenstraat
en: The heavenly bodies: fixed stars, planets and comets. The square is the centre of the oldest part of the garden village of Oostzaan, where the streets are named after heavenly bodies.

name: Stettineiland
en: An important historical Swedish and Prussian port for exporting timber. The city is now Polish and called Szczecin. The original council decision spelled it 'Stennin'; this was later corrected.

name: Steve Bikoplein
en: Steve Biko (1946-1977), who fell in the non-violent resistance against racial discrimination in South Africa. From 21 September 1904 to 1 February 1978 this was the Pretoriusplein.

name: Steven Vennecoolstraat
en: Architect (1659-1719), whose buildings include the Deutzenhofje on the Prinsengracht.

name: Stichtstraat
en: The name for the whole secular territory of the Bishop of Utrecht, which ran from Bodegraven up to and including the city of Groningen; Amstelland also belonged to it. Later the term narrowed to today's province of Utrecht.

name: Stieltjesstraat
en: Thomas Jan Stieltjes (1856-1894), mathematician, who contributed to analysis and number theory.

name: Stierstraat
en: The constellation (Taurus, the Bull), also a sign of the zodiac.

name: Stoel en Spreehof
en: Teunis Stoel (1852-1912) and Marius Spree (1875-1925), who together ran the Plantage Schouwburg theatre in the Plantage, staging real popular plays such as works by Justus van Maurik.

name: Stoelenmatterspad
en: Basket-making was originally a typical travelling trade. The name is linked to the world of travelling people and refers to the caravan site here.

name: Stokerkade
en: The trade name for those who stoke fires or furnaces, especially on locomotives and ships.

name: Stolwijkstraat
en: A village east of Gouda (Zuid-Holland).

name: Stompetorenstraat
en: A village in the Schermer, near Alkmaar (Noord-Holland).

name: Stoofsteeg
en: Probably so called because a few one-room dwellings stood here, where poor people lived: the alley appears in 1464 as Stovestege, and stove means room (compare German 'Stube'). The alley was also once known as Sint Jans Molenpad.

name: Stoombootweg
en: The road leads to the place on the Landsmeerdijk where the former station of the steamboat service to Amsterdam stood.

name: Stoomgemaalstraat
en: The pumping station that drains the polder, which replaced the windmill in the course of the nineteenth century.

name: Stormsteeg
en: Because this part of the city lay on its outermost edge until the sixteenth century, it took the full brunt of storms. The alley's name probably arose from this.

name: Stormvloedkeringstraat
en: A hydraulic structure (storm surge barrier) meant to prevent flooding at extremely high water.

name: Stoutenburggracht
en: A village south of Hoevelaken (Utrecht), named after the former castle that belonged to Van Oldenbarnevelt.

name: Strackéstraat
en: Johan Ph. Stracké (1817-1892), sculptor, who made statues of Tollens (Rotterdam), Boerhaave (Leiden) and Jan van Nassau (Utrecht), and in Amsterdam among other things the sculpture on the façade of the Sint Jacobsgesticht on the Plantage Middenlaan. (Not to be confused with F. Stracké, who made the bust of Prince Hendrik.)

name: Stralsundbrug
en: Stralsund is a German port by the island of Rügen on the Baltic. The names in the Houthavens are taken from places the Netherlands traded with a great deal in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Stralsundgracht
en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

name: Strandboulevard
en: Refers to the important beach this street runs along, which also gives Strandeiland its name.

name: Strandeilandlaan
en: The name refers to the future Strandeiland (beach island).

name: Strandvlietpad
en: Named after the metro stop this path leads to. Strandvliet was the name of an old farm near Duivendrecht.

name: Strawinskylaan
en: Igor Stravinsky (1882-1971), Russian-born American conductor and composer of operas and ballet music, among them 'The Rite of Spring'.

name: Strawinskypad
en: Igor Stravinsky (1882-1971), Russian-born American conductor and composer of operas and ballet music, among them 'The Rite of Spring'.

name: Streefkerkstraat
en: A village in the Alblasserwaard on the Lek (Zuid-Holland).

name: Strekkerweg
en: The trade name for someone who shapes metal, for example by a series of successive upsetting blows at right angles to the direction of stretch, as in forging. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding industry of Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Stromarkt
en: Named after the function this square-like piece of street had in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries (a straw market).

name: Stromboliweg
en: A volcanic island north-east of Sicily, part of the Aeolian (Lipari) archipelago.

name: Struisgrasstraat
en: A grass (bent grass) found all over the world.

name: Stuurmankade
en: Someone who steers a vessel (a helmsman or mate).

name: Stuyvesantstraat
en: Peter Stuyvesant (1611/12-1672), colonial administrator and governor of Curaçao, the last director of the colony of New Netherland, which had to be ceded to the English at the Peace of Breda (1667). He promoted trade with America and the West Indies.

name: Subangstraat
en: The name of the airport of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

name: Suezhaven
en: An Egyptian port at the entrance to, and giving its name to, the Suez Canal, opened in 1869.

name: Suikerdiefjestraat
en: A small bird (the bananaquit), one of the best-known birds of the Netherlands Antilles.

name: Suikerpeerpad
en: An old Dutch variety of pear. The path lies on the former De Bongerd allotment gardens.

name: Suikerplein
en: This square and the surrounding streets were laid out on the site of the former Wester sugar refinery, which once provided a living for many families in the Spaarndammerbuurt.

name: Sumatrakade
en: An island in Indonesia.

name: Sumatraplantsoen
en: An island in Indonesia.

name: Sumatrastraat
en: An island in Indonesia.

name: Surinamekade
en: Refers to the country of Suriname.

name: Surinameplein
en: Named after Suriname.

name: Surinamestraat
en: Named after Suriname.

name: Suze Groenewegplantsoen
en: Politician (1875-1940), a teacher in Rotterdam, from 1914 a member of the SDAP party executive, a member of the Provincial States of Zuid-Holland and the Rotterdam city council, and the first woman member of the House of Representatives (1918-1937). As an MP she worked among other things for allowing women to be appointed mayor.

name: Suze Robertsonstraat
en: Painter (1855-1922) of Breitner's school, who painted mainly still lifes.

name: Swammerdamstraat
en: Jan Swammerdam (1637-1680), anatomist and naturalist, who made important microscopic studies, preserved in his 'Bybel der natuure' (Bible of nature).

name: Syphonsluis
en: A lock that works by means of a siphon, a mechanism for drawing off water.

name: Taandwarsstraat
en: Taan is a yellow-brown dye made from oak bark and used to preserve fishing nets and sails. The tanneries (taanderijen), once spread throughout the city, were from around 1623 permitted only on the Realeneiland because of the fire risk.

name: Taanstraat
en: Taan is a yellow-brown dye made from oak bark and used to preserve fishing nets and sails. The tanneries (taanderijen), once spread throughout the city, were from around 1623 permitted only on the Realeneiland because of the fire risk.

name: Tafelbergweg
en: The name of a hill near Blaricum (Noord-Holland).

name: Tagorestraat
en: Rabindranath Tagore (1861-1941) was the first Indian writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Talbotstraat
en: William Henry Fox Talbot (1800-1877), English philosopher, Egyptologist, mathematician, linguist, physicist and photographer, a founder of modern photography. In the 1830s he experimented with photographic processes and developed a negative process that made it possible to print more than one copy from a negative.

name: Talmastraat
en: Aritius Sybrandus Talma (1864-1916), Reformed minister and later Anti-Revolutionary statesman, leader of the Christian Workers' Union and a director of the Patrimonium housing foundation, Minister of Agriculture from 1908 to 1913. He played an important part in improving bad conditions in public housing.

name: Taman Sapituin
en: Taman Sari means flower garden in Indonesian.

name: Tamariskhof
en: An evergreen shrub (tamarisk) with (pale) pink flowers that thrives on the coast.

name: Tan Malakastraat
en: Tan Malaka (Suliki 1894 - Kediri 1949) qualified as a teacher in Haarlem. During his stay in the Netherlands (1913-1919) he became more active in the Communist Party. After returning he joined the Communist Party founded by Henk Sneevliet. The colonial authorities arrested him and banished him from the Indies. Back in the Netherlands he was the first Indonesian to stand for a seat in the House of Representatives (1922). He was not elected and left for the Soviet Union. Until 1927 he was an agent of the Communist International (Comintern) in South-East Asia, leading a hidden and hunted life. Only in 1945 did he return to Indonesia, where, as a left-wing threat to the government, he was locked up again. In 1949 he was executed without trial by an army unit of the Republic.

name: Tante Saarbrug
en: Sara Bacharach, better known as Tante Saar (Aunt Saar), honorary citizen of Amsterdam, sold flowers on the Rembrandtplein for more than sixty years and kept her stock on the Thorbeckeplein. She was a well-known Amsterdam figure. In bitter poverty she earned a living for her family of nine children by selling flowers: early in the morning she took a little train to the auction in Aalsmeer to buy them, first walking the city with a basket and later keeping a stall on the Rembrandtplein. She survived several concentration camps and lost three children and six grandchildren, but she was a very strong woman, and much about her is recorded in the Amsterdam archives. She was born in 1887 and died in 1982. She came from the old Jewish proletariat, a hard-working woman and a true Amsterdammer.

name: Tartaud-Kleinhof
en: The acting couple Frits Tartaud (1857-1946), actor-director and head of the Rotterdam theatre company, and his wife Alida Klein (1873-1938), a gifted tragedienne.

name: Tasmanstraat
en: Abel Jansz. Tasman (1603-1659), navigator and explorer. On his voyages of 1642 and 1644 he discovered the island named after him, Tasmania, and New Zealand (both in 1642).

name: Teerketelsteeg
en: This alley, which originally ended at the water where the Koggestraat now is, ran behind the house 'de Teerketel' (the tar kettle) on today's Spuistraat, where tar was boiled and sold in the sixteenth century.

name: Tefelenstraat
en: A small village on the Maas, north-west of Oss.

name: Tegenhouderstraat
en: The metalworker who works with the riveter, holding the rivet head in place with a sledgehammer while the riveter closes it (the holder-up). The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding industry of Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Teilingen
en: A thirteenth-century castle, now a ruin, at Sassenheim (Zuid-Holland), known as the place where Jacoba of Bavaria lived and died.

name: Teixeira de Mattosstraat
en: Named after the family of Portuguese-Jewish origin who later founded a bank at Prinsengracht 746. The bank went bankrupt in 1966.

name: Tekkopstraat
en: A small village in the municipality of Woerden (Utrecht).

name: Teleportboulevard
en: The office district around Sloterdijk station, of which this road is the central axis, had the unofficial name Teleport when it was laid out: a name borrowed from America for a business area with advanced internal and external communication systems. The original intention of developing the area that way was only partly realised.

name: Telescoophof
en: A telescope for astronomical observation.

name: Tempelhofstraat
en: The name of Berlin's former Tempelhof airport, closed in 2008.

name: Ten Katestraat
en: Jan Jacob Lodewijk ten Kate (1819-1889), minister and poet, who also translated Goethe, Dante and Andersen. Widely read at first, he was pushed aside after the movement of the Tachtigers (the Eighties poets).

name: Tenderstraat
en: The wagon behind a steam locomotive that carries coal and water.

name: Tenerifestraat
en: A Spanish island off the African coast, one of the Canary Islands.

name: Teniersstraat
en: David Teniers the Younger (1610-1690), Southern Netherlandish painter, who founded the Antwerp Academy in 1663. He is known for his tavern scenes and peasant fairs.

name: Ter Boede
en: Originally a medieval castle near Koudekerke (Walcheren), now a stately country house from about 1740.

name: Ter Gouwstraat
en: Jan ter Gouw (1814-1894), teacher and a well-known historian of Amsterdam.

name: Ter Haarstraat
en: Bernard ter Haar (1806-1880), minister and poet of the school of Tollens, who wrote religious and domestic poems, and from 1854 was a professor at Utrecht.

name: Ter Hooge
en: A medieval castle near Koudekerke (Zeeland), substantially rebuilt and partly rebuilt anew in 1755.

name: Ter Kleef
en: A former castle, built at the end of the fourteenth century and blown up by the Spanish in 1572 after the siege of Haarlem. A farm-like building, a tower and a heap of stones still remain in Haarlem-Noord.

name: Terheideweg
en: A village south of The Hague, known in Dutch history for the naval battle of 1653 against the English in which Admiral Maarten Harpertszoon Tromp was killed.

name: Terletstraat
en: A hamlet on the Arnhem-Apeldoorn road.

name: Termietergouw
en: The farm 'de Termiet', to which the road leads. (Termiet comes from ter Miede, and mieden are hay meadows.)

name: Termieterweg
en: The farm 'de Termiet', to which the road leads. (Termiet comes from ter Miede, and mieden are hay meadows.)

name: Termini
en: The main railway station in Rome.

name: Ternatestraat
en: An island in the Moluccas (Indonesia).

name: Terpstraat
en: An artificial dwelling mound, called a terp in Friesland. Such mounds occur in various forms in other provinces too, under the names woerd, werd or wierde.

name: Terschellingstraat
en: A Wadden island (Friesland).

name: Tervurenpad
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Teslastraat
en: Nikola Tesla (1856-1943), Serbian-American engineer, born in Croatia, and physicist, who emigrated to America in 1884. An associate of Edison, he made countless inventions in alternating-current and high-frequency technology. The unit of magnetic induction is named after him.

name: Tesselschadestraat
en: Maria Tesselschade Visscher (1594-1649), poet, who with her sister graced the Muiderkring (the Muiden Circle). She was a daughter of Roemer Visscher, who gave her this name at birth because he had just lost many of his ships off Texel (Tessel-schade, Texel damage).

name: Tetje de Jongbrug
en: Theodora (Tetje) de Jong (Uithoorn, 2 May 1918 - Drachten, 21 January 1999) was the first salaried woman police commissioner in the Netherlands. In 1954, the year the first women joined the uniformed service of the Amsterdam police, De Jong was appointed chief inspector. On 1 January 1964 she was officially appointed commissioner of police in Amsterdam. In 1977, for her great importance to the Amsterdam police, she received a royal honour as an Officer of the Order of Orange-Nassau.

name: Teugestraat
en: A village in the municipality of Voorst (Gelderland).

name: Texashaven
en: Texas is one of the 50 states of the United States of America.

name: Texelplein
en: A Wadden island (Noord-Holland).

name: Texelweg
en: A Wadden island (Noord-Holland).

name: Teylerplein
en: The oldest museum in the Netherlands: Teylers Museum in Haarlem. The eighteenth-century merchant Pieter Teyler van der Hulst left his fortune to promote art and science. In 1784 the museum began with one room displaying physical instruments, extinct animals and drawings. Over time the collection has grown to include paintings, coins and fossils, among other things.

name: Th. J. Lammerslaan
en: Theodorus Johannes Lammers (1890-1972), Amsterdam architect of the later Amsterdam School, the man behind the Vrije Universiteit's Physiological Laboratory on the Valeriusplein.

name: Th. K. van Lohuizenlaan
en: Theodoor Karel van Lohuizen (1890-1956), architect and town planner, who laid the basis of the General Extension Plan for Amsterdam, published in 1934. He worked closely with Cornelis van Eesteren.

name: Th. Weeversweg
en: Theo Weevers (1875-1952), professor of botany in Amsterdam, founder of government care for nature conservation and chairman of the State Commission on nature reserves and nature conservation.

name: Theemsweg
en: A river in England (the Thames).

name: Theo Fransmanbrug
en: Theo Fransman, from 1981 to 1990 the first chairman of the Amsterdam-Noord district, who worked to find new uses for the NDSM site after the yard closed.

name: Theo Frenkelhof
en: Theodorus Maurits Frenkel (1871-1956), actor and theatre and film director, a scion of the famous Bouwmeester theatre family. He directed some two hundred films in England, France and Germany, and between 1915 and 1922 several feature films in the Netherlands. He had international success with his adaptation of Heijermans's play 'Brand in De Jonge Jan', in which he also acted.

name: Theo Mann-Bouwmeesterhof
en: The actress Theodora Mann, née Bouwmeester (1850-1939), sister of Louis Bouwmeester and one of the greatest tragediennes. Her star roles included Tosca, Lady Macbeth and Mary Stuart.

name: Theo Thijssenhof
en: Theodorus Thijssen (1879-1943), Amsterdam teacher and educationalist, who wrote novellas and novels about school and childhood, of which 'Kees de jongen' is the best known.

name: Theo van Doesburgstraat
en: The pseudonym of Christian E.M. Küpper (1883-1931), painter and designer of stained glass under Mondrian's influence, and the driving force of the 'De Stijl' group (1917). As an architect he worked with Rietveld.

name: Theodoor van Hoytemastraat
en: Painter (1863-1917), mainly of animals, draughtsman and lithographer.

name: Theodorus Dobbestraat
en: Resistance fighter (1901-1944), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Dieren.

name: Theodorus Majofskistraat
en: Theodorus Johannes Majofski (1770-1836), actor of Polish descent and founder of a famous acting family, in his day one of the most important figures of the Amsterdam stage.

name: Theophile de Bockstraat
en: Painter (1851-1904), best known for his nature scenes.

name: Theophilusstraat
en: A rhymed legend of the Virgin Mary from the fourteenth century.

name: Thérèse Schwartzeplein
en: Thérèse van Duyl-Schwartze (1851-1918), portrait painter. At the request of the painter Lizzy Ansingh her first name was included in full, to make clear that she was a woman.

name: Thérèse Schwartzestraat
en: Thérèse van Duyl-Schwartze (1852-1918), portrait painter. At the request of the painter Lizzy Ansingh her first name was included in full, to make clear that she was a woman.

name: Theseusstraat
en: In Greek mythology the hero of Attica who, with Ariadne's help, overcame the Minotaur.

name: Tholenstraat
en: One of the Zeeland islands, separated from Noord-Brabant by the water called the Eendracht.

name: Thomas à Kempisstraat
en: Thomas van Kempen (1380-1471), philosopher, from Kempen in the Rhineland, author of the famous work 'The Imitation of Christ'.

name: Thomas Hoodstraat
en: English scholar of the late sixteenth century, who taught astronomy and navigation in London among other subjects and wrote on the use of sea charts. In 1602 a translation of his work appeared in Amsterdam as 'Tgebruijck vande zeecaerte' (the use of the sea chart).

name: Thomas Prinslaan
en: Resistance fighter (1885-1942), who committed sabotage at the Kromhout engine works where he worked and helped prepare the February Strike of 1941. He was executed by firing squad at Soesterberg on 19 November 1942.

name: Thomas R. Malthusstraat
en: Thomas Robert Malthus (1766-1834), British historian and economist. In 1798 he published his pamphlet 'An Essay on the Principle of Population', arguing that population grows faster than the economy, which would lead to overpopulation and social misery.

name: Thomas van Aquinostraat
en: Italian theologian and philosopher (1225-1274), one of the great scholastics, who sought to make the Church's teaching comprehensible to reason.

name: Thomas van Erpehof
en: Professor of Oriental languages (1584-1624) at the University of Leiden, a bosom friend of Hugo de Groot.

name: Thorbeckeplein
en: Jan Rudolf Thorbecke (1798-1872), liberal statesman and professor at Leiden, prime minister and several times Minister of the Interior. His most important achievement was the revision of the constitution in 1848. This was originally part of the Reguliersgracht; after that stretch was filled in in 1874 the name Reguliersplein arose. In 1876 Thorbecke's statue by the sculptor F. Leenhoff was unveiled here, which prompted the square's present name. (The statue bears the inscription Optimo civi cives: the citizens to the best citizen.)

name: Thorn Prikkerstraat
en: Named after Johan Thorn Prikker (1868-1932), who worked in the Symbolist, Impressionist and Art Nouveau styles.

name: Tichelstraat
en: Named after the many tile and brick works (tichelbakkerijen) here in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Tidorestraat
en: An island in the Moluccas (Indonesia).

name: Tielstraat
en: The town in the Betuwe on the Waal, a centre of fruit and vegetable growing.

name: Tienenpad
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Tiengemetenstraat
en: The little Zuid-Holland island in the Haringvliet.

name: Tienraaikade
en: A village north-east of Venray (Limburg), in the former municipality of Meerlo, now Horst aan de Maas.

name: Tijl Uilenspiegelstraat
en: The hero of a chapbook of around 1500 (Till Eulenspiegel), whose roguish pranks are seen as personifying the Flemish national character. The story was retold in 1867 by Charles de Coster, and in a symphonic poem by Richard Strauss.

name: Tijnmuiden
en: The English port of Tynemouth, near Newcastle, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Tijnmuidenbrug
en: The English port of Tynemouth, near Newcastle, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Tilanusstraat
en: Christiaan Bernhard Tilanus (1856-1943), professor of surgery in Amsterdam, son of J.W. Tilanus, professor from 1867 to 1893, and grandson of the equally famous professor C.B. Tilanus (1828-1873). He specialised in bacteriology and later also orthopaedics. He soon saw the importance of first aid by laymen at accidents: on his initiative a brochure was distributed in 1893 that led to the founding of the first first-aid society in the Netherlands, the 'Vereeniging Eerste Hulp bij Ongelukken', which later received the title Royal. He also founded the Clinical School, the training college for midwives and the Orthopaedic Society.

name: Timo Smeehuijzenbrug
en: Timo Smeehuijzen was a 20-year-old soldier killed in Afghanistan on 15 June 2007. Before that he went to school at the nearby Fons Vitae lyceum, hence this location. The bridge also honours all the other soldiers who died in Afghanistan.

name: Timorplein
en: An island of the Lesser Sunda Islands in Indonesia, half of which was Portuguese territory.

name: Timorstraat
en: An island of the Lesser Sunda Islands in Indonesia, half of which was Portuguese territory.

name: Tintorettostraat
en: Jacopo Robusti (1518-1594), who called himself Tintoretto, Italian painter and one of the leading painters of the Venetian school.

name: Tip Maruggstraat
en: Silvio Alberto 'Tip' Marugg (Willemstad, 1923 - Willemstad, 2006) was a writer and poet. After gaining his MULO diploma in 1942 he spent five years in military service, then worked for Shell, where he discovered writing through the staff magazine Passaat. He made his debut in 1958 with the novel 'Weekendpelgrimage'. His third novel, 'De morgen loeit weer aan' (1988), was nominated for the AKO Literature Prize, and in 1989 he received the Cola Debrot Prize. Island life plays a large part in his books, which have been translated into several languages.

name: Titiaanstraat
en: The painter's name of Tiziano Vecellio (c. 1488-1576), famous master of the Venetian school.

name: Titus Brandsmabrug
en: This bridge is named after Titus Brandsma (1881-1942), Roman Catholic priest and professor of theology at Nijmegen. As spiritual adviser in 1942 he urged the Catholic dailies not to carry NSB propaganda. That same year he was taken to Dachau, where he died.

name: Titus van Rijnstraat
en: Son of Rembrandt van Rijn and Saskia van Uylenburgh (1641-1668), who sat as a model several times. From 1660 he ran an art dealership in the painter's work with Rembrandt's companion Hendrickje Stoffels, which shielded Rembrandt from his creditors. He was buried in the Westerkerk.

name: Tjalkstraat
en: A flat-bottomed inland sailing ship with a rounded stem and gaff rig (a tjalk).

name: Tjepmapad
en: A former country estate near Vleuten (Utrecht), of which only the seventeenth-century gatehouse remains.

name: Tjerk Hiddes de Vriesstraat
en: Frisian admiral (1622-1666), killed in the Second Anglo-Dutch War off Dunkirk.

name: Tjeukemeerhof
en: A lake in southern Friesland.

name: Tjotterspad
en: An inland sailing yacht of shallow draught (a tjotter).

name: Tobias M.C. Asserstraat
en: Jurist (1838-1913), known at home and abroad in the field of private international law. He became a professor in Amsterdam in 1862 and a member of the Council of State in 1893. In 1911 he received the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Toetsenbordweg
en: Street name in the Information Technology category.

name: Tofana
en: A mountain peak in Italy, 3243 metres high.

name: Tolbrugstraat
en: After the toll gate (tol) on the corner of today's Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was levied from about 1780 until the area was annexed in 1896, for the upkeep of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 11 February 1886).

name: Toldwarsstraat
en: After the toll gate (tol) on the corner of today's Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was levied from about 1780 until the area was annexed in 1896, for the upkeep of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 11 February 1886).

name: Tolhuiskanaal
en: After the inn Het Tolhuis, once a much-frequented place, built in 1662 when a carriage road was laid out here and a toll introduced. From 1887 to 1912 the celebrated concerts of the then popular Seventh Regiment under bandmaster Joh. Zaagmans were given in its garden.

name: Tolhuisweg
en: After the inn Het Tolhuis, once a much-frequented place, built in 1662 when a carriage road was laid out here and a toll introduced. From 1887 to 1912 the celebrated concerts of the then popular Seventh Regiment under bandmaster Joh. Zaagmans were given in its garden.

name: Tolkamerstraat
en: The village with a border post near Lobith (Gelderland) on the Rhine, here the busiest border crossing by water in the world.

name: Tollensstraat
en: Hendrik Frederik Tollens (1780-1856), Rotterdam merchant who became known as a popular poet.

name: Tolsendestraat
en: A former church village south of Yerseke (Zeeland), flooded in 1530.

name: Tolstraat
en: After the toll gate (tol) on the corner of today's Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was levied from about 1780 until the area was annexed in 1896, for the upkeep of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 11 February 1886).

name: Tom Schreursweg
en: Cornelis Petrus Antonius Schreurs (1896-1956), who as early as 1923 took the initiative for radio sports broadcasts, especially of international football matches.

name: Tomatenstraat
en: The fruit.

name: Toministraat
en: A port on the island of Sulawesi (Celebes) in Indonesia.

name: Tommaso Albinonistraat
en: Italian composer (1671-1750), probably self-taught, who worked as chamber musician to Ferdinando Carlo, Duke of Mantua. Johann Sebastian Bach three times took themes by Albinoni as the starting point for his own compositions. Albinoni wrote instrumental works and some fifty operas.

name: Ton de Leeuwstraat
en: Composer (1926-1996), at the Sweelinck Conservatory in Amsterdam from 1959 to 1987, first as senior teacher of composition and from 1984 as artistic director. He explored the relation between East and West in music and received many prizes, among them the Prix Italia and the Matthijs Vermeulen Prize.

name: Tondenpad
en: A hamlet in the municipality of Brummen, west of Zutphen (Gelderland).

name: Tongelaer
en: A former fifteenth-century castle at Mill, municipality of Beers (Noord-Brabant), of which only a square gate tower remains.

name: Tongerenstraat
en: A hamlet and estate west of Epe (Gelderland).

name: Tonia Stieltjesplein
en: Tonia Stieltjes (1881-1932) was born in the Czaar Peterstraat, the daughter of an Afro-Surinamese man born in slavery. She worked to improve the working and living conditions of domestic staff and is regarded as the first Black woman trade unionist. She also lives on in the many portraits for which she posed as a model.

name: Top Naeffstraat
en: Anthonetta van Rhijn, née Naeff (1878-1953), novelist and theatre critic, whose works include biographies of Willem Royaards and Sarah Bernhardt.

name: Top Rinckerstraat
en: Friedrich Johannes Wilhelm Rincker (1877-1939), one of the leading figures of Dutch cricket, who played in 43 international matches.

name: Topaasstraat
en: A yellow gemstone (topaz).

name: Topkapipad
en: The Topkapı Museum in Istanbul, one of the finest surviving examples of secular architecture in Istanbul, originally the palace of the sultans and open as a museum since 1924. Its collection holds the most varied objects that belonged to the Ottoman court, including weapons, porcelain, jewellery, clothing and miniatures.

name: Torensluis
en: The name of this fixed bridge refers to the Jan Roodenpoortstoren, the tower that once stood here beside the gate in the city wall and was pulled down in 1829. The base of the tower is still at the side of the bridge.

name: Torensteeg
en: The alley runs to the spot where the Jan Roodenpoortstoren once stood beside the gate in the city wall. After the wall was demolished the tower survived until 1829. Its base is still at the side of the bridge, the Torensluis.

name: Torenven
en: An old local name: a marsh (ven) near the tower.

name: Torontobrug
en: This double bascule bridge is named after the city of Toronto in Canada, a sister city of Amsterdam. On 2 October 1974 Mayor David Crombie of Toronto unveiled a plaque here to confirm the sister-city relationship, and Toronto therefore also has an Amsterdam Bridge.

name: Torresstraat
en: Luis Vaez de Torres (flourished 1606), Spanish navigator, who in 1606 sailed through the strait named after him, the Torres Strait between Australia and New Guinea.

name: Torricellistraat
en: Evangelista Torricelli (1608-1647), Italian physicist and professor at Florence, inventor of the Torricelli tube, a forerunner of the mercury barometer. The former municipality of Watergraafsmeer named this street Dr. Leydsstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 30 December 1921).

name: Tosaristraat
en: A mountain village and plain in East Java, the highest settlement on the island and one of the most popular holiday resorts under Dutch rule.

name: Tosarituin
en: A mountain village and plain in East Java, the highest settlement on the island and one of the most popular holiday resorts under Dutch rule.

name: Tourniairestraat
en: Bachigaloupi Tourniaire (1850-1921), in his day a much-loved actor who excelled in comic roles, and his son Oscar Tourniaire (1880-1939), who played many Shakespeare roles.

name: Touwbaan
en: The street was laid out on the site of the ropewalks of the Dutch East India Company in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Touwbaanpark
en: The street was laid out on the site of the ropewalks of the Dutch East India Company in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Touwslagerstraat
en: A trade name from shipbuilding (ropemaker). The name recalls the many shipyards here in earlier centuries.

name: Transformatorweg
en: A device for converting electric current from one voltage to another.

name: Transvaalkade
en: The land beyond the Vaal River, formerly an independent Boer republic and after the war of 1899 to 1902 a province of the Union of South Africa. The street arose from the remainder of the Lange Overamstelstraat (named by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel) and the Ringstraat (council decision of 21 September 1904); Nieuwer-Amstel originally named the quay Ringkade.

name: Transvaalplein
en: The land beyond the Vaal River, formerly an independent Boer republic and after the war of 1899 to 1902 a province of the Union of South Africa. The street arose from the remainder of the Lange Overamstelstraat (named by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel) and the Ringstraat (council decision of 21 September 1904); Nieuwer-Amstel originally named the quay Ringkade.

name: Transvaalstraat
en: The land beyond the Vaal River, formerly an independent Boer republic and after the war of 1899 to 1902 a province of the Union of South Africa. The street arose from the remainder of the Lange Overamstelstraat (named by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel) and the Ringstraat (council decision of 21 September 1904); Nieuwer-Amstel originally named the quay Ringkade.

name: Treilerhof
en: A treiler or trawler is a sea-fishing vessel that fishes with a trawl net.

name: Tretjakovlaan
en: Named after the Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow, whose building was completed in 1900. The collection is based on the art collection of Pavel Tretyakov, who gave it to Moscow in 1892, and is famous for its unique collection of icons.

name: Trianonpad
en: The name of two small palaces in the park of Versailles: the Grand Trianon, built for Louis XIV (1687-1688), and the Petit Trianon, built for Louis XV (1762-1768).

name: Trichtstraat
en: A village on the Linge, north-west of Geldermalsen (Gelderland).

name: Trijn Hullemanlaan
en: Resistance fighter (1912-1941), involved in many underground activities and a member of the 'Krijn Breur' resistance group.

name: Trimurtistraat
en: S.K. Trimurti (1912-2008), Indonesian journalist, writer and teacher in the independence movement against Dutch colonial rule, and the Republic's first Minister of Labour (1947-1948).

name: Troelstralaan
en: Pieter Jelles Troelstra (1860-1930), lawyer, politician and Frisian poet, co-founder of the SDAP in 1894 and a member of the House of Representatives from 1897 to 1924.

name: Troepiaalsingel
en: A brightly coloured bird (troupial), which usually flies in large flocks (troepen), hence the name.

name: Trompenburgstraat
en: A former country estate on the Amstel, named after its owner at the time, the admiral Cornelis Tromp. After his death in 1691 the burgomaster Nicolaas Witsen moved in. In the early twentieth century the Spyker car factory and then the Nestelroy-Trompenburg paper mill were based here. The street was originally called Trompstraat (council decision of 21 December 1899).

name: Trouringhstraat
en: The title of a didactic poem by Jacob Cats (the 'Trouringh', wedding ring).

name: Truus Wijsmullerbrug
en: Geertruida Wijsmuller-Meijer (1896-1978) was already bringing Jewish refugees from Central Europe to safety through the Netherlands before the Second World War. In 1938 and 1939, with Adolf Eichmann's permission, she organised weekly transports of 500 children from Frankfurt, Vienna or Prague to England. In August 1939 she organised the evacuation of the Jewish population of Danzig in Poland. After war broke out she escorted transports to Marseille or Spain on their way to Palestine. She also arranged food parcels for Jewish children in Westerbork, and managed to save 50 children in Westerbork from deportation to Poland. After the war she was a VVD member of the Amsterdam city council in 1945-1946 and 1949-1966, and then worked on the adoption of foreign children.

name: tt. Melaniaweg
en: The turbine tanker Melania, 330 metres long and of 250,000 tons, delivered to Shell in 1969. The ship was built at the yard of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM) in two halves, welded together after launching. Melania is the name of a shell (Shell's trademark).

name: tt. Melissaweg
en: The turbine tanker Melissa, built in 1965 by Van der Giessen-De Noord, owned first by N.V. Verenigde Tankkustvaart and then by P.A. van Es & Co. N.V.

name: tt. Neveritaweg
en: A turbine tanker of 110,000 tons, the last tanker built entirely by the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM), in 1968 for Royal Dutch Shell, and at the time the largest supertanker ever built in the Netherlands.

name: tt. Vasumweg
en: The turbine tanker Vasum, built in 1955 at the yard of the Nederlandsche Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij for Royal Dutch Shell. Vasum is the name of a shell (Shell's trademark). The road was laid out on the site of the former NDSM yard.

name: Tugelaweg
en: A river in South Africa, the Boers' southern line of defence in the war of 1899 to 1902, where there was heavy fighting against the British.

name: Tuigerstraat
en: The trade name for someone who rigs and unrigs ships (a rigger). (A ship's rigging comprises all the ropes and wires for working the masts, hoisting gear and davits.) The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding industry of Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Tuilstraat
en: A village on the Waal opposite Zaltbommel (Gelderland).

name: Tuimelaarstraat
en: A dolphin (the bottlenose dolphin), no longer than 2.5 metres, dark, living in groups and found worldwide. The tuimelaar is very agile and is often kept in dolphinariums.

name: Tuin van Hera
en: Greek goddess of marriage and childbirth, wife and also sister of Zeus. Hera was also worshipped as a guardian of herds; the cow was one of the animals sacred to her.

name: Tuinbouwstraat
en: The growing of vegetables, fruit and flowers (horticulture).

name: Tuinderijlaan
en: Refers to the De Bongerd allotment park.

name: Tuinstraat
en: Tuin (garden) here means a yard or enclosed space. The street name comes from the Stadstimmertuin (the city's carpentry yard, the Stadswerf), which lay here from 1612 to 1660 (by the Lijnbaansgracht) and to which the street led.

name: Tulastraat
en: Tula, nicknamed Rigaud, was one of the leaders of the uprising of enslaved people that broke out on Curaçao in August 1795. In September 1795 he was captured and executed.

name: Tulpbrug
en: This fixed bridge is named after Nicolaes Tulp (1593-1674), lecturer to the surgeons' guild at the Athenaeum Illustre. He was also several times burgomaster of Amsterdam, but is best known for his anatomy lesson, immortalised by Rembrandt.

name: Turbinestraat
en: A machine in which liquid or steam drives a bladed wheel, used among other things to generate electricity.

name: Turbón
en: A mountain peak in Spain, 2492 metres high.

name: Turfdraagsterpad
en: When this path still ran as far as the (Oude) Turfmarkt, the women who worked at the peat market (turf carriers) lived in the cottages along it.

name: Turfsteeg
en: Named after the peat warehouse of the Oudezijds Huiszittenarmen (poor relief, later the Arsenal), which the alley runs past.

name: Turnerstraat
en: A gymnast, practitioner of gymnastics, one of the old Greek sports.

name: Turnhoutplantsoen
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Tussen de Bogen
en: After its position between the railway viaducts. The spaces between these viaducts were locally called bogen (arches).

name: Tussen Kadijken
en: When a great deal of land had built up through silting outside the old sea dike (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike, or quay dike (kadijk), was built. It was originally called the new sea dike, but that name later fell out of use. When this new dike was raised further, people spoke of the Laagte (low part) and the Hoogte (high part) of the Kadijk. Until 1943 the Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat. This is because it lies in line with the Plantage Kerklaan, although it has never been connected to it.

name: Tussen Meer
en: Named after a former farm on the Uitweg near the Sloterpolder, demolished in the 1950s to build the Slotermeer district.

name: Tussendek
en: Achterdek (afterdeck): one of the decks of a ship.

name: Tutein Noltheniusstraat
en: Rudolf Peter Johannes Tutein Nolthenius (1851-1939), hydraulic engineer, who drew up plans for moving the mouth of the Maas.

name: Twee Koningskinderenstraat
en: Named after the fairy tale 'The Two King's Children' by the Brothers Grimm.

name: Tweede Anjeliersdwarsstraat
en: An anjelier (carnation) is a flower belonging to the pink family.

name: Tweede Atjehstraat
en: The northern part of the Indonesian island of Sumatra (Aceh), known above all for the Aceh War (1873-1904), with which the name of General Van Heutsz is linked.

name: Tweede Bloemdwarsstraat
en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion of 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which it is named. From 1614 to 1878 the windmill 'De Blom' stood on the bastion; it was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

name: Tweede Boerhaavestraat
en: Hermannus Boerhaave (1668-1738), professor of medicine at Leiden. He enjoyed international fame. The street name Boerhaavestraat (First to Fourth) has been changed several times. It was set as Boerhaavestraat on 15 November 1876 and changed to Eerste Boerhaavestraat on 15 November 1882. This change was reversed on 10 December 1884. On 13 October 1897 the street was extended under the same name, and finally, on 19 February 1908, it was split into the present Eerste and Tweede Boerhaavestraat. The Tweede, Derde and Vierde Boerhaavestraat, named in 1882, were replaced by the names Deymanstraat, Ruyschstraat and Blasiusstraat.

name: Tweede Boomdwarsstraat
en: In this part of the Jordaan, streets are named after flowers, shrubs and trees. In the seventeenth century, the street was also called Lindeboomstraat.

name: Tweede Breeuwersstraat
en: A trade name. A breeuwer (caulker) sealed the seams between the planks of a ship's hull. In the seventeenth century many caulkers lived in the Eerste Breeuwersstraat (formerly Breeuwersstraat), working at the shipyards on the Prinseneiland and Realeneiland. In 1895 the parallel street was given the same name, which made the additions Eerste and Tweede necessary.

name: Tweede Ceramstraat
en: An island in Indonesia.

name: Tweede Coehoornstraat
en: Menno Baron van Coehoorn (1641-1704), fortress builder and engineer-general of fortifications.

name: Tweede Constantijn Huygensstraat
en: Poet and prose writer (1596-1687), whose works include 'Hofwijck' and epigrams (sneldichten). He was secretary to several successive stadholders. Before 1894 parts of these streets were called Eerste and Tweede Bilderdijkstraat (council decisions of 15 May 1878 and 19 December 1883).

name: Tweede Disteldwarsstraat
en: The plant (the thistle). The Distel streets, except the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919 to meet quickly the great demand for homes for the workers of the industry that grew fast after the First World War.

name: Tweede Egelantiersdwarsstraat
en: Named after the shrub berberis (barberry).

name: Tweede Goudsbloemdwarsstraat
en: The flower (the marigold), of the daisy family.

name: Tweede Helmersstraat
en: Jan Frederik Helmers (1767-1813), Amsterdam broker who devoted himself to letters. His works include 'De Hollandsche Natie' (1813). The second part of the Eerste Helmersstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 and was then called Hofdijkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 9 May 1890). The start of this street was originally a short side street of the Nassaukade called Sophiapark.

name: Tweede Hugo de Grootstraat
en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of international law. As a leader of the Remonstrants he was drawn into church disputes and imprisoned at Loevestein on the orders of Prince Maurice. He escaped from there in a book chest in 1621.

name: Tweede Jacob van Campenstraat
en: Architect (1595-1659), designer of the city hall on the Dam, now the Royal Palace, though he was not allowed to complete the work. Van Campen also built the Heiligewegspoort in 1636 and worked on palaces for Prince Frederik Hendrik. The street was split into Eerste and Tweede after the stretch between them was sold to the Heineken brewery in 1930.

name: Tweede Jan Steenstraat
en: Painter (1626-1679), mostly of domestic scenes: merry, untidy interiors. That gave rise to the expression 'a Jan Steen household' (een huishouden van Jan Steen).

name: Tweede Jan van der Heijdenstraat
en: Painter and engineer (1637-1712), inventor of the fire engine with a hose and of a new model of street lamp. Painter of portraits and townscapes.

name: Tweede Keucheniusstraat
en: Levinus W.C. Keuchenius (1822-1893), Anti-Revolutionary statesman and fierce opponent of the state school. Minister of the Colonies from 1888 to 1890.

name: Tweede Kostverlorenkade
en: After the Kostverlorenwetering, dug in 1413 to give a shorter waterway to the Haarlem and Leiden lakes. According to some, the name Kostverloren (cost lost) comes from the heavy legal costs of this channel, which was a bone of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609. The name Kostverloren occurs in several places in the Netherlands.

name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat
en: The southern European ornamental tree (the laurel).

name: Tweede Leeghwaterstraat
en: Jan Adriaanszoon Leeghwater (1575-1650), hydraulic engineer. As overseer and millwright he worked on many land reclamations, including the Beemster. He drew up the first plan to drain the Haarlemmermeer.

name: Tweede Leliedwarsstraat
en: All these streets are named after the oldest of them, the Oude Leliestraat, already mentioned in 1560. It takes its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' (in the white lily) on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Torensluis). After 1612 the name passed to the canal dug in line with it, and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets in the Jordaan.

name: Tweede Lindendwarsstraat
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Tweede Looiersdwarsstraat
en: The tanneries and the hide trade, after which this street and nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal ring are named, were at first sited outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came inside the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after these long-flourishing trades, starting with the Runstraat (run is tanbark) and the Huidenstraat (hides street). After 1658 the tanneries spread to land east of the Vijzelgracht, where the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat are now. Before it was filled in, the Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision of 1 June 1898).

name: Tweede Marnixplantsoen
en: Philips of Marnix, Lord of Sint-Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and adviser of Prince William of Orange, drafter of the Compromise of Nobles (1568), and possibly the poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 where the city ramparts had stood, which were levelled between 1820 and 1840.

name: Tweede Nassaustraat
en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. Before it was named in 1879, the quay was called Buitensingel.

name: Tweede Oosterparkstraat
en: Named after the nearby Oosterpark, and originally (council decision of 15 November 1882) named Eerste, Tweede and Derde Parkstraat. The Eerste Oosterparkstraat was earlier called Oetgenspad, after Frans Hendriks Oetgens, a sixteenth-century burgomaster over whose land several paths were laid. Until 1895 the street name applied as far as the Linnaeusstraat. In that year the stretch along the park was given the park's name.

name: Tweede Passeerdersdwarsstraat
en: Passeren is the preparing and working of Spanish leather. When this kind of leatherwork was banned in central Amsterdam in 1631, the passeerderij settled here, next to the tanneries already there.

name: Tweede Rozendwarsstraat
en: The flower (the rose).

name: Tweede Schinkelstraat
en: The name recalls the old roadside inn Schinkelhaven. Before 1922 the street was part of the Schinkelkade.

name: Tweede Sweelinckstraat
en: Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck (1562-1621), a musician of great renown and organist of the Oude Kerk. He wrote many compositions on the psalms and love songs. Before 1896 part of the Tweede Sweelinckstraat lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel as the Tweede Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 22 August 1890).

name: Tweede Tuindwarsstraat
en: Tuin (garden) here means a yard or enclosed space. The street name comes from the Stadstimmertuin (the city's carpentry yard, the Stadswerf), which lay here from 1612 to 1660 (by the Lijnbaansgracht) and to which the street led.

name: Tweede Van der Helststraat
en: Bartholomeus van der Helst (1612-1670), painter of militia and regents' group portraits.

name: Tweede van Swindenstraat
en: Jean Henri van Swinden (1746-1823), philosopher, mathematician and physicist, professor at Franeker and from 1785 in Amsterdam. He sat on the commission that fixed the metre, after which he worked out the metric system introduced in the Netherlands in 1816.

name: Tweede Vogelstraat
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Tweede Weteringdwarsstraat
en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries this was the paving yard.

name: Tweede Weteringplantsoen
en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries this was the paving yard.

name: Tweede Wittenburgerdwarsstraat
en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

name: Tweelingenhof
en: The sign of the zodiac (Gemini, the Twins).

name: Twellostraat
en: A village in the municipality of Voorst (Gelderland) on the old Apeldoorn-Deventer road, surrounded by several estates.

name: Twentestraat
en: The eastern part of the province of Overijssel.

name: Twikkel
en: A castle at Delden (Overijssel), built in 1347 and rebuilt and enlarged several times since.

name: Twiske
en: Twiske is the (West) Frisian word for 'between': it refers to the boundary ditch between the Waterland and the Zaan reclamations. The present recreation area near Oostzaan still bears the name.

name: Twiskestraat
en: Twiske is the (West) Frisian word for 'between': it refers to the boundary ditch between the Waterland and the Zaan reclamations. The present recreation area near Oostzaan still bears the name.

name: U.J. Klarenstraat
en: Uilke Jan Klaren (1852-1947), founder of the playground movement in Amsterdam.

name: Ubbo Emmiushof
en: Historian (1547-1625), the first rector magnificus of the University of Groningen.

name: Uffizilaan
en: The Galleria degli Uffizi in Florence, a museum. Most of the building was put up between 1560 and 1580. The painting collection is based on the art collection of the Medici family and includes works of the Florentine, Venetian and Dutch schools.

name: Uilenburgergracht
en: The island of Uilenburg, which came within the city in 1593 together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known for certain, but it probably comes from the marshland here, called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was formed by joining the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

name: Uilenburgersteeg
en: The island of Uilenburg, which came within the city in 1593 together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known for certain, but it probably comes from the marshland here, called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was formed by joining the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

name: Uilenburgerwerf
en: The island of Uilenburg, which came within the city in 1593 together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known for certain, but it probably comes from the marshland here, called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was formed by joining the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

name: Uilengouw
en: Uil (owl) is the nickname of the people of Zunderdorp.

name: Uitdammer Die
en: The hamlet of Uitdam, on the IJsselmeer dike north of the municipal boundary. The road came to Amsterdam when the former municipality of Ransdorp was abolished in 1921, under the name Waterlandse zeedijk. (Uitdam = outer dam, outer dike.)

name: Uitdammerdijk
en: The hamlet of Uitdam, on the IJsselmeer dike north of the municipal boundary. The road came to Amsterdam when the former municipality of Ransdorp was abolished in 1921, under the name Waterlandse zeedijk. (Uitdam = outer dam, outer dike.)

name: Uiterwaardenstraat
en: The land along the rivers between the summer and winter dikes, which floods in winter (floodplains).

name: Uitgeeststraat
en: A village in Noord-Holland.

name: Uithoornstraat
en: The Noord-Holland town of Uithoorn is named here because the Uithoorn barge skipper moored on the Amsteldijk level with this street.

name: Uitwegpad
en: Before the western garden suburbs of Slotermeer and Osdorp were built, the Uitweg was a country road between the Osdorperweg and the Haarlemmerweg, parallel to and west of the former Slotermeer (now the Sloterplas). A number of farms stood along it, which are commemorated in another part of this district.

name: Uiverbrug
en: The Uiver was the legendary KLM aircraft that took part in the 1934 air race from London to Melbourne and won first prize in the race's handicap section. Like the Uiver, this bridge is made of aluminium.

name: Ukkelhof
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Uranusstraat
en: The planet (Mars).

name: Urkstraat
en: A former island in the Zuiderzee, now in the Noordoostpolder. Amsterdam bought the island in 1660 to control the shipping route across the Zuiderzee.

name: Usselincxhaven
en: Willem Usselincx (1567-1647), Flemish merchant and seafarer, founder of the West India Company in 1621.

name: Utopia
en: From 'ou topos', Ancient Greek for 'no place'. The concept was introduced in 1516 by the English humanist Thomas More, whose book Utopia describes a hypothetical society of that name with socialist and communist features.

name: Utrechtsebrug
en: After the city of Utrecht.

name: Utrechtsedwarsstraat
en: After the city of Utrecht.

name: Utrechtsestraat
