en: After the city of Utrecht. The street comes out on the Frederiksplein, where the Utrechtsepoort (Utrecht gate) once stood (demolished in 1860). The Nieuwe Utrechtseweg is the new arterial road to Utrecht; the old road ran by way of Duivendrecht and Abcoude.

name: Vaalmuiden
en: The English port of Falmouth, on the south coast of Cornwall, in a spelling found on Dutch sea charts of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

name: Vaalrivierstraat
en: A river (tributary of the Orange River) that formed the border between the Orange Free State and the Transvaal, known from the Boers' two wars of independence.

name: Vaartstraat
en: A canal (vaart).

name: Valburgdreef
en: A village in Gelderland, near Nijmegen.

name: Valckenierstraat
en: Gillis Valckenier (1623-1680), nine times burgomaster of Amsterdam between 1665 and 1680. The street was laid out on the filled-in stretch of the Nieuwe Lijnbaansgracht.

name: Valentijnkade
en: François Valentijn (1666-1727), minister and writer in the former Dutch East Indies, who wrote the standard work 'Oud en Nieuw Oost-Indiën' (old and new East Indies) and translated the Bible into Malay.

name: Valeriusplein
en: Adriaan Valerius (c. 1575-1625), notary in Veere, known for the collection of folk songs he compiled, still known today as the 'Nederlandtsche Gedenck-clanck'.

name: Valeriusstraat
en: Adriaan Valerius (1575-1626), notary in Veere, known for the collection of folk songs he compiled, still known today as the 'Nederlandtsche Gedenck-clanck'.

name: Valkenburgerstraat
en: The island of Valkenburg or Marken, which came within the city around 1600. The origin of the name Valkenburg is unknown; perhaps there was once a house with a gable stone or a shipyard of that name. A gable stone with Valkenburg is also found elsewhere (Nieuwendijk 62/68).

name: Valkenisseweg
en: A village that disappeared into the Westerschelde in a storm flood in January 1862.

name: Valkenstein
en: A lost castle that stood near Poortugaal on IJsselmonde (Zuid-Holland).

name: Valkenweg
en: The bird of prey (the falcon). The start of the Valkenweg disappeared when the IJ tunnel was built, so the Valkenweg ferry became the Adelaarsweg ferry (now Meeuwenlaan).

name: Valkhof
en: The Valkhof, by the Waal bridge in Nijmegen, was originally founded around 800 by Charlemagne. The castle was rebuilt in 1155 by Emperor Frederick Barbarossa and demolished in 1797, apart from the surviving Carolingian chapel and some remains of walls.

name: Valreep
en: The opening in a ship's bulwark where the gangway ladder is fixed. Originally the name of a rope ladder (reep = rope).

name: Valschermkade
en: The Dutch word for parachute.

name: Valutaboulevard
en: Valuta is the general word for currency.

name: Van 't Hofflaan
en: Jacobus H. van 't Hoff (1852-1911), chemist, professor in Amsterdam from 1878 to 1896 and then in Berlin, who laid the foundations of stereochemistry and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901. The street came over from the municipality of Watergraafsmeer in 1921 under the name Koninginnelaan (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 31 July 1902).

name: Van Abbestraat
en: The Stedelijk Van Abbemuseum in Eindhoven. The art collector Henri van Abbe gave Eindhoven a museum of contemporary art in 1936, whose collection then consisted mainly of works Van Abbe had bought himself. Over the years the museum has built up an important collection, including works by Picasso, Chagall, Mondrian and Appel.

name: Van Alphenstraat
en: Hiëronymus van Alphen (1746-1803), poet, best known for his children's verse.

name: Van Baerlestraat
en: Caspar van Baerle or Barlaeus (1584-1648), Remonstrant minister and from 1632 professor at the Athenaeum, a renowned orator and writer of Latin poems. Part of this street was originally called Houbrakenstraat (council decision of 10 June 1880) and another part Roelof Hartstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 23 June 1893).

name: Van Beuningenplein
en: Coenraad van Beuningen (1622-1693), burgomaster of Amsterdam, statesman and envoy to various foreign courts.

name: Van Beuningenstraat
en: Coenraad van Beuningen (1622-1693), burgomaster of Amsterdam, statesman and envoy to various foreign courts.

name: Van Bleiswijkstraat
en: Pieter van Bleiswijk (1724-1790), statesman, Grand Pensionary of Holland from 1771 to 1787, who joined the opposition to Stadtholder William V and was removed from office in 1787.

name: Van Boetzelaerstraat
en: Pieter Alexander Baron van Boetzelaer (1759-1826), one of the burgomasters of Amsterdam from 1813 to 1824. After 1824 Amsterdam was governed by a single burgomaster.

name: Van Bommel-Van Dampad
en: The Museum Van Bommel Van Dam in Venlo. In 1967 Maarten van Bommel and his wife Reina van Bommel-van Dam gave their art collection to the municipality of Venlo, and in 1971 it was housed in a museum named after the couple. The collection ranges from paintings and drawings by Dutch artists to wooden sculptures from Africa.

name: Van Boshuizenstraat
en: Koenraad van Boshuizen was bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland from 1515 to 1530.

name: Van Bossestraat
en: Peter Philip van Bosse (1809-1879), liberal statesman, several times Minister of Finance and of the Colonies, who campaigned for free trade.

name: Van Brakelstraat
en: Jan van Brakel (1618-1690), naval officer under Admiral De Ruyter (the Four Days' Battle, the raid on Chatham).

name: Van Breestraat
en: Johannes Bernardus van Bree (1801-1857), composer, violinist, conductor and music teacher, the first conductor of the Caecilia society, who composed cantatas and masses.

name: Van de Sande Bakhuijzenstraat
en: The Van de Sande Bakhuyzen family of painters, among them Hendrikus (1795-1860), of the Romantic school, Julius (1835-1925), painter of townscapes and landscapes, and Gerardina (1826-1895), painter of flowers and fruit.

name: Van de Veldestraat
en: The brothers Adriaen van de Velde (1636-1672), landscape painter, and Willem van de Velde (1633-1707), painter of seascapes.

name: Van der Boechorststraat
en: Lord Floris van der Boechorst, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland from 1340 to 1347.

name: Van der Duijnstraat
en: Adam F.J.A. Count van der Duyn van Maasdam (1771-1848), one of the triumvirate (with Van Hogendorp and Van Limburg Stirum) that took charge of the government in 1813 and prepared the restoration of the stadtholder's family.

name: Van der Helstplein
en: Bartholomeus van der Helst (1612-1670), painter of militia and regents' group portraits.

name: Van der Hoopstraat
en: Joan Cornelis van der Hoop (1742-1825), after the upheaval of 1813 chairman of the provisional government of Amsterdam, and in 1814 Minister of the Navy.

name: Van der Pekstraat
en: Jan Ernst van der Pek (1865-1919), architect, who designed several blocks of workers' housing, mainly in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Van der Vijverstraat
en: Cornelis van der Vijver (1789-1855), historian, in particular of old Amsterdam.

name: Van Diemenkade
en: Anthony van Diemen (1593-1645), Amsterdam merchant, governor-general of the Dutch East Indies from 1636 to 1645. He sent Tasman on the voyage of 1642 that discovered Van Diemen's Land (Tasmania) and New Zealand. The street was laid out on the former Barentskade (council decision of 20 November 1878).

name: Van Diemenstraat
en: Anthony van Diemen (1593-1645), Amsterdam merchant, governor-general of the Dutch East Indies from 1636 to 1645. Together with Tasman he discovered New Holland (Australia) and Van Diemen's Land. The street was laid out on the former Barentskade (council decision of 20 November 1878).

name: Van Eeghenlaan
en: Christiaan Pieter van Eeghen (1816-1889), Amsterdam merchant and chairman of the supervisory board of De Nederlandsche Bank, who took the initiative for laying out the Vondelpark.

name: Van Eeghenstraat
en: Christiaan Pieter van Eeghen (1816-1889), Amsterdam merchant and chairman of the supervisory board of De Nederlandsche Bank, who took the initiative for laying out the Vondelpark.

name: Van Effenstraat
en: Justus van Effen (1684-1735), man of letters, whose work includes a French translation of Defoe's 'Robinson Crusoe'.

name: Van Gentstraat
en: Willem J. Baron van Ghent (1626-1672), lieutenant-admiral, who in 1667 sailed up the Thames and captured the English flagship (Chatham). He was killed in the Battle of Solebay in 1672. The street came to Amsterdam in 1921 under the name Piet Heinstraat (council decision of Sloten, 8 March 1910).

name: Van Gilsestraat
en: Maarten van Gilse (1918-1943), resistance fighter, born in Munich, executed by firing squad in Amsterdam, and Jan Hendrik van Gilse (1912-1944), resistance fighter, born in Munich, executed by firing squad in The Hague.

name: Van Hallstraat
en: Floris Adriaan van Hall (1791-1866), Amsterdam lawyer, who as Minister of Finance in 1844 took drastic measures to pay off the enormous national debt, and in 1848 led the conservative opposition.

name: Van Hanxleden Houwertstraat
en: Johan Coenraad H.F. van Hanxleden Houwert (1906-1945), resistance fighter, born in Medemblik, executed by firing squad in Limmen (Noord-Holland).

name: Van Heemskerckstraat
en: Jacob van Heemskerck (1567-1607), navigator sent out by Amsterdam in 1596 to find a sea route to the Indies 'round the north'. Heemskerck later became an admiral and was killed fighting the Spanish at Gibraltar. He is buried in the Oude Kerk.

name: Van Heenvlietlaan
en: Jan van Heenvliet, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland in 1396/1397.

name: Van Helt Stocadestraat
en: Nicolaas van Helt Stocade (1615-1669), painter, mainly of portraits.

name: Van Hilligaertstraat
en: Paulus van Hillegaert (1595-1640), painter.

name: Van Hogendorpplein
en: Gijsbert Karel van Hogendorp (1762-1834), liberal statesman and pensionary of Rotterdam, who with Van der Duyn van Maasdam and Van Limburg Stirum prepared the restoration of Dutch independence after the fall of Napoleon, and chaired the constitutional commission.

name: Van Hogendorpstraat
en: Gijsbert Karel van Hogendorp (1762-1834), liberal statesman and pensionary of Rotterdam, who with Van der Duyn van Maasdam and Van Limburg Stirum prepared the restoration of Dutch independence after the fall of Napoleon, and chaired the constitutional commission.

name: Van Houweningenstraat
en: Elsje van Houweningen, the maidservant of Hugo de Groot, who in 1621 helped him escape from Loevestein Castle in a book chest.

name: Van Karnebeekstraat
en: Jhr. Abraham Pieter Cornelis van Karnebeek (1836-1925), statesman, Minister of Foreign Affairs, vice-president of the First Hague Peace Conference and chairman of the Carnegie Foundation, and Jhr. Herman Adriaan van Karnebeek (1874-1942), statesman, Minister of Foreign Affairs, president of the League of Nations Assembly and author of the treaty with Belgium.

name: Van Kinsbergenstraat
en: Jan Hendrik van Kinsbergen (1735-1819), admiral at the Battle of the Dogger Bank in 1781, who reorganised the navy.

name: Van Koetsveldstraat
en: Cornelis Eliza van Koetsveld (1807-1893), minister and writer, whose 'Godsdienstige en zedelijke novellen' (religious and moral novellas) attacked the misery of rising capitalism. His best-known novel is 'De Pastorie van Mastland' (the Mastland parsonage).

name: Van Leijenberghlaan
en: Arent van Leyenbergh, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland around 1400.

name: Van Limburg Stirumplein
en: Leopold Count van Limburg Stirum (1758-1840), captain in the States army, who in 1813 took on the provisional government with Van Hogendorp and Van der Duyn van Maasdam and prepared the arrival of King William I.

name: Van Limburg Stirumstraat
en: Leopold Count van Limburg Stirum (1758-1840), captain in the States army, who in 1813 took on the provisional government with Van Hogendorp and Van der Duyn van Maasdam and prepared the arrival of King William I.

name: Van Linschotenstraat
en: Jan Huygen van Linschoten (1563-1611), well-known navigator and explorer, who wrote several travel accounts of the East and West Indies.

name: Van Marumstraat
en: Martinus van Marum (1750-1837), physician and mathematician, who built an electrostatic machine and wrote a dissertation on the movement of fluids in plants. From 1784 he was director of the Teylers Foundation.

name: Van Middellandtstraat
en: Pieter van Middellandt, rear admiral, who fought under Admiral De Ruyter off Etna in 1676 and was killed that same year in the Battle of Palermo.

name: Van Miereveldstraat
en: Michiel J. van Miereveld (1567-1641), portrait painter.

name: Van Mierlobrug
en: Henricus Antonius Franciscus Maria Oliva (Hans) van Mierlo (Breda, 18 August 1931 - Amsterdam, 11 March 2010), Dutch journalist and politician. In 1966 he and Hans Gruijters were the main founders of the social-liberal party Democraten '66, which he led in two separate periods, sitting in both the Senate and the House of Representatives. In the 1980s he was Minister of Defence in the Van Agt II and III cabinets, and from 1994 to 1998 Minister of Foreign Affairs and deputy prime minister in the 'purple' Kok I cabinet, which came about partly thanks to him. In 1998 he left politics and was given the title Minister of State.

name: Van Moerkerkenstraat
en: Pieter Hendrik van Moerkerken (1877-1951), man of letters and art critic, professor at the Academy of Fine Arts in Amsterdam.

name: Van Mourik Broekmanstraat
en: Gerrit H. van Mourik Broekman (1875-1948), hydraulic engineer, from 1900 professor in Santiago (Chile) and adviser to the Chilean government, and from 1924 professor at Delft.

name: Van Musschenbroekstraat
en: Petrus van Musschenbroek (1692-1761), physicist and professor at Duisburg, Utrecht and Leiden, inventor of the Leyden jar (1746), who demonstrated that a heated rod lengthens.

name: Van Neckstraat
en: Jacob van Neck (1564-1638), Dutch admiral, who twice sailed to the Moluccas for the East India trade, laying the foundations of Dutch trade with the East Indies, and was afterwards several times burgomaster of Amsterdam.

name: Van Nijenrodeweg
en: Gijsbrecht van Nijenrode, bailiff of Amstelland, Waterland and Gooiland in 1357-1358. Part of the road disappeared in 1986 when the street Beysterveld was laid out.

name: Van Noordtgracht
en: Olivier van Noort (1558-1627), navigator and ship's captain, who sailed round the world via the Strait of Magellan from 1598 to 1601 and later wrote an account of the voyage.

name: Van Noordtkade
en: Olivier van Noort (1558-1627), navigator and ship's captain, who sailed round the world via the Strait of Magellan from 1598 to 1601 and later wrote an account of the voyage.

name: Van Noordtstraat
en: Olivier van Noort (1558-1627), navigator and ship's captain, who sailed round the world via the Strait of Magellan from 1598 to 1601 and later wrote an account of the voyage.

name: Van Oldenbarneveldtplein
en: Johan van Oldenbarnevelt (1547-1619), statesman and Land's Advocate of Holland, who gave the impetus for founding the Dutch East India Company. After many years of working with Prince Maurits he came into conflict with him and finally died on the scaffold.

name: Van Oldenbarneveldtstraat
en: Johan van Oldenbarnevelt (1547-1619), statesman and Land's Advocate of Holland, who gave the impetus for founding the Dutch East India Company. After many years of working with Prince Maurits he came into conflict with him and finally died on the scaffold.

name: Van Ollefenstraat
en: Daan van Ollefen (1824-1900) and Christina da Silva (1809-1881), an acting couple. Mrs Van Ollefen-da Silva was one of the three stars of the Leidseplein.

name: Van Ostadestraat
en: Adriaen van Ostade (1610-1685), painter of peasant life. The stretch between the Amsteldijk and the Sweelinckstraat was formerly called Hoedemakersstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 20 March 1883) and was numbered from the Amsteldijk, as the Kuipersstraat and other nearby streets laid out by Nieuwer-Amstel before 1896 still are. When this stretch was renamed Van Ostadestraat in 1904, it had to be renumbered.

name: Van Rappardstraat
en: Willem Louis C. Ridder van Rappard (1798-1862), statesman, Minister of Finance in 1847.

name: Van Reedestraat
en: Hendrik Adriaan van Reede tot Drakenstein (1636-1693), of a noble Utrecht family, who left for Asia in 1656 in the service of the VOC, where he studied the tropical flora to improve the supply of medicines.

name: Van Reenenstraat
en: Jhr. Gerlach Cornelis Joannes van Reenen (1818-1893), burgomaster from 1850 to 1853, then Minister of the Interior until 1856, and afterwards for many years president of the House of Representatives and a member of the Council of State.

name: Van Reigersbergenstraat
en: Maria van Reigersberch (1589-1653), wife of Hugo de Groot.

name: Van Rensselaerstraat
en: Kiliaen van Rensselaer (c. 1586-1643), jeweller and member of the Amsterdam chamber of the West India Company, who founded the colony of Rensselaerswijck near New Amsterdam (New York).

name: Van Riebeeckhavenweg
en: Jan Anthonie van Riebeeck or Riebeek (1618-1708), who in 1652, in the service of the Dutch East India Company, founded the Cape Colony at the Cape of Good Hope.

name: Van Slingelandtplein
en: Simon van Slingelandt (1666-1736), secretary of the Council of State from 1690 to 1725 and Grand Pensionary from 1727 to 1736, who sought to improve the constitution of the state and wrote political writings in four volumes.

name: Van Slingelandtstraat
en: Simon van Slingelandt (1666-1736), secretary of the Council of State from 1690 to 1725 and Grand Pensionary from 1727 to 1736, who sought to improve the constitution of the state and wrote political writings in four volumes.

name: Van Speijkstraat
en: Jan Carel Josephus van Speijk (1802-1831), an Amsterdam orphan boy who became a naval officer. During the Belgian revolt in 1831 he blew up his ship near Antwerp rather than surrender.

name: Van Spilbergenstraat
en: Joris van Spilbergen (1568-1620), navigator, who sailed round the world from 1614 to 1617.

name: Van Suchtelen van de Haarestraat
en: Jhr. Anthon Hendrik Peter Karel van Suchtelen van de Haare (1869-1946), the last burgomaster of the municipality of Sloten (1909-1921).

name: Van Swindendwarsstraat
en: Jean Henri van Swinden (1746-1823), philosopher, mathematician and physicist, professor at Franeker and from 1785 in Amsterdam. He sat on the commission that fixed the metre, after which he worked out the metric system introduced in the Netherlands in 1816.

name: Van Tuyll van Serooskerkenplein
en: Frederik W.C.H. Baron van Tuyll van Serooskerken (1851-1924), the first chairman of the Dutch Olympic Committee.

name: Van Tuyll van Serooskerkenweg
en: Frederik W.C.H. Baron van Tuyll van Serooskerken (1851-1924), the first chairman of the Dutch Olympic Committee.

name: Van Walbeeckstraat
en: Johannes van Walbeeck (1601-1649), sea captain of the West India Company, who led the expedition that conquered Curaçao (1634).

name: Van Woustraat
en: Geert van Wou (c. 1450-1527), renowned bell-founder from Kampen.

name: Van Zeggelaarstraat
en: Gerrit van Zeggelaar (1868-1934), writer and journalist, known for his publications and lectures on Waterland. The street came over from the municipality of Landsmeer on 1 August 1966, with the names Thorbeckestraat, Borgesiusstraat and Groen van Prinstererstraat.

name: Vancouverstraat
en: George Vancouver (1757-1798), English navigator, the first to sail round the island named after him, Vancouver Island (off the west coast of Canada).

name: Varenweg
en: A plant family (ferns) that reproduces by spores.

name: Varikstraat
en: A former municipality on the Waal, in the Tielerwaard (Gelderland), now part of the municipality of Neerijnen.

name: Varkenssluis
en: This bridge is named after the pig market held here in the sixteenth century.

name: Vasco da Gamastraat
en: Portuguese explorer (1469-1524), who in 1497-1498 opened the sea route to India round the Cape of Good Hope.

name: Vätternkade
en: The second largest lake in Sweden, in the south of the country.

name: Vechtstraat
en: The river that flows into the IJsselmeer at Muiden.

name: Veebrug
en: Named after the former cattle market (veemarkt).

name: Veelaan
en: Named after the former cattle market (veemarkt).

name: Veemarkt
en: Named after the former cattle market (veemarkt).

name: Veemkade
en: A company that stores goods and runs warehouses (a veem). The Dutch vemen grew out of the seventeenth-century guilds of weigh-house porters.

name: Veenbesstraat
en: A red, sometimes white berry with a fresh, sour taste. There are two kinds: the small cranberry and the cranberry proper. The first grows in raised bogs; the second is common on Terschelling, after a barrel of cranberries washed ashore there in the mid-nineteenth century.

name: Veenderijbrug
en: This bridge was built around 1919 as a drawbridge over the Scheisloot, which served the peat digging in the Osdorper Binnenpolder, when the drainage channel behind the Osdorperweg was also widened into the Osdorpervaart so that peat boats could sail as far into the area as possible.

name: Veenendaalplein
en: A town in the Gelderse Vallei (Utrecht).

name: Veerstraat
en: A veer is a place where, and a boat with which, people are taken across a waterway (a ferry).

name: Veeteeltstraat
en: The branch of farming concerned with keeping (and breeding) livestock.

name: Vegastraat
en: The star Vega or Wega in the constellation Lyra, one of the brightest stars in the northern sky.

name: Velazquezstraat
en: Diego Rodríguez de Silva y Velázquez (1599-1660), Spanish painter of history pieces and portraits.

name: Veldbiesstraat
en: A grass-like plant (wood-rush), found mainly in the northern hemisphere.

name: Veldhuizenstraat
en: A village in the municipality of Vleuten-De Meern (Utrecht).

name: Veldzicht
en: A farm on the former Uitweg, demolished to build the western garden suburbs. Before 1975 this street was called Heijningspad (council decision of 16 January 1958), a name withdrawn when the Heining was named.

name: Velserweg
en: The Noord-Holland municipality of Velsen, where the North Sea Canal was dug through the dunes. Until the Van Riebeeckhaven was dug, the road ran from Sloterdijk to the municipal boundary, and before it was named in 1938 it was called Middenweg (Grote IJpolder) and Frogerweg.

name: Veluwelaan
en: The part of the province of Gelderland between the Gelderse Vallei and the Gelderse IJssel.

name: Venetiëhof
en: The Italian port to which the former KNSM ran a regular service.

name: Venetiëstraat
en: The Italian port to which the former KNSM ran a regular service.

name: Venhuizenstraat
en: The village between Hoorn and Enkhuizen (Noord-Holland).

name: Vennepluimstraat
en: A kind of reed.

name: Verbindingsdam
en: A dam in the Ertshaven.

name: Verbindingstraat
en: The names express the function. The dam links the IJ island, laid out in 1898, with the Handelskade. The street was laid out before the great annexation of 1896, so that residents of Nieuwer-Amstel living here on the edge of Amsterdam could reach their town hall on the Amsteldijk over their own municipality's ground.

name: Verdistraat
en: Giuseppe Verdi (1813-1901), Italian opera composer, whose works include 'Aida', 'Rigoletto' and 'La Traviata'.

name: Verfstraat
en: A reference to the Vettewinkel paint factory, later Sigma, on the Cruquius site from 1934 to 2008.

name: Verlengde Stellingweg
en: A stelling is the gallery on struts around a tall windmill, from which the miller turns the cap into the wind and takes in the sails. In 1976, for traffic reasons, part of the Stellingweg was renamed Molenaarsweg and another part was added to the Appelweg.

name: Verleunstraat
en: Johannes Adrianus Jozef Verleun (1919-1944), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in The Hague.

name: Veronesestraat
en: Paolo Caliari, called Veronese (1528-1588), Italian painter of large decorative canvases.

name: Vertrouwen
en: Confidence (vertrouwen) in being able to reach the goal set.

name: Verversstraat
en: This trade name (dyers) recalls the cloth industry, important in Amsterdam in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. After 1593 the cloth dyers were allowed to settle only between the Kloveniersburgwal and the Zwanenburgwal. At that time the Groenburgwal was called the Verversgracht.

name: Vervoorenstraat
en: Louis Christiaan Vervooren (1895-1944), resistance fighter, born in Rotterdam, died in Bruttig (Germany).

name: Vespuccistraat
en: Amerigo Vespucci (1454-1512), Florentine explorer, who sailed along and described the coasts of America. That is probably why America is named after him and not after Columbus.

name: Vianenstraat
en: A small fortified town on the Lek (Zuid-Holland).

name: Victor Rutgersstraat
en: Victor Henri Rutgers (1877-1945), resistance fighter, who died in the Bochum concentration camp (Germany). Rutgers was a lawyer and statesman, Minister of Education in 1925 and from 1928 a professor at the Vrije Universiteit in Amsterdam.

name: Victoria Welbystraat
en: Victoria Welby (1837-1912) was a prominent British philosopher and theorist of language.

name: Victorieplein
en: The square was given this name in 1946 to mark the victory of the Allied countries. Before that it was called Daniël Willinkplein, after the poet (1676-1722) known for his Amstellandsche Arcadia (council decision of 22 March 1922).

name: Vier Heemskinderensluis
en: This bridge is named after the gable stone showing the Four Sons of Aymon (the Vier Heemskinderen) on the corner house of the Herengracht and the Leidsegracht.

name: Vier Heemskinderenstraat
en: Named after the gable stone showing the Four Sons of Aymon (the Vier Heemskinderen) on the corner house of the Herengracht and the Leidsegracht.

name: Vierde Vogelstraat
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Viermasterstraat
en: A sailing ship with four masts, usually a barque.

name: Vierwindendwarsstraat
en: This curious name (four winds) probably comes from a gable stone of a house or warehouse that stood here on the Realeneiland. A similar stone gave a house on the Lindengracht the name ''t huis in de vier blazende winden' (the house in the four blowing winds).

name: Vierwindenstraat
en: This curious name (four winds) probably comes from a gable stone of a house or warehouse that stood here on the Realeneiland. A similar stone gave a house on the Lindengracht the name ''t huis in de vier blazende winden' (the house in the four blowing winds).

name: Vijfde Vogelstraat
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Vijgepeerpad
en: An old Dutch variety of pear. The path lies on the former De Bongerd allotment gardens.

name: Vijverhoef
en: An old knightly manor near Breukelen on the Vecht, originally of 1670 and demolished in 1812, celebrated by Vondel. The present Vijverhof, on the same site, dates from 1867.

name: Vijzelgracht
en: The name probably comes from the former residents Cornelis Arents Vijselaar (around 1600) and Jan Vijselaar (around 1632). The Vijzelstraat was then a short street running as far as today's Reguliersdwarsstraat. When the street was extended, the name passed to the extension too, and until the eighteenth century people spoke of the Oude and Nieuwe Vijzelstraat. The Vijzelgracht, dug between 1660 and 1670, was filled in in 1934.

name: Vijzelstraat
en: The name probably comes from the former residents Cornelis Arents Vijselaar (around 1600) and Jan Vijselaar (around 1632). The Vijzelstraat was then a short street running as far as today's Reguliersdwarsstraat. When the street was extended, the name passed to the extension too, and until the eighteenth century people spoke of the Oude and Nieuwe Vijzelstraat. The Vijzelgracht, dug between 1660 and 1670, was filled in in 1934.

name: Vikingpad
en: A collective name for groups of adventurers, exiles, traders and emigrants from Denmark, Norway and Sweden who raided the coasts of 'Frisia', especially in the ninth century.

name: Vilvoordestraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Vincent van Goghstraat
en: Vincent Willem van Gogh (1853-1890), painter and draughtsman, who worked first in the Borinage and Drenthe before leaving for France in 1886, where he made most of his best-known paintings. He was of great importance for the development of painting.

name: Vinkenstraat
en: The strip south of the Haarlemmerdijk, between today's Binnen Oranjestraat and the Haarlemmerplein, was called the Rietvink in the sixteenth century after an old inn. The street laid out here in the seventeenth century was then called Rietstraat, Vinkenstraat and Middenstraat by turns, and in the end the name Vinkenstraat stuck. The first public Protestant sermon was preached on the Rietvink in 1566, when that was not yet permitted inside the city.

name: Violette Corneliushof
en: Photographer (1919-1998), who during the Second World War became involved in the artists' resistance, working for the underground magazine 'De Vrije Kunstenaar' and later for the Persoonsbewijzen Centrale (forged identity papers). After the war she became an architectural photographer and finally chose reportage photography.

name: Violettenstraat
en: An old name for the flower the violet.

name: Virginiahof
en: Virginia Dementricia, later Virginia Gaai (Aruba, 1842 - after 1867), was an enslaved woman who rebelled against her owners on Aruba. She repeatedly broke the rules imposed on her and was punished with forced labour each time. In 1859 she tried to run away, which failed and led to more hard labour and a prison sentence. Soon after her release Virginia was arrested again and accused of 'street disturbance and resisting the police', and this time given corporal punishment. Her owner sold her in 1860. Slavery was abolished in 1863. The last that is known of her is that she gave birth to a son, Marcelino Martis Gaai, in Willemstad on 2 June 1867. In 2005 the Aruban artist Vanessa Paulina immortalised Virginia in a three-panel multimedia screen, and she has since been regarded as a symbol of resistance to slavery on Aruba.

name: Virginiastraat
en: Virginia Dementricia, later Virginia Gaai (Aruba, 1842 - after 1867), was an enslaved woman who rebelled against her owners on Aruba. She repeatedly broke the rules imposed on her and was punished with forced labour each time. In 1859 she tried to run away, which failed and led to more hard labour and a prison sentence. Soon after her release Virginia was arrested again and accused of 'street disturbance and resisting the police', and this time given corporal punishment. Her owner sold her in 1860. Slavery was abolished in 1863. The last that is known of her is that she gave birth to a son, Marcelino Martis Gaai, in Willemstad on 2 June 1867. In 2005 the Aruban artist Vanessa Paulina immortalised Virginia in a three-panel multimedia screen, and she has since been regarded as a symbol of resistance to slavery on Aruba.

name: Visseringstraat
en: Simon Vissering (1818-1888), professor of political science at Leiden and Minister of Finance, who as early as 1848 campaigned for IJmuiden as a new seaport.

name: Viveportenstraat
en: A chapel village on Terschelling that disappeared in storm floods in the sixteenth century.

name: Vlaardingenlaan
en: A town in Zuid-Holland on the Nieuwe Maas.

name: Vlaggemast
en: The ship's mast on which the flag is flown.

name: Vlakkerweg
en: The trade name for someone who flattens metal with a flatter hammer. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding industry of Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Vleutenstraat
en: A place in Utrecht.

name: Vliegtuigstraat
en: The means of air transport using lifting surfaces (wings).

name: Vlielandstraat
en: A Wadden island (Friesland).

name: Vlierweg
en: A plant (elder) with white flowers and black berries.

name: Vlietstraat
en: A drainage canal (vliet).

name: Vlimmerenstraat
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Vlothaven
en: The nearby Vlothaven, dug in 1931, was originally shallow and, as part of the timber harbour, meant for timber rafts (vlotten). Around 1960 it was deepened and made suitable for seagoing ships.

name: Vlothavenweg
en: The nearby Vlothaven, dug in 1931, was originally shallow and, as part of the timber harbour, meant for timber rafts (vlotten). Around 1960 it was deepened and made suitable for seagoing ships.

name: Vluchthavenbrug
en: Probably named after the part of the harbour where small ships could moor in bad weather (a harbour of refuge).

name: VOC-kade
en: The Dutch East India Company (VOC), founded in 1602 for the East Indies trade and run by seventeen directors (the Heeren XVII). From Batavia, its administrative centre in Asia, it built up a network of trading posts. In 1799 the state took over the company.

name: Voetbalstraat
en: Refers to the sports park with football clubs that was here.

name: Voetboogstraat
en: The street was laid out in 1649 on the shooting range of the Crossbowmen's Doelen.

name: Vogelenzangstraat
en: A village in the dune region, on the edge of the Amsterdam water-supply dunes.

name: Vogelkade
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Vogelplantsoen
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Vogelplein
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Volendammerweg
en: A village south-east of Edam, known for its traditional dress.

name: Volewijckbrug
en: This bridge is named after De Volewijck, a small peninsula in the IJ rich in birds, over which the city gained authority in 1393. Until 1795 a mass gallows with stakes stood on this land, on which the bodies of criminals hanged on the Dam were displayed.

name: Volewijkshof
en: The spit of land north of the IJ, directly opposite the centre of Amsterdam. As early as 1360 there was a gallows field here, where the bodies of the executed were hung up and displayed. After the arrival of the Batavian Republic in 1795 the practice was banned.

name: Volharding
en: Perseverance (volharding) in pursuing the goal.

name: Volkerakstraat
en: The water between Overflakkee and Noord-Brabant, closed off from the Haringvliet and the Hollands Diep by a dam in 1970 (Hellegatsplein).

name: Voltaplein
en: Alessandro Volta (1745-1827), Italian physicist and professor at Pavia, who made various inventions in electricity. The unit of electrical potential, the volt, is named after him.

name: Voltastraat
en: Alessandro Volta (1745-1827), Italian physicist and professor at Pavia, who made various inventions in electricity. The unit of electrical potential, the volt, is named after him.

name: Von Guerickestraat
en: Otto von Guericke (1602-1682), German physicist, inventor of the air pump and the electrostatic machine. The Magdeburg hemispheres, used to demonstrate the effect of air pressure, are named after him (Von Guericke was burgomaster of Magdeburg). The street was originally named Wolmaransstraat by the municipality of Watergraafsmeer (council decision of 26 February 1915). In 1922 all the streets in this neighbourhood were given new names.

name: Von Humboldtstraat
en: Alexander Baron von Humboldt (1769-1859), naturalist and scientific explorer, who travelled in South America and Siberia, a founder of climatology and plant geography.

name: Von Liebigweg
en: Justus von Liebig (1803-1873), German chemist, researcher of artificial fertilisers, who devised a method for making meat extract.

name: Von Zesenstraat
en: Philipp von Zesen (1619-1689), German historian, whose works include 'Beschreibung der Stadt Amsterdam' (description of the city of Amsterdam).

name: Vondelbrug
en: Joost van den Vondel (1587-1679) was a poet who wrote many tragedies, the best known of which is 'Gijsbrecht van Aemstel'.

name: Vondelkerkstraat
en: The street was taken over under this name from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel. No naming decision by that municipality, or its reason, has been found. The Vondelkerk, built in 1873 to a design by Pierre Cuypers, is about a kilometre away and so cannot have been the reason for the name.

name: Vondelpark
en: Joost van den Vondel (1587-1679), poet, who wrote 24 tragedies as well as poetry on heroes and heroic deeds. The part of the street that lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1896 was first called Verlengde Vondelstraat. Led by C.P. van Eeghen, a group of Amsterdammers drew up a plan in 1864 for a park for riding and walking, which was then carried out to a design by L.D. Zocher. The first part opened in 1865. When a statue of Vondel was placed here in 1867, the park was named Vondelpark.

name: Vondelstraat
en: Joost van den Vondel (1587-1679), poet, who wrote 24 tragedies as well as poetry on heroes and heroic deeds. The part of the street that lay in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1896 was first called Verlengde Vondelstraat. Led by C.P. van Eeghen, a group of Amsterdammers drew up a plan in 1864 for a park for riding and walking, which was then carried out to a design by L.D. Zocher. The first part opened in 1865. When a statue of Vondel was placed here in 1867, the park was named Vondelpark.

name: Voorboezem
en: A boezem is a body of inland water without a fixed water level (a storage basin).

name: Voorburgstraat
en: A town in Zuid-Holland, a suburb of The Hague.

name: Voordek
en: One of a ship's decks (the foredeck).

name: Voordewind
en: A nautical term, especially in sailing: with the wind dead astern. The term is also often used figuratively (plain sailing).

name: Voorlandpad
en: A former farmstead on the Middenweg, built in 1689 as Meerenburg and renamed Voorland in 1722. It was demolished in 1934 to make way for Ajax's De Meer stadium.

name: Voormalige Stadstimmertuin
en: The City Carpentry Yards (workshops and stores for building materials) were here from 1660 to 1899. They are now on the Van Reigersbergenstraat.

name: Voornestraat
en: The western part of the Zuid-Holland island of Voorne-Putten.

name: Voorsteven
en: The foremost part of a ship's hull (the stem).

name: Voorthuizenstraat
en: The village in the municipality of Barneveld (Gelderland).

name: Vorselaarstraat
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Vorticellaweg
en: A microscopic water creature: a single-celled ciliate with a bell-shaped head and a contractile stalk.

name: Vosmaerstraat
en: Carel Vosmaer (1826-1888), writer and critic, clerk at the court in The Hague and then at the Supreme Court. Originally a classicist, he later supported the movement of the Tachtigers. His works include 'Nanno' and a translation of the Iliad and the Odyssey.

name: Vossenbesstraat
en: Also called red whortleberry (lingonberry), a plant of the heather family, native to the Netherlands and growing on poor soil. Because of its sour, somewhat astringent taste the lingonberry is usually made into compote.

name: Vossiusstraat
en: Gerardus Johannes Voss, who called himself Vossius (1577-1649), philologist and historian, professor successively at Heidelberg, Leiden and, from 1631, together with Barlaeus at the Amsterdam Athenaeum. His textbook on rhetoric (1648) was very influential.

name: Vredeman de Vriesstraat
en: Jan Vredeman de Vries (1527-1606), architect and painter, who also worked in several foreign cities and through his designs, books and engravings spread the Dutch Renaissance style.

name: Vredenburgerbrug
en: Named after the Vredenburgersteeg and the well-known seventeenth-century inn Vredenburg, on whose site the Roman Catholic old people's home Vredenburg was built in 1835, now converted into housing.

name: Vredenburgersteeg
en: A very well-known seventeenth-century inn, which stood where the Roman Catholic old people's home Vredenburg was built in 1835, now converted into housing. Before the inn there were successively a brewery of burgomaster Kornelis Jacobsz and a salt works here, hence the former names Cornelis Jacobsz Brouwersteeg and Zoutkoperssteeg. The name Rottenest also occurred.

name: Vredenhofpad
en: Named after the neighbouring Vredenhof cemetery on the Haarlemmerweg.

name: Vredenhofweg
en: Named after the neighbouring Vredenhof cemetery on the Haarlemmerweg.

name: Vredespleintje
en: The name was chosen in 2016 by local residents and refers to the theme of 'peace' (vrede), written about by at least thirteen eighteenth- and nineteenth-century writers after whom streets in the neighbourhood are named. The square used to host the Solidarity Festival, and in 2010 the festival 'Wereldburgers van Amsterdam' (world citizens of Amsterdam).

name: Vreelandplein
en: A village on the Vecht (Utrecht). The castle of the same name was demolished in 1529 on the orders of Charles V.

name: Vreeswijkpad
en: A Utrecht town on the Lek opposite Vianen, now part of the municipality of Nieuwegein.

name: Vriesseveem
en: A veem is a company that stores goods in its warehouses and delivers them from there. Each veem had its own emblem, after which it was named. These could be hats of different colours and shapes (among them Blauwhoeden, blue hats, and Klapmutsen). They also took their names from where their workmen came from (among them the Vriesseveem and the Zeeuwse Veem).

name: Vrijburg
en: A former country estate on the Haarlemmerweg.

name: Vrije Geer
en: An old name for part of the municipality of Sloten, a triangular area stretching from the south-east tip of the Slotermeer to the Haarlemmermeer. It lay outside Amsterdam's jurisdiction (1100 roeden), and its inhabitants were traditionally exempt from paying certain levies to the Counts of Holland.

name: Vrijheidslaan
en: This avenue, originally called Amstellaan, was renamed Stalinlaan after the Second World War, after the Soviet leader Joseph Stalin, because the Soviet Union had brought about our liberation together with the Allies. After the Russian intervention in the Hungarian uprising of 1956 the name was changed to Vrijheidslaan (freedom avenue).

name: Vrijzicht
en: A former farm in the old municipality of Sloten.

name: Vrolikstraat
en: Gerardus Vrolik (1775-1859) and his son Willem Vrolik (1801-1863), both professors of medicine in Amsterdam, who brought together a large collection of anatomical specimens. The first part of this street is now called Wibautstraat.

name: Vrouwenmantelstraat
en: A plant (lady's mantle), native to Europe, northern and western Asia, North America and Greenland, traditionally used among other things against severe menstrual pain and menopausal complaints.

name: Vuurwerkerplantsoen
en: A vuurwerker is, or was, a trade in the metal industry.

name: Vuurwerkerweg
en: A trade name: someone who works the glowing metal in a smithy.

name: W.J. Bijleveldstraat
en: Wolter Jan Bijleveld (1902-1945), resistance fighter, born in Makassar, died in Völklingen (Germany), head of the communications and intelligence service of the Ordedienst (O.D.).

name: W.J. Knoopstraat
en: Lieutenant-general (1811-1894), who helped campaign for the founding of the Netherlands Red Cross.

name: W.L. Penningstraat
en: Willem Levinus Penning (1840-1924), poet under the pseudonym M. Coens.

name: Waagdragerhof
en: Weigh-house porters (waagdragers) were responsible for weighing goods at the Waag, carrying them from the warehouses to the weigh house.

name: Waaigat
en: An old name for an opening in the row of houses along a canal (a wind gap). There were also waaigaten on the Warmoesstraat and the Rapenburgerstraat.

name: Waalenburgsingel
en: A polder on Texel (north of the village of De Waal): meadows and marshland with rich fauna and flora.

name: Waalseilandbrug
en: Named after the word 'waal', meaning a stretch of water enclosed by rows of piles, where ships could winter or be repaired.

name: Waalstraat
en: A branch of the Rhine from Nijmegen to Gorinchem, after which it joins the Maas and is called the Merwede.

name: Waddendijk
en: A shallow area outside the dikes that dries out at low tide (mudflats), especially in the Wadden Sea.

name: Waddenweg
en: A shallow area outside the dikes that dries out at low tide (mudflats), especially in the Wadden Sea.

name: Wagenaarstraat
en: Jan Wagenaar (1709-1773), historian and city historian of Amsterdam, whose works include the 'Vaderlandsche Historie' (21 volumes) and a history of Amsterdam in three volumes.

name: Wageningendreef
en: A town in Gelderland.

name: Wagenstraat
en: The name recalls the wagon square, a stand for wagons coming from outside the city, by the Regulierspoort.

name: Wakkerstraat
en: Jacobus Philippus van Medenbach Wakker (1784-1860), notary and burgomaster of the municipality of Watergraafsmeer from 1817 to 1853. The street is named after him because he lived there.

name: Walborg
en: A seventeenth-century country house on the Maas near Laak (Limburg), of which only a ruin remains.

name: Walcherenstraat
en: One of the Zeeland islands, now fully joined to Zuid-Beveland by the reclamation of the Sloe.

name: Wannepad
en: A Belgian town (Spa) in the province of Liège.

name: Waregemstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

name: Watermaalpad
en: A Belgian town in the province of Brabant.

name: Weegbreestraat
en: The plant family (gentians).

name: Werengouw
en: A weer is a long strip of land between two boundary ditches; the ditch between two weren is sometimes called a werengouw. By council decision of 27 October 1971 part of the road was added to the Buikslotermeerplein.

name: Westerdok
en: The closing dike, built between 1830 and 1834, that turned the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to the Station Island at the end of the 1880s, part of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 when the Haarlemmer Houttuinen were widened.

en: The closing dike, built between 1830 and 1834, that turned the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. name: Westerkoggestraat
en: A polder in West-Friesland.

name: Westmallepad
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Weteringlaan
en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. The Schans was once the rampart on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century the walls and ramparts were demolished. Parts were turned into promenades (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen), and a road was built that was at first called the Schans along its whole length but later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was laid out on the site freed by the demolition of the flour and bread factory. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries this was the paving yard.

name: Weteringschans
en: The streets lie in the Weteringbuurt. The names recall the Wetering, which originally flowed from outside into the Spui; the Boerenwetering is a remnant of it. name: Wevelgemstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

name: Wielewaalstraat
en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

name: Wijde Kerksteeg
en: After the Oude Kerk, which the alleys lead to from the Warmoesstraat, part of which was originally called Kerkstraat.

name: Wijde Lombardsteeg
en: After the nearby lommerd, or Bank van Lening (pawnshop), founded in 1614.

name: Wilgenweg
en: The deciduous tree: a beuk is a beech.

name: Wilhelminastraat
en: Wilhelmina Helena Pauline Maria, Princess of Orange-Nassau (1880-1962), daughter of King William III and Queen Emma, Queen of the Netherlands from 1898 to 1948.

name: Willebroekstraat
en: Belgian town in the province of Antwerp.

name: Wismargracht
en: The names of the canals refer to the names of the bridges that cross them.

name: Wittenburgergracht
en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. One of the first yards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. This is very probably where the name Wittenburg comes from.

name: Wittenburgerkade
en: One of the three eastern islands (with Kattenburg and Oostenburg), laid out in the second half of the seventeenth century and built up with shipyards and houses from the start. name: Wognumerpad
en: A village in Noord-Holland.

name: Wognumerplantsoen
en: A village in Noord-Holland.

name: Wognumerstraat
en: A village in Noord-Holland.

name: Wolderwijdpad
en: One of the Veluwe border lakes (randmeren).

name: Zeilmakerstraat
en: A trade name from shipbuilding (ropemaker). The name recalls the many shipyards here in earlier centuries.

name: Zelzatestraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of East Flanders.

name: Zesde Vogelstraat
en: The streets in this neighbourhood are named after birds.

name: Zonhovenstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Zonnebeke
en: A Belgian town in the province of West-Vlaanderen (West Flanders).

name: Zonnehof
en: The central body of the planetary system to which the Earth belongs (the sun).

name: Zonneplein
en: The central body of the planetary system to which the Earth belongs (the sun).

name: Zonneweg
en: The central body of the planetary system to which the Earth belongs (the sun).

name: Zorgzaam
en: The group of women who regularly hold their silent march on the Plaza de Mayo in Buenos Aires (Argentina), wanting the truth about the fate of their husbands and children who disappeared under the generals' regime. Against the weapons of violence and empty talk, they show through their solidarity and persistence their struggle for truth, freedom and justice. Several streets around this square are named after the virtues they stand for (opmerkzaam = attentive).

name: Zutendaalstraat
en: A Belgian town in the province of Limburg.

name: Zwaluwstraat
en: The songbird (the cuckoo).

name: Zwanenplein
en: The water bird (the duck).
